author: Khyl Ramos, Ben Radford
title: Gen Z protests, Pax Silica and fighting for an ecosocialist future
content:
Khyl Ramos works on climate justice, labour rights and grassroots organising in the Philippines. He is the deputy project manager at Transform Asia Gender and Labor Institute and youth coordinator for the Party of the Labouring Masses (PLM).

Ramos was a guest speaker at the recent Ecosocialism 2026 conference in Magan-djin/Brisbane, where he sat down with Green Left’s Ben Radford to discuss last year’s Gen Z protests, recent opposition to the United States-led Pax Silica initiative and the need for ecosocialist alternatives.

How would you characterise the Gen Z protests in the Philippines last year?

The Gen Z uprising in the Philippines last year was simultaneous with the protests in Indonesia, Nepal and Bangladesh.

The president revealed in July that there was a flood control scandal, in which congresspeople, along with other senior government officials and contractors had corrupted billions of pesos in public funds.

The funds were supposed to go to disaster preparedness and disaster risk reduction management, because we’re a very flood-prone country. But the people in charge of the Department of Public Works and Highways, as well as lawmakers — since they deliberate on the budget in Congress — pocketed the money.

That was the start [of the protests] — students were really enraged about that, especially university students, since there are many universities in Manila situated in flood-prone areas, and they see this as a broader systemic issue of corruption.

In terms of the [Gen Z] movement, it’s very spontaneous. [PLM] tried to maximise on organising around that spontaneity. We’ve revived our youth and student groups; however, not just university students — we are trying to expand to senior high school students — 16- to 17-year-olds — as a new force in the movement.

We’ve been explaining the issue through a number of youth and students’ assemblies against corruption and political dynasties we held in November, 2025. We related it to issues that students can easily understand, for example, around education funding, [and what it would mean] if funds were allocated to education instead of being corrupted.

We’ve been centring our argument to fuel the movement — [explaining] how corruption is really affecting not just grassroots communities, but also students.

We are building an independent youth movement, separate from parents as well, because some of the youth are quite shy when their parents are around. As people in the party say: “Don’t let the parents get involved, let the students do the organising.”

How do the recent Pax Silica protests tie in with struggles for climate justice and resisting green colonialism?

Pax Silica is a US-led economic and technological security initiative, with the US trying to gather allies from around the region. Australia is also part of that alliance, along with Japan and more than 20 other countries, including the Philippines. [The US] has been trying to move its allies away from China, since China is one of the leading countries in the critical minerals and semiconductor industries.

Now, we are being targeted as one of the centres for the Pax Silica initiative. They’re trying to build AI data centres and a manufacturing and semiconductor processing hub in New Clark City [in Central Luzon, about 100 kilometres northwest of the capital, Manila], which will occupy around 1600 hectares of land, which indigenous communities are living on. It is their ancestral lands, which they will face displacement from.

When we started the campaign around April this year, it wasn’t well known... But the campaign against Pax Silica has really boomed in the past two months, because they’ve been trying to fast-track it.

There are different progressive movements making solidarity visits to the area to see the situation and put forward a campaign.

[Pax Silica] also has a geopolitical agenda because of the US conflict with China. We’re in the middle of it, especially with the continuous installation of US presence [through the] Enhanced Defence Cooperation Agreement (EDCA). We had five [EDCA sites] in 2023, and it’s increased to nine now.

Filipino and US troops are doing [joint] military exercises ... firing guns and detonating bombs. Last May 2026, in Leyte, Eastern Visayas, a US Tomahawk cruise missile was launched as part of the Balikatan [military] exercises, and struck a designated target area in Nueva Ecija. The impact on the ground is really being felt by our communities.

They’re …

author: Danica Rachel
title: Protest called against October arms fair in Perth
content:
The Land Forces Exposition 2026, to be held at the Perth Convention and Exhibition Centre on 6-8 October, will be a three-day extravaganza of exhibitions, talks and luncheons, where the main topic of conversation is how best to kill people. More than 20,000 weapons company executives, politicians and military personnel from around the world are expected to attend.

We have to protest against this outrageous celebration of death and destruction.

Photos from the 2024 event on the front page of the

Land Forces website

 are enough to make you ill. A smiling representative of Anduril, a company specialising in AI-powered warfare, shows off a battle drone. A live demonstration of a robot dog, presumably designed to carry autonomous weapons, takes place on the exhibition floor. A drone as big as a car hangs from the ceiling.

Lockheed Martin, the world’s biggest arms dealer—and builder of the F-35 fighter jets Israel uses to bomb Gaza—will have its latest death machines on display. As will Elbit Systems, Israel’s biggest weapons company.

Senior executives from Anduril and BAE Systems will speak on a panel discussing “the realities of Ukraine, Iran and other current conflicts”. Today’s bloodshed used as a case study to make tomorrow’s killing more efficient. What could those “other conflicts” be? Israel’s invasion of Lebanon? One assumes that there’s much these monsters have learned from Gaza, too.

Lockheed Martin and BAE will be joined by Babcock, Boeing, Honeywell, Northrop Grumman and Thales. Aside from all having had significant roles in providing Israel’s weapons for use in Gaza, they are all on the exclusive list of companies involved in creating nuclear weapons.

The list goes on, and on, and on. More than 650 companies will have exhibits on the floor, all of them dealing in weapons, military hardware or AI systems for warfare.

To say the state Labor government is rolling out the red carpet for this smorgasbord of warmongers would be an understatement. It is going above and beyond to keep conference-goers comfortable by pouring $11.5 million into security.

Special legislation gives police the power to set up checkpoints, stop and search anyone for any reason, and ban anyone they like from a significant section of Perth’s CBD, including a major train and bus station, for ten days surrounding the event.

Police Minister Reece Whitby said of the laws: “We saw the scenes that occurred when Land Forces was held in Melbourne in 2024, and we do not want to see anything like that here in Perth”. Whitby was referring to the

protest by 1,500 people

 against the last iteration of this festival of death.

None of this—the war profiteering, the authoritarian police powers, the increased drive towards a world of total war—should pass without protest.

So a coalition of anti-war and Palestine solidarity organisations has called a demonstration against Land Forces on 6 October, 5pm, at Yagan Square in the Perth CBD. We need as many people as possible to make it clear that we reject Land Forces and everything it represents.

author: AWSM
title: Why I Won’t Vote ~ A SYMPOSIUM #1
content:
Anarchy 37, March 1964, Why I Won’t Vote

Voting : “The instrument and symbol of a freeman’s power to make a fool of himself and a wreck of his country”

The saying that ” only a fool would put a loaded gun into the hands of an idiot ” is an especially apt analogy of government. An idiot (usually well-meaning) considers himself clever enough to run the affairs of a large number of people by taking a seat in parliament. A large number of people, acting like fools, vote for his party’s policy then spend the next few years grumbling about the results. The error in approach is that the voter thinks that he will get what he voted for. If he could vote for those who in fact control the country, say the Governors of the Bank of England, the directors of the industrial corporations and those behind the ministries, the illusion of democracy would be more understandable.

The real centres of power lie far beyond the people’s influence at elections. These remain constant whatever Party is ” in power “. In the terms of centralised ” democracy ” the only possible argument to justify voting is that marginal benefits may be gained. The state only incidentally attends to the well-being of its subjects. Its main concern is its power relation to other states, of which the most perfect expression is in war.

I am on the side of people anywhere who are prepared neither to live nor die for something that in the long run can only militate against survival and the conditions that make life worth living. Our immediate action must, by its nature, be to oppose that pathetic gesture, voting. It must be direct and direction. We can learn to live as free men and women only by organising against the condition we are in.

The Tenants Association, Consumers Association, and Direct Action in industry all provide opportunities for people to experience directing their own lives in positive ways towards positive ends.

Only by direct involvement in society can the individual hope to transform himself and his world. Freedom cannot be given, it must be taken; and the free society can only grow from experiments in the problems (ethical and organisational) of community.

Voting does not, and cannot, mean government by consent. By voting, one acts on the assumptions that certain men are fit to govern, and that a majority is necessarily right. Also should the state, acting in the name of a (frequently fictitious) majority, declare war, the individual loses the right to live, if he ever had it.

To me, voting is complicity with the State and a negative action, therefore I do not vote.

author: James Plested
title: Victorian Socialists’ election campaign in full swing
content:
The Victorian state election will take place in just over two months, on Saturday 28 November. The Victorian Socialists’ campaign is now in full swing, with local campaign activity taking place daily across Melbourne and regional Victoria.

The scale of the campaign—with VS candidates set to run in all 88 lower house seats and all eight upper house regions across Victoria—is beyond anything the socialist left in Australia has attempted for generations (if ever). Even just a few years ago, a statewide campaign like this would have been unthinkable. That it’s happening at all is something of a breakthrough.

Between 1 June and 19 September, VS volunteers knocked on more than 80,000 doors, already well on track to reach the 2022 campaign total of around 190,000. The party received around 2,000 requests for campaign signs to be put on front fences and in yards, eclipsing the 2022 total of 1,000, with hundreds of orders a week still coming in. More than 2,400 people donated to the campaign, and almost 1,800 registered for a party event. 

New branches are springing up everywhere. Wherever they do, we’re finding people who want to get involved. VS events in places like Pakenham, a suburb on the far south-eastern fringe of Melbourne—more than 50 kilometres from the CBD—are attracting many new faces. And we now have active branches in regional centres including Geelong, Warrnambool, Ballarat and Bendigo, and the beginnings of branches in Shepparton, Wodonga and Warragul. 

We’re accustomed to being almost completely overlooked by the mainstream media, but the sheer size of our campaign this time means we’re increasingly difficult to ignore.

ABC News reported

 on the VS campaign launch on 1 August, and Channel 9 reported on our “all-in” Footscray doorknock on Sunday 16 August, which was attended by more than 350 volunteers. VS candidate for the Northern Metro upper house region Omar Hassan has become something of a regular fixture on talkback radio 3AW’s morning show with Tom Elliot—most recently on the topic

“what is socialism?”

VS candidates in the regions are attracting particular attention.

Hera Sheppard,

 in the seat of

South-West Coast

 (comprising Warrnambool, Port Fairy, Portland and surrounds), has been featured in several articles in the

Warrnambool Standard

, including the front cover. An

article at ABC News

 and an appearance on ABC Radio followed—the latter

drawing the ire

 of Australia’s richest billionaire Gina Rinehart, who objected to Hera’s claim that she was pushing for Australians to work for $2 a day (in the 2012 quote Hera referenced, Rinehart worried about Australia’s competitiveness when “Africans want to work, and its workers are willing to work for less than $2 per day”). It certainly helps that, at 18, Hera is one of the youngest candidates ever to run for parliament in Australia, but regional media in general have shown a keen interest in VS candidates everywhere. 

Signs also suggest the campaign is resonating. In Footscray, where VS volunteers have already knocked on around 17,000 doors, and the campaign has put up more than 200 yard signs, a steady trickle of people have turned up to volunteer at the campaign office after receiving VS material.

There’s no escaping the fact that politics in Victoria has shifted decisively to the right, and it’s likely either a Liberal or a Liberal-One Nation Coalition government will be elected on 28 November. But there’s no shortage of people who are horrified by the rise of One Nation and who are relieved to find, when visited by a VS volunteer, that there’s a party offering a genuinely anti-establishment alternative on the left. 

Hassan tells the story of Mary, an 82-year-old he met while doorknocking in the outer northern suburb of Thomastown. A long-time Labor voter, Mary told Omar that she wouldn’t vote for the ALP this time because “they’ve completely lost their way”. He later recounted:

She described playing with all the Italian and Yugoslav kids, going to each other’s houses and having great fun. ‘It made life richer, having all the different cultures, growing up together’.

author: AWSM
title: Errico Malatesta – Vote? What For?
content:
George: This beer’s not too bad, is it?

Jack: Yes, it’s alright, but what a price!

George: Shocking – especially when you remember what things used to cost. Still, you can’t wonder with all these taxes. It costs you twice as much to live as it used to. They put up the price of some things, and say you can do without them. But you can’t do without bread, and food, and clothes – you have to pay the rent all the same, and then there are the taxes on this and the rates – on our wages too! What a life! And it’s our own fault! If we wanted to we could alter things. The working class has the remedy in its own hands.

George: Easy enough! You’ve got a vote?

Jack: What’s that got to do with it?

George: Have you, or haven’t you?

Jack: Well, I’m entitled to a vote – but I never make use of it.

George: There you are! You’ve got a vote, but you just won’t take the trouble to use it, and then you wonder why things are so bad. You deserve all you get, honestly! People like you are responsible for all the trouble in the world!

Jack: Alright, alright, keep your hair on! Just tell me what’s the good of voting?

George: It’s obvious. Who makes the laws? The M.P.’s. Elect good M.P.’s and you get good laws.

Jack: Good councillors and good M.P.’s? We’ve heard that for a long time. But you’d have to be deaf, dumb, and blind not to notice it’s the same stooges that always get in. Oh, it’s wonderful to hear them when they’re after votes at election time. They pat you on the back, ask after the wife and kids, kiss the baby, promise you railways, bridges, work, cheap bread, less taxes, higher wages, protection – absolutely everything! And once they get in, they’re no better than anyone else. Goodbye promises! The wife and kids may starve, there’s no more or less work than before, the whole town can be falling to pieces for all they care. They’ve other things to think about than your troubles! Then a few years later they start the ballyhoo again. It doesn’t matter what colour the party is: they’re all the same. As soon as they’re elected, they forget all about you. They’re in their clubs and at their select dinners, and they don’t even trouble to come and have a look at you until the next election.

George: That’s correct! But why elect the rich? Don’t you know that the rich only live on the work of the masses? So how do you expect them to worry about the masses? All they think of is getting as much out of the ordinary man as they can.

Jack: Now you’re talking! But it’s not only the rich. There’s the other type, who want to get elected so they can become rich.

George: That’s true. So don’t let’s vote for them. Let’s elect workers, experienced friends of ours, as you might say, and then we won’t be fooled.

Jack: Oh, we’ve got some of your “experienced friends” in now, and they’re no different from our acknowledged enemies! Anyhow, what do you mean, “let’s elect – let’s elect.” As if we – you and me – could do as we like!

George: But it’s not only us two. If each one of us tried to convert other people and they would do the same, labour would have a majority, and we could elect whoever we liked. And that’s when we could form a government of the workers, and then . . .

Jack: And then it would be a paradise – I mean for those who were in Parliament! You’re arranging things a bit too quickly! Those in command always have the majority. The rich are always in power. Just imagine a poor worker, perhaps with an ill wife and four hungry kids, and you tell him to risk his job and get thrown out of his house to starve; just to give his vote to a candidate his master doesn’t like. Just try and convince those poor devils who can be thrown out of work by their boss whenever he likes. They’re never free; if they want to be free, they don’t want to waste their time voting – just take what they need.

George: But if we didn’t do that, no-one would vote. We couldn’t go to the workers and ask them to vote for our party, and say at the same time that votes were useless.

Jack: That’s just it! And on top of that you have to make election promises you know you can’t keep. And then you have to stand in with the Government, and mix with the well-to-do, and all the rest of it. As soon as any of your men are elected they have to kow-tow to the people you admit are the opponents of the workers. So why the hell talk about propaganda when the first thing you do is to counteract propaganda?

George: But you must admit, it’s an advantage to have our own men with …

author: Tom Bramble
title: What’s the deal with productivity?
content:
The bosses are trying to convince workers that lower corporate taxes, fewer regulations and workers’ rights, and less union power would be good for real wages. What they really want is more profits at the expense of the working class.

For years, business lobby groups have decried what they call Australia’s “productivity crisis”. They don’t say workers are producing less than they used to; they say they aren’t increasing production as quickly as before and aren’t keeping pace with overseas productivity growth.

It’s true: growth in workers’ hourly output has slowed over the past decade, and Australian workers don’t produce as much value for the bosses as American workers. But the bosses argue that this means living standards are held back, and prices rise more than they otherwise would, contributing to the cost-of-living crisis.

They say that government regulations (rules about wages, hours of work, health and safety standards, construction standards, environmental protections and professional and occupational registration requirements) and trade unions are preventing business investment. Their solution is “deregulation”, “slashing red tape”, “more competition”. These are simply code words for attacking the working class.

Let’s break this down. First, what is productivity? The simplest definition is “output per hour”. For BlueScope Steel, it could be tonnes of steel produced per hour per worker. For a childcare centre operator, it could be the number of children in care per worker per day. Lift those and productivity rises.

But who benefits? Does the steel worker or childcare worker see their wage rise automatically if they get more done? Of course not. In the first instance, all the money made from extra production by every group of workers goes to the capitalists, not the workers. Workers’ standard of living depends on how much they fight for. And that applies across the whole economy.

The bosses say some of the additional money coming in from workers’ extra effort will come back through higher wages and maybe more jobs. They argue: “a rising tide lifts all boats”. Is that true, though?

First, productivity in Australia may have slowed in the past couple of decades, but it has still risen. Yet household living standards are no higher than they were in 2012. There is no indication that workers are seeing any of the higher value they produce in the form of higher real wages.

A starker example is the United States, which bosses always point to as the high-productivity benchmark, where output per worker is higher and rising faster. In that country, workers’ share of national income is now at its lowest since World War Two—the productivity gains have gone to the capitalists, who have grown ever wealthier at workers’ expense.

Take things down another level. Even if bosses shared a cut of the higher revenue from increased productivity with workers, or unions successfully struck to extract a higher wage, bosses would still be ripping off workers.

All wealth ultimately comes either from the world’s natural resources or from human labour. You only have to see what happens when workers go on strike to see the truth of this—nothing gets produced, not a wheel turns, the childcare centres lie empty. All the machinery, all the factories, all the railway lines can only be put to good use if workers labour on them. And these in turn are the product of previous generations of workers’ labour.

What the capitalists call productivity should really be called exploitation: the extraction of value from the worker over and above the cost of their reproduction, i.e. what is necessary to get them to come to work each day in the form of wages. They call it profit; in fact, it’s theft from the worker.

This theft lies at the heart of capitalism. It explains why the workers labour their whole lives and have not much more than their home to hand on to their kids, and often not even that. While their employer has significantly expanded their operations at the workers’ expense. Some of the bosses may blow the money on a more self-indulgent lifestyle, but personal greed doesn’t get to the heart of it.

Every boss is driven to extract more from their workers, i.e. to lift productivity, because if they don’t, their rivals will, and they will be undercut and go out of business. The winner is the boss who can exploit their workers the most. That’s why every boss in every country demands that governments make it easier for them to rip off their …

author: Lucy Millett
title: Students demand climate action in lead-up to COP31
content:
It has become abundantly clear that federal Labor’s net-zero deadlines mean nothing. Despite promising to act on the climate emergency, its approach to climate action are hollow threats of “reform” that enable coal and gas companies to continue profiting and growing.

In the lead-up to the COP31 summit, students are demanding better.

The net-zero initiative, which Labor has signed, commits it to reduce emissions 62-70% below 2005 levels by 2035, and achieve net-zero by 2050.

The Climate Council, among others, say this timescale to reduce polluting carbon emissions going into the atmosphere is not only not fast enough to limit the temperature rise to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels — as the 2015 Paris Agreement sets out.

But global climate pollution is not being cut fast enough and Australia is one of the main culprits.

The NSW Independent Planning Commission has just approved the Hunter Valley Operations Continuation Project on September 30, despite regional communities, including some in the industry, campaigning for sustainable jobs elsewhere.

Another 800 million tonnes of greenhouse gas emissions from this giant coal mine will contribute to the climate emergency.

Climate Council Councillor and former Commissioner of Fire and Rescue NSW, Greg Mullins, said: “This is a decision that every community in NSW will end up paying for, including those who are still recovering from worsening fires and floods fuelled by climate pollution. What NSW exports as coal, we import back as bushfires, floods, heatwaves and droughts. Climate harm does not stop at the border, and neither does the responsibility for it.”

While the federal Labor still has to sign off on this expansion, we know from its track record that it will. Since coming to power, Labor has approved or extended 37 fossil fuel projects.

They include Woodside’s North West Shelf fossil gas fossil export extension in Western Australia (approved until 2070), new gas extraction near the Victorian Otways (until 2045), Glencore’s Ulan Coal Modification in central west NSW (until 2035), extension and expansion of Middlemount Coal Mine in Queensland (until 2053), drilling 1695 new gas wells to feed Queensland’s gas export facilities (until 2081) and the expansion of BHP’s Saraji coal mine (until 2063) in central Queensland.

Sydney Students For Climate formed because we are demanding action. We were the students who walked out of class over the Black Summer fires, 2019-2020.

We are organising a protest on October 24, on Gadigal Country, before the COP31 climate summit to present our demands to the Labor government — which is playing a key role as negotiator and co-host.

We see this rally as an important part of rebuilding a mass public focus, which can be strong enough to pressure the government to make real, meaningful climate action.

End new and expanded coal and gas mines. This would end fossil fuel production and the exportation of these non-renewables to global powers, which profit from on-selling and creating more dangerous emissions.

This requires binding emissions targets for the coal and gas sector.

Anthony Albanese’s government has delayed action, introduced isolated policies, which has discouraged the adoption of fast-tracked net-zero initiatives. It means Australia is on the back foot for the 2035 and 2050 deadlines.

An early phase-out could lead to a properly funded, fair transition for affected communities. This would mean investing in local industries, including retraining the coal and gas workforce and remodelling the built infrastructure. Such an approach could secure long-term employment opportunities. This is another of our rally’s demands.

Federal and state governments unwillingness to take these measures is greatly affecting the choices of regional communities, leading to a growing anger with net-zero and renewable energy policy.

Our rally is demanding more than new promises and a commitment to deadlines.

Labor must stop approving coal and gas projects that grow our carbon footprint.

We refuse to accept COP31 targets that look good on paper while dangerous emissions, which are not counted by the Paris Agreement, continue to rise.

While communities are feeling the brunt of the government’s inaction, coal and gas companies’ pockets grow heavier.

We’ve seen enough catastrophic weather events in our short lives, and it is time we do something about it!

[Lucy Millett is a Sydney Students for Climate organiser. Get in touch on Instagram …

author: Emma Black
title: Strangulation: How did attempted murder become normal?
content:
A 16-year-old woman from Sydney’s northern beaches died in hospital in late August after reportedly being strangled during consensual sex with her partner. The tragedy has sparked a long-overdue reckoning with the consequences for young women of the pornification of sex and the normalisation of sexual violence that has come with it.

In recent years, sexual strangulation has gone from being a relatively marginal phenomenon to an everyday sexual practice. In Australia, 61 percent of young women report having been strangled during sex, according to a

2024 survey

 of thousands of 18- to 35-year-olds. Men are most likely to be the stranglers. There is no safe way to strangle someone. According to David Corlett and Marie Crabbe, founders of anti-strangulation advocacy group Breathless:

“Potential 

consequences

 [of strangulation]

range from

 neck pain to loss of bladder and bowel control, headaches, memory loss, seizures, brain damage, stroke and, as seems to be the case with the young woman from the northern beaches, death. The risks and consequences are cumulative, so the more someone is strangled, the more likely they are to suffer harm.”

Only a tiny percentage of middle-aged and older adults have engaged in sexual strangulation, but among young people it’s become commonplace. Maree Crabbe, who is also the director of

It’s Time We Talked

, says strangulation wasn’t an issue before about 2019. But things have changed dramatically since then. “In recent years, we’ve been hearing it’s become normal for young people of all backgrounds, socioeconomic groups, cultures, sexual orientations”, she recently told the

Sydney Morning Herald

.

So how did a potentially deadly act become a normal sexual practice?

The main driver is pornography.

Recent research

 found more than 60 percent of 18- to 35-year-olds had encountered sexual strangulation depicted in pornography. One study comparing the content in the most popular pornography across the two and a half decades to 2024 found that sexual strangulation has gone from almost non-existent to featuring in 15 percent of scenes.

Pornography has become the de facto sex education system for millions of young people. And strangulation is just the latest trend in an industry that maximises profits by selling more extreme depictions of violent and degrading treatment of women.

A landmark 2010 study of best-selling pornographic videos, published in the journal

Violence Against Women

, found that 88 percent contained physical aggression, while 49 percent of scenes contained verbal aggression. Perpetrators were usually male, whereas targets were overwhelmingly female. Targets most often showed pleasure or responded neutrally to the aggression.

So the vast majority of mainstream pornography, whether it depicts strangulation or not, reinforces the idea that violence and humiliation are not only permissible, but pleasurable for women. The pornography industry has “blood on its hands” for propagating this sort of violent content, according to Chanel Contos, founder of

Teach Us Consent

.

An example of how normalised strangulation during sex has become came from this year’s Eurovision song contest.

Romania’s 2026 song entry

 “Choke Me” repeats the words “choke me” 30 times in three minutes. The song also contains the lyrics “It’s hard to breathe in” and “make my lungs explode”.

Many mainstream commentators

emphasise

 the importance of avoiding “kink-shaming” when addressing the issue of sexual strangulation with young people. This dresses up the prioritisation of men’s sexual gratification over women’s safety as sex-positive open-mindedness. And it wilfully ignores the fact that sexual desires and practices are not simply a matter of individual preference; they are shaped and constructed in a society where women are not equal to men, and enormous profit can be made from sex by companies competing for market share.

The reality is that people’s sexual inclinations have not radically changed on their own over the last 50 years, such that the majority of men now enjoy inflicting harm on women. Market forces have pushed things in this direction. In an attempt to be more sensational and attract market share, pornography companies have taken the male-dominant trope that underpins the construction of mainstream heterosexuality and pumped it up to a new extreme. This has shaped attitudes to sex and sexual desire, which in turn further reinforces the business model. And …

title: Κινητοποίηση αλληλεγγύης στον απεργό πείνας και πολιτικό πρόσφυγα Soner Inanç, Παρασκευή 2/10, 09.00 στο Υπουργείο Μετανάστευσης και Εργασίας
content:
Από Solidarity with Migrants:


ΚΑΛΕΣΜΑ ΣΕ ΚΙΝΗΤΟΠΟΙΗΣΗ/CALL TO DEMO [GR/ENG]


Κινητοποίηση στο Υπουργείο Μετανάστευσης και Εργασίας την Παρασκευή 02/10 09:00 (Λεωφόρος Θηβών 196-198)


Ο Soner Inanç πολιτικός αγωνιστής για τα εργατικά δικαιώματα και τις δημοκρατικές ελευθερίες είναι από τις 27 Αυγούστου σε απεργία πείνας σε καθεστώς κράτησης, ενώ κινδυνεύει με άμεση απέλαση λόγω της ενδεχόμενης απόρριψης της αίτησής του για άσυλο. O πολιτικός πρόσφυγας Soner Inanç αναγκάστηκε να εγκαταλείψει την Τουρκία καθώς έχει στοχοποιηθεί για τη δράση του από το τουρκικό κράτος και ήδη έχει φυλακιστεί στο παρελθόν για τη συμμετοχή του στο κίνημα του Gezi Park. Μετά την απορριπτική απόφαση ως προς το αρχικό αίτημα ασύλου του, Soner Inanç κατέθεσε αίτημα ακύρωσης και ακολούθησε όλες τις σχετικές διαδικασίες. Τέλη Ιουλίου, συνελήφθη και βρέθηκε σε διοικητική κράτησης στο ΑΤ Λαυρίου.


Ένα μήνα μετά, μεταφέρθηκε στη Θεσσαλονίκη με σκοπό την απέλαση του. Μετά από τέσσερις εβδομάδες στέρησης βιταμινών, αναγκαίων για την μη ύπαρξη μόνιμων επιπτώσεων, το αίτημα αυτό άρχισε να καλύπτεται όπως όφειλε εξαρχής μετά από συνεχή πολιτική κινητοποίηση και δημοσιογραφική κάλυψη για τον κίνδυνο τον οποίο διατρέχει αν δεν του χορηγηθούν. Το ΠΡΟΚΕΚΑ Παρανεστίου οφείλει παράλληλα ως απεργός πείνας ο Soner Inanç να παρακολουθείται από ανεξάρτητη ιατρική επιτροπή για να διασφαλιστεί η απρόσκοπτη άσκηση της ως πολιτική δράση με συγκεκριμένα αιτήματα: τη συνέχιση της διαδικασίας απόδοση ασύλου, την μη απέλαση του στην Τουρκία και την απελευθέρωσή του. Ο Soner δηλώνει αποφασισμένος να συνεχίσει στον αγώνα του, αφού κρατείται άδικα, περιμένοντας νέα απόφαση για το άσυλό του.


Ως Solidarity with Migrants, γνωρίσαμε τον Soner στο στρατόπεδο προσφύγων Οινοφύτων όπου πάντα προσπαθούσε με όλα τα δυνατά μέσα να υποστηρίζει τα δικαιώματα όλων των προσφύγων με μια βαθιά διεθνιστική προσήλωση. Η “λογική” των αποφάσεων της υπηρεσίας ασύλου καταδεικνύει τις συνέπειες των μεγάλων αλλαγών που έχουν επέλθει στο καθεστώς ασύλου τα τελευταία έτη καθώς έχουμε να κάνουμε με την καταστρατήγηση της έννοιας του πολιτικού ασύλου. Γι’αυτό και ο αγώνας του Soner είναι και αγώνας για το πολιτικό άσυλο γενικότερα και χρειάζεται τη στήριξη όλων μας.


Στηρίζουμε σε όλα τα επίπεδα την άμεση απελευθέρωση και απόδοση πολιτικού ασύλου. Σε αυτήν την κατεύθυνση καλούμε σε:

author: Mag
title: Kahlschlag bei VW ab 2024? Autobauer plant Kürzungen in Milliardenhöhe, um »Effizienz« zu steigern
content:
Dossier


„…

Seit Anfang Oktober verhandelt das VW-Management mit dem Betriebsrat hinter verschlossenen Türen über ein »Effizienzprogramm«, das die Kosten in den kommenden drei Jahren um zehn Milliarden Euro senken soll. Nun zeichnet sich ab, welche Formen der Kahlschlag namens »Accelerate forward« (Forwärtsbeschleunigung) annehmen könnte. Wie am Montag das Handelsblatt berichtete, plant Schäfer, allein in der Verwaltung der VW AG zwischen 4.000 und 6.000 Stellen zu streichen. Die betroffenen Angestellten sollen bevorzugt über Alterszeitregelungen entsorgt werden, den Rest könnten Abfindungsprogramme erledigen. Ziel sei es, die Zahl der Beschäftigten dauerhaft zu reduzieren, Neueinstellungen sollen auf ein Minimum reduziert werden. Passend dazu wurde schon Anfang November ein Einstellungsstopp für die wichtigsten deutschen Standorte Wolfsburg, Hannover, Braunschweig, Salzgitter, Emden und Kassel verhängt. Selbst bei den höchstbezahlten Tarifbeschäftigten der Gruppe »Tarif-Plus«, die aktuell rund 9.000 Mitarbeiter umfasst, will der Autobauer den Rotstift ansetzen

…“

Artikel von Ralf Wurzbacher in der jungen Welt vom 14.11.2023

 

 und mehr dazu und den Alternativen (für alle Auto/Metall-Belegschaften):


VW kündigt zentrale Pfeiler des Volkswagen-Haustarifvertrages: Kein „übles Foul“ (IG Metall), sondern eine Kriegserklärung an alle Opfer der Jagd nach Maximalprofiten


Übles Foul an der Belegschaft: Vorstand kündigt reihenweise Tarifverträge – Beschäftigungssicherung bis Ende 2030 bleibt unantastbar


„

IG Metall und Betriebsrat kündigen Widerstand an, heftiger Konflikt zum Jahreswechsel bahnt sich an


Volkswagen will massiv in die tariflichen Arbeitsbedingungen seiner Beschäftigten eingreifen und kündigt dafür zentrale Pfeiler des Volkswagen-Haustarifvertrages. Im tariflichen Überprüfungsgespräch (nach § 7 Zukunftstarifvertrag) hat die VW-Arbeitgeberseite am heutigen Mittwoch die Kündigung zahlreicher, bestehender Tarifverträge überreicht. Damit stellt Volkswagen zum Beispiel tarifliche Zulagen, Ausbildungsübernahmen sowie Schutzregelungen für ältere und gesundheitlich eingeschränkte Beschäftigte infrage.


Am heutigen 30. September läuft die Frist zur Kündigung von Tarifverträgen zum 31. Dezember aus. Die Kündigungen würden damit bereits zum 1. Januar 2027 wirksam werden. Für die Beschäftigten bedeutet das: Volkswagen will ihnen bereits ab Januar unmittelbar ins Portemonnaie greifen – und stellt zugleich Leistungen infrage, die über Jahrzehnte tariflich erkämpft wurden. Rechtlich bedeutet eine Kündigung eines Tarifvertrags zwar nicht, dass sämtliche darin enthaltenen Regelungen unmittelbar wegfallen, zum Teil gibt es eine unterschiedliche Nachwirkung.


Wichtig ist zugleich: Die Beschäftigungssicherung ist von den aktuellen Kündigungen nicht betroffen. Sie ist bis Ende 2030 befristet und könnte vor Ablauf dieser Frist auch gar nicht gekündigt werden. Darauf weist die IG Metall erneut hin, denn tarifliche Beiträge der Beschäftigten sind bereits erbracht. (…)


Mit der Kündigung zahlreicher Tarifverträge eröffnet das Unternehmen zudem ein neues Feld für die Tarifauseinandersetzung 2026. Dieses gehört jedoch nicht in das von der IG Metall beantragte heutige Überprüfungsgespräch, sondern an den tariflichen Verhandlungstisch. (…)Volkswagen will Leistungen angreifen, die für viele Kolleginnen und Kollegen fest zu ihrer Einkommensplanung gehören. Gleichzeitig geht es um etwas Grundsätzlicheres: Tarifverträge sind bei Volkswagen über Jahrzehnte ein Instrument gewesen, um wirtschaftliche Veränderungen gemeinsam und verlässlich zu gestalten. Jetzt stellt der Vorstand einen erheblichen Teil dieses Gefüges infrage. Besonders problematisch ist unter anderem auch der drohende Eingriff in den Manteltarifvertrag

…“

Meldung der IG Metall bei Volkswagen vom 30.09.2026

 


Siehe aich Fragen und Antworten zu den gekündigten Tarifverträgen im

MITBESTIMMEN!-Extrablatt vom 30.09.2026

author: cnt.es
title: CNT-Regional Centro se adhiere a la acampada por el derecho a una vivienda digna
content:
La Regional Centro de la Confederación Nacional del Trabajo (CNT) manifiesta su adhesión y apoyo a la

acampada convocada por el Sindicato de Inquilinas en la Puerta del Sol de Madrid por el derecho a una vivienda digna

.


El acceso a una vivienda digna se ha convertido para la clase trabajadora en un problema cada vez más difícil de afrontar. Alquileres desorbitados, precariedad laboral, salarios insuficientes, desahucios y la utilización de la vivienda como un activo para la especulación están expulsando a muchas personas de sus barrios y condenándolas a vivir en condiciones cada vez más precarias.


Desde la CNT entendemos que

la vivienda es un derecho y no una mercancía

. No podemos aceptar que las necesidades básicas de las personas estén subordinadas al beneficio económico de grandes propietarios, fondos de inversión, empresas inmobiliarias o intereses especulativos.


Por ello, consideramos fundamental la organización colectiva de las personas afectadas. Las experiencias de organización de inquilinas, vecinas y trabajadoras demuestran que

frente a los problemas que sufrimos individualmente, la respuesta está en la solidaridad, el apoyo mutuo y la acción colectiva

.


La Regional Centro de la CNT se suma a esta movilización y anima a sus sindicatos, afiliadas y afiliados a participar en la acampada y en las acciones convocadas en defensa del derecho a una vivienda digna. Los sindicatos CNT Madrid y CNT Comarcal Sur, ya están participando activamente desde el primer día y su presencia en la Puerta del Sol es permanente.


Reivindicamos:


Una vivienda digna y accesible para todas.


El fin de los desahucios y de la violencia habitacional.


Alquileres que puedan ser asumidos por la clase trabajadora.


La defensa de los barrios frente a la especulación y la expulsión de sus habitantes.


El control y la organización colectiva frente a los intereses de quienes hacen negocio con una necesidad básica.


La vivienda como derecho, no como mercancía.


Que la vivienda pública no pase nunca a manos de especuladores.


La lucha por la vivienda es también una lucha sindical y social como los son también la lucha por la educación pública y la de las educadoras infantiles de 0-3 , en la actualidad en huelga indefinida. Porque las condiciones de vida de la clase trabajadora no terminan en el centro de trabajo:

el salario, el alquiler, los suministros y el acceso a una vivienda digna, la educación y sanidad públicas forma parte de nuestras condiciones de vida

.


Por todo ello, desde la

Regional Centro de la CNT

 expresamos nuestra solidaridad con la acampada de la Puerta del Sol y con todas las personas y organizaciones que participan en esta movilización.


Frente a la especulación y la precariedad, organización y apoyo mutuo.


¡Por el derecho a una vivienda digna!


La entrada

CNT-Regional Centro se adhiere a la acampada por el derecho a una vivienda digna

 se publicó primero en

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

.

author: Radikal Perspektif
title: Anarko-Sendikalizm ve Çifte Örgütlenme
content:
Yazan: Matthew Crossin


Çeviren: Gorthim


Çevirilen Asıl Metin


PDF Linki


İşçi sınıfının mücadeleci bir hareketini yeniden inşa etmekle ilgilenen anarşistler bugün nasıl örgütlenmelidir?


Anarşistler olarak, patronlara karşı mücadelemizin seçimler yoluyla ya da parlamentoda değil, işyerinde yürütüldüğünü biliyoruz. İş arkadaşlarımızla örgütlendiğimizde, kâr elde etme imkânlarını bozan eylemler gerçekleştirdiğimizde ve farklı sektörlerdeki mücadelelerimizi birbirine bağladığımızda güç kazanırız.


Söylemesi kolay, yapması zor. Peki, bu tür bir hareketi inşa etmek için hangi stratejileri kullanmalıyız?


Anarşistler, mücadelemizin devletin içindeki politikacılara devredilemeyeceği gibi, mevcut sendikalardaki hesap verme yükümlülüğü olmayan bürokratlara da boyun eğmememiz gerektiği ve patronlara veya politikacılara yalakalık yapan legalist taktiklerine umut bağlayamayacağımız konusunda hemfikirdir.


Peki ne yapmalıyız? Yeni sendikalar mı kurmalıyız? Eğer anarşistseniz ve sendikalarımızın anarşist ilkelere göre (ideal olarak devrim gibi uzun vadeli bir hedef doğrultusunda) yönetilmesini istiyorsanız, elbette

anarşist

 sendikalar kurmalısınız, değil mi? Kendilerini

anarko-sendikalist

 olarak görenler genellikle tam da bunu yapmamız gerektiğini savunurlar.


Dünya çapında işyerlerini gerçekten örgütlemiş bir avuç anarko-sendikalist sendika bulunmaktadır. İşçileri patronlara karşı mücadele etmek üzere bir araya getirdikleri ve mücadelenin kontrolünü tabana bıraktıkları ölçüde, bu sendikaların bazı iyi işler başardığını kabul edebiliriz.


Ancak bu stratejiyle birlikte gelen ve çoğu anarşist-sendikalist grubu korkunç derecede etkisiz kılan, hatta İspanyol CNT gibi en güçlü örnekleri bile tehlikeye atan bazı sorunlar vardır. Eğer bir depoya ya da ofise girip iş arkadaşlarıma, “

Anarko-sendikalist sendikaya katılmalısınız. Bu, anarşist ilkeler üzerine kurulmuş, nihai hedefi kapitalizmi ve hükümeti şiddetli bir devrimle devirmek olan bir sendikadır.

’ dersem, o örgütün kapsamını, bunun iyi bir şey olduğuna zaten katılan, böyle bir gruba imza atmaya istekli ve belki de bunu yapmak için mevcut sendikalarından ayrılmaya bile hazır olan iş arkadaşlarımla sınırlamış olurum.


Anarko-sendikalistler genellikle bunun bir sorun olmadığını söylerler; çünkü anarşist sendika (adına rağmen) yalnızca yapısı bakımından anarşisttir; hem anarşistlere hem de anarşist olmayanlara açıktır. Bu tür bir anarşist sendikacılık, örgütün devrimci bir politikaya sahip olmasına özel bir önem vermez.


Ezici çoğunluğu oluşturan birçok anarşist olmayan işçinin – anarşizmin gerçekte ne anlama geldiğini anlamadıkları veya böyle bir gruba katılma cesaretinden yoksun oldukları sürece – bir “anarşist” sendikaya üye olma fikrinden yine de uzak duracaklarını bir kenara bırakırsak (anarşizmin gerçekte ne anlama geldiğini anlamadıkları veya böyle bir gruba katılma konusunda kendilerine güven duymadıkları sürece), anarşistlerden oluşmayan ya da toplumsal devrime bağlılık konusunda bir fikir birliği bulunmayan bir örgütün gerçekten “anarşist” olduğunu ne ölçüde söyleyebiliriz?


Anarşizm sadece karar verme biçimlerimizle değil, alınan kararların içeriğiyle de ilgilidir. Örgütlerin üyelerinin kontrolü altında olması, delegeler arasında koordinasyonun sağlanması ve delegelerin, seçmenleri tarafından kendilerine verilen görevlere sıkı sıkıya bağlı kalmalarıyla bürokratik temsilcilerden ayrılması olumlu bir durumdur. Bu tür yapılar en iyi türden faaliyetleri teşvik eder ve anarşist örgütlenme anlayışının merkezinde yer alır. Bununla birlikte, otoriterlik karşıtı karar alma biçimleri,

mutlaka

 devrimci anarşist siyasetle tutarlı kararlara yol açmaz.


Anarşist olmayanlarla dolu ve devrimci anarşist programa olan bağlılık konusunda bölünmüş bir anarşist sendika kurmuş olursak, sözde “anarşist” örgütün hedeflerimizle veya ilkelerimizle çelişen bir şekilde davrandığı bir durumla karşı karşıya kalabiliriz. Liberter iç yapısına rağmen, bu örgüt amacına uygun olmayan bir makine olacak, ancak onu doğası gereği anarşist olarak gören militanların sadakatini her zaman koruyacaktır. Anarşist sendikayı bu şekilde görenler, onun korunmasını, sözde temsil ettiği anarşist hareket için mutlak bir öncelik olarak göreceklerdir.

author: Jonathan Rosenblum
title: Amazon Is Deploying AI to Spy on Its Workers and Bust Unions Before They Form
content:
Internal company documents obtained by a Canadian labor board show how Amazon is tracking workers’ every move.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

The 18th-century notion of the panopticon — a circular prison design with a guard station in the middle, allowing a single officer to enforce discipline by keeping watch over all the prisoners — has become real in the 21st century through AI-driven surveillance against workers: It’s the Amazon warehouse.

It should be no surprise that the company that harnessed technology to create a vast, $2.7 trillion empire would employ the same sophistication to enforce workplace discipline and tamp down insurgent unionization efforts. A recent disclosure of Amazon’s internal “employee relations” documents reveals just how extreme Amazon’s methods of warehouse surveillance and control have become.

Amazon employs what it calls the “Atlas” model, inputting into a computerized model a staggering amount of information on workers, their thoughts and behaviors, the workplace environment, and myriad other factors — “hundreds of data points,” according to the company. Atlas produces not just a granular measurement of ongoing worker unrest, worksite by worksite around the world, but also a prediction model for future organizing. It’s like the “precrime” police in the film Minority Report who use psychic powers to identify and apprehend would-be criminals before they act — except in this case, it’s an AI-driven tool used by the billionaire owners of one of the richest companies in history to head off rebellion among its low-wage workforce. And this is not Tom Cruise play-acting; it’s very real.

Workers anywhere who have endured anti-union campaigns can relate to stories of overbearing surveillance by management; the Atlas model, however, takes the spying to an entirely new level.

Details of the Atlas model came to light recently as a result of a legal dispute between Amazon and Unifor, the Canadian private sector union. Last year, British Columbia’s Labour Relations Board awarded union certification to Unifor at Amazon’s YVR2 warehouse outside Vancouver, finding that the company had broadly interfered in the union drive. It was the second union certification at Amazon in North America — the other being the 2022 union win at JFK8 in Staten Island, New York. But in contrast to the U.S., where Amazon has managed to stall bargaining for four and a half years because of weak labor laws, the B.C. Labour Relations Board ordered Amazon to recognize the union and negotiate. Contract bargaining commenced last December.

Not surprisingly, Amazon has dragged its feet in negotiations, prompting the union to file unfair labor practice charges with the Labour Board. Following a series of hearings earlier this year, the Labour Board found that Amazon violated provincial law. In August it ordered a remarkable step — first-contract arbitration at YVR2. That fight remains in play, but as a result of the legal proceedings, Amazon was required to turn over documents to the Labour Board and Unifor. Unifor has shared them with Truthout, and they can be viewed here.

Atlas produces not just a granular measurement of ongoing worker unrest, worksite by worksite around the world, but also a prediction model for future organizing.

In addition to the Atlas model revelation (beginning on Page 19 of the document), the material includes more than 100 pages that reveal in great detail how Amazon trains its frontline managers in union-busting. My colleague at the Center for Work and Democracy, Ben Fong, has written about this other portion of the disclosed material.

“Amazon’s own documents pull back the curtain on what workers have been telling us for years,” said Justin Gniposky, Unifor’s organizing director. “Behind the friendly PR, Amazon sees workers as property and treats their fundamental right to unionize as a threat to be managed and then eliminated.”

Amazon did not respond to Truthout’s request for comment on the Atlas model.

The documents describe the Atlas model as “a labor risk framework to clarify how Amazon evaluates emerging workforce issues, labor union targets, and internal or external labor threats.” The Atlas model ingests hundreds of data points: employee trainings completed; health and safety incidents, from simple first-aid cases to serious injuries; feedback from workers on management …

author: Unknown
title: Sinema salonları neden boş?
content:
Yılmaz Erdoğan’ın “Sinemayı geri alacağız, sinemayı kurtarmamız lazım” sözleri sinema sektörünün önemli tartışmalarından biri oldu. Yılmaz Erdoğan’ın Vizontele serisinin üçüncü filmini duyururken yaptığı açıklama, sinema dünyasında ve sosyal medyada tartışmalara yol açmıştı. Katıldığı bir programda sinema kültürünün salonlardan uzaklaştığını ve bu durumdan rahatsızlık duyduğunu belirten Erdoğan, “Sinemayı geri alacağız, sinemayı kurtarmamız lazım” ifadelerini kullandı.

Sinema salonlarının eski canlılığını kaybetmesi, beyaz perdenin geleceğinin ne olacağı, sinemanın yaşadığı sorun yalnızca seyirci kaybıyla sınırlı değil. Bugünün seyircisini anlayan filmler üretilmemesi, sinemanın halkın derdini dile getirmemesi, gerçek sorunlarını anlatmaması, ticari bir alan olarak görülmesinin yanı sıra iktidarlar eliyle de bilinçli olarak sinemanın etkisinin zayıflatılmasıyla ilgili.

Türkiye’de 1960 ile 1980 arasındaki sınıf mücadelesi, halk hareketleri Türkiye sinemasını da etkilemişti. Daha toplumcu, sınıf mücadelesi eksenli filmler çekilmeye başlanmıştı. Yükselen toplumsal hareket ve onun yarattığı kültür egemen sınıfların şiddetiyle karşılandı. Çünkü iktidar için sinema tehlikeliydi. Halkın bir sanat dalı olması açısından etkisi büyüktü. Sinema hem sözel hem de görsel etkiye sahip olduğu için toplumu dönüştürme olasılığı da fazlaydı. Egemen sınıflar, binlerce kişinin aynı anda ortak bir duyguda birleşmesinin gücünün farkındaydı. Onun için ’80 darbesinde birçok filmi yasakladılar. Darbe ve onun ürünü olan neoliberalizm uygulamaları ile bütün yaşam yeniden yapılandırıldı. Çok kanallı televizyonların günlük yaşama girmesiyle popüler ve ticari kaygılara teslim olundu. Televizyon kanalları önce seyircisini yarattı, sonra da yarattığı bu seyirciyi veri alarak üst sınıfların masal dünyasının hikâyelerini anlattı. Bu furyadan sinema da etkilendi.

Bugün sinema alanında dijital platformlar çok gelişti. İstediğin filme, istediğin anda, dijital platformlarda, anında erişebiliyorsun. Ama dijitalleşmedeki ilerleme sinemanın yok olacağı anlamına gelmiyor. İyi bir toplumsal hikâye ve gerçek bir sinema filmi sunulduğunda insanlar sinema salonlarına gidiyor. Bugün dijital alanda müzik dinliyoruz, basketbol, voleybol, futbol gibi spor karşılaşmalarını izliyoruz. Ama yine de salonlar ve stadyumları dolduruyoruz. Burada mekanın önemi de ortaya çıkıyor. Sinema salonları duyguların paylaşıldığı önemli bir kültür mekânı aynı zamanda. Bugün sinemaya yapılan en büyük kötülük, salonların AVM’lere taşınması oldu.

Sinema salonlarının yeniden dolmasını tartışacaksak Adana yazlık sinemalara değinmek yerinde olur. Sinemanın emekçi halk için tek eğlence olduğu 1960-80 yılları arasında Adana’da her gün yüzün üzerinde film gösterimi yapılırdı. Özellikle 1960 ve 1980’li yıllarda sinema Adana’nın en önemli ekonomik, toplumsal ve kültürel faaliyetlerinden biridir. Çünkü o zamanlar Adana büyük bir işçi şehridir. İşçilik düzenli bir çalışma ve düzenli bir gelir demekti, bu düzenlilik kendine ait bir eğlenme ve dinlenme zamanını mümkün kılıyordu. Sinema ise toplumsal bir eğlence aracıydı. Diğer önemli bir yanı da Adana şehrinde 200 kadar sinema salonu bulunuyordu. Mahalleler, fabrikaların etrafında oluşmuştu ve bu mahallelerde en az bir yazlık sinema vardı. Her mahallede işçilerin, emekçilerin evinden çıkıp gideceği yazlık sinema salonları mevcuttu. title: Claudio Katz: “Hay que construir la izquierda para derrotar a Milei”
content:
Tras la repercusión de la Marcha de la Bronca, Claudio Katz analizó el rol de la izquierda en la coyuntura actual, donde juegan cada vez más fuerte dos variables: el retroceso de Milei y un potencial estallido económico.


Las incógnitas sobre el peronismo, la apuesta del establishment a perpetuar el esquema de ajuste, explotación laboral y saqueo del país que logró establecer durante la actual gestión, la impunidad de la Corte Suprema y la agresividad del imperialismo estadounidense en la región son datos ineludibles del escenario presente ante los cuales la izquierda deberá plantearse nuevas tácticas y compromisos, consideró Katz, si quiere llegar al gobierno y disputar el poder.


Indymedia: – ¿Cómo ves el papel de la izquierda luego de la Marcha de la Bronca?


Claudio Katz:

 – Está cumpliendo un papel muy positivo ante todo en la acción callejera. La marcha fue un éxito

 por la

 concurrencia y el impacto de un acto político, que traspasó la resistencia social y democrática a los atropellos de Milei. Contrastó frontalmente con la capitulación de la CGT que deja pasar el ajuste.


La movilización alcanzó el nivel más alto de una convocatoria de

la izquierda. Superó lo conseguido con la “Plaza del No” en los años 90 y con las grandes concentraciones que en el pasado articulaba el

PC. Exhibió un nivel de politización muy superior a las marchas piqueteras e ilustró nuevamente cómo gravita la izquierda en las coyunturas de inmovilidad del peronismo.


Esa indefinición del justicialismo se vio por ejemplo cuando ganó Alfonsín, durante el neoliberalismo de Menem o en la época de Alianza. Actualmente, vuelve a aflorar por momentos y por eso hubo cierta presencia de militantes o simpatizantes del peronismo en la marcha. Igualmente te diría que el dato más significativo fue la centralidad de Myriam

Bregman. La movilización consolidó su protagonismo y la consiguiente incidencia de la izquierda en las próximas elecciones.


Indymedia: –

Pero cuál es la proyección electoral efectiva de Myriam, porque las encuestas resaltan una imagen muy positiva sin equivalencia en la intención de voto…


Claudio Katz: – Hay infinitas especulaciones sobre esa relación y no tiene mucho sentido obsesionarse con el tema, cuando falta más de un año para la elección. El número de votos que lograría el FIT-U depende de escenarios muy

abiertos con dos variables centrales: el retroceso de Milei y un potencial estallido económico, que podría repetir lo ocurrido tantas veces en la Argentina.


Foto:

Nicolas Solo ((i))


Nadie sabe si el gobierno podrá sostener el tipo de cambio hasta el 2027. La recesión, la pobreza y el endeudamiento podrían desencadenar el mismo tipo de rebelión que sepultó a De la Rúa o la protesta masiva que derrotó a Macri. No cabe duda que la izquierda estará en la primera línea de ese eventual estallido.


Pero en cualquier caso su crecimiento dependerá de lo que suceda con el peronismo y en ese campo hay varios cursos posibles de división o cohesión y de amoldamiento conservador o resurgimiento progresista.


Por el momento se verifica una gran fractura en el justicialismo, entre corrientes de adaptación y crítica al modelo que la clase dominante apuntala con Milei. En general predomina la postura de no decir nada a la espera de lo que más conviene. Pero mientras tanto, un fascista como Cúneo participa del espacio de Kicillof, que a su vez emite mensajes de adaptación tipo Alberto Fernández y elude comentarios básicos de denuncia del genocidio de Palestina. Pero lo que haría como presidente es un misterio. Conviene recordar que nadie imaginaba el giro progresista de Néstor y Cristina antes del 2001 y sería un error ignorar la recomposición que logró el peronismo al calor de la gestión kirchnerista.


Indymedia: –

 ¿Por qué importa ese dato?


Claudio Katz: – Porque conforma el escenario en el que actúa la izquierda. Desconociendo ese hecho es muy difícil desenvolver estrategias para derrotar a Milei, revertir el ajuste y reconquistar los derechos populares. Ese camino transita por llegar al gobierno y disputar el poder, mediante frentes comunes y acuerdos de lucha con los sectores dispuestos a reconstruir el país, apostando a un gobierno que en sus primeros días de gestión revierta de un plumazo todo lo hecho por Milei.


Foto:

Nicolas Solo ((i))

title: Per soli sette centimetri
content:
La mattina dell’undici settembre del 1926, cento anni fa, il capo del fascismo, il suprematista e dittatore Benito Mussolini, si salvò dallo scoppio della bomba SIPE per soli sette centimetri.


Gino Lucetti, anarchico risoluto, alle 9.20 aspetta l’auto di Mussolini a Roma vicino Porta Pia. Quando la vede arrivare, innesca l’accenditore della SIPE, conta fino a quattro, poi tre secondi per il volo di venti metri, la SIPE rimbalza dal semitettuccio sulla strada, la bomba esplode nel tempo calcolato; il capo del fascismo, purtroppo, si salva per sette centimetri.


Mussolini, diciannove anni dopo, in fuga travestito, finirà catturato e fucilato dai Partigiani il 28 aprile del 1945, quindi appeso a piazzale Loreto a Milano.


Gino Lucetti


fece tutto per bene; quei sette centimetri avrebbero cambiato la storia.


Gli anarchici della Lunigiana dedicarono a Gino Lucetti un battaglione partigiano che combattè fascisti e nazisti ben oltre la Liberazione del 25 aprile 1945.


Gino Lucetti muore ad Ischia il 17 settembre del 1943, tre giorni dopo essere uscito dalle carceri fasciste.

author: daniel
title: Der AfD-Faschismus
content:
Zum Begriff „Faschismus“ Zunächst: ‚Faschismus’ ist sowohl eine soziologische Kategorie als auch ein moralischer Begriff. Im moralischen Sinne gilt: ‚Nie wieder Faschismus!‘ ‚Faschismus‘ ist also ein Begriff mit einem Ausrufezeichen. Dies hat er mit den Unterdrückungsbegriffen wie ‚Antisemitismus‘, ‚Rassismus‘, ‚Sexismus‘, ‚Klassismus‘ usw. gemein. Man muss sich diese Begriffe nicht nur als wisschenschaftlich-soziologische Begriffe denken, sondern auch als Ausruf-Begriffe. Sie geben den Betroffenen die Markierungsmacht: „Du Rassist!“, „Das ist behindertenfeindlich!“. Es handelt sich um Stopp!-Signale, um Interventionsbegriffe. Sie sind nicht in erster Linie von und für akademische Debatten konzipiert, sondern für die Betroffenengruppen, damit diese Antisemitismus, Rassismus, Sexismus, Klassismus, Ableismus benennen, stoppen und zurückdrängen können. Es handelt sich aber darüberhinausgehend auch um soziologische Begriffe, die gesellschaftstheoretisch diskutiert und im historischen und internationalen Vergleich präzisiert werden.

Entsprechendes gilt auch für den Faschismus, ein Begriff wie ein Biohazard- oder Strahlungswarnsignal. Ein Begriff, der aber leider auch verdreht und verwässert wird, wie sonst kaum eine Vokabel. Gerade weil der Begriff Faschismus negativ aufgeladen ist, wie Giftgas, wird er auch gerne von den Rechten instrumentalisiert, indem sie von „Linksfaschismus“ reden.

Immer wieder wird versucht, die NSDAP als „links“ darzustellen. Nichts an der NSDAP war links und was es an entfernt anmutenden sozialistischen Ideen in der NSDAP gab und sich in der SA von Ernst Röhm zeigte, wurde sehr schnell zerschlagen – und zwar von den Vorfahren zweier Adliger, die am Aufbau der AfD zentral beteiligt waren: August Baron von Finck und Beatrix von Storch, geborene Herzogin von Oldenburg.

Von der NSDAP zur AfD 1: August Baron von Finck

August Baron von Finck senior war Erbe. Zu seinen geerbten Unternehmen gehörte die Allianz-Versicherung. Dessen Direktor Kurt Schmitt war bereits seit 1930 mit Hermann Göring von der NSDAP befreundet und nahm an mehreren Geheimtreffen mit der NSDAP teil und spendete ihr Millionenbeträge. Unmittelbar nach der Machtübernahme, im April 1933, wurden die NS-Betriebszellen entmachtet und alle sozialistischen Verstaatlichungsträume wurden beendet, als Schmitt Reichswirtschaftsminister wurde. Baron von Finck spendete übrigens auch – eine lohnenswerte Investition, da er später von der „Arisierung“ jüdischer Banken profitierte. August Baron von Fincks Sohn, August Baron von Finck junior, hatte auch bereits mehrfach für rechte Parteien gespendet, aber auch für eine Kampagne des neoliberalen Bürgerkonvents, an dessen Spitze später Beatrix von Storch sitzen sollte. Finck baute in seinem Unternehmensgeflecht eine verzweigte Organisation des sogenannten „Rechtslibertarismus“ auf, die Staat und Demokratie abschaffen will. Ich gehe davon aus, dass es Finck war, der im November 2012 Bernd Lucke auf die Idee brachte, eine eigene Partei – die AfD – zu gründen. Fincks Mitarbeiterin Dagmar Metzger wurde zusammen mit Konrad Adam und Bernd Lucke im Februar 2013 die erste Sprecherin der AfD und über Metzger lief die Anschubfinanzierung der AfD durch August Baron von Finck.

Von der NSDAP zur AfD 2: Beatrix von Storch

Der Großvater mütterlicherseits von Beatrix von Storch bekleidete in der NS-Zeit das Amt des Reichswirtschaftsministers.Ihr Großvater väterlicherseits wurde bereits in Schleswig-Holstein von Heinrich Himmler besucht, als dieser noch in München Landwirtschaft studierte. Eine ihrer Großtanten war die zweitwichtigste Frau in der SS und ebenfalls von Himmler sehr angetan. Ein angeheirateter Großonkel war Adjutant von Himmler und organisierte die Erschießung des offen schwulen SA-Führers Ernst Röhms. Damit war dann nicht nur der Rest alles irgendwie „linken“ in der NSDAP beseitigt, sondern Himmler nutzte die Erschießung Röhm als Startschuss zur Gründung der „Reichszentrale zur Bekämpfung von Homosexualität und Abtreibung“. Beatrix von Storchs heutige Aktivitäten sind davon nicht allzuweit entfernt bzw. stehen in der Tradition ihrer „Ahnen“. Auch Storch hatte mit der Entstehung der AfD zu tun. Während eines Kongresses ihrer „Zivilen Koalition“ 2011, wo sie mit Hans-Olaf Henkel gemeinsam auf dem Podium saß, wurde erstmals diskutiert, ob man eine neue rechte Partei brauche. Henkel und Storch bejahten dies und Jürgen Elsässer, der gerade erst sein neofaschistisches Compact-Magazin gegründet hatte …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: DeSantis, Cabinet Designate Major Muslim American Group as “Terrorist”
content:
Florida Republicans have spent months maneuvering to grant DeSantis the authority to ban the group.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Far right Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis and his cabinet have voted to designate the U.S.’s leading Muslim civil rights group as a “domestic terrorist organization,” threatening to shutter and impose severe penalties on the group and its state affiliate simply to serve the GOP’s political crusades, critics said.

The 427-page document recommending “terrorist” designations for the Council on American-Islamic Relations (CAIR) and its Florida chapter was approved over the course of just 30 seconds at DeSantis’s cabinet meeting on Tuesday, according to the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU).

Contained within the approved packet, submitted by the Florida Department of Law Enforcement, were also recommendations for “antifa” and dozens of other groups already named as foreign terrorist organizations by the federal government to be listed as “terrorist” groups.

CAIR is the largest Muslim civil rights group in the U.S. If these designations go into effect, CAIR and CAIR-Florida could be forced to shutter its work in the state.

Because of the broad design of the designation, those who associate with the group could also face harsh penalties. Universities would be mandated to expel students who “promote” the group. And, according to the ACLU, CAIR and CAIR-Florida would be barred from seeking legal representation because their lawyers would face prosecution from the state for doing so.

The ACLU and other legal partners have pledged to file a legal challenge against the designation on behalf of CAIR and CAIR-Florida, preventing it from going into place. ACLU counsel say that, at the meeting on Tuesday, they were barred from being able to present arguments against the designation, which they say was done simply because DeSantis and his Republican cabinet see CAIR as a “threat” because of its faith-based mission.

“Gov. DeSantis’s use of Florida’s dangerous new ‘terrorism’ designation regime against CAIR and its Florida chapter is baseless and unconstitutional,” said Hina Shamshi, who directs the ACLU’s National Security Project. “As the country’s leading Muslim civil rights group, CAIR is being targeted not because it poses a threat to public safety, but because doing so serves a political agenda at the expense of Floridians’ rights.”

The legal filing would build upon the ACLU’s existing lawsuit against the designation, which DeSantis and Republicans have been trying to push through for months. Last December, DeSantis issued an executive order to designate CAIR as a “terrorist” group, but that was quickly paused by a federal judge, who issued an injunction against it. The judge said that DeSantis exceeded his authority in issuing the orders.

Then, in April, the legislature passed two new laws, HB 1471 and HB 1473, aimed at granting DeSantis the authority to make the designations. The newly passed laws grant DeSantis and his cabinet the unilateral power to designate domestic terrorist organizations, ban state funds from being sent to schools with any affiliation with those groups, and ban Florida courts from enforcing Islamic law, or Sharia.

One version of one of the bills, introduced in the Florida Senate, was reportedly authored by DeSantis’s office as he sought more ways to punish student protesters for pro-Palestine demonstrations.

CAIR, meanwhile, issued a statement in January questioning whether DeSantis’s original orders were done in retaliation for the group’s public records request “seeking to expose possible coordination between his administration, Israeli government officials, and anti-Muslim influence networks that have worked to smear Florida Muslims and civil rights organizations.”

author: Ezra
title: Paris ermöglicht Auslieferung des Antifaschisten Gino an Deutschland: No Extradition!
content:
Paris ermöglicht Auslieferung des Antifaschisten Gino an Deutschland: No Extradition!


Gino wird beschuldigt, sich zusammen mit anderen Antifaschist*innen im Februar 2023 in Budapest an körperlichen Auseinandersetzungen mit Nazis beteiligt zu haben. Damals fand der

NS

-verherrlichende „Tag der Ehre“ statt, das jährlich stattfindende europaweit größte Nazi-Vernetzungstreffen, wogegen es antifaschistische Proteste gab. Die Vorfälle nahm Ungarn zum Anlass für eine internationale Kriminalisierungswelle gegen Antifaschist*innen, wobei sich vor allem die deutschen und 

US

-amerikanischen Behörden der Repressionsoffensive engagiert anschlossen.

Auch in Deutschland laufen Prozesse im Budapest-Komplex, wobei Ende September 2025 als erste die Nürnberger Antifaschistin Hanna zu fünf Jahren Haft verurteilt wurde – ohne jede Beweise. Seit Anfang 2026 läuft in Düsseldorf das Budapest-Großverfahren gegen sechs Antifaschist*innen, und auch im Dresdner Antifa-Großprozess wird mehreren Angeklagten eine Beteiligung an den Vorfällen in Ungarn vorgeworfen. Die meisten in Deutschland Beschuldigten sind schon seit Jahren in Untersuchungshaft. Parallel dazu wurde heute in Budapest das Strafverfahren gegen Maja T., Gabriele M. und Anna M. beendet und vom Revisionsgericht der Schuldspruch und die grotesk hohen Haft- und Geldstrafen im Wesentlichen bestätigt.

Zu den international verfolgten Antifaschist*innen gehört auch Gino, der in Mailand aufwuchs, aber einen albanischen Pass hat. Er lebte zuletzt jahrelang in Finnland und floh vor den Verfolgungen im Budapest-Komplex nach Frankreich, wo er im November 2024 für mehrere Monate in Haft genommen wurde, weil Ungarn per Europäischem Haftbefehl seine Auslieferung verlangte. Angesichts der katastrophalen Menschenrechtslage, insbesondere der drohenden Folter, und mit Verweis auf die fehlende Rechtsstaatlichkeit in Ungarn lehnte es die Auslieferungskammer des Pariser Berufungsgerichts im April 2025 ab, Gino an Budapest zu überstellen.

Als enge Bündnispartnerinnen bei der ungarisch-deutschen Verfolgungsjagd gegen Antifaschist*innen erließen daraufhin die deutschen Behörden Ende 2025 einen eigenen Europäischen Haftbefehl gegen Gino und verlangten seine Auslieferung, um ihn in Deutschland anzuklagen. Zur Begründung verweist die Bundesanwaltschaft darauf, dass zwei der Nazis, die in Budapest verletzt worden sein sollen, die deutsche Staatsangehörigkeit besitzen. Im Fall von Deutschland fiel es der Pariser Justiz deutlich schwerer, die offen politische Verfolgung und die unübersehbaren Rechtsbrüche im Umgang mit Antifaschist*innen zu benennen, die einer Auslieferung im Wege stehen. Dabei besteht das hohe Risiko, dass die deutschen Behörden anschließend Gino an Ungarn ausliefern und das Pariser Urteil von 2025 auf diese Art rechtswidrig umgehen. Eine Auslieferung könnte entweder direkt nach der Ankunft erfolgen oder aber nach einem Prozess und mehrjähriger Haft in Deutschland. Die Gefahr ist umso größer, als der Antifaschist weder Deutscher noch

EU

-Bürger ist. Aber der politische Druck aus Deutschland ist enorm, und am 18. September 2026 hatte deshalb bereits das Berufungsgericht Ginos Auslieferung beschlossen, wogegen die Verteidigung vor das Kassationsgericht zog. Die heutige Sitzung des Kassationsgerichts bestätigte die Auslieferung an Deutschland endgültig.

Die Entscheidung war ein Schock und löste unmittelbar starke Proteste vor allem in Paris aus. In den letzten Wochen hatte sich eine internationale Solidaritätskampagne formiert, die besonders in Frankreich und Italien zu Massenprotesten und breiter gesellschaftlicher Unterstützung für Gino führte. Hunderte Prominente unterzeichneten eine Petition, die die drohende Auslieferung scharf ablehnte und die Verfolgung von Antifaschist*innen im Budapest-Komplex anprangerte. Für heute Abend sind zudem mehrere Proteste im ganzen Land angekündigt.

„Die heutige Entscheidung des Pariser Kassationsgerichts, Gino nach Deutschland auszuliefern, ist ein Skandal und zeigt, dass auch in Frankreich Grund- und Menschenrechte nicht länger für Antifaschist*innen gelten. Schließlich muss Gino nicht nur mit schwerer politischer Verfolgung und langer Haft in Deutschland rechnen, sondern auch die rechtswidrige Auslieferung an Ungarn fürchten“, erklärte Hartmut Brückner vom Bundesvorstand der Roten Hilfe e. author: Bulatlat Contributors
title: Cultural workers vs fascism, demolition
content:
MANILA — A movement of cultural workers against demolition and police brutality expressed political dissent through a cultural event on September 26 at Vinzon’s Hall, University of the Philippines Diliman.

Dubbed “Gobyerno Sindikato, Panagutin,” Defend the Hood called for an end to fascist measures of the Philippine National Police, including the demolition of their communities.

Skaters, B-boy dancers, graffiti artists, and other performers got together to showcase their talents.

Youth skaters used the occasion to denounce the Marcos Jr. administration’s use of force in repressing and illegally arresting activists, including minors. They also condemned police brutality, citing the violent arrest at the last state of the nation address (SONA) in July where the police illegally arrested 51 protesters.

Among them was Dupa, a member of Defend the Hood and a skater from Pook Malantic in barangay UP Campus.

Read: ‘Overkill; | Groups slam police arrests of activists during SONA 2026 protest

Dupa and their community are no strangers to being labeled as deviant or dangerous by authorities even within campus premises. Nevertheless, skateboarding has become essential for their community as a means to express themselves and their way of activism.

For Dupa, they skated to “raise people’s awareness of what is happening in our communities, because of plans of demolition and harassment from authorities.”

Dupa’s community is threatened with displacement due to the construction of the UP SDG Park, a 24-hectare project that covers Area 17, Pook Aguinaldo, and Pook Malantic in barangay UP Campus. As early as July, the community began setting up barricades to prevent the construction of the project and to resist police surveillance.

“Why do they not care about the youth’s livelihoods? Our education?” Dupa asked during the program.

B-boy dancers like ElloRisco joined in solidarity with the community. “B-boying is just something you do, it’s like fliptop but you instead converse through movement.” (AMU, DAA)

Real names are withheld for security reasons.
