title: Türkiye-Yunanistan gerilimi: Sadece bir sınır sorunu değil emperyalist planda yer kapma meselesi
content:
Seyit Aldoğan [email protected]

Atina- Son dönemde Ortadoğu, Doğu Akdeniz, Ege ve İran ekseninde gelişen ABD-İsrail savaşının yaygınlaşma eğilimi, bir anlamda Türk-Yunan ilişkilerini de tetikledi. Bu durum Türkiye basınında “Atina’da deprem”, “Atina gerilim istiyor”, “Yunanistan ve İsrail ablukası” benzeri manşetlerin atılmasına neden oldu. Karşılıklı restleşmeler, uyarılar ve milliyetçi söylemlerle düşmanlığı körükleyen değerlendirmeler havada uçuşuyor.

Dünyada emperyalist rekabetin kızışmasına, pazar paylaşımı mücadelesine ve emperyalist savaşların yaygınlaşma eğilimi içine girmesine paralel olarak, üzerinde yaşadığımız coğrafyada da enerji nakil hatları, hidrokarbon rezervleri ve deniz taşımacılığı gibi etkenlere bağlı olarak Türkiye-Yunanistan ilişkilerinde yeni bir gerginliğe doğru gidildiği görülüyor.

ABD ve onun bölgedeki vurucu gücü olan İsrail yeni bir yapılanmayı hedeflerken, bölgedeki gerici yönetimler pastadan pay kapmak, emperyalist sistemin bir parçası olarak varlıklarını sürdürmeyi güvence altına almak ve bölgesel çıkar dengeleri içinde daha iyi bir mevzi tutmak amacıyla dış politika, ticaret, silahlanma ve ittifaklarda yeni yönelimler içine giriyorlar. Bölge gericiliklerinin çıkarlarının farklılıklar göstermesi emperyalizme bağımlılıkla çelişmediği gibi, tersine bu bağımlılığı daha da güçlendiren birer etmen haline geliyor.

Bölgedeki gelişmelere bu perspektifle bakıldığında Türkiye ve Yunanistan arasında anlaşmazlık konusu olan sorunların klasik anlamda bir sınır sorunu olmaktan çıktığı açıkça görülecektir.

Rusya Karadeniz, Balkanlar ve Doğu Avrupa’dan abluka altına alınıyor. Yunan adalarına hava savunma sistemlerinin yerleştirilerek Ege kontrol altına alınmaya çalışılıyor. Doğu Trakya ABD-NATO üssüne çevriliyor. Öte yandan Doğu Akdeniz’de İsrail, Güney Kıbrıs ve Yunanistan arasında enerji nakil anlaşmasının yürürlüğe girmesi, Yunanistan’ın münhasır ekonomik bölge çerçevesi içinde uluslararası tekellerle yaptığı anlaşmalar, enerji rezervlerinin önemi, Ortadoğu’ya müdahalede bölgenin önem kazanması, Çin ve Rusya ile girişilen rekabet vb. gelişmeler Türkiye ile Yunanistan arasındaki sorunların artık klasik anlaşmazlıklar olmaktan çıktığını gösteriyor. Gelişmeler, Ege ve Doğu Akdeniz’i emperyalist yayılmacılık, paylaşım ve egemenlik rekabetinin açıkça görüldüğü alan durumuna getiriyor.

Yunanistan’da 1973 yılında yıkılan Albaylar Cuntası sonrasından bugüne kadar kurulan en işbirlikçi yönetim olan Kiryakos Miçotakis’nin Yeni Demokrasi (ND) hükümeti, Ege’de ve Doğu Akdeniz’de Yunan sermayesinin çıkarları doğrultusunda başta ABD, İsrail ve sonrasında AB ile, son derece stratejik anlaşmalar yapmış bulunuyor. Mısır, Lübnan, BAE, Suudi Arabistan ile askeri ve ticari ve teknik ilişkiler geliştirdi. Bu arada özellikle Fransız ve Alman tekellerinin çıkarlarının sözcülüğünü de yapıyor.

Erdoğan hükümeti ise ABD ve AB destekli İsrail, Yunanistan ve Güney Kıbrıs kesimi eksenine karşı Suriye’de sahip olduğu etkiyi, son süreçte Pakistan ve Suudi Arabistan ile kurulan “Mekke ittifakı”nı, ABD ve NATO politikaları ile tam bir uyum içinde olan tutumunu; Trump’ın övgüsünü kazanan İran ve Filistin politikasını, NATO politikaları çerçevesi içinde artan silahlanma harcamalarını kullanarak elini güçlendirmeye ve bölge ülkeleriyle kurduğu ekseni güçlendirmeye çalışıyor.

Kuşkusuz her iki ülkenin bağımlılığı daha fazla artıran bu tutumlarının ana nedeni sadece Türk-Yunan ilişkileri ve Ege-Doğu Akdeniz gibi sorunlarla açıklanamaz. Esas neden bölgede oluşan ya da oluşması olası olan dengelerden pay kapma yarışıdır. Türkiye’yi asıl kaygılandıran İsrail’in bölgede oyun kurucu duruma gelme planlarıdır. Örneğin “yavru vatan” ilan edilmesine ramak kalan Suriye’de İsrail’in etkisinin artması ve Colani hükümeti ile anlaşma masasına oturulması, Arap ülkeleriyle İbrahim anlaşmalarının imzalanması, Yunanistan’ın AB üyesi olarak Türkiye ile bölgesel çıkarlar üzerinden iş birliği yapan ülkeler ve tekellerle ekonomik, askeri ve ticari ilişkiler geliştirmesi Türkiye’nin yayılmacı politikaları önünde ciddi engeller oluşturuyor.

Son süreçte ise Yunanistan, Kıbrıs ve İsrail arasında çekilen elektrik hattı ve Türkiye tarafından hazırlanan “Mavi vatan” kanunu ve “deniz parkları” kararı, iki ülke arasında gerginliğin yeniden yükselmesine neden oldu. Yunan hükümeti “Mavi vatan” kanununun “hiçbir geçerliliğinin olmayacağını” savunurken, Dışişleri Bakanı Yorgos Gerapetritis defalarca “Yunanistan her türlü tahrike karşı koymaya hazırdır” …

author: Sarah Raymundo
title: Blood Rush | $100 barrel, super El Niño and Pax Silica: Energy hegemony, enclosure, and national liberation
content:
The AI-assisted illustration of the proposed 1,600-hectare industrial hub to be located in New Clark City in Capas, Tarlac. Photo courtesy of the People’s Television Network

The convergence of crude oil surpassing $100 per barrel and the acceleration of El Niño to “super” status—drawn from projections and reports by energy-market analysts, international economic-monitoring bodies, and climate agencies tracking compound global shocks—exposes the deep structural crisis of monopoly capitalism. This dual rupture demonstrates how imperialist war-making, extractive plunder, planetary warming, and the ongoing enclosure of the countryside function not as separate phenomena, but as interconnected expressions of the same underlying logic of capital accumulation.

The rapid climb of crude oil past $100 per barrel cannot be detached from the escalation of U.S.-led imperialist aggression, military blockades, and regional destabilization. Financialized markets and transnational fossil-fuel monopolies exploit war and artificial scarcity to protect superprofits, while the resulting inflation functions as a mechanism of structural extraction from working classes in colonies and semicolonies. Peripheral societies are forced to absorb the crisis through debt traps, budget cuts, declining purchasing power, and reduced national sovereignty. High energy prices further incentivize ruling elites to expand speculative and destructive extraction projects in the name of energy security and geopolitical hegemony.

This energy regime is increasingly bound up with “Pax Silica”—the global alliance centered on microelectronics, semiconductor supply chains, and automated defense systems. Localized military interventions rely on a global network of critical mineral extraction, energy consumption, and defense technology transfer. The fusion of high-tech militarism and fossil capital reinforces imperialist control over global supply lines, shifting the operational costs of planetary warfare directly onto the working classes of the Global South.

At the same time, a “super” El Niño brings the violence of ecological crisis directly to the doorsteps of the global peasantry, smallholders, and urban poor. Although the historical carbon footprint belongs overwhelmingly to the industrial centers of the imperialist world, the physical destruction—manifested in crop failures, severe drought, flooding, and damaged infrastructure—falls disproportionately on semicolonial societies. Framing these events as merely “natural disasters” shields the capitalist mode of production from critique and obscures climate catastrophe as an institutionalized assault on oppressed and economically vulnerable populations.

Far from resolving the agrarian question, this ecological and economic squeeze accelerates what Paris Yeros calls generalized semiproletarianization. In this condition, households that have lost all or part of their means of production do not become fully dependent on wages. Instead, they combine precarious employment with small-scale farming, petty trade, subsistence production, care work, and other sources of livelihood (Yeros, 2023). Across much of the Global South, this blurs the conventional boundary between peasant and worker and produces socially fragmented labor forces that move between rural and urban economies (Moyo & Yeros, 2005; Moyo et al., 2013; Yeros, 2024).

Under conditions of monopoly capitalism, these labor reserves can weaken workers’ bargaining power and shift the costs of social reproduction onto households and communities (Marx, 1976; Yeros, 2023). Millions may circulate between degraded smallholder farming, informal street trade, temporary migration, and precarious wage work without being absorbed into secure urban industrial employment. Rather than representing a simple transition from peasant production to wage labor, semiproletarianization describes a durable social formation in which rural and urban livelihood strategies remain interdependent (Yeros, 2023).

To propose “ecosocialism” as a generic, off-the-shelf alternative to this twin crisis, without subjecting the term itself to critical scrutiny, is to risk reproducing a dangerous conceptual trap. Much dominant Western-centered ecosocialist discourse reduces the problem to an abstract, planet-wide carbon-accounting exercise. In doing so, it can erase the national question, gloss over the unresolved agrarian question, and ignore the necessity of national-liberation struggles in …

author: Publicación Abierta
title: Elecciones Brasil 2026, una batalla contra el imperialismo
content:
Las amplias elecciones que el próximo 4 de octubre tendrán lugar en Brasil, en las que se elegirán presidente, gobernadores y legisladores, son de importancia estratégica para nuestra Abya Yala y para todo el globo terráqueo. Brasil es el 5to país más extenso, está entre las 10 economías más grandes y demográficamente ocupa el séptimo lugar en el mundo.


Por otra parte, el Brasil de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, del Partido de los Trabajadores (PT), forma parte de los BRICS, quienes vienen abogando por un orden mundial más justo y equilibrado; su principal socio comercial es China, con una tendencia al crecimiento en su intercambio comercial; ha hecho fuertes críticas al ente sionista que, con la ayuda de los EE. UU., está ejecutando un genocidio contra el pueblo palestino. Todo lo anterior lo convierte en el principal objetivo del presidente Trump en el hemisferio. Ya le ha impuesto a las importaciones de EE. UU. desde Brasil, entre el 12.5 % y el 50 % de aranceles, lo que ha hecho descender las exportaciones brasileñas hacia los EE. UU. a sus niveles más bajos desde 1997, lo que ha afectado negativamente su economía, expresado esto, en el bajo crecimiento de su PIB durante 2026.


Trump y su secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio, se han estado pronunciando a favor de la candidatura de Flavio Bolsonaro y criticado ferozmente el juicio que se le siguió a Jair Bolsonaro, por el intento del golpe de Estado, llegando al extremo de tomar medidas coercitivas unilaterales contra el juez que llevó la causa.


La intromisión de los EE. UU. en los asuntos internos de otros países es bien conocida. title: Nationale Demo - Smash Imperialism - 11. Oktober
content:
Bewegung 11. Oktober


Der Imperialismus hat seine Transformation in eine neue Phase begonnen. Die Hegemonie des von den USA angeführten imperialistischen Blocks läutet ihr eigenes Ende ein. Dies zeigt sich – um nur einige Beispiele zu nennen – in eskalierenden Angriffskriegen (Iran), Genoziden (Palästina, Sudan) und Ressourcenkriegen (Kongo). Ebenso werden im Stellvertreterkrieg zwischen der NATO und Russland in der Ukraine abertausende Leben von oftmals zwangsrekrutierten Arbeiter:innen für europäische und US-Interessen geopfert. Andernorts bestrebt das US-Imperium – wie sich in Kuba und Venezuela in äusserster Brutalität zeigt – verstärkt den absoluten Machtanspruch auf Lateinamerika, in US-Perspektive als eigene Einflusszone angesehen, auch "backyard" genannt.


Aus Angst unterzugehen, schlägt die Bestie wild um sich. Die materielle Übermacht schwindet immer mehr und der Hauptkonkurrent China – und damit auch viele Verbündete der Volksrepublik – gewinnt an globalem Einfluss. Die Kapitalist:innen schüren Krise um Krise: Sei es der unmittelbar bevorstehende Klimakollaps, die Faschisierung der westlichen Staaten, die zunehmende Überwachung durch KI und die aggressive Umverteilung von unten nach oben.


Die Lügen der herrschenden Klasse werden immer offensichtlicher. Sie versuchen uns für dumm zu verkaufen, indem sie uns erzählen, in Gaza gäbe es einen Waffenstillstand. Indem sie legitimen und notwendigen Widerstand als "Terrorismus" deklarieren. Indem sie Palästina als "Israel" bezeichnen. Damit versuchen sie den Status Quo aufrechtzuerhalten: Eine weisse Vorherrschaft, die es ihnen erlaubt, ungebremst Kapital anzuhäufen und ihr Territorium gewaltsam zu erweitern.


Im Kongo fördern multinationale Konzerne im Dienste westlicher Mächte seit über 30 Jahren Genozid, um das Land im Chaos versinken zu lassen. Durch aktive Destabilisierung lassen sich die Ressourcen leichter abbauen und das Land ausbeuten. Dasselbe geschieht im Sudan, wo ein sogenannter "Bürgerkrieg" befeuert wird, um die zahlreichen Bodenschätze auszubeuten.


Dies sind nur einige wenige Beispiele von zu vielen, die aufzeigen, dass Millionen von Menschenleben (vor allem Schwarzes und Braunes Leben) den Herrschenden scheissegal sind. Was zählt, sind kurzfristige Gewinne. Alles auf Kosten von Mensch und Natur.


Das US-Imperium agiert dabei mit einer militärischen Gewalt und einer Grösse, die alle bisherigen Ausmasse übersteigt. Weiter ist das US-Militär der mit Abstand grösste Einzelverbraucher fossiler Brennstoffe und damit der grösste Umweltverschmutzer der Welt.


Unsere individuellen Initiativen, die Umwelt zu schützen und zu respektieren, verenden im Angesicht der wütenden Bestie in völliger Bedeutungslosigkeit. Doch der Fokus auf individuelles Konsumverhalten offenbart einen tieferliegenden Mechanismus: Nachhaltiges Verhalten wird zum Massstab erhoben und wer davon abweicht, wird verurteilt. Die Logik dahinter: "Divide and rule"


So wird unser Fokus und unsere Energie auf die gegenseitige Kontrolle gelegt, anstatt die Tausenden von Bomben zu stoppen, die Mensch und Natur komplett zerstören. Symptombekämpfung wird als Lösung hochstilisiert; wertvolle Zeit, die wir im Kampf für Klimagerechtigkeit brauchen könnten, geht verloren.


Wir müssen endlich verstehen: Der Kampf gegen die globale Kriegsmaschinerie und der Kampf für Klimagerechtigkeit ist ein und derselbe Kampf!


Die bürgerliche Demokratie möchte uns klarmachen, dass wir mittels Abstimmungen etwas verändern können und verkauft uns, dass wir mit unserem individuellen Konsumverhalten die Natur "retten können". Demokratie gibt uns zu verstehen: "Alle Menschen sind gleich". Doch wenn wir genauer hinschauen, verstehen wir die bürgerliche Demokratie als Teil des Problems. Denn auch sie ist nur ein Mittel, das Volk zu unterdrücken und eines freien Lebens zu berauben und somit die Kapitalinteressen der herschenden Klasse zu befriedigen. Unter dem Vorwand der "Demokratsierung" (eigentlich "Zivilisierung") werden seit jeher Länder angegriffen, Überausbeutung legitimiert und Proteste gewaltsam niedergeschlagen. Die Aussengrenzen werden aufgerüstet, Menschen illegalisiert. Militarisierung und Aufrüstung wird auf Kosten der Gesundheit und Bildung vorangetrieben. Faschistoides Gedankengut schiesst wie Pilze aus dem Boden und zeigt sich in Form von Parteien, in Gesetzesvorlagen, in medialer Hetze, oder dem Antifa-Verbot. Der Diskurs wird mithilfe von liberalen Parteien schrittweise gegen rechts verschoben …

author: Charlotte Reck
title: Spain’s Tenants’ Rights Protesters Win Reforms After 87-Year-Old Evicted
content:
Spain’s government has approved new measures to support tenants’ rights following widespread protests – but they need approval from congress and campaigners say they do not go far enough. 


Around 30,000 people marched through Madrid on Saturday, and

hundreds remained for days

 in encampments across the capital’s central plazas, after an 87-year-old woman was forcibly removed from her home of 70 years on a stretcher. 


Maricarmen Abascal was evicted after her rent rose from €500 (£428) to €1,650

and she was unable to pay

. Urbagestión – the investment firm that owns the property – has now been forced to allow her to return and pay €533 in rent.  


The eviction prompted the Madrid Tenants’ Union to draw up the Maricarmen decree, which calls for a law against evicting vulnerable individuals without offering them alternative housing. It also proposes curbing unjustified price increases, a freeze on rents and an automatic renewal of leases to prevent unjustified evictions. 


Spain’s Socialist Workers’ party-led coalition government approved the extension of rental contracts, the ban on evicting vulnerable renters and the regulation of seasonal and room rentals that interfere with the supply of affordable housing, although measures must now be approved in congress, where the coalition lacks a majority.


But the government has split its proposal into two decrees – the first is concerned with banning evictions and introducing regulations, while the second considers automatic lease renewals. While it is believed that the conservative Catalan and Basque parties will throw support behind the first decree, it is thought likely the parties will reject the second.


Alicia Del Río, a Tenant’s Union spokesperson, said splitting the proposals into separate decrees was “a tactic of tearing something into shreds so that all that’s left are scraps.” 


“The union demands the implementation of the Maricarmen decree in its entirety,” she

told the Guardian

. “They have to accept what people are demanding.”


Spain’s health minister Mónica García wrote on X:


“What a month ago was unimaginable has now been achieved thanks to social mobilisation, the encampment, that clamour from the streets that pushes forward and serves as a lever for change.”

 


She added: “Now, the challenge ahead of us is to defend these measures in congress.”

title: Le 4ème n'est pas à vendre
content:
La militarisation de la ville, la financiarisation de l'habitat et du logement, la privatisation des espaces publics, la construction de frontières – tant formelles que symboliques –, les politiques de sécurité publique fondées sur le profilage racial et la criminalisation de la pauvreté constituent les fondements d'un urbanisme néolibéral et du néofascisme en tant que projet de ville.


À Marseille

, un nouveau rapport à la ville semble s'être imposé à marche forcée : gentrification, privatisation, évacuation de squats et augmentation exponentielle des loyers. Les conséquences retentissent dans tous les aspects de la vie quotidienne : habitant•es chassé•es du centre-ville par le tourisme de masse et des loyers prohibitifs, disparition de lieux emblématiques et multiplication de logements vacants.


Au sein du 4ème

, après les Airbnb, nous voyons apparaître les colivings, immeubles entiers destinés à la location à court et moyen terme à des tarifs prohibitifs pour la plupart d'entre nous, qui semblent être le nouvel eldorado de la spéculation immobilière.


Ceci n'est pas une fatalité mais bien un projet délibéré ayant pour but final l'enrichissement de holdings immobilières aux dépens des habitants et habitantes, qui voient s'envoler le prix du logement.


Par ailleurs, l'obsession de transformer chaque mètre carré de terrain en produit rentable empêche l'apparition de lieux propices à la solidarité et à la convivialité : locaux associatifs, jardins autonomes et partagés, équipements sportifs et jeux pour les enfants.


La financiarisation de l'habitat est l'affaire de nous toutes et tous.


Face aux problématiques du mal-logement, d'insalubrité, de la mise en péril, des charges et loyers exorbitants, répondons par une solidarité sans faille.


Comité antifasciste du 4ème

title: La Justicia suspende el desalojo a los obreros de Fate
content:
Sigue firme la lucha con el Sutna a la cabeza.


La Justicia suspende 

la orden de desalojo a la ocupación

 de la planta de Fate. Tras siete meses y medio, los obreros siguen firmes en su lucha contra el lock out patronal y en defensa de los puestos de trabajo. 

La sala II de la Cámara de Garantías concedió el recurso de Casación con efecto suspensivo sobre la medida que, el 17 de septiembre, había ordenado el desalojo del predio de San Fernando en beneficio de la patronal de Javier Madanes Quintanilla.

Por Prensa Obrera.


El recurso de impugnación había sido presentado por la abogada Liliana Alaniz, denunciando que la arbitraria resolución atentaba contra el derecho a huelga, a la libertad sindical y que iba a tener consecuencias irreversibles ya que iba a permitir a la patronal de Fate culminar el vaciamiento de la planta. Además, cuestionaba que se desplazaba un conflicto laboral al ámbito penal.


#URGENTE

 La justicia resolvió que no puede ejecutarse el desalojo de FATE.


Sigamos rodeando de solidaridad esta lucha.


FATE NO SE CIERRA

https://t.co/04yFQJxxvq


pic.twitter.com/UjMqknjtol


— Prensa Obrera (@prensaobrera)

September 29, 2026


La pelea por la reapertura productiva de la fábrica de neumáticos, preservando todos los puestos de trabajo, se mantiene así firme, con el Sutna a la cabeza. Una lucha obrera emblemática, que contrasta con la entrega de la burocracia sindical de la CGT y las CTAs ante miles de despidos.


Además de enfrentar la recesión y la ofensiva antiobrera de Milei, denuncia que Kicillof no los recibe y la Legislatura bonaerense sigue dilatando el tratamiento del proyecto de ley de ocupación temporánea para reactivar la fábrica y sostener la fuente laboral de 900 familias.


Por eso los obreros de Fate recogen una enorme solidaridad popular, que desde la orden de desalojo 

había tenido nuevas expresiones

 con vigilias, pronunciamientos, actividades artísticas y movilizaciones. Sigamos poniendo todo el apoyo para que triunfen los trabajadores del neumático y el Sutna.

author: Isaac Nellist
title: Balmain meeting calls for public housing in Bays West, opposes Labor’s plan
content:
Bays West includes public land at Glebe Island, White Bay and parts of Rozelle and Lilyfield. Labor’ wants to hand this to developers to build high-rise apartments; it proposes only 10% be reserved for “affordable” or “essential worker” housing.

The 150-strong meeting was organised by the Better Future Coalition (BFC), comprising resident groups which oppose NSW Labor and the Labor-dominated Inner West Council’s (IWC) pro-developer planning schemes.

Many community and housing groups supported the meeting including Leichhardt Matters, Save Dully, Action for Public Housing, Save Marrickville, Hands off Glebe, Friends of Erskineville, Doing Density Better, Mosman Matters and others.

Judy Mundey, a long-time activist and barrister set the framework for discussion by outlining the historic decline in public housing across NSW and the consequent rise in homelessness, housing insecurity and expensive rents and house prices.

“It’s not as if the government is not aware we have a housing crisis; there is no shortage of announcements and promises … but almost all proposals involve the private sector.”

Mundey said there are “almost daily” reports on dodgy developers, to whom Minns is handing over public land.

“If we’re going to address the housing crisis, we need less privatisation of public land and more well designed public housing,” Mundey said.

“In opposition, Labor said any surplus land would be subject to a mandatory requirement for 30% of social, affordable and universal housing. But now in government, at Bays West, it has reduced that to 10% for affordable and essential worker housing.

“There is no commitment for public housing to be any part of the plan. This is a failure to utilise public assets to address the social injustice inflicted on so many, a failure to ensure a decent, safe, secure home, essential for health and wellbeing.”

Architect and urban designer Eddie Ma gave details about what is known about the Bays West plan. He said Minns had commissioned international architecture firms to make proposals.

Ma emphasised that the plans could be changed — for better or for worse. “It should be the community that decides what we do with Bays West, not the government and certainly not architects.”

Former independent Inner West councillor John Stamolis said that the inner west was one of the country’s highest density areas and that it was ridiculous for Labor to accuse people who want better planning of opposing any development. He said there needed to be more public housing now because of the security it brings.

Greens MP for Balmain Kobi Shetty said it was hard to know a lot about Labor’s plan as it has been vague. She said the Greens welcome Labor’s commitment to delivering the Glebe Island Bridge as an essential walking and cycling link.

Ben Radford, a town planner and Green Left journalist, MCed the meeting, which voted overwhelmingly to adopt a resolution opposing Labor’s plan, calling for community consultation and to add a sixth point calling for any housing at Bays West to be public.

BFC had invited Philippa Scott, Labor’s candidate for Balmain and deputy mayor of IWC, to come and listen to the concerns. She did not reply.

[Isaac Nellist is a member of the Better Future Coalition and is the Socialist Alliance candidate for Balmain in the NSW elections.]

author: Helmut Weiss
title: Gegen Mietpreisexplosion die Deutsche Wohnen & Co enteignen: Ein guter Anfang
content:
Dossier


Die Kampagne zur Enteignung der „Deutsche Wohnen“ ist ein guter Anfang. (Denn die Vonovia&Co sind ja auch noch da…). Mit Sicherheit wird in diesem Zusammenhang die Reaktion ihre übliche Gegenkampagne starten, des Bürgers Eigenheim sei in Gefahr – und Ältere werden sich vielleicht noch erinnern, dass es in der BRD auch einmal eine Sozialdemokratie gab. Die sich bei ihren, wie immer begrenzten, Schritten gegen den Vorwurf verteidigen musste, sie wolle dem „deutschen Arbeiter“ seine Villa im Tessin nehmen. Diese Aussicht kann und soll eine solche Kampagne also nicht verhindern oder auch nur beschränken. Denn Gründe dafür gibt es mehr als genug – von der unbeeindruckten Fortsetzung der Preistreiberei bei den Mieten durch große – und kleinere – Wohnungsgesellschaften, bis hin zur Stadt- und Baupolitik diverser Landesregierungen. Eine Entwicklung, die vielleicht Städte wie Berlin oder Frankfurt im Zentrum der Aufmerksamkeit haben mag – aber „das Böse ist immer und überall“, auch in Duisburg oder Niedersteppenbach. Zu den aktuellen Entwicklungen im Widerstand gegen den Mietenwahnsinn und dessen ungebrochene Fortsetzung siehe

die Kampagnenseite


 und hier:


Studie: Vergesellschaftung von Wohnbeständen: Ausgestaltung entscheidend für Finanzierbarkeit, Rechtssicherheit und Umsetzbarkeit


„Eine Vergesellschaftung großer Wohnungsbestände wird den Wohnraummangel in Deutschlands Großstädten nicht beheben. Dazu braucht es Neubau in großem Stil. Dennoch kann die Vergesellschaftung als ergänzendes Element sinnvoll sein, um das Bezahlbarkeitsproblem von Mieten zu vermindern, ergibt eine neue Studie am Beispiel der Situation in Berlin. Wichtig ist dabei aber erstens, dass der ohnehin angespannte Berliner Landeshaushalt nicht belastet wird und zweitens, dass die Vergesellschaftung so umgesetzt wird, dass nicht zugleich der Neubau leidet. Zu diesem Ergebnis kommen Prof. Dr. Sebastian Dullien vom Institut für Makroökonomie und Konjunkturforschung (IMK) der Hans-Böckler-Stiftung, Dr. Patrick Kaczmarczyk und Prof. Dr. Tom Krebs von der Universität Mannheim sowie Prof. Dr. Achim Truger von der Universität Duisburg-Essen. Die Ökonomen zeigen am Beispiel Berlins, dass die Vergesellschaftung von Wohnungen nicht nur sozialpolitisch sinnvoll, sondern – je nach Modell – auch wirtschaftlich und fiskalisch tragbar sein kann. Die bei einer Überführung von rund 210.000 Wohnungen in Gemeineigentum fällige Entschädigung für die privaten Wohnungsunternehmen veranschlagen die Forscher auf rund 13,5 Milliarden Euro. Bei kluger Ausgestaltung der Vergesellschaftung wäre das ohne Kürzungen im Berliner Landeshaushalt finanzierbar. Die Forscher haben drei verschiedene Modelle zur Vergesellschaftung von Wohnbeständen untersucht. Variante 1: Eine neu zu gründende Anstalt des öffentlichen Rechts (AöR) übernimmt die Wohnungen. Variante 2: Die sechs landeseigenen Wohnungsunternehmen (LWU) übernehmen die Wohnungen. Variante 3: Die sechs Wohnungsunternehmen werden in eine Anstalt des öffentlichen Rechts integriert und übernehmen die Wohnungen. Nach Analyse der Forscher ist Variante 2 am besten geeignet, um rechtliche, finanzielle und organisatorische Risiken einer Vergesellschaftung so weit wie möglich zu minimieren. (…)


Die Wohnungen könnten direkt oder über den Umweg einer vorübergehend eingerichteten AöR den sechs bestehenden LWU übertragen werden. Diese bewirtschaften bereits mehrere hunderttausend Wohnungen und verfügen über die notwendigen technischen und organisatorischen Kapazitäten, die natürlich ausgebaut werden müssten. Die Entschädigungen würden finanziert über zusätzliches, vom Land bereitgestelltes Eigenkapital der LWU sowie eine Fremdfinanzierung der jeweiligen Wohnungsunternehmen. Das Risiko, dass Ausgaben und Verschuldung der Wohnungsbauunternehmen zum Sektor Staat gerechnet werden, wäre deutlich geringer als bei Variante 1 mit einer dauerhaft errichteten zentralen AöR. Nach Einschätzung der Forscher ist das ein zentraler Vorteil des Modells. Hinzu kommt als weiterer Pluspunkt die Anbindung an die existierenden, erfahrenen Unternehmen. Diese würde auch das Risiko vermindern, dass der Wohnungsneubau durch organisatorische Überforderung leidet, weil die Senatsverwaltung vollständig mit dem Aufbau der AöR absorbiert ist. (…)


Nimmt das Land Berlin Kredite auf, um das Eigenkapital eines öffentlichen Unternehmens aufzustocken, steht der zusätzlichen Verschuldung ein finanzieller Vermögenswert in Form der Beteiligung gegenüber. Solche …

author: Amy Goodman
title: Eviction of 87-Year-Old Sparks Protest Encampment Over Spain’s Housing Crisis
content:
“We want to change the whole model of housing in Spain,” says Sabina Carrau of the Madrid Tenants’ Union.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

The eviction of 87-year-old María del Carmen Abascal Martín in Madrid, after an investment fund bought her apartment building and more than tripled her rent, has become a symbol of Spain’s rising cost of living and sparked nationwide protests against corporate greed and wealth inequality. Over 600 protesters are now camped outside Madrid’s regional government headquarters demanding new tenant protections.

“What we have is a lot of furious people, enraged people, that are demanding from the government and from the public institutions that they give us give us some sort of solution,” says Sabina Carrau, a spokesperson for the Madrid Tenants’ Union, which is supporting the “Maricarmen decree” named after Abascal, set to be debated by Spain’s government this week.

Housing in Spain, as in much of the world, “is really connected to tourism, really connected to having and buying a house to make a speculation,” says socialist parliamentarian Tesh Sidi, who is calling instead for the guaranteed right to housing and “the right to have an affordable life.” Sidi, the only Sahrawi member of the Spanish parliament, also comments on Spain’s colonial relationship to Western Sahara and the state of Sahrawi rights and self-determination.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: Today we’re broadcasting from London, tomorrow Copenhagen, and the rest of the week from Berlin. But we’re turning now to the Spanish capital of Madrid. A protest encampment over the cost of housing and housing instability has entered its third day as over 600 residents are now camped in front of the regional government headquarters at the Puerta del Sol plaza to demand new protections for tenants. Tens of thousands of people marched in the streets of Madrid Saturday. Demonstrations are also occurring across Spain.

Protests began Wednesday over the eviction of 87-year-old María del Carmen Abascal Martín, referred to just as Maricarmen, who was forcibly removed from her home of more than 70 years after an investment fund bought her apartment building and more than tripled, or more, her rent. Police broke down the door of her home and removed Maricarmen, who is 87 years old, on a stretcher as hundreds of supporters gathered outside. She later released a video message to supporters from her hospital bed.

MARÍA DEL CARMEN ABASCAL MARTÍN: [translated] I have not been able to defend my home, but I have fought so others can learn to fight for theirs. My home has been my life, and now I have to leave it behind. But that doesn’t mean I’m not going to keep fighting.

AMY GOODMAN: Protesters, camped in tents with sleeping bags in the Puerta del Sol plaza, say they won’t leave unless meaningful government action is taken.

SARA BARROS: [translated] What we are demanding is that the rental market be regulated, because rents are unaffordable and people simply cannot afford them. There are abuses taking place that can leave vulnerable people out on the street, such as Maricarmen, an 87-year-old woman with a disability who has no alternative housing after living in her home for 70 years.

LUCAS GARCIA: [translated] We are going to stay here until things change. There’s talk of a decree on Tuesday, and we will remain here until measures that we consider sufficient are adopted.

JORGE OTXOA: [translated] We are protesting so that we could claim and so the government listens to us, listens to a society that is tired of speculation, tired of corruption and tired of a system that sidelines the vast majority of the population. This is why we are here.

title: Kocaağa: Debt brake and social cuts deepened Germany’s crisis
content:
Muhlis Kocaağa, a member of Bremen's state parliament for Die Linke (The Left), discussed the reasons behind the rise of the far right in Germany, particularly in the eastern states, and Die Linke's role in opposing this trend.


Kocaağa said shrinking state budgets, the debt brake (Schuldenbremse) and cuts to social services had disrupted social stability. He also highlighted shortcomings in infrastructure and public services related to migration policies.


He said Germany was facing global geopolitical crises, rising energy costs, challenges arising from industrial transformation and a deepening housing crisis. Kocaağa stressed the urgent need to develop public and social policies to address these problems.


There has recently been a significant rise in the far right in Germany, particularly in eastern and North-Eastern Germany. How do you interpret this situation? Do you think the state is, in a sense, paving the way for it?


I assume you are referring to the state elections and the political situation in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, one of Germany's coastal states. There are two main reasons for this situation. My view differs somewhat from that of other politicians, and I have expressed it in political discussions as well.


The rise of the far right is generally attributed to the current government's social policies, particularly its tendency to restrict pensions, healthcare and social benefits. That certainly has an impact, but it is not the main determining factor. In my view, the fundamental reason is the existence of a deep-rooted, widespread right-wing tendency in Germany. Sometimes this tendency remains hidden, while at other times it emerges when the opportunity arises.


It reveals its true face whenever an opportunity for protest presents itself. This right-wing tendency has always existed in Germany, but it was less visible because the conditions were not favourable. Some attribute the current situation solely to opposition to government policies or to protest voters. Although protest voters certainly exist, we must not overlook the influence of the widespread right-wing tendency in Germany. Their existence does not change that underlying reality.


Some figures on the left, including those who were previously part of Die Linke but later formed the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW), have suggested that they could break the firewall (Brandmauer) against Alternative for Germany (AfD) and form a government with it. How do you assess this position?


It is not always easy to predict how people's character will develop in politics. Even when these figures were part of Die Linke, they consistently adopted problematic positions in our discussions and were among those responsible for creating internal disputes within the party.


I consider their suggestion that they could break the firewall or cooperate with the AfD extremely dangerous for two reasons.


The first is their willingness to sacrifice everything for political power. It reflects an attitude of: "As long as I am in power, it doesn't matter what I have to sacrifice."


The second is their attempt to establish an opportunistic position for themselves in those regions. Ultimately, both approaches have the potential to harm society.


There has also been a noticeable increase in support for the left, particularly in Berlin. Die Linke lost votes in the early 2020s but has since seen its support rise. How do you explain this momentum?


The first reason is that the internal disputes and divisions within the party leadership have come to an end. The party's unity and solidarity have resonated positively with voters.


The second reason is that living conditions in Germany are becoming increasingly difficult. Die Linke is one of the parties offering the most concrete and consistent policies to make people's lives easier.


There is also a third factor we should not overlook: the rise of the right naturally strengthens its opposite. There is a significant group of voters who consciously support Die Linke in order to prevent the AfD from gaining votes.


Turning to budgetary constraints at state and municipal level, what is the situation regarding budget pressures, cuts to social services and infrastructure investment, particularly in cities such as Bremen and Bremerhaven?

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Quebec Liberal Sandrine Rioux prioritizes health care, housing, cost of living
content:
Nunatsiaq News reached out to each candidate running in the Ungava riding ahead of Quebec’s Oct. 5 provincial election. Here’s what Quebec Liberal Party candidate Sandrine Rioux had to share with us.


Quebec Liberal Party candidate Sandrine Rioux said the reason she decided to run for office is simple: she wants to help people.


“My main goal is to help people, to be there, to be present, and to write good legislation at the National Assembly of Quebec,” said Rioux, speaking to Nunatsiaq News Tuesday from Chibougimou, where she was born and raised.


She’s among five candidates running in Ungava, the largest riding in the province geographically.


Her main priorities are improving access to health care, constructing more homes, addressing the cost of living and ensuring profits generated from resource development benefit communities.


Her party has a goal of building 100,000 homes per year in Quebec, she said, and wants to implement deadlines for housing authorities to encourage quicker development.


Each community, no matter how remote, should have a baseline 24-7 access to front-line health care services like doctors, nurses and pharmacists, she said. Telemedicine can fill gaps when specialists aren’t available.


At least five per cent of Quebec’s health budget should be dedicated to prevention, she said, and if elected, she wants to reduce Nunavik’s reliance on fly-in-fly-out health-care professionals.


Rioux has been involved with the Liberal party since 2019 and was president of its Ungava association.


She has a degree in business technology management from Université de Sherbrooke and a professional background in business analysis and marketing.


But she always held an interest in politics, she said, working for Élections Québec during the 2018 provincial election as an administrative assistant. It was one of her first jobs out of university and one that allowed her to visit each of Nunavik’s villages.


So far during the campaign, Rioux has visited Chapais, Chisasibi, Oujé-Bougoumou, Matagami, Mistissini, Radison, Waskaganish and Waswanipi. Travelling to Nunavik isn’t in the budget, but she said Kuujjuaq is first on her list if she gets elected.


“I really genuinely hope, if the people trust me, and invest in me, to be able to represent them at the National Assembly,” she said. “I want to make sure the lines of communication are always open.”

title: Mari Carmen, barınma hakkı için mücadeleye çağırıyor
content:
İspanya'da barınma hakkı eylemleri cumartesi günü de başkent Madrid'de devam etti. (Fotoğraf: AA)

2021 yılından bu yana İspanya ekonomisi, Avro Bölgesi ortalamasının üzerinde bir büyüme kaydederek, Almanya, Fransa veya İtalya gibi geleneksel olarak daha güçlü diğer Avrupa ekonomilerinin büyüme oranlarının iki, hatta üç kat üstüne çıkıyor. 2026 yılı için OECD, İspanya’nın GSYİH’sinde yüzde 2.6’lık bir büyüme öngörürken, Avro Bölgesi için ise yüzde 0.7 ile yüzde 1 arasında bir büyüme tahmin ediliyor. Diğer Avrupa ülkeleriyle karşılaştırıldığında düşük enerji fiyatları, turizmin gücü ve dünyanın en yaşlanan ülkelerinden biri olmasına rağmen göçten kaynaklanan bol işgücü ile yabancı sermaye girişi, bu büyümenin belirleyici faktörleri. İspanya’da yapısal bir sorun olan işsizlik oranı bile 2020’deki yüzde 16 seviyesinden bugün yüzde 9.87’ye gerilemiş durumda. Örneğin, 2025 yılında 600 binden fazla yeni istihdam yaratıldı.

Ancak bu makroekonomik rakamların mükemmelliğine rağmen, gerçekte kârlar şirketlerin cebinde kalıyor ve işçilere ulaşmıyor. Ay sonuna zorlukla gelen ve yoksulluk ve/veya sosyal dışlanma riskiyle karşı karşıya kalan insanların sayısı giderek artıyor. İspanya’nın 50 milyonluk nüfusunun 12.5 milyonu bu durumda. Bu rakam AB ortalamasının 4.8 puan üzerinde ve 4.1 milyon kişi aşırı yoksulluk içinde. Özellikle endişe verici olan ise 2.6 milyon çocuk ve ergen genci (yüzde 33.8) etkileyen çocuk yoksulluğu. Bu oran, Bulgaristan ve Romanya ile birlikte Avrupa Birliği’ndeki en yüksek oran.

“Zengin” ve ekonomisi gelişen bir ülkede bu düzeyde yoksulluk nasıl mümkün olabilir? Bunun iki önemli nedeni var. Birincisi, iş güvencesizliği. İstihdam edilen kişi sayısındaki artışa rağmen iş güvencesizliği ve düşük ücretlerin, birçok insanı işsiz kalma riskiyle karşı karşıya bırakması. Asgari ücretteki büyük artışa (2018’de aylık 736 avrodan 2026’da 1221 avroya çıkarıldı) rağmen enflasyon, maaş artışlarından daha hızlı artıyor.

Nüfusun bir kesiminin yoksullaşmasına katkıda bulunan bir diğer belirleyici faktör, konut ve kira fiyatlarındaki artışlar. İspanya’da barınma anayasal bir hak olmasına rağmen, gerçekte konutlar artık bir hak olmaktan çıkıp bir yatırım ve spekülasyon konusu haline gelmiş durumda. Konut fiyatları son on yılda yüzde 35, sadece son bir yılda ise yüzde 12.5 oranında arttı.

Ortalama bir konut satın almak, ortalama bir maaşın tamamının 8 ya da 9 yıl biriktirilmesini gerektiriyor. Bazı büyük şehirlerde veya turistik yerlerde bu süre çok daha uzun. İspanya geleneksel olarak ev sahipliği kültürü olan bir ülke, ancak fiyatların artması nedeniyle nüfusun çoğunluğu için ev satın almak imkansız hale geldi ve kiralık konut talebi arttı. Bununla birlikte, İspanya’da kiralık konutların emekçilere maliyeti 10 yılda yüzde 94 artmış durumda. Bu artışın yüzde 10’u sadece son bir yılda gerçekleşti, ancak bölgeler arasında önemli farklılıklar bulunuyor.

Sonuçlar korkunç. Gençler ortalama olarak 30 yaşına kadar bağımsız yaşayamıyor ve bu, Avrupa ortalamasından dört yıl daha geç bir yaş. Birçok aile gelirlerinin yarısından fazlasını kiraya harcamak zorunda; diğer pek çok kişi, hatta aileler bile, bir evi paylaşmak zorunda kalıyor. Birkaç yıl önce bir daire kiralamaya yetecek fiyatlarla bugün bir evin içindeki tek bir oda kiralanabiliyor ve tür kiralamalar da artmış durumda. Madrid gibi yerlerde bir dairedeki odanın kirası 800 avroya kadar çıkıyor. Balear Adaları gibi turistik yerlerde pek çok kişi, bir çatı altında uyuyabilmenin tek yolu olarak karavan satın almayı tercih ediyor.

Bu durum özellikle göçmenler için ciddi bir sorun, zira bu kadar yüksek fiyatları karşılama zorluğuna ek olarak, maruz kaldıkları ayrımcılık da kiralık konutlara erişimlerini zorlaştırıyor. Aynı durum, tek ebeveynli aileler, güvencesiz işlerde çalışanlar ya da işsiz kalanlar için de geçerli.

2020 yılından bu yana İspanya’da 150 binden fazla evden çıkarma vakası yaşandı. Bu rakam, 2014’teki 68 binden 2025’te 24 bin 500’e kadar düşmüş olsa da, hâlâ dayanılmaz derecede yüksek. Sadece bu yılın ilk çeyreğinde 4 bin 5 tahliye gerçekleşti. Bu da günde ortalama 44, yani her yarım saatte bir tahliye anlamına geliyor. Evini kaybetmenin yarattığı dramaya ek olarak, birçok durumda tahliye edilen kişilere sokakta kalmak ya da sadaka ile geçinmekten başka bir alternatif sunulmuyor.

Ve bu, 8 yıldır sol koalisyonun yönettiği bir ülkede yaşanıyor. Hükümetin bir Konut Bakanlığı kurduğu ve sorunu çözmeye yönelik bir Konut Yasası’nın kabul edildiği doğrudur. Ancak …

author: Unknown
title: Bir hayat için kaç kişiyiz?
content:
Türkiye’de engelli kişilerin şüpheli ölümlerine, işkence ve eziyet iddialarına ilişkin takip ettiğimiz dosyalarda bazen on, bazen on beş kişiyiz.


Etrafımıza baktığımızda birbirini iyi tanıyan engelli hakları savunucularını ve kan ağlayan aileleri görüyoruz. Madrid’de yetmiş yıldır yaşadığı evden çıkarılan Maricarmen’in hikayesini okurken aklıma bizim bu halimiz geldi…


Maricarmen Abascal, 87 yaşında, engelli bir kadın. Madrid’in Retiro semtinde, gençliğinden beri yaşadığı evden 23 Eylül 2026’da sedyeyle çıkarıldı. Kapıda ve binanın içinde bekleyenler tahliyeyi durdurmaya çalıştı; polis onları püskürttü.


Maricarmen ambulansla hastaneye götürülürken, evinin önünde onun yalnız olmadığını söyleyen insanlar vardı. O gün tahliyeyi engelleyemediler. Ama hikaye, ambulansın sokağın köşesinden dönmesiyle bitmedi.


Aynı gün Madrid’de binlerce kişi sokağa çıktı. Euronews’un haberine göre, başkentteki gösteriye on binden fazla kişi katıldı. Protestolar başka kentlere yayıldı. İnsanlar “Hepimiz Maricarmen’iz” diyordu. Kiracılar örgütlerinin sonraki çağrısı da tek bir kişinin adını çoğaltıyordu: “Bütün Maricarmenler için.” Yaşlı ve engelli kadının evinden çıkarılması, birbirini tanımayan insanların ortak meselesi haline gelmişti.

 


Maricarmen’in yanında duran herkes onun komşusu değildi. İspanya’da sokağa dökülen binlerin aynı yaşta olmaları, aynı engelliliği yaşamaları, aynı şirketle karşı karşıya bulunmaları gerekmedi. Halk, bir kişinin başına gelenle kendi hayatları arasında bağ kurabildi. O bağın kurulabildiği yerde, bir tahliye dosyası yalnızca kiracıyla ev sahibi arasındaki uyuşmazlık olarak kalmadı; mülkiyetin, barınmanın ve kamu gücünün nasıl ilişkilendiği de tartışmaya açıldı.


Üstelik bu hikayede sermaye, adı konulamayan soyut bir güç değil. Evin sahibi Urbagestión, Urbagesa ticari adıyla gayrimenkul yatırımları alanında faaliyet gösteriyor. Şirket kendisini bir yatırım fonu değil, “

küçük bir işletme

” olarak tanımlıyor. İnsanları evinden eden küçük bir işletme…


Madrid’deki Kiracılar Sendikasının aktardığına göre, Maricarmen’e sunulan seçenekler arasında, evinden otuz kilometre uzakta, aylık 1.200 avro isteyen bir bakım kurumu da vardı. Belediye “yardım” sunduğunu, sendika ise bu seçeneğin onun gelirini ve yaşadığı çevreyle bağlarını gözetmediğini söylüyordu.


Bir insanın başını sokabileceği başka bir yer bulmakla, hayatını sürdürebilmesini sağlamak arasındaki fark burada beliriyor. Alıştığı çevre, ilişkileri, gündelik hayatını nasıl yaşayacağına dair tercihleri basit bir taşınma işleminin ayrıntıları değil. 


Madrid’deki dayanışmanın bir başka boyutu da sosyal hizmet çalışanlarının bu itirazıydı.

Samur Social

 işçi komitesi, tahliyelere katılmayı reddeden bir metni çalışanlara iletti. Sosyal hizmet çalışanları, mesleki değerlendirmelerinin dikkate alınmadığını; bazen tahliye edilen kişiye sunabilecekleri hiçbir barınma seçeneği olmadan görevlendirildiklerini anlattı. 


Aynı sosyal hizmet çalışanları, özel bir şirket bünyesinde istihdam edildikleri için bu tutumun kendileri bakımından taşıdığı risklerden de söz ediyordu. İşçi komitesinin anlatımına göre hizmeti yürüten Grupo 5, bir yatırım fonu tarafından satın alınmıştı. Böylece konutun yatırım konusu olması ve bakım emeği yarıştırıldı. Yani, bir yanda evinden çıkarılan kişinin desteğe ihtiyacı, diğer yanda o desteği vermekle görevli çalışanın iş güvencesi vardı. Tam da bu durum, bizim için çok tanıdık…


Türkiye’de takip ettiğimiz dosyalarda hissettiğimiz yalnızlığı bu bağlamda düşünüyorum. Şüpheli bir ölümün aydınlatılmasını, işkence ve eziyet iddialarının araştırılmasını isterken yalnızca delillerle uğraşmıyoruz. O hayatın neden herkesinki kadar önemli olduğunu yeniden anlatmak zorunda kalmanın ağırlığını da taşıyoruz. Aynı yüzler, birbirini tanıyan aynı insanlar, yakınlarının başına ne geldiğini öğrenmek için adliyelere gidip gelen aileler…


Engelli bir kişinin işkence görmesi, şüpheli koşullar altında hayatını kaybetmesi, yalnızca engellilik alanında çalışanların ilgileneceği bir konu olabilir mi?


Bir bakım kurumundaki şüpheli ölüm, sadece o kurumda yakını bulunanların sorunu olarak kalabilir mi? Dosyanın teknik yönleri uzmanlık gerektirebilir; fakat bir insanın şiddetten korunmasını, söyleyeceği sözünün dinlenmesini ve ölümünün aydınlatılmasını istemek uzmanlığa bağlı değil. Orada bulunmak için benzer bir hayatı yaşamak gerekmiyor…

title: Fransa'daki lise öğrencilerinin eylemleri Belçika'ya sıçradı
content:
Belçika basınında yer alan haberlere göre, Fransa'da yaklaşık bir haftadır devam eden lise protestoları Belçika'ya sıçradı.

Liege'deki çeşitli ortaöğretim kurumlarında öğrenciler sabah saatlerinde derslerin başlamasını engelleyen eylemler yaptı.

Eylemlerden "Athenee de Fragnee", "Athenee Royal de Montegnee", "Institut Maria Goretti", "College Saint-Barthelemy", "Saint-Laurent", "Saint-Sepulcre" ve "Institut Marie-Therese"in de aralarında bulunduğu çok sayıda okul etkilendi.

Liege'nin Hors-Chateau bölgesindeki Institut Marie-Therese önünde durum zaman zaman gerginleşti, okulun önünde ateş yakıldı ve bölgeye çok sayıda polis sevk edildi.

Polis, bazı okulların önünde havai fişek türü patlayıcılar, yumurta, elma ve bariyerlerin fırlatıldığını ve çeşitli noktalarda hasar meydana geldiğini iddia etti.

Esneux, Vise, Angleur ve Soumagne beldelerindeki bazı okullarda da eylemler görüldü. Vise, Angleur ve Soumagne'da öğrenciler kısa süre sonra okullara dönerken, diğer bazı kurumlarda ise öğrenciler ve öğretmenlerin okula girişini engellemek amacıyla gözcü hatları oluşturuldu.

Polis ve yerel kaynaklar, eylemlerin öğretmenler ya da sendikalar tarafından değil, öğrenciler tarafından başlatılan spontane bir hareket olduğunu aktardı.

Öğrenciler, sınıflardaki öğrenci sayısının azaltılmasını, yeterli sayıda öğretmen görevlendirilmesini, öğrenci ve velilerin karar süreçlerinde daha fazla dinlenmesini ve eğitimin herkes için erişilebilir olmasını talep ediyor.

Öğrenciler ayrıca eğitim alanında alınacak kararların geleceklerini olumsuz etkilememesi gerektiğini savunuyor.

Olaylara ilişkin soruşturma açılırken, polis Liege kentinde 6 kişinin gözaltına alındığını açıkladı.

Liege'de yetkililer, yarın eğitime ara verildiğini duyurdu.

Valonya-Brüksel Federasyonu hükümeti Eğitim Bakanı Valerie Glatigny, öğrencilerin "bir araç olarak kullanıldığı" iddiasında bulunarak, eğitimde hiçbir önlemin onlara sağlanan desteği azaltmadığını savundu.

Glatigny, herkesin kararlara itiraz etme hakkı olduğunu ancak işin şiddete dönüşmemesi gerektiğini öne sürerek"Öğrencilerin sınıfa girmesini engellemek, polislere cisim atmak, okul dışından gelen kişilerin baskısı altında tahribat yapmak kabul edilebilir değildir" ifadesini kullandı.

Fransa'da ilk olarak Paris ve çevresinde yoğunlaşan öğrenci eylemleri, daha sonra ülkenin diğer bölgelerine yayıldı.

29 Eylül'de yüzlerce lise, protesto ve blokajlardan etkilenirken, bazı kentlerde öğrencilerle güvenlik güçleri arasında gerginlik yaşandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Protests for Kurdish-language education continue in Rojava
content:
The protests against restrictions on Kurdish-language education in Rojava, which have been continuing for weeks, are ongoing. In Girkê Legê and Rimêlan, students boycotted classes. In Qamişlo, Til Temir, and Dirbêsiyê, students, teachers, and education workers also protested for the right to mother-tongue education.


The protests are directed against a decision by the Education Ministry of the Islamist transitional government in Damascus to limit Kurdish in schools to three hours of instruction per week. Protesters are demanding the continuation of Kurdish-language education and constitutional recognition of Kurdish in Syria.


Trilingual statement in Qamişlo


In Qamişlo, students and staff from the Şehîd Şervan, Canşêr, Dilxwaz, Heqî, and Omîd schools gathered in front of Canşêr School. A joint statement was read out in Kurdish, Arabic, and English. Student Mêrva Emo read the Kurdish version, teacher Wasil Esaed the Arabic version, and teacher Rojîn Mihemed Mûsa the English version.


In the statement, the students referred to the decades-long repression of the Kurdish population and the achievements of the Rojava Revolution. They described the current decisions as a continuation of a policy aimed at erasing Kurdish history and identity. They said that reducing Kurdish-language instruction was a first step in this direction.


At the same time, the students emphasized that their protest was not directed against other languages. Their aim, they said, was to protect their own language. They called on the relevant authorities to make their demands public and work toward the constitutional recognition of Kurdish in Syria. “Education in the Kurdish language is our natural right,” student Hêlîn Iniz said. She called for all teaching materials to be made fully available in Kurdish.


Protests in Til Temir and Dirbêsiyê


Protests against the restriction of Kurdish-language education to three hours per week were also held in and around Til Temir. At Al-Mansaf School in the northern countryside, teachers and students demanded that the Kurdish population’s right to mother-tongue education be guaranteed. They called for Kurdish to be taught on an academic basis in educational institutions, while also protecting Kurdish literature and cultural heritage.


In the town of al-Qaracina, Kongra Star supported the demands with a separate statement. Speaking in front of the women’s organization’s center, board member Îbtîsam El Şahîn emphasized the importance of language for identity, culture, and social heritage. Kurdish children, she said, must have the right to receive their education in their mother tongue.


In Dirbêsiyê, students from Şehîd Roza Cûdî School joined the protests. In a statement read out by Leyla Îsmaîl, they reaffirmed their right to mother-tongue education and called for the protection of the Kurdish language.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Berlin 4" Lawyer on Pro-Palestine Protest Crackdown & Germany's Unconditional Support for Israel
content:
Democracy Now!

's Amy Goodman is in Berlin, Germany, this week, where the crackdown on pro-Palestine speech is shaped by the German policy of

Staatsräson

, or “reason of state.” The concept refers to Germany's commitment to the existence of the Israeli state in light of the Holocaust. Since the start of Israel’s war on Gaza in 2023,

Staatsräson

 has manifested itself as German military aid to Israel and heavy policing of Palestine activism inside Germany.


“Germany’s guilt regarding the Holocaust” has been “abused to justify the support of the genocidal war of Israel against the population in Gaza,” says Berlin-based lawyer Alexander Gorski, who recently represented the “Berlin Four,” three European Union citizens and one United States citizen whom Germany attempted to deport for participating in pro-Palestine campus protest. Gorski, who also represented the British Palestinian surgeon Ghassan Abu-Sittah and the leftist Greek economist Yanis Varoufakis when they were denied entry into Germany ahead of a pro-Palestine conference in Berlin, discusses Germany’s use of immigration law to crack down on anti-Zionist activism, which he says the state wholly conflates with antisemitism.


“Germany has a historic responsibility for challenging antisemitism, but at the same time, what we should learn — especially as Germans — from the Holocaust, that 'never again' means never again for anyone,” says Gorski.

title: Stop Pesticides - Mobilisation internationale le 3 octobre 2026 à Saint‑Pierre‑la‑Garenne (Eure)
content:
Les pesticides tuent, de plus en plus et depuis bien trop longtemps

 

! Le 3 octobre 2026, nous, paysan·nes, travailleurs et travailleuses agricoles, personnes malades et habitant·es de territoires contaminés convergeront vers le site de Syngenta à Saint-Pierre-la-Garenne, dans l'Eure. Nous y appelons à une manifestation massive pour dénoncer les ravages de l'industrie agrochimique et obtenir la mise à l'arrêt de ce site majeur, emblématique de l'impunité dont bénéficient les multinationales qui nous empoisonnent. Simultanément, des mobilisations auront lieux sur plusieurs autres continents pour dire «

 

Pesticides, Syngenta, ni ici ni ailleurs

 

!

 

»


Appel des

Soulèvements de la Terre


Les pesticides tuent, de plus en plus et depuis bien trop longtemps, en premier lieu les travailleurs et travailleuses agricoles. Les quelques multinationales qui en tirent profit intoxiquent toujours plus les terres et les populations. Depuis des années, nous accumulons pourtant les preuves, les alertes et les combats : dossiers de reconnaissance de maladies professionnelles, recours juridiques, enquêtes de terrain, rassemblements devant des points de captage d'eau pollués, manifestations, accompagnement des personnes contaminées... Pourtant, nous ne sommes toujours pas entendu.es. Alors que les scandales sanitaires à ce sujet se multiplient, les pouvoirs publics et les instances européennes continuent de favoriser un modèle agricole soumis aux pesticides et de légiférer en ce sens. Ils installent ainsi une insécurité chimique sur la population entière, C'est pourquoi nous avons engagé une campagne d'actions pour désarmer les infrastructures de production des pesticides sur nos territoires et promouvoir une autre agriculture.


Pourquoi arrêter ce site

 

?

Un site qui contamine durablement


Le site de Saint-Pierre-la-Garenne illustre concrètement les dégâts de ce système. Depuis des décennies, Syngenta y produit de nombreux pesticides dangereux. Les nappes phréatiques voisines sont fortement polluées, et des arrêtés préfectoraux interdisent régulièrement aux riverain.es d'utiliser l'eau de leurs puits pour arroser leurs cultures. Dans les environs, les pathologies, notamment certains cancers, sont en constante augmentation. Le territoire lui-même en subit les conséquences durables.


La santé des salarié.es menacée


Cette pollution s'accompagne de conditions de travail indignes. Sur les 150 salarié·es du site, plus de la moitié sont en procès avec leur employeur au sujet des primes de douche, que l'entreprise refuse de verser. Or le Code du travail impose à l'employeur de mettre à disposition des douches et des installations sanitaires adaptées dans les établissements où sont réalisés certains travaux insalubres et salissants. Ces obligations prennent un sens particulier lorsque les travailleur·euses manipulent chaque jour des substances chimiques toxiques et que des maladies professionnelles associées sont reconnues sur le site.


Un système derrière ce site

Interdits ici, les produits sont vendus ailleurs


L'usine s'inscrit aussi dans une économie d'exportation des poisons. Jusqu'en 2023, elle produisait encore des substances actives de pesticides interdites en Europe, que ce soit pour leur usage agricole, leur production, leur stockage ou leur circulation. Ces produits étaient ensuite envoyés vers d'autres continents, avec des conséquences sociales et environnementales dramatiques. Des pratiques comparables se poursuivent dans d'autres sites industriels proches, notamment chez

BASF

 à Saint-Aubin-lès-Elbeuf. Ce commerce des toxiques repose sur une logique de double standard et de colonialisme chimique que nous refusons : ce qui est interdit ici ne doit pas être imposé ailleurs.


À moins de deux kilomètres se trouve également le site de Nufarm, autre acteur majeur de l'agrochimie, qui produit notamment de l'imidaclopride, du glyphosate ou de la butraline. Jusqu'en 2025 au moins, l'entreprise a exporté en Afrique de l'Ouest et sans accord des pays importateurs d'importants volumes de prochloraz, un fongicide retiré du marché français en 2021 en raison de ses effets sur les cancers hépatiques et sur l'environnement. Malgré ces faits, aucune sanction n'a été prise par les services de l'État.


La captation des semences


Le site de Saint-Pierre-la-Garenne abrite notamment le Centre d'Étude Technique d'Application des Produits de Protection des Semences (

CETAPPS

), où d'importants volumes de semences …

title: Marokkos Jugend protestiert: „Wir haben Fußballstadien, wo bleiben die Spitäler?“
content:
Dossier


„

In Marokko geht die Gen Z für bessere Bildungschancen und gegen Korruption auf die Straße. Der Ärger über die Ausgaben für die Fußball-WM 2030 ist groß und der Zeitpunkt der Proteste brisant. Seit Tagen protestieren junge Menschen in mehreren marokkanischen Städten gegen das marode Bildungs- und Gesundheitswesen. Es sind die größten Anti-Regierungs-Proteste in Marokko seit Jahren. Die Demonstranten, die größtenteils der Generation Z angehören, prangern erstmals lautstark die aus ihrer Sicht falschen Prioritäten der Regierung an. (…) In Marokko empören sich die Protestierenden nicht nur über die Perspektivlosigkeit der Jugend, sondern auch über die hohe Jugendarbeitslosigkeit: Knapp jeder Dritte ist ohne Arbeit. Richtig zu brodeln begann es am vergangenen Wochenende, dem letzten im September, nachdem in diesem Monat allein acht Frauen bei der Geburt ihrer Kinder in einem öffentlichen Krankenhaus in der Küstenstadt Agadir gestorben waren

…“

Artikel vom 1. Oktober 2025 in derstandard.de

 

, siehe weitere Informationen:


Parlamentswahl in Marokko: Warum die Jugend eher auswandern als wählen will…


Parlamentswahl in Marokko: Ein Land, zwei Welten


„

Für die Fußball-WM 2030 macht sich Marokko schick, doch die Menschen ächzen unter der Wirtschaftskrise. Das Vertrauen in die Politik geht gegen null. (…)


Die marokkanische Hauptstadt erholt sich von einer Touristensaison, die von nicht enden wollenden Hitzewellen, Starkregen und dem Besucheransturm des Afrika-Cups geprägt war. Eine Art Generalprobe für die Fußball-WM 2030, die in Spanien, Portugal und Marokko stattfinden soll. Ein historisches Projekt, das die 32-Millionen Einwohner-Nation zusammenschweißen soll und für das überall im Land gebaut, erneuert und investiert wird. Doch weder die WM, die Parlamentswahlen noch der Klimawandel erregen derzeit die Gemüter. Sobald es um die explodierten Kosten für Lebensmittel und das Leben überhaupt geht, kippt die Stimmung. (…) Doch die Flugblätter der Parteien lassen viele der von den mobilen Werbeteams Angesprochenen offenbar gleich wieder fallen. Überall, in Rabat, Casablanca oder Tange, sammeln Reinigungsteams der Stadtverwaltung auf Papier gedruckte Parolen auf. «Zukunft», «Hoffnung» und «Fortschritt» heißt es darauf, viele Marokkaner lässt dies kalt.


Auch vor dem Gerichtsgebäude von Ain Sebaa ist es normalerweise still. Hier im Norden von Casablanca warten Familien von Angeklagten auf den Beginn der Prozesse gegen Söhne oder Ehemänner. Während der Straßenproteste der Gen Z, der unter Dreißigjährigen, im letzten Herbst waren hunderte Demonstranten verhaftet worden. Viele warten immer noch auf die Verkündung eines Urteils, andere noch immer auf die Anklageschrift. Zum wiederholten Mal hat sich eine kleine Gruppe von Demonstranten im Norden der Wirtschaftsmetropole unter die Eltern im Park vor dem Gericht gemischt.


«Freiheit für Yassir», «Freiheit für alle Inhaftierten», skandieren sie. Die Umstehenden ignorieren den Protest weitgehend, auch aus Furcht vor den Beamten in Zivil, die immer dort auftauchen, wo sich Menschenmengen treffen. Der populäre Graffiti-Künstler Yassir Mounbir hat angeblich mit einem seiner Bilder den König beleidigt und wartet im Gefängnis auf sein Verfahren.


Für seine regierungskritischen Tags hat sich der 22-jährige Künstler aus Casablanca bei den Anhängern der Gen Z-212 Bewegung einen Namen gemacht. Schon vor dem Sturm der Jugend auf Ceuta am 31. Juli gingen die Behörden gegen die Rapperszene vor. Mit ihren Texten könnten sie wohl über Nacht eine neue Protestbewegung anzetteln. Das ist die Lehre aus dem Sturm der 80.000 auf die spanische Enklave.


Der marokkanische Staat reagiert auf die Gen Z-Bewegung und Ceuta in gewohnter Manier mit der Verhaftung der Anführer. Die Anklageschrift gegen Youssir Mounbir kennt wohl nicht einmal sein Rechtsanwalt. Wegen eines Streiks der Anwälte finden derzeit nur wenige Verfahren statt, auch die Gerichte haben ihre Arbeit teilweise eingestellt.


«Der Streik der Anwälte für einen besseren legalen Status kommt den Machthabern vor den Wahlen doch gelegen», sagt ein Freund von Mounbir. Es verstehe sich von selbst, dass sein Name nicht gedruckt werden könne, sagt er. Und schaut in der Menge nach unerwünschten Beobachtern des Protests. «Keiner meiner Freunde wählt», sagt der 24-jährige Student. «Wir, die junge Generation, sind Hauptthema im Wahlkampf, aber keine Partei bietet irgendetwas Konkretes an. Dabei haben wir bereits im letzten Herbst doch …

author: LAMA
title: Ireland: Pre-Budget Protest
content:
The Irish Left held a protest recently in anticipation of the upcoming budget. The article discusses the overall situation in Ireland and explores the nature of the protest.

Donald Trump visited Ireland recently. It was a two-day visit so he could play golf. The estimated cost to the Irish taxpayer is reported to be in excess of 20 million Euros (Clare Echo, 6/8/26). Not surprisingly, the visit caused controversy and resulted in mass protests. The latter is a good thing. What is strange, however, was the lack of enthusiasm for a protest held just one week later in Dublin.

A protest was called for September 19 th in Parnell Square, Central Dublin, as a pre-Budget demonstration. The budget is due to be announced on October 6 th by Finance Minister Simon Harris on behalf of the right-wing coalition of Fianna Fail and Fine Gael. The government is sitting on a surplus, but indications are they intend to do little or nothing to help those in need of support.

There are a number of basic issues that highlight a social crisis in the 26 Counties. A big one is housing. Social housing is no longer being built people are waiting years on lists and private landlords are allowed to get away with exorbitant rents. It is not unusual for people to pay 40 or 50% of their income on rent. That’s if you can actually find somewhere in the first place. Many young people are living in the bedrooms they grew up in, since availability is as much a problem as affordability. Outright homelessness is on the rise too. The Department of Housing figures show that those in emergency housing increased 9.1% over the year to July 2026 (RTE 28/8/26). Among those was a 16% increase in families (Focus Ireland 28/8/26).

The problem does not only occur on a national level. The grassroots housing campaign group Community Action Tenants’ Union (CATU) is battling against Dublin City Council. Council executives have increased rents for tenants in public housing, the excuse being that there isn’t money to keep public housing in reasonable condition, so it will have to come out of rent increases. The increase voted on in April offers no exemptions for pensioners, people on welfare, or disability recipients. For many of those groups dependent on fixed incomes, any increase will further diminish their quality of life.

Besides housing, another concern is basic resource infrastructure. Due to extremely hot weather conditions, a hosepipe ban was enforced between July and the middle of September in the Greater Dublin Area, and parts of Wexford, Wicklow, Meath, Kildare and south Tipperary.

Uisce Eireann (UE) is the state-owned company that was responsible for overseeing the ban. UE declared the prohibition “…for activities including watering gardens, washing private vehicles and leisure boats, filling domestic swimming or paddling pools, ornamental fountains and garden ponds except where such use is required for commercial purposes [emphasis added]”, (RTE, 22/7/26). In other words, business got a pass and the average person had to toe the line.

Although UE is a state company, it is in fact structured as a commercial semi-state company with share holders. The two shareholders are government ministers. It is clear from all this whose interests are seen to take priority. It is not the people at the bottom.

In addition, electricity prices are rising. Several suppliers have announced increases, with some already taking effect and others about to. For example, SSE Airtricity is increasing electricity rates by 9.4% from October 5 th , with the typical bill rising by about 8.9% or 172 Euros a year (The Irish Times, 4/9/26). Another is Pinergy, which imposed a 7.6% increase (RTE 14/8/26). The result is on a straight Euro-per-kWh measure, Ireland now has the highest electricity costs in the European Union (EU), at about 40% above the EU average! (ec.europa.eu). While the average person is clearly struggling to pay these increases, data centres and big tech companies (with the latter only paying 12.5% tax) pay wholesale rates for their water and electricity, while using a huge percentage of the national consumption. Its not too hard to see who the state favours.

Examples could be multiplied across various other aspects of the cost-of-living crisis. One such being a 15% increase in public transport, announced to take place from January (thejournal.ie 3/9/26).Many working people rely on buses and trains to commute to work, and such increases only add to the burden we face …

author: CMI Argentina
title: “Las protestas y las luchas en las que participaron Milton y Eneas no son terrorismo”
content:
La Coordinadora contra la Represión Policial e Institucional (CORREPI) y la Gremial de Abogados reclaman el cierre de la causa contra Milton Iván Tolomeo y Eneas Germán Gallo Salomone Croft, detenidos por haber participado de la masiva protesta ante el Congreso de la Nación contra la regresiva reforma laboral.


Compartimos el comunicado de CORREPI y la Gremial de Abogados:


LAS PROTESTAS Y LAS LUCHAS EN QUE PARTICIPARON MILTON Y ENEAS NO SON TERRORISMO LIBERTAD A MILTON Y ENEAS, CIERRE DE LA CAUSA.


El 11 de febrero de 2026 el Congreso Nacional perpetró un verdadero crimen al sancionar la llamada Ley de Reforma Laboral, que destruyó 200 años de derechos conquistados por las y los trabajadores de Argentina. Ese día hubo una masiva movilización en la Plaza de los Dos Congresos, con la participación de las centrales sindicales, infinidad de gremios y multitud de personas que manifestaron su repudio a lo que sucedía en el recinto.


Unos días después, varias personas que fueron “identificadas” a través de dudosos mecanismos de ciberpatrullaje y reconocimiento facial resultaron detenidas, acusadas de graves delitos por haber participado de la manifestación multitudinaria.


Desde mediados de febrero, dos trabajadores, Milton Iván Tolomeo y Eneas Germán Gallo Salomone Croft, están detenidos en la prisión federal de Marcos Paz. A la vez, Oscar Rubén “Homero” Aguirre y Néstor Gabriel Barrera fueron detenidos y excarcelados, pero siguen procesados en la misma causa.


Cuando Milton fue detenido, se lo incluyó, por orden del Ministerio de Seguridad Nacional, en el SIGGPLAR (Sistema Integral de Gestión para Personas Privadas de la Libertad de Alto Riesgo), destinado a terroristas de gran peligrosidad, lo que significó un aislamiento absoluto, sin posibilidad de comunicarse ni tener visitas de sus familiares ni de sus defensores, con apenas una o dos horas de recreo para poder salir de su celda, usar los baños, comer o salir al patio, vigilado en todo momento por personal no identificado del Servicio Penitenciario Federal enmascarado con balaclavas.


Logramos, al mes, sacarlo de ese infierno y lograr su pase a un pabellón común.


Se los acusa por los delitos de tenencia de material incendiario, atentado y resistencia a la autoridad e intimidación pública, Milton y Eneas como coutores y Homero y Néstor como partícipes.


Como si eso fuera poco, ya esa acusación prevé la pena de 5 a 15 años de prisión, el Fiscal Stornelli requirió el agregado del agravante previsto en el art. 41 quinquies del Código Penal, que establece la duplicación de penas cuando el hecho se comete “para aterrorizar a la población u obligar a autoridades públicas nacionales, gobiernos extranjeros o agentes internacionales a realizar un acto o abstenerse de hacerlo”.


Este artículo fue incorporado al Código Penal en 2011 (ley 26.734), como parte de la batería de “leyes antiterroristas” dictadas a partir de 2007 por presión del GAFI (Grupo de Acción Financiera Internacional) y otros organismos internacionales de control financiero, y fue ampliado aún más en 2024 con la ley 27.739. Es una circunstancia agravante transversal a todo el Código Penal, que automáticamente lleva al doble la escala penal prevista, sin respetar el criterio de proporcionalidad de la pena.


Tanto al momento de su sanción inicial durante la presidencia de Cristina Fernández, como ante su reforma en la actual gestión de Javier Milei, desde las organizaciones populares y sectores académicos advertimos que es una norma peligrosísima, plagada de vaguedades, con expresiones completamente abiertas a la interpretación, como “aterrorizar a la población”, cuya definición queda discrecionalmente en manos de jueces y fiscales que decidan descargar todo su poder punitivo apuntando más a presuntas intencionalidades subjetivas del autor que a las características concretas de una conducta específica.


Decíamos también que, aunque la misma norma indica que esa agravante no se debe aplicar cuando los hechos de que se trate tuvieran lugar “en ocasión del ejercicio de derechos humanos y/o sociales o de cualquier otro derecho constitucional”, como es el de resistir una medida legislativa que cercena derechos, la falta de precisión de las definiciones que permiten cualquier interpretación intencionada de jueces y fiscales obedientes al poder político habilitan la indiscriminada persecución de la protesta y su híper criminalización.


Desde el inicio de la gestión del gobierno de la Libertad Avanza …

title: Appel à se mobiliser et à manifester pour la libre circulation et contre les frontières et l'enfermement le 4 octobre à 14h place de la comédie à Montpellier.
content:
Adissiatz ! Nous sommes une interorga de collectifs et de personnes s'organisant contre les frontières et l'enfermement dans les pays d'oc, des Pyrénées aux Alpes en passant par la Méditerranée, à la croisée des états français, italien et espagnol. Nous vous invitons à nous rejoindre pour une manifestation le 4 octobre à Montpellier pour lutter contre le continuum colonial entre frontières, enfermement et fabrique de l'illégalité. Nous souhaitons la disparition des frontières et la libre circulation pour toustes ! RDV à 14h à la comédie !


Adissiatz ! Nous sommes une interorga de collectifs et de personnes s'organisant contre les frontières et l'enfermement dans les pays d'oc, des Pyrénées aux Alpes en passant par la Méditerranée, à la croisée des états français, italien et espagnol. Nous vous invitons à nous rejoindre pour une manifestation le 4 octobre à Montpellier pour lutter contre le continuum colonial entre frontières, enfermement et fabrique de l'illégalité. Nous souhaitons la disparition des frontières et la libre circulation pour toustes ! RDV à 14h à la comédie !


Depuis le hangar d'Arenc à Marseille dans les années 70, emprisonnant les algériens après leur révolution anti-coloniale, les lieux d'enfermement n'ont fait que se multiplier. CRA pour Centre de Rétention Administratif, ou une prison pour les personnes qui n'auraient pas les « bons papiers » (toulouseanticra.org). Au delà des CRA, nous militons contre toutes les entraves à la libre circulation des personnes. Frontières, prisons, hospitalisations forcées, assignations à résidence, expulsions, expropriations, accaparements de terres, ségrégation, colonisation sont des dispositifs injustes utilisant la violence pour déplacer, bloquer et enfermer les personnes contre leur volonté.


En 2023, l'état français a annoncé un doublement des places en CRA pour atteindre 3000 en 2027. A Béziers, 140 places sont prévues, à côté d'une prison de 1200 personnes (prévue pour 800) et d'un futur hopital psychiatrique, pour créer comme souvent un complexe carcéral et répressif, où transférer facilement les personnes à qui l'on vole leur liberté. Le terrain a été clôturé et mis sous vidéo-surveillance, après que nous l'ayons occupé lors de la mobilisation d'octobre 2025.


Les récentes lois européennes (Règlement retour, 2026) vont toujours plus loin dans la création de statuts de citoyenneté inférieurs. Par des entourloupes juridiques, les personnes arrivées dans l'UE sans visa ne sont pas considérees comme réellement sur le territoire, et n'ont donc pas les mêmes droits. Au delà des CRA, les personnes peuvent être enfermées dans des 'zones d'attente' jusqu'à 6 mois, puis expulsées dans des 'hubs de retour', prisons et camps construits hors de l'UE. En parallèle FRONTEX coordonne la création d'une force armée de fichage et de répression évoquant l'ICE états-unienne, et le nombre de frères et soeurs mort.es en mer et aux frontières augmente chaque jour.


Le harcèlement des personnes sans les « bons papiers » permet de réprimer et contrôler les corps minorisés, précarisant, enfermant et broyant les personnes, fabriquant par la peur et la violence une main d'oeuvre docile à bas coût pour enrichir les puissants.


La manifestation du 4 octobre est déclarée. le parcours : comédie - préfecture - arceaux... Nous vous invitons toustes à participer mais sans drapeaux d'organisations. Manifestons ensemble sous la bannière commune de la libre circulation, de la régularisation de tous les sans-papiers, de la disparition des frontières et contre les CRA !


Feu aux CRA, feu aux prisons, feu aux frontières ! Solidarité avec toutes les personnes ciblées par l'illégalité, et force à toustes celleux qui luttent à l'intérieur ! Rejoignez-nous le 4 octobre à 14h place de la Comédie à Montpellier pour résister ensemble à ce système raciste et colonial - et un jour peut-être y mettre fin.


Plus d'infos sur insta : anticra_mtp.


Contact : we_anti_CRA_3_4_octobre_2026@disroot.org.
