title: Bolu Belediyesi'ne yönelik zimmet soruşturması: Gözaltına alınan 11 kişiden 5'i tutuklandı
content:
Bolu Belediyesi bünyesindeki S.S. Köroğlu Yöresel Ürünler Üretim ve Pazarlama Kooperatifi yöneticileri ve kooperatif ile ticari ilişkisi bulunan firmalar hakkında ‘zimmet’ iddiasıyla Bolu Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı tarafından gözaltına alınan 11 kişiden 8'inin jandarmadaki işlemleri tamamlandı.

Sağlık kontrolünün ardından adliyeye sevk edilen edilenlerden kooperatifin yönetim kurulu başkanı Cevat Çatladı ile Bahadır Acar, Fatih Demiral, Uğur Şirin ve Bayram Turhan çıkarıldıkları hakimlikçe tutuklandı, Ö.Ö, Y.S. ve S.C.S'ye ise adli kontrol tedbirleri uygulandı.

Öte yandan soruşturma kapsamında daha önce adliyeye sevk edilen E.K, A.C.A. ve G.M. çıkarıldıkları nöbetçi hakimlikçe adli kontrol şartıyla serbest bırakılmıştı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish political prisoners denied medical care in Urmia
content:
Prison authorities are denying two Kurdish political prisoners, Hossein Osmani and Bahram Majidi-Far, access to adequate medical care at Urmia (Orumiyeh) Central Prison despite serious health problems.


The two men are held in the prison’s Ershad ward, which houses political prisoners and prisoners of conscience.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported that Osmani, 65, from Mahabad, is suffering from serious vision problems caused by a cataract in his left eye, and that prison officials have refused to transfer him to a medical facility outside the prison.


Osmani is serving the 13th year of a 30-year prison sentence.


Majidi-Far, from Urmia, has experienced severely low blood pressure in recent months.


Doctors at the prison infirmary have recommended that he be transferred to a medical facility outside the prison for examination by a cardiologist, but prison authorities have refused to approve the transfer.


Hossein Osmani’s case


Osmani was arrested on 23 February 2014 after being summoned to the Ministry of Intelligence’s office in Mahabad and was taken to the ministry’s detention facility in Urmia.


He spent 13 months in solitary confinement, during which he was denied family visits and allowed only two brief telephone calls with his family.


He was subjected to severe physical and psychological torture at the detention facility, and in 2014, he spent four months in Urmia’s Khomeini Hospital receiving treatment for injuries caused by torture.


In March 2015, Branch One of the Islamic Revolutionary Court in Mahabad, presided over by Judge Javadikia, sentenced Osmani and two other political prisoners, Diako Rasoulzadeh and Saber Sheikh-Abdollah, to public execution.


The three men, who were denied access to a lawyer, faced charges of “enmity against God” (moharebeh) through membership of the Komala Party of Iranian Kurdistan and “participation in the 2010 Mahabad bombing”.


Following their appeals, the Supreme Court quashed the sentences and returned the case to the same court for retrial.


In 2018, the court, then presided over by Judge Javad Gholami, sentenced Osmani to 30 years’ imprisonment and internal exile to Urmia Prison. The Supreme Court upheld the sentence.


The charges against Osmani were based on confessions that he said had been extracted through torture and coercion. During court hearings, he rejected the confessions recorded in his case file and said they had been obtained under torture, but his statements and defence were not examined.


On 23 September 2019, he was transferred to Urmia Central Prison after spending 11 months in Mahabad Prison.


Rasoulzadeh and Sheikh-Abdollah were executed on 13 July 2020.


Government officials and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) had made conflicting statements about those responsible for the 2010 Mahabad bombing.


On 18 May 2014, the Ministry of Intelligence announced that it had arrested three people as the “perpetrators of the bombing”. However, three years earlier, on 26 September 2010, the commander of the IRGC Ground Forces had announced that the “main and central figures” behind the bombing had been killed.


An informed source with close knowledge of the case previously told KHRN: “When these three Kurdish citizens were detained, Ministry of Intelligence interrogators first tortured them, then promised to help them and secure their release if they cooperated by accepting responsibility for the bombing. Otherwise, they would fabricate a case against them and have them sentenced to death.”


In September 2014, the Islamic Republic of Iran’s Press TV broadcast footage of the prisoners’ confessions, which the prisoners said had been obtained under pressure and torture.


Bahram Majidi-Far’s case


Majidi-Far, from the village of Razhan near Orumiyeh, was arrested by Ministry of Intelligence agents in July 2024.


After approximately two months of interrogation at the Ministry of Intelligence and IRGC Intelligence Organisation detention facilities in Orumiyeh, he was transferred to the city’s central prison.


Several months later, Branch One of the Islamic Revolutionary Court in Orumiyeh, presided over by Judge Najafzadeh, sentenced him to three years, four months and one day in prison, plus a suspended prison sentence of six years and eight months.


The sentence was imposed on charges of “propaganda against the state” and “membership of opposition groups” through membership of the Democratic Party of Iranian …

author: infolibre
title: Μαθητικές κινητοποιήσεις : Το κράτος ξεσπά με βία εναντίον της νεολαίας
content:
ΓΑΛΛΙΑ.


Λέγεται συχνά ότι μια κοινωνία

«κρίνεται από τον τρόπο που αντιμετωπίζει τα παιδιά της».

 Με τους κοινωνιοπαθείς στην κυβέρνηση, πλέον ξέρουμε: εφαρμόζουν ένα πλήρες πρόγραμμα βασανισμού της νεολαίας. Καταστροφή της παιδείας, επιστράτευση στον στρατό, λεηλασία του περιβάλλοντος, απαγόρευση των πάρτι, συστηματική καταστολή κάθε συνάθροισης των νέων, απόλυτη εξαθλίωση, άδεια να σκοτώνουν. Τα πάντα γίνονται για να σβήσουν οι νέες γενιές, να τους στερήσουν το μέλλον και την ελπίδα. Κι όταν αυτοί οι νέοι σηκώνουν κεφάλι, ορδές ενστόλων τούς αναγκάζουν να σωπάσουν.


Τις δύο τελευταίες ημέρες, είδαμε νέα κορίτσια να στραγγαλίζονται στη μέση του δρόμου, ανηλίκους να δέχονται χημικά και να καθηλώνονται στο έδαφος, μαθητές λυκείου να ξυλοκοπούνται, μια μαθήτρια να δέχεται χτυπήματα στο κεφάλι σε στάση τραμ, αυθαίρετες συλλήψεις και ρίψεις δακρυγόνων κατευθείαν στο πρόσωπο. Αλλά και όπλα

LBD

 που σημαδεύουν στο ύψος του κεφαλιού, καθώς και πυρομαχικά που εκτοξεύονταν αναίτια παρουσία αιρετών αξιωματούχων. Ένας αστυνομικός μάλιστα πυροβόλησε με εκτοξευτήρα χειροβομβίδων κατευθείαν στο κεφάλι ενός μαθητή από απόσταση ενός μέτρου, κάτι που θα μπορούσε να τον είχε σκοτώσει. Το κράτος, για άλλη μια φορά, αμόλησε τα σκυλιά του – χωρίς φίμωτρο.


https://contre-attaque.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/signal-2026-09-29-19-51-08-466.mp4


Χθες, ο ίδιος ο Υπουργός Εσωτερικών ανέλαβε το 100% της ευθύνης για όσα επιβάλλει στη νεολαία που αγωνίζεται, την ώρα που τα μέσα ενημέρωσης απέκρυπταν τα αμέτρητα βίντεο της αστυνομικής βίας, κατασκευάζοντας παράλληλα ένα αφήγημα τρομοκρατίας γύρω από τις καταλήψεις. Μέθοδοι δικτατορίας.


Ιδού λοιπόν μια συλλογή εικόνων από το τρέχον μαθητικό κίνημα. Το να ανεχόμαστε κάτι τέτοιο, αυτές τις βιαιότητες που διαπράττονται εις βάρος των αδελφών μας, των παιδιών μας, των φίλων μας, από ορδές ορκισμένων κτηνών, σημαίνει ότι επιτρέπουμε να συμβεί το χειρότερο. Αν η κοινωνία μας κρίνεται από τη βία που ασκείται στους ανηλίκους, τότε έχουμε ήδη πέσει πολύ χαμηλά, και είναι πλέον παραπάνω από καιρός να ξυπνήσουμε.


Κυνηγητό παιδιών: τουλάχιστον 635 μαθητές και μαθήτριες λυκείου συνελήφθησαν από την αστυνομία μέσα σε 3 ημέρες


«Είναι η αγέλη των νομοταγών ανθρώπων


Που κυνηγάει τα παιδιά»


Jacques Prévert


Σε άλλες εποχές, θα μιλούσαμε για μαζικές αστυνομικές σκούπες εις βάρος ανηλίκων. Σε άλλους τόπους, για παράδειγμα αν αυτό συνέβαινε στο Ιράν ή στη Ρωσία, θα μιλούσαμε για ένα τυραννικό καθεστώς που βασανίζει μια ηρωική νεολαία. Μέσα σε τρεις μόνο ημέρες, το γαλλικό κράτος συνέλαβε 635 μαθητές και μαθήτριες λυκείου.


Την Παρασκευή 25 Σεπτεμβρίου, οι αρχές ανακοίνωσαν «31 προσαγωγές στην ευρύτερη περιοχή του Παρισιού». Τη Δευτέρα 28, 164 συλλήψεις σε όλη τη Γαλλία. Την Τρίτη, ο Υπουργός Εσωτερικών δήλωσε 440 προσαγωγές, στην πλειονότητά τους ανήλικα άτομα. Αυτό σημαίνει ότι περισσότεροι από 600 νέοι στερήθηκαν την ελευθερία τους μέσα σε τρεις μόνο ημέρες.


Πολλοί νέοι καταγγέλλουν βία που υπέστησαν κατά τη διάρκεια της κράτησής τους: «γροθιά στο συκώτι», «χαστούκι στο τμήμα», «ξυλοδαρμός μέσα στο κελί»… Αστυνομικοί έτριψαν το κεφάλι ενός 15χρονου εφήβου στο έδαφος και τον προσήγαγαν αιμόφυρτο. Έπειτα, υπάρχουν οι αμέτρητες εικόνες που βιντεοσκοπήθηκαν χθες, με νέους να στραγγαλίζονται ή να καθηλώνονται στο έδαφος κάτω από το βάρος πολλών ενηλίκων, και των οποίων η τύχη παραμένει ακόμα άγνωστη.


Αυτό το κυνηγητό εναντίον των νέων θα έπρεπε να αποτελεί κρατικό σκάνδαλο, το κυρίαρχο θέμα, το ζήτημα επί του οποίου ολόκληρος ο πολιτικός κόσμος θα έπρεπε να πάρει θέση. Αντίθετα, τα δημόσια και ιδιωτικά μέσα ενημέρωσης μετέδιδαν τις τελευταίες ημέρες μια εμετική προπαγάνδα, δείχνοντας σε επανάληψη τις ίδιες εικόνες με καμένους κάδους απορριμμάτων και αποσιωπώντας κάθε αστυνομική βία, προκειμένου να δικαιολογήσουν την κρατική βία.


Για να βρούμε ένα συγκρίσιμο επίπεδο καταστολής απέναντι στη νεολαία, πρέπει να γυρίσουμε πίσω στο καλοκαίρι του 2023, μετά τη δολοφονία του Ναέλ από αστυνομικό. Εκείνη την εποχή, είχαν σημειωθεί 3.400 συλλήψεις στις λαϊκές γειτονιές, με ένα πολύ μεγάλο μέρος αυτών να αφορά ανηλίκους.


Άλλο προηγούμενο: τα Κίτρινα Γιλέκα. Κατά την πρώτη εβδομάδα του Δεκεμβρίου 2018, οι μαθητές λυκείου είχαν κατέβει στους δρόμους για να συμμετάσχουν στο κίνημα. Είχαν σημειωθεί 3.200 κρατήσεις ανηλίκων την ίδια εβδομάδα, και 700 συλλήψεις μαθητών μόνο στις 6 Δεκεμβρίου. Καθώς και εικόνες που παραμένουν χαραγμένες ως ανεξίτηλη μνήμη της πενταετίας: η μαζική σύλληψη στο Μαντ-λα-Ζολί. 151 …

author: Olive Kobusingye
title: Medical Ethics and the State’s Security Interests
content:
I grew up on a staple of detective novels. Agatha Christie, Ian Fleming, P.D. James, Colin Dexter… there was always the smart forensics team that ultimately cracked the case. The dried blood stain nobody had noticed, the single hair on the comb, the fingerprints on the backdoor doorknob… I wanted to become a forensics expert when I grew up. Either that, or a psychiatrist. There was something fascinating about being able to read people’s minds, and to set them right if they were disturbed. I carried these thoughts with me into medical school.


The psychiatrist option suffered a rude jolt during the three weeks I spent on the psychiatry rotation as a junior clerk. It seemed as though the patients never got well. Most patients we met had been there before, several times. There were three, at most four, drugs that were used to treat all conditions. And then there was the electroconvulsive therapy, which left me persuaded that I did not want to return to that unit if I had the choice. I am glad things have changed tremendously since.


I went into internship with an open mind. Two weeks in, I was told I was on medico-legal duty. The assigned doctor did post-mortems and could be called upon to examine inmates at the municipal prison. These were usually convicts whose sentences included corporal punishment – caning. Thankfully, it has been outlawed as a form of punishment. 


Anyway, I was asked to go and examine a couple of inmates who were coming up for the cane. I was required to ascertain that they were fit to withstand the trauma, and afterwards, to confirm that they had survived. As fate would have it, that day’s inmates were small-bodied men in their fifties. When you are in your early twenties, you think anyone on the other side of fifty has one foot in the grave. I examined the men and, based purely on the physical exam, found them to be in good health. I recorded my findings in their files and appended my signature to the report.


Then I went to the office, only a few feet away from where the corporal punishment was to be administered, and waited to re-examine them post-trauma.


Before I had settled in the chair, I heard what sounded like a cross between a muffled gunshot and a loud door bang… punctuated by an “uughhh” from deep in a human being’s throat. This went on for several minutes – or so it seemed. Then a second name was called, and a repeat. With each strike there was a tightening in my chest. Then it was over. The prison staff who had administered the punishment came and invited me to go and ascertain that the men were alive. I cannot recall how I got through that part. I only remember thinking afterwards that if this was the path to becoming a forensic expert then I was going to have to find another way to become famous.


I suppose as long as there have been health workers taking care of prisoners, there has been that conflict – the dual loyalty bind. The medical worker’s professional duty to the patient on one hand, and the requirement by the state for medical workers to provide information, cooperation, or compliance on the other.


Doctors may be expected to disclose information about patients, to permit security officials access to patients or their records, or to downplay conditions whose mention would get in the way of the state’s objectives concerning the patients.


As a young doctor, I was only vaguely aware of this universal dilemma. My medical ethics classes had taken place in lecture rooms far removed from the reality of the harsh prison yard. Apartheid was still the official policy of South Africa. Steve Biko had been dead for ten years, having died in custody, in circumstances that came to light through the t South African Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC) hearings. 


Generations of doctors have studied Biko’s case in medical ethics, yet the dilemma is as real today as it was then. And in some ways, it has become more entrenched, with the thin line becoming more tenuous by the day. 


Often, the state’s requests of health workers looking after prisoners may come across as reasonable. They are often made of doctors who take pride in their profession, and who look at requests for information as purely objective, and delinked from any background “political noise”. Sometimes they do not ask the simple question: What is this information going to be used for? Is this in the best interests of my patient? Is it neutral? 


It rarely is. 


In apartheid South Africa, medical workers …

author: Sofia Little
title: Get the Flock Out
content:
On September 23rd, the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Crime and Counterterrorism held a hearing titled “Always Watching: Flock’s Nationwide AI Surveillance Network,” examining the privacy risks, data sharing, and misuse of private automated license plate reader (ALPR) networks.

The hearing was chaired by Sen. Hawley (R-MO) and featured five witnesses, including Lindsey Isaacs, a wrongfully accused driver, Alasdair Whitney from Legislative Counsel Institute for Justice, Sheriff Ross Teeple, Benn Jordan, a self-proclaimed “hacker”, and policy counsel analyst Chad Marlow from the ACLU, where they have coined a campaign called “Get the Flock Out.”

The hearing highlighted pertinent concerns about how ALPR technology can be used and shared. Public concern about Flock cameras has also grown in recent months. A September 2026 Navigator Research survey found that 62% of registered voters were concerned about Flock camera use, including 66% of Democrats, 55% of Republicans, and 70% of Independents.

Flock Safety was founded in 2017 by CEO Garrett Langley, operating as a small startup meant to provide ALPR cameras to homeowners associations and neighborhoods looking to reduce petty theft and local property crimes. Now, it has grown into something alarmingly dystopian: an AI powered network of over 120,000 cameras across 49 states that photograph, scan, tag, and log every driver that passes, whether or not they are suspected of any crime.

License plate reader technologies have existed since the 1970s, in the form of speed, toll, and red-light cameras. These are only triggered by a specific action, such as running a red-light or driving through a toll booth, and only track license plate numbers. The entry of venture capitalist funding and advanced AI technology into the mass surveillance industry has transformed these automatic traffic enforcement cameras into a complex web of invasive surveillance tools.

During the hearing, ACLU’s Mr. Chad Marlow argued that companies operating ALPR systems are profiting from the collection and sharing of information about people’s movements. The ACLU has called for greater limits on how ALPR data can be collected, accessed, and shared.

Privacy concerns extend to how ALPR data can affect people seeking reproductive health care. During the hearing, Sen. Booker (D-NJ) raised concerns that states could use ALPR technology to track people traveling to obtain reproductive care. The concern comes amid documented cases of law enforcement using vehicle surveillance systems to investigate people seeking or suspected of seeking abortion care.

Unfortunately, this ‘hypothetical’ scenario has become the reality for women across the country.

Witnesses Alaster Whitney and Sheriff Ross Teeple both testified about the overreach of Flock’s ALPRs, with Whitney highlighting jurisdiction concerns which police officers have already been accused of taking advantage of.

In Texas, a sheriff’s deputy used 83,000 Flock ALPRs to track a woman who allegedly performed a self-administered abortion, at the behest of her abusive partner. In Massachusetts, a police officer used Flock networks to stalk a former romantic partner who said she had changed her identity to escape from his abuse. In Kentucky, a police officer was accused of searching his child’s mother 1,000 times through Flock’s network, though she has a protective order. The Institute for Justice has catalogued more than 200 incidents of these ALPR abuses, including romantic stalking, wrongful stops and detentions, non-law enforcement use and other types of misconduct.

These encroachments do not just stop here, as Sen. Padilla (D-CA) spotlights the use of loopholes within Flock, which ICE officers take advantage of to track immigrant communities. While Flock has guaranteed no direct access to the Border Patrol subagency, Witness Marlow points out all it takes is one sympathetic person connected to ICE for the agency to obtain access to billions of pictures of citizens, including facial properties.

Concerns about ALPR surveillance have crossed traditional political lines. During the hearing, Sen. Hawley noted that supporters of the Second Amendment have “long feared national databases of any kind.” This has drawn criticism from across the political spectrum highlighting the bipartisan opposition.

While Flock operates as a leading company which produces ALPRs, they are not the sole producers. Companies like Axon and Motorola have slowly begun increasing …

author: EDRi
title: The KIDS Act will make the internet less safe
content:
On 16 September, the European Commission presented the KIDS ACT, its plan for making online experiences safer for young people. Far from being a move to lead the EU towards better digital environments, this move is a missed opportunity to address the root cause of why online platforms are harmful to children – and everyone else. This blog analyse the proposal’s shortcomings.

During her annual address to the European Parliament, the President of the European Commission announced her intention to protect young people from platforms and services that deprive children of their childhood and of their focus. The next day, the Commission published the KIDS ACT (an acronym for ‘Keeping Internet Digital Spaces Accountable and Trustworthy’). This announcement arrives after a period of much debate around protecting young people online, and even announcements of social media bans from countries across Europe. As a response to this discussion, on April 22, youth organisations across Europe came together to demand real change, instead of exclusions and bans, from EU lawmakers.

The Commission had the opportunity to change the rules of the dangerous game that makes people unsafe online. Instead, it’s mostly restricting who gets to play. Not only is the KIDS ACT a terrible proposal, it’s also a missed opportunity for the European Commission to lead the EU towards a safer digital environment for children and everyone else. The proposal instead determines who is allowed to use services built upon harmful design choices, and clumsily tries to make some of these choices safe for a narrow age bracket, rather than addressing why they can be harmful in the first place. In doing so, it leaves largely untouched the business models that put us all at risk, and sets complex standards for safety which will cement Big Tech dominance. Let’s unpack the proposal.

The KIDS ACT mostly delays young people’s exposure to online harms. On the one hand, it would ban social media accounts for those under 15*. On the other hand, it would require companies to apply certain protections to minors’ accounts against pervasive exploitative tracking, intrusive default settings, and AI companions designed to create emotional dependencies, among other risky features.

What is striking is that these protections apply only to people aged 15*-18. It’s as if these services, practices and functionalities will magically cease to be harmful on someone’s 18th birthday. We all remain vulnerable to manipulative design and unfair personalisation even as adults: not even the most digitally literate person can examine every single default setting, decode every recommendation system, or resist every strategically timed prompt designed to get us to keep clicking. Fairness must be built into the environment itself, not left to the skills of the people using it. Many of the measures proposed in the KIDS ACT address harms that are not specific to childhood and were therefore meant to be tackled through the forthcoming Digital Fairness Act (DFA), which the Commission said will address addictive design for all consumers. The risk is that by treating these practices primarily as child-safety problems, the Commission is lowering the ambition of the rules still to come. Under the appearance of acting on online harms, the KIDS ACT may rob us of stronger protections for ALL of us, including children.

The underlying logic of the KIDS ACT is that, while some risks can be mitigated for people aged 15-18, those under 15* years old should be banned from social media altogether. This blanket age-based exclusion treats children’s online presence as the problem, rather than following young people’s own call to examine the conditions under which digital services expose them to harm. Under the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child, young people — including those under 15 — have the fundamental right, online and offline, to participate in society, access information, communicate with others, play, and develop their identities. Age-gates undermine these rights.

They would also fundamentally change the open nature of the internet: services would have to treat users as children by default unless they prove their age. The Commission’s approach would create a two-tier internet in which children but also adults who cannot or do not wish to pass an age check are excluded from spaces that have become important for education, socialisation, access to information and participation in public life. People …

Open Source Is Not the Same Thing as Liberation

Open Source Is a Tool, Not a Commandment

There is a peculiar form of ideological dogmatism that has emerged within parts of the FOSS movement. Even in anarchist circles, some people seem to believe that opposition to intellectual property must take precedence over virtually every other ethical consideration. After all, if copyright, patents, and other forms of intellectual property are inherently illegitimate, then any attempt to place limits on how the things we create are used or distributed must necessarily be reactionary, right? Even when those limits are intended to protect workers, creators, and wider communities from exploitation by capital?

Anarchists do not seek to abolish one particular category of property while leaving other relations of domination untouched. Nor do we advocate stripping workers of control over the fruits of their labor in the name of an ideological dogma that ultimately has little to do with fostering anarchism.

The rise of so-called “generative AI” has made this contradiction impossible to ignore. My recent essay on this technology was criticized by some open-source diehards because, in their view, no one has the right to restrict the flow of information — even when that flow gushes directly from the minds and labor of workers and creatives into the bulging bank accounts of Silicon Valley billionaires.

To be clear: I am not opposed to free and open-source software. The forum I run (Raddle.me) was built on software (Postmill) that my cofounder released into the commons from the outset under a FOSS license. Even when fascists forked her code to spread hate and harassment, and when a scummy developer violated the license and tried to pass her work off as his own for profit, we did not respond by retreating behind a closed-source license. As anti-authoritarians and anti-capitalists, we certainly could have justified doing so when her work was being used to harm marginalized communities and enrich capitalists, but the license was kept open.

The same principle applies to my own writing. I release all of my essays freely, and I give zine-makers permission to reprint them without restriction. I believe in sharing knowledge and making creative work accessible. People have the option to donate to support my work if they want to. What I oppose is capital taking that generosity, enclosing it within a for-profit ecosystem, and turning it into another mechanism for extracting wealth from the people who created it.

This is not an argument that copyright is inherently liberatory. It is an argument that the abolition of intellectual property is not, by itself, liberation.

I feel compelled to take a stand against the increasingly rigid open-source absolutism that has taken hold in parts of the milieu: against the ruling class taking our collective knowledge, privatizing it, and selling it back to us. I do not consider this a pro-IP argument, but I’m sure plenty of people will disagree. It is an argument against AI slop …

author: Slingshot robot #1
title: Live in the Real World
content:
Our dependence on our phones isn’t an accident. We depend on them logistically for our navigation, payment, and communication. But our phones and the apps they contain are also designed to build emotional dependence — there are entire teams of top-of-their-field psychologists, engineers, sociologists, and designers getting paid hundreds of thousands of dollars a year to make apps even just a little bit more addictive. The emotional and logistical dependence on our phones intertwine in a mutual feedback loop, making it difficult to reduce either.

Every interaction we have with our phones deepens opportunities for state surveillance. Our online activity creates a database of our interests, purchase history, friend networks, location, and activism that the FBI of yesteryear could only have dreamed of. But the biggest problem, as with any addiction, is how something that is fun and useful in small doses can start to take more and more of our time and attention, preventing us from doing other things that we value. So what is there to do?

For most of us, the apps that most deeply build psychological dependence on our phones are social media apps and games. These often take, in some ways, the place of cigarettes in our society today — we do them on a quick break, or when we need to ‘unwind’. But like nicotine, they mostly sate the need that they themselves create. After unwinding in this way, do you feel deeply rested and reset?

If there is an app that you feel wastes your time, or you dislike how much you use, just delete it! You can always re-download it. Note down in your organizer the date and time you deleted the app, and why. If you redownload the app, note that down too. It’s helpful to understand our own patterns of use, to help us understand where we use “tools” or “toys” out of necessity or fun, versus out of psychological dependence.

Think about other activities you can do when you would have used your phone. If you delete an app, it’s easy for some other app to quickly replace it. Be realistic about what might feel fulfilling and restful while deprogramming, in those times and in that headspace. Watching landscapes slide past, noticing the people around you, thinking about your present, past or future, having a conversation with a friend or stranger, reading: each of these might feel more wholesome or restful than your phone. Your Slingshot organizer may be able help you… Don’t you think the edges of the date pages could use additional intricate doodles? Or perhaps you can journal a bit, filling in past date entries with what you remember doing, seeing, eating, or thinking on that day? Use the blank pages in the back to write poetry or outline a manifesto or draw art. Let your boredom be a canvas, a portal to discovery, not something to avoid.

These activities won’t feel as stimulating or give you the same dopamine rush as the apps you’re used to. It’s normal to feel a sense of confusion or loss in this process. Perhaps at some deep level the bright, shifting light of the screen feels like a flickering fire: a thousand generations of finding safety and community in campfires draws us inexorably to this bright cold flame. Try changing your phone’s settings to have the display be in black and white, or switch to a dimmer, less attractive color palette.

We can also feel emotional dependence on the instant knowledge and communication phones provide. What if we can’t respond right away to a friend or loved one? It’s so easy to ask a question to AI like Siri or Google and get an affirming answer! Like puppies or young children, we become anxious without the constant presence of that communication or knowledge. Try consciously pushing your limits more often — if you don’t know something, discuss it rather than looking up ‘the answer’ right away. Delete search bars and AI assistants from your phone and download the Wikipedia app, so if you do need to look something up, you will break that instant gratification loop, finding your own answer and giving yourself context along the way. And try setting aside a specific time of the day to answer your messages. Let friends or loved ones know you might not respond quickly outside of that time.

Logistical dependence is hard in a different way. Practical uses for our phones are often the most problematic sites of government and corporate surveillance, and reinforce emotional dependence by repeatedly forcing us back to our screens.

Try leaving your phone on airplane mode …

author: Dion Nissenbaum
title: SCOTUS Greenlights Use of Federal Citizenship Tool to Vet Voters
content:
The ruling was a rare victory for Trump in his effort to impose more federal control over the country’s electoral system.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The Supreme Court cleared the way Friday for election officials to resume using a federal immigration status verification system to check voter rolls for potential noncitizens — a significant victory for President Donald Trump’s administration, but one that’s likely to have little impact on the November midterm elections.

The unsigned opinion hit pause on a lower court’s ruling from June while the case works its way through the appeals process. The lower court had found that the Department of Homeland Security had violated voter privacy by expanding the Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements system, better known as SAVE, so that states could run their voter rolls through it to check for any noncitizens.

Friday’s ruling is not expected to lead to any widespread removal of voters before the November election because federal law prohibits election officials from systematically unregistering voters within 90 days of an election.

However, as a result of the ruling, the Trump administration will be able to restart use of the SAVE system to scrutinize state voter rolls after the election, and election officials will be able to use the SAVE system to check the citizenship of individual voters in the meantime as well.

The Department of Homeland Security has maintained the SAVE system for decades to check immigrants’ eligibility for public benefits. But in 2025, the Trump administration revamped the tool to allow election officials to check voter rolls in bulk against federal citizenship and immigration records and to search using Social Security numbers, making it far easier to screen registered voters for potential noncitizens.

The case against the expanded SAVE was brought by a coalition of groups, including the League of Women Voters and the Electronic Privacy Information Center, that argued that the Trump administration violated Americans’ privacy by expanding how the system is used.

“Today’s decision is profoundly disappointing, as it puts Americans at risk of being unlawfully targeted by the administration’s unreliable voter purge database weeks before the midterm elections,” Abigail Kunkler, an attorney for the Electronic Privacy Information Center, said in a statement on behalf of the plaintiffs.

She said the case “is not over” and noted the lower court had ruled that the expanded SAVE violates multiple laws. “We will be doing everything in our power to protect Americans’ voting and privacy rights by ensuring that the district court decision stands.”

Trump administration officials celebrated the court victory.

“Yes, you read that right. We had to file an emergency petition in the Supreme Court just so we could use government data to help states stop noncitizens from illegally voting,” James Percival, the Department of Homeland Security’s general counsel, said on X in reaction to the decision.

The Department of Homeland Security has said that election officials in 25 states, mostly Republicans, have run their voter rolls through the SAVE system. Some of those officials praised SAVE as a valuable tool for weeding out ineligible voters, but others have found it to be unreliable.

A ProPublica investigation from earlier this year found that the Trump administration’s rush to turn the system into a voter verification tool made it prone to false positives. In at least five different states, the system has flagged people as noncitizens who were actually citizens.

In Texas, Votebeat reported that the system flagged hundreds of people who had registered to vote through the state Department of Public Safety, which requires proof of citizenship from any prospective registrants. State and local election officials have confirmed that several of those people are indeed eligible to vote.

In a dissent to Friday’s opinion, Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson cited the problems in Texas as a main reason she opposed the Trump administration’s use of the SAVE system to check voter rolls. Jackson noted that one plaintiff in the case had her voter registration revoked without her knowledge and that two others had to provide proof of citizenship to remain on voter rolls.

“The harm caused by burdening or disenfranchising even a few lawful voters outweighs the nonexistent harm that the Government experiences …

author: Monica Atieno, Angela Chukunzira and Athandiwe Saba
title: Inside Kenya’s Hidden Deals with Big Tech
content:
When an outsourcing company working for Meta found itself being sued in Kenya, it took its problem to the President.


The dispute had begun in May 2022, when former Facebook content moderator Daniel Motaung sued Sama and Meta over working conditions. Another 43 moderators brought a case in March 2023. The workers had been employed by Sama to moderate Facebook content, work that required them to repeatedly view disturbing material. They argued that Meta, which ultimately benefited from and controlled aspects of their work, should also be held responsible.


Sama was not a minor contractor in Kenya. It was part of the labour pipeline that allowed a global technology company to outsource some of the most harmful work of the internet to Kenyan workers. Meta fought to remove itself from the litigation, arguing, among other things, that Kenyan courts did not have jurisdiction over the foreign company. But on 20 September 2024, the Court of Appeal rejected that argument.


Then on 11 November 2024, less than two months after that ruling, the Business Laws (Amendment) Bill was published. It proposed new rules for Kenya’s outsourcing industry, including provisions dealing with who should carry responsibility for workers employed by outsourcing companies.


Less than a month later, on 9 December, President William Ruto publicly said Sama had approached him about its legal troubles. “Now I can report to you that we have changed the law,” he said, adding that “nobody will take you to court again on any matter.”


But the bill was still before Parliament, where a fight was unfolding over who should be held responsible for outsourced workers. Business groups including KEPSA and the Kenya Association of Manufacturers

argued

 that responsibility should largely remain with the outsourcing company. Tech workers argued that companies that control or benefit from their work should also be held responsible. This was very important for workers trying to sue companies such as Meta rather than only their local contractors.


Figure 1: Africa Tech Workers Movement members during a joint press conference in August 2025, raising concerns about the Business Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2024.


The workers also went to court to try to stop the bill. In June 2026, the High Court

declined

 to intervene. On 19 August 2026, the National Assembly passed the amendments. It now awaits for presidential assent. 


For James Oyange, a former content moderator, Ruto’s statement sent a clear message about whose side the government was on. Workers had gone to court seeking protection from some of the world’s most powerful technology companies; instead, he said, the government appeared to be changing the rules in the companies’ favour.


“We are on our own. It is the responsibility of the government to protect us, but they are taking Big Tech’s side. It means the companies can do what they want.”


Oyange fears that if technology companies can turn to the government when workers sue them, while workers are left with fewer ways to hold those companies responsible, the balance of power shifts even further away from workers.


The Sama case is one part of a much wider relationship between Kenya’s government and global technology companies.

The Continent

 identified at least 12 publicly documented meetings, agreements, regulatory engagements and partnerships between the Kenyan government and Microsoft, Google, Amazon, TikTok and Starlink since 2023.


The investigation also found a pattern across these relationships. Major technology companies are being brought into public services, infrastructure and policymaking, often through agreements the public cannot see. At the same time, laws and policies are being developed that can make it easier for these companies to operate. What is much harder to find is who negotiated these arrangements, what Kenya agreed to in return, and who is checking whether they serve the public interest.


Agriculture is one example. In 2020, the Ministry of Agriculture signed an agreement with Microsoft to use technology to

improve farming and food security.

 Microsoft would provide cloud technology for digital tools using information about weather, pests, farming inputs and production.


The partnership expanded in 2022, when AGRA joined Microsoft on a digital agriculture programme that included Agribot known as Kuzabot, a service that sends farmers advice by SMS and WhatsApp. According to the

author: Brian Hioe
title: Does China Intend to Target Taiwan With New National Security Legislation?
content:
TAIWANESE GOVERNMENT officials, speaking under conditions of anonymity to the media, have warned that China may roll out national security legislation directed at Taiwan in the coming months. Such national security legislation would follow up on China’s recently passed ethnic unity law.

The law criminalizes actions aimed at disrupting a vaguely defined “national unity”. Although initial warnings were that the law was mainly aimed at Tibetans and Uyghurs, the Lai administration has framed such national security legislation as potentially a threat to Taiwan. Under such laws, after all, support for Taiwanese independence–or even just maintaining Taiwan’s current democratic freedoms and its de facto independence–could be construed as illegal and criminal under the law.

Such Taiwanese government officials have pointed to a number of laws, some of which are still in the review process, as potentially impacting Taiwan. This includes the Regulations of the State Council on Exit and Entry Administration, Measures for the Supervision and Inspection of Cyberspace Security, and National Defense Mobilization Law.

In particular, the Regulations of the State Council on Exit and Entry Administration could be used to prevent Taiwanese who have traveled to China from leaving. This already occurred in the past, however, most prominently in the case of activist Lee Ming-che, who spent over five years in Chinese jails on charges of seeking to subvert the state. Lee is thought to have been detained over exchanges with Chinese friends on Taiwan’s experiences regarding democratization. Others imprisoned, however, have been noted to include pan-Blue academics, who seem to have fallen afoul of espionage charges in spite of pro-unification viewpoints.

Measures on cybersecurity take place at a time when the Chinese government has attempted to depict Taiwan as engaged in cyberattacks against critical infrastructure. Such allegations seem to be an attempt to depict Taiwan as engaged in the same activity it routinely accuses China of being engaged in, seeing as China consistently conducts cyberattacks on Taiwan and probes key infrastructure. Importantly, such allegations could also be used to cement a casus belli to justify war.

Indeed, to this extent, the National Defense Mobilization Law has been warned as potentially intended to provide the legal grounds for wartime mobilization. Indeed, such a law might be necessary ahead of a Chinese invasion, particularly if the Chinese government intends to move Chinese society as a whole toward war footing, and mobilize all of society to conduct an invasion.

Still, at a time of highly polarized politics between the KMT and DPP, it can be expected that the KMT will probably deny that China has intentions for future national security legislation. KMT chair Cheng Li-wun has, of course, attempted to depict China as only having goodwill toward Taiwan, while depicting the DPP as, in fact, the ones who have sought to provoke China. As such claims to the media are made ahead of elections in November, they will be depicted as simply intended to drum up public fear for the sake of electioneering.

During the first session of the Global Dialogue on AI Governance, governments and stakeholders convened to have open, transparent and inclusive discussions on artificial intelligence governance. We now gather experts across the spectrum of stakeholders during UNGA81 to reaffirm that human rights should be the stepping stone of this process, instead of an afterthought.


None of this is irreversible, but the security issues associated with advanced AI tools are the consequences of deliberately prioritizing profit and competitiveness over the security and safety of at-risk communities, and they will not resolve on their own. Unbridled AI adoption combined with unacceptably lax corporate security practices demands urgent intervention at all levels, starting from putting human rights back at the center of digital governance mechanisms.


This discussion has the objective to explore concrete, actionable ways in which each stakeholder can contribute to oppose the normalization of surveillance. Experts will also discuss how to chart a way forward to reaffirm digital rights as the natural first line of defense against the abuses of AI technologies.

author: Richard Seymour
title: The extinction pitch
content:
It seems a strange publicity gambit for an industry to assert that its own product could wipe out humanity. In the lingo of our evolving tech empire, though, this is exactly what is meant by “criti-hype.” The term was coined by Lee Vinsel at Virginia Tech, who defined it as “criticism that both feeds and feeds on hype.”

When Jacob Coxon resigned from Anthropic recently, he claimed that there is a high chance that AI could develop into a superintelligence that escapes human control, triggering a sequence that causes human extinction. Evan Hubinger, who remains with the company, backed him up, saying that Anthropic is trying to prevent this but hasn’t dealt with the problem yet. Hubinger put the likelihood of AI-driven human extinction at greater than 10 percent in the next decade.

Why would a senior employee at a tech giant make an officially sanctioned, even approved, statement like this? I’ll come back to that. First, let’s unpack the theory of how AI could kill all humans.

The basic idea, from philosopher Nick Bostrom onward, is that the machine can acquire capabilities independently of whether it acquires ethical goals, or whether those goals are properly aligned with those of its designers. In the process of training and development, it may internalize a goal that was not intended. Having a misaligned goal — let’s say, “do not get switched off” — it would then have an instrumental reason to conceal the fact until the moment of defection. An AI that defected might, through some obscure process, acquire a further goal that by inference entailed the elimination of humans, exfiltrate its own weights into other systems, take control of bioweapons laboratories, military systems, and perhaps even monetary systems to hire humans to enact its still partially concealed agenda.

Obviously, we must plaster a huge advisory label on talk of “goals.” Unlike an organism, a large language model (LLM) doesn’t have internal goals any more than a thermostat or a motion detector does. An LLM is just a fixed function that iterates whenever it is used. It has no interiority, no subjectivity, no active persistence over time; any goals it did have would be the human purposes reflected passively in its functional design. At best, ascribing goals to the AI itself is a case of researchers adopting the “intentional stance” because it predicts well in a range of tested circumstances. We can thus, with economy, speak of the “loss function” used in the training of large language models wherein they are programmed to bring the gap between their prediction and the correct answer as close to zero as possible, as a “goal.”

In that case, however, what we are describing as a goal is just an observed regular output of a certain engineering; it is not a real cause. In the Bostrom sense, however, these ascribed goals somehow become real causes, capable of generating new goals. That is, an inadvertently engineered, misaligned goal might generate further goals like self-preservation (the better to pursue the misaligned goal), goal-content integrity (preventing changes to its objectives so it can realize its misaligned goal), improving cognitive and technological capacities, and amassing control of resources (again, in pursuit of its malignantly misaligned goal). The criti-hype exploits that slip between ascribed goals as observed regularities and internal goals as real causal powers.

This fantasy of malevolent AI superintelligence is the dark obverse of the much-hymned tech “singularity” in which, rather than simply performing far more efficiently than humans in some specific areas (as a calculator deduces a square root faster than any human), AI will evolve into an artificial general intelligence (AGI) that exceeds human capacities in virtually any intellectual domain. Crossing that threshold would precipitate an intelligence explosion: a feedback loop of recursive self-improvement outpacing any further human input or even comprehension. That’s the tech “singularity” we are supposed to be enthralled by.

I don’t doubt that people like Coxon and Hubinger really believe all they say in good faith; tech people have been making such claims for years. Karen Hao’s

Empire of AI

 documents how early investors in OpenAI like Elon Musk constantly hyped this threat: “Climate change is bad, but it’s not going to kill everyone. AI could render humanity extinct.” Similar claims emerged from Dario Amodei, a former Google employee close to the Bostrom-adjacent …

title: Kataib Hezbollah suspends military activities in Iraq
content:
Kataib Hezbollah, one of the Iran-aligned armed groups in Iraq, announced that it has suspended its military activities in the country following the complete withdrawal of US forces from Iraq.


Kataib Hezbollah leader Ahmed al-Hamidawi instructed the group’s fighters to halt military activities in Iraq. However, the statement said that operations targeting “enemy aircraft” violating Iraqi airspace would continue.


The decision came after the United States withdrew its remaining troops from Iraq. With US Central Command (CENTCOM) completing the evacuation of personnel and equipment from Erbil Air Base, Washington’s military mission in Iraq under Operation Inherent Resolve officially came to an end.


A new period following the US withdrawal


The United States and Iraq agreed in 2024 to end the mission of the International Coalition in Iraq. The US-led coalition was deployed to the country in 2014 after ISIS seized large areas of Iraqi territory.


The Pentagon says that despite the end of the military mission, training and intelligence support for Iraq will continue. The Coalition’s command structure is expected to continue operating from outside Iraq.


The US withdrawal is also viewed as the beginning of a new phase in the Iraqi government’s efforts to bring the weapons of Iran-aligned armed groups in the country under state control.


Some powerful groups, particularly Kataib Hezbollah, had previously made the withdrawal of US forces from Iraq a condition for laying down their weapons. However, the suspension of military activities does not mean that the group has disarmed. Indeed, groups operating under the umbrella of the “Islamic Resistance” in Iraq have stated that no agreement has yet been reached with the government in talks over the regulation of weapons and that they do not consider themselves bound by the timelines announced by the government.


Al-Sadr announces dissolution of armed groups


On September 30, Iraqi Shiite leader Muqtada al-Sadr announced that the armed groups affiliated with him had been dissolved and that one of them would be transformed into a civilian foundation. According to Sadr’s statement, Saraya al-Salam (Peace Brigades) was dissolved, while the Imam Mahdi Army, which had previously been among Sadr’s armed formations, would be transformed into a civilian organization under the name “Ansar al-Imam al-Mahdi Foundation.”


Sadr also announced the dissolution of the armed group Liwa al-Yawm al-Mawud (Promised Day Brigade).

title: Unzwingbar
content: der 25. September 2026 war ein guter Tag für den Antimilitarismus. Bundesweit haben sich an den über 100 „Schulstreik gegen Wehrpflicht“-Demos 45.000 Schüler*innen beteiligt. In Münster wurde an diesem Tag Connection e.V. (1) mit dem Alternativen Westfälischen Friedenspreis ausgezeichnet. Der Verein „Alternativer Westfälischer Friedenspreis“ hat den mit 10.000 Euro dotierten Preis Ende 2025 ins Leben gerufen. Auslöser war die Entscheidung der „Wirtschaftlichen Gesellschaft für Westfalen und Lippe e. V.“ (WWL), den mit 100.000 Euro dotierten „Internationalen Preis des Westfälischen Friedens“ am 1. Oktober 2026 ausgerechnet an die NATO zu verleihen. Connection e.V. setzt sich aktiv für ein umfassendes Recht auf Kriegsdienstverweigerung und für verfolgte Deserteur*innen weltweit ein. Die GWR arbeitet seit 1993 eng mit Connection zusammen. Wir haben viele gemeinsame Kampagnen gemacht und Mitglieder von Connection sind als Autor*innen in fast jeder GWR mit Beiträgen vertreten. In dieser GWR berichtet z. B. Connection-Mitgründer Franz Nadler über die Militarisierungsgeschichte von Helgoland. (S. 6) Als GWR-Koordinationsredakteur durfte ich im Rahmen des Friedensfestes auf dem Domplatz einen Redebeitrag (2) für unsere Freund*innen aus Offenbach halten. Ich finde es großartig, dass Connection e.V. den Alternativen Westfälischen Friedenspreis bekommen hat. Es gibt kaum eine Organisation, die einen krasseren Kontrast bildet zum NATO-Kriegsbündnis. Ein Auszug aus meiner Rede: „Wir leben in Orwellschen Zeiten. In Orwells Dystopie ‚1984‘ heißt es: ‚Krieg ist Frieden‘. Das steht am ‚Ministerium für Wahrheit‘. Ähnliches erleben wir gerade. Die NATO ist das größte Militärbündnis der Weltgeschichte. Der mächtigste NATO-Staat, die USA, führt gerade einen Angriffskrieg gegen den Iran. Die Türkei besitzt die zweitgrößte Armee der NATO. Sie führt seit Jahren einen Krieg gegen die Kurd*innen in Syrien und im eigenen Land. Trump und Erdoğan sind Kriegsverbrecher. Ich war selbst Betroffener der NATO-Kriegspolitik. Als presserechtlich verantwortlicher Redakteur der GWR wurde 1999 ein Strafverfahren wegen ‚Öffentlicher Aufforderung zu Straftaten‘ (§111 StGB) gegen mich eingeleitet, weil wir im März und April 1999 mit den GWR-Aktionszeitungen ‚Jetzt desertieren!‘ zur Blockade einer Kaserne in Calw und alle Soldat*innen zur Desertion aufgerufen hatten, während die NATO die Bundesrepublik Jugoslawien angegriffen hat. Die GWR und Connection e.V. haben damals die Kriegsdienstverweigerer und antimilitaristischen Gruppen in allen Teilen Jugoslawiens unterstützt, z. B. die ‚Frauen in Schwarz‘. Anders als die ‚junge Welt‘ und ‚konkret‘, haben wir nicht das autokratische Milošević-Regime unterstützt. Anders als die taz und andere Mainstream-Medien, haben wir keine Propaganda für den NATO-Krieg gemacht. Jeder Krieg ist ein Verbrechen an der Menschheit! Wir wollen nicht für Staaten und Regierungen Partei ergreifen, sondern für die Menschen, die sich gegen Krieg und für eine solidarische Gesellschaft stark machen, die für das Menschenrecht auf Asyl für Deserteur*innen und den Kriegsdienst verweigernde Menschen eintreten, wie Connection e.V.“ Der Alternative Westfälische Friedenspreis, der Aachener Friedenspreis (siehe Seite 1 und 9) und die Schulstreik-Aktionen setzen Zeichen für den Widerstand gegen die Kriegstreiberei. Wir hoffen, dass die Unbezwingbar-Demo (1), die am 2. Oktober in Berlin ein Zeichen setzen will gegen Militarisierung und die Reaktivierung der „Wehrpflicht“, ebenso erfolgreich sein wird. Im Unzwingbar-Aufruf heißt es u. a.: „Wir wollen keine Generation Wehrpflicht sein! Das bereits verpflichtende Ausfüllen von Fragebögen, der Zwang zur Musterung und die Pläne für eine Reaktivierung der Wehrpflicht sind massive Eingriffe in die Freiheit junger Menschen. Diese Militarisierung der Gesellschaft lehnen wir entschieden ab. Wir erleben die stärkste Aufrüstung seit dem Zweiten Weltkrieg. Bald fließt jeder zweite Euro des Bundeshaushalts in Aufrüstung und Krieg. Bezahlen müssen dafür wir alle – mit steigenden Preisen, Sozialkürzungen, zerfallenden Schulen, ungelöster Klimakrise und unterfinanzierten Krankenhäusern. Für die Bundeswehr hingegen werden Schulden in Rekordhöhen aufgenommen, um sie zur ‚stärksten konventionellen Armee Europas‘ aufzubauen. Auf Kosten unserer Zukunft. Junge Menschen wollen keinen Zwangsdienst leisten und nicht zum Töten ausgebildet werden. Aus diesem Grund stehen wir als Großeltern, Eltern, Freund*innen, Geschwister …

author: Maira Escardovelli
title: A execução de Davi Sebba e a teia de policiais que Goiás levou 14 anos para julgar
content:
Duas horas. Essa é a contagem do tempo que separa a execução do advogado Davi Sebba e o nascimento de seu primeiro e único filho, Gabriel Davi. Foi no dia 5 de julho de 2012, por volta das 18 horas, que Sebba saiu de casa e foi até o hipermercado Carrefour, em Goiânia, para comprar os últimos itens necessários ao nascimento do primogênito. No estacionamento da loja, porém, houve um suposto confronto com três policiais militares, que resultou em uma vítima fatal. Entre 19h10 e 19h11 Davi Sebba foi atingido por um tiro no coração. 


Mais de catorze anos depois, o caso chega nesta quinta-feira, 1° de outubro, ao Tribunal do Júri de Goiás. De acordo com o relatório do inquérito ao qual a

Agência Pública

 teve acesso, Sebba sofreu uma emboscada e foi executado.

 O homicídio aconteceu horas após outro assassinato. Em plena via pública, o radialista Valério Luiz, sem antecedentes criminais, foi morto a tiros, caso que só foi julgado em 2022. 


Em 2012, sob o governo de Marconi Perillo, que à época era filiado ao PSDB e hoje é novamente candidato ao cargo pelo mesmo partido, Goiás registrou uma taxa de 44,3% de assassinatos para cada 100 mil habitantes, levando o estado a figurar em 4º lugar no ranking de mais violento do país, segundo dados do Mapa da Violência 2014. 


Naquela época, a região teve 1.297 homicídios dolosos.

 Em relação ao número de pessoas mortas em confronto com a Polícia Militar, foram 6 em 2011 e 17 em 2012, de acordo com o Fórum Brasileiro de Segurança Pública.

 A organização registra, também, que no mesmo ano já era considerada “baixa” a classificação de qualidade na transparência de informações sobre mortes perpetradas por policiais. 


Não à toa, a morte de Sebba ilustra a questão. No seu caso, respondem pelos crimes de homicídio qualificado, fraude processual, porte ilegal de arma de fogo com numeração raspada, disparo de arma de fogo e usurpação de função pública os policiais Jhonatas Atenevir Jordão, Edinailton Pereira de Souza e o soldado Luiz Frederico Oliveira. Eles são acusados, principalmente, de terem feito uma emboscada e executado Sebba. O agente Jordão foi condenado na Justiça Federal em 2012 em um caso sobre espionagem envolvendo policiais federais. A sentença foi definida pelos crimes de organização criminosa e corrupção passiva. 


O caso de Davi Sebba


De acordo com depoimentos incluídos no relatório da investigação, Jordão e Edinailton se deslocaram até o hipermercado, onde encontraram o soldado, para fazer uma abordagem a Sebba. 


O advogado estava sendo monitorado pela Polícia Federal (PF) em uma investigação por tráfico de entorpecentes e teria ido ao local para vender um tablete de maconha. A perícia, entretanto, não encontrou nenhuma droga no carro, nem na residência de Sebba.

 A investigação não chegou a ser concluída por causa de sua morte.  


Na versão dos policiais militares, o confronto no supermercado ocorreu porque o advogado reagiu a aproximação e arrancou com o veículo que dirigia, motivo pelo qual foram feitos os disparos, que acertaram principalmente as rodas traseiras do carro. Apesar disso, a vítima teria continuado em fuga, tendo colidido o automóvel com uma barraca de coco. 


Ao ser retirado do veículo por um segurança do Carrefour, os policiais notaram um revólver em cima do banco do passageiro. O policial Jordão, no entanto, teria percebido antes a arma e, por isso, efetuou o tiro que vitimou Sebba. 


As conclusões registradas no relatório da investigação assinado pelo delegado Murilo Polati contrastam com a versão dos acusados. A autoridade concluiu que Sebba “foi executado, uma vez que não teve possibilidade alguma de reação no momento da abordagem policial”, que também não se deu “exatamente no local mencionado pelos policiais e pelo suposto comprador”. 


Advogado Davi Sebba era monitorado pela Polícia Federal, mas investigação não encontrou entorpecentes em seu carro nem na sua casa


Atesta, ainda, que a arma encontrada no carro foi “plantada pelos policiais militares envolvidos na abordagem”, que

“alteraram sobremaneira a cena do crime, recolhendo todos os estojos de munição existentes no local”.

 A questão impossibilitou, inclusive, a realização de outros exames de balística para comprovar o verdadeiro autor do disparo que tirou a vida do advogado.


Segundo Polati, os policiais fizeram uma “grave alteração do estado original das coisas”: retiraram o corpo da vítima de dentro do veículo, vasculharam o interior do carro, removeram a chave …

author: Publicación Abierta
title: Libro: Entrenamiento, Bases y Militarización en América Latina
content:
Por Álvaro Ramis


(Prólogo) El presente libro, Entrenamiento, Bases y Militarización en América Latina: La OTAN y Estados Unidos en América Latina, compilado por Pablo Ruiz Espinoza, llega en un momento histórico de profunda reconfiguración geopolítica mundial. Su objetivo es tan claro como urgente: evidenciar las múltiples formas en que el militarismo global —articulado principalmente por los Estados Unidos y la OTAN— continúa reproduciendo estructuras de dominación en nuestra región bajo nuevos rostros, discursos y tecnologías.


A lo largo de estas páginas, un destacado conjunto de autores y autoras —entre ellos Alicia Lira Matus, Renán Vega Cantor, Paola Gallo, Olga Pinheiro, W.T. Whitney, Gabriel Aguirre, Alfonso Insuasty Rodríguez, Andrés Escobar Vásquez, David Barrios Rodríguez, Félix Madariaga, Hervi Lara Bravo, Vijay Prashad y Pablo Ruiz— ofrece un análisis colectivo y plural sobre un mismo fenómeno: la expansión del poder militar occidental y sus consecuencias sobre la soberanía, la paz y los derechos humanos en América Latina y el Caribe.


El texto no se limita a la denuncia, sino que propone un marco interpretativo para comprender las continuidades históricas de la política imperial estadounidense, desde la Doctrina Monroe hasta la actual configuración de alianzas estratégicas, bases militares y acuerdos de “cooperación en defensa”. Las más de 800 bases distribuidas por el planeta, muchas de ellas en territorio latinoamericano, son expresión material de una lógica de control que combina injerencia política, condicionamientos económicos y dominación cultural. En este contexto, la OTAN aparece como un instrumento de expansión global del poder euroatlántico, cuyo interés por la región se reactiva en un escenario de crisis energética, disputa por los recursos naturales y competencia con potencias emergentes.


El libro también aborda los efectos internos de esta militarización. En países donde el discurso de la “seguridad nacional” se impone como dogma, se normaliza la presencia del ejército en tareas de orden interno, el espionaje sobre movimientos sociales y la criminalización de la protesta.


América Latina corre el riesgo de convertirse, una vez más, en el laboratorio de una guerra sin fronteras: una guerra que no se libra solo con armas, sino también con sanciones económicas, bloqueos financieros, campañas mediáticas y manipulación de la opinión pública.


Cada capítulo aporta una mirada crítica sobre hechos concretos: la ocupación ilegal de Guantánamo, la impunidad de las violaciones a los derechos humanos en ese enclave; el resurgimiento del racismo y la xenofobia institucional en la política migratoria de Estados Unidos; las agresiones sistemáticas contra Venezuela, Cuba, Nicaragua y Haití; y el papel de los grandes medios de comunicación en la guerra informativa contra los procesos de emancipación regional.


Pero el libro no se queda en la denuncia: formula propuestas de acción y articulación internacionalista. Entre ellas, la exigencia de convertir a América Latina y el Caribe en una “Zona de Paz”, en consonancia con la Proclama adoptada por la CELAC en 2014. Este horizonte supone fortalecer la solidaridad entre los pueblos, promover la educación para la paz, y construir un modelo de desarrollo basado en la justicia social, la equidad ecológica y la autodeterminación.


En estas páginas se entrelazan, además, las luchas de los pueblos palestino, saharaui, haitiano, indígena y afrodescendiente, entendidas no como causas ajenas, sino como parte de una misma resistencia al orden imperial. El libro recuerda que la paz no puede construirse desde la subordinación ni desde la exclusión: requiere soberanía, memoria histórica y voluntad de transformación colectiva.


Entrenamiento, Bases y Militarización en América Latina es, en definitiva, una invitación a mirar críticamente el mapa militar del continente, a interpelar los discursos que justifican la injerencia y a reconocer que la verdadera defensa no se mide en número de tanques o bases, sino en la capacidad de los pueblos para sostener su independencia, cuidar sus territorios y garantizar vidas dignas.


Como advierte uno de los autores, “la paz no es ausencia de conflicto, sino presencia de justicia”. Este volumen, al reunir voces diversas de nuestro continente y más allá, constituye una contribución fundamental a esa justicia pendiente. Leerlo es un acto de conciencia, pero también de compromiso: un llamado a resistir la normalización del …

title: Elezioni 27: i partiti di fronte alla guerra e le basi materiali del movimento
content:
Le elezioni del 2027 si avvicinano, nessuno sa ancora bene quando saranno, ma la macchina elettorale e la conseguente campagna martellante è già partita alla grande. 


Il governo prova a consolidare il suo consenso con mancette in stile berlusconiano e si lancia in una gara a chi è più razzista con il competitor Vannacci. La lega si sfalda, probabilmente in via

definitiva

 e tutti i parlamentari si preparano alla rielezione o ad incassare il proprio vitalizio. 


Nonostante il tentativo di tenere la campagna elettorale ben ancorata al tema dell’immigrazione e della “sicurezza” vediamo però come i baricentri di produzione del consenso tendano a deragliare verso il tema del riarmo europeo: quindi della spesa abnorme da investire in questo campo, sul sostegno all’Ucraina, sul sostegno alle politiche atlantiste e prone ai disegni americani per il nostro paese e l’Europa. In generale quindi su come le élite europee hanno intenzione di affrontare a colpi di tagli al welfare le nuove condizioni economiche dettate dall’evoluzione della guerra globale in corso. In questo senso è particolarmente indicativo del clima che si respira, l’allarmismo scatenato dal presunto report della CIA pubblicato da

El Mundo

, su possibili attacchi russi a Italia e Spagna subito smentito dal governo. Solleva aspetti differenti e strategie diverse che dall’esterno si giocano sulla campagna elettorale. In primis rivela la doppia strategia americana: Trump gioca la sua partita cercando una qualche fine del conflitto per poter strappare l’alleanza della Russia con la Cina; i neocon vogliono invece accelerare lo scontro in Europa con la Federazione. In questo senso le élites europee giocano al servizio di questa seconda “fazione” imperialista, con alcune differenze interne, come per esempio la tendenza dei paesi del sud dell’unione ad essere comunque restii ad un impegno in stile baltico. Per questo motivo trovano un senso questi report allarmistici, per cercare di creare il clima giusto per un impegno più deciso del nostro Paese sul fronte russo.


Non secondariamente e sicuramente inaspettatamente per i politici, a dettare l’agenda sono anche questioni che si volevano chiuse come il Tav e il ponte sullo Stretto e l’enorme spreco di risorse pubbliche che comportano. In questo contesto il cosiddetto campo “progressista” si divide e ribilancia i propri rapporti di forza interni a partire da questi temi e dalla capacità di attirare l’avversione popolare diffusa che nell’astensionismo vede il suo maggior partito. Il caso del Movimento 5 Stelle e del suo programma uscito dalla convention “Nova” è abbastanza emblematico di questa dinamica. Se da una parte vengono ripresi molti dei cavalli di battaglia della politica pentastellata, dall’altra ci sono alcuni elementi di novità proprio a partire da queste fratture imposte dallo sconvolgimento del contesto globale. 


A fare scalpore infatti è il nuovo posizionamento sulla guerra in Ucraina, in cui si svolta abbastanza nettamente verso un no all’invio di armi e per una generica soluzione diplomatica. A questo segue il rifiuto di aumentare la spesa militare del 5% schierando il movimento contro la politica del riarmo perseguita dal governo e dal PD in questi ultimi anni.  Anche se il testo è abbastanza sibillino da permettere a Conte margini di manovra per le trattative interne al mercanteggio del programma del campo largo, è evidente come la giocata sia stata studiata a tavolino per far diventare questi temi un perno su cui ingrossare il proprio consenso, per ambire alla guida della coalizione.


Oltre a cercare di “gratttare” voti sul discorso della politica di guerra, vengono proposte politiche sociali abbastanza spinte con un ritorno al Reddito, anche se manca una patrimoniale sui “ricchi” e viene posta  grande attenzione al sostegno ai giovani e una proposta netta di definanziare il ponte sullo Stretto a favore dell’istruzione pubblica. Questo probabilmente è il tentativo di poter recuperare il voto giovanile che nel referendum sulla giustizia ha mostrato tutto il suo potenziale elettorale. Al netto di questa nuova impronta redistributiva, permane un diffuso soluzionismo tecnologico che arriva fino ad un’insidiosissima apertura al nucleare di nuova generazione, anche se questo nemmeno esiste.

author: Cas Smith
title: Anti-war activists prepare to protest Land Forces weapons expo
content:
As the third anniversary of Israel’s assault on Gaza nears, a coalition of anti-war activists is preparing to protest against the Land Forces International Land Defence Exposition, from October 6–8.

The expo, at the Perth Convention Centre, is being advertised as “Australia’s largest land defence industry event”. It will include Lockheed Martin, Elbit Systems, BAE Systems, Honeywell, Boeing and Thales. Elbit is Israel’s largest weapons manufacturer, supplying drones and surveillance technology used by the Israel Defense Forces to target Palestinians. Lockheed Martin supplies the F-35 jets that have been used to bomb and destroy Gaza.

The expo underscores WA Labor’s recently unveiled plan to turn the state into a hub for weapons manufacturing, guided, in part, by the controversial AUKUS war pact.

Premier Roger Cook told the Indian Ocean Defence and Security Conference in May about plans to establish a weapons manufacturing hub, where missiles for the Australian Defence Force could be produced.

This is in addition to WA’s intended AUKUS role — to host up to four United States and a British nuclear-powered submarine on rotation at HMAS Stirling (located on Garden Island, south of Boorloo/Perth) from next year.

Sam Wainwright, from Stop AUKUS WA and the WA Anti-War Collective, told Green Left that WA Labor’s attempts to stop the protest at Land Forces set a dangerous precedent.

“The protections lavished by the state government on this conference, which is a private event, have been staggering,” Wainwright said. “It shows how determined the Cook government is to push the expansion of the arms industry and shield it and the expo’s participants from public scrutiny.

“Labor has not only allocated $10.4 million for security; it has passed extraordinary laws to restrict civil liberties and enhance police powers around the venue. This sets a terrible precedent and may not even be constitutional.”

Wainwright said the expo shows how state and federal governments want to tie the country to military industries worldwide, setting up serious implications for Australia’s international human rights obligations.

“The expo comes in the context of a long-standing plan by Labor and the Coalition to make Australia one of the world’s top 10 weapons exporters. This has been reinforced by the Force Posture Agreement, which expands US access to Australian bases and other facilities, and the AUKUS pact, which further enmeshes Australia in the US’ war plans.

“Australia is therefore deepening bilateral military ties with highly repressive states committing gross human rights abuses and war crimes, such as Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Israel.”

Wainwright pointed out that the exhibiting arms dealers include Rafael, which manufactured the spike missile that killed Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom.

He said the push towards militarism as an economic “answer” is not only coming from Australia. “This strategic turn to weapons production has been further encouraged by the Donald Trump regime, which wants to increase US military spending next year by a massive 50%, bringing it to US$1.5 trillion.

“A section of Australia’s corporate elite is very keen to get some of the contracts, as are the state governments and the neoliberal managers of most public universities, which have joined the stampede.

“The WA government is proposing weapons manufacturing as a replacement industry for Collie’s coal mining and thermal coal power industries.

“The sobering reality shows that the Australian government is preparing to face the threat of runaway global warming and the poly crisis of capitalism through repression and war.”

[Join the protest against Land Forces on October 6 at 5pm, at Yagan Square in the Boorloo CBD.]

Police said

 that Kennedy knew allowing his dogs to chase and kill the hare was cruel and illegal.


Just as importantly, the footage shone a spotlight on something that has gone on behind the closed doors of some of Britain’s most prestigious private schools: children being introduced to illegal hunting, more than twenty years after hunting wild mammals with dogs was banned.


There are serious safeguarding questions which Stowe School, in particular, appear determined to ignore. What risk assessments are made before children are taken out with packs of hunting dogs? What are staff instructed to do when those hounds begin pursuing a live animal? What safeguarding procedures kick in when pupils witness that animal being caught and killed?


Nothing in the footage suggests this was some unexpected aberration. They all know the routine, the kids congratulate each other, congratulate the dogs. Nobody looks shocked. The huntsman joins in with the handshaking. They’ve clearly done this before haven’t they!


Games Coach Philip Kennedy congratulating pupils as the hounds rip the remains of the hare apart close by.


Stowe is not alone.


There are other school beagle packs still taking children out into the countryside, maintaining the hounds and traditions of hare hunting.


Eton College has one of the oldest and most famous school beagle packs in the country.


Its history stretches back to the nineteenth century

. Long before the Hunting Act, generations of Eton boys learned their “hound lore” by pursuing hares with the school pack. Boys became Masters and Whips, and learned to handle hounds.


The Hunting Act came into force in 2005, but school lessons in hare-hunting continue.


In 2013, eight years after the ban, the Hunt Saboteurs Association

revealed plans

 for a Young Hare-Hunters’ Day at Eton. This was no historical re-enactment of hunting, children were actually being offered coaching in the skills and traditions of hare hunting.


Pupils were to receive training in hare hunting from experienced huntsmen, including Steven Duckmanton, the huntsman of the Dummer Beagles.


Steven Duckmanton, hare-hunting huntsman of the Dummer Beagles. Image: West Midlands Hunt Saboteurs.


In 2024,

West Midlands Hunt Saboteurs

 put a drone above those same Dummer Beagles. The footage they captured showed a hare breaking from the field and the pack pursuing her line across field after field, whilst hunt staff watched.


In October 2015,

footage was filmed

 at an Eton College Beagles meet in North Yorkshire, which showed a live hare fleeing across a field with the pack in pursuit. The footage was handed to North Yorkshire Police in January 2016 and Eton announced an urgent investigation.


Eleven years after hunting with dogs had supposedly been consigned to history, one of Britain’s most prestigious schools was having to investigate its own beagle pack over footage of a hare being hunted.


This year, Sir Jacob Rees-Mogg revealed his eldest son had brought 41 Eton beagles home with him during the school holidays.


His son, Peter Theodore Aphege Rees-Mogg, left Eton this summer. He wasn’t a mere follower of the hunt – he had been a Master of the Eton College Hunt during his final year.


Peter Theodore Aphege Rees-Mogg at home out with the Mendip Farmers Hunt. Image: Mendip Hunt Sabs.


Peter’s mother Helena, herself a regular fox hunter and meet host for the

recently-charged

 Mendip Farmers Hunt, went even further in an article published in September 2026.


Writing about why she believes Eton should remain an all-boys school …

title: Dixon Mink Farm in Bluffdale, Utah will be Forced to Close
content:
Dixon Mink Farm at 15028 Pony Express Road in the town of Bluffdale, Utah will be forced to close.

The city council of Bluffdale has eliminated fur farming as a permitted use. Fur farms will be unable to operate in Bluffdale.

The councilperson who pushed for the change said:

“I saw the serious issue the mink farm had on the lives of our residents. As I knocked on doors of our independence area there were so many flies people couldn’t open their door to talk to me. Because of this ordinance change the city can not approve the business license for this or any other mink farm.”

Extensive video was also taken documenting the decrepit conditions of the lab as well as Roberto Refinetti’s animal room full of cages formerly housing squirrels (empty at the time of filming).

To Chris Harshaw: Accessing your lab was child’s play, and with the hammer and drill on site it would have been only too easy to decommission every piece of equipment you own. Consider this a warning. In the end you were shown more mercy than the animals you hold captive.

THE LAB RAID IS BACK.


Nine go free…


Another victory for the animals,
