author: winter oak
title: Never Accidentally Offer Luxury Recycled Cream Cakes to Portuguese Vegan Punks!
content:
This is the fifth and final chapter from the book 

King of the Squatters

 by jaybo which we are delighted to be able to share on Winter Oak. The whole text can be found as a pdf

here

.


I had enjoyed going for food at the social centre twice weekly. But it became tiresome for me to recognise blatant hierarchies and leaders when their on-line blurb claimed that they were anarchists against leaders, organised along horizontal lines, not vertical, top-down power structures. But my relationship with the social centre was completely destroyed one afternoon, after I had just recycled some expensive, fancy cream cakes.


In front of our house, a fiesta had been happening all weekend, so lots of drunken revellers engulfed our usually quiet home. Our squat had been under siege for the three days, being attacked by young adults who threw stones and came into our building looking for trouble. I had not been sleeping well and was very tired one day as I ate some luxury recycled cream cakes in the city centre. Then the social centre’s leader passed me and stopped to speak. We had only ever seen each other previously at the centre, never in public. I offered yer man a fancy cake, without thinking that they were patently not vegan.


He refused and asked me exactly where our squat was. I innocently told him directions to our home. Then he left to go on a demonstration against workers’ exploitation. That night as I walked home, I was stopped dead in my tracks by fresh graffiti on the bridge just before our squat. In big white letters it simply stated, “vegan limit!!!” I had no doubt that the vegan punk anarchist leader had just sprayed the graffiti as some kind of attempted bullshit intimidation directed at me. Because I had offered to share my hard-earned cakes with him.


I never went back to the social centre after that. I was so angry that I knew if I had returned then I would have certainly made trouble and probably have given the leader an excuse to ban me anyway. I hate egos and authoritarians. However, as always, I tried to turn a negative into a positive. That incident inspired one of my most popular signs for The Whimsical Atrocity Theatre (TWAT): “I only eat vegans”.


The next day, TWAT proudly unveiled its new message to the world. It worked immediately. The show was good. I was a little bit worried that one or more of the social centre vegan punks would pass by, see the sign and beat me up. I was probably safe in my theatre, as I usually had a police escort at one side, looking out for the tourists’ safety. But they knew where I lived.


Some brave souls came and spoke to me during or after my cardboard shenanigans. But things reached dizzying heights for TWAT when an American woman came up to me and asked me how much my signs were. I was absolutely flabbergasted. Someone wanted to buy my recycled carton signs. I replied to her spontaneously that, if she wanted to buy a sign, then she had to tell me how much it was. She put four euros into my hat for “I only eat vegans”. Black permanent marker pen on quality recycled cardboard.


Women were flirting with me almost every day when I performed, but I was caught completely off guard when an extremely attractive, well-dressed young French woman came up to me with her friends, picked up the condoms and said, “OK, let’s go!” She was absolutely serious and in a pathetic response, I replied, “You’re wearing a wedding ring.” She countered with, “It’s only an engagement ring. This is my last chance. Are you coming?” Her friends’ looks assured me that she was absolutely serious. I did not go. One of her friends looked at me as though I must have been insane. One of several potentially delicious sexual opportunities that I missed in life.


As the summer really heated up, it felt as though all of Portugal’s crazy folk were coming out of the woodwork and heading for fun in Lisbon. As I worked one day, a sun-drenched, handsome, young man swaggered up the steps towards me. He wore rags as clothes, had matted, unkempt hair flopping all over his face and had a long stick over his shoulder, with a cloth bundle tied up at the other end. He asked if he could write something on one of my signs. I told him he could, so he picked up “this sign was my bed” and wrote on it, “but I washed it in my jacuzzi first”, which killed me and the audience. Then he shouted for all to hear, “We are homeless because we choose to be.”


Before his departure, he asked me if he could take a condom because …

author: PETA-Team
title: Geheimsache Tierversuche: Neue ZDF-Doku zeigt Tierleid hinter verschlossenen Labortüren
content:
Symbolbild


Die neue „37°“-Dokumentation „Geheimsache Tierversuche – Unter Ausschluss der Öffentlichkeit“ geht der Frage nach, was eigentlich mit Tieren in Versuchslaboren geschieht – und warum die Öffentlichkeit so wenig davon sehen darf.


Am 

29. September 2026 um 22:15 Uhr im ZDF

 sehen die Zuschauer:innen hinter die Kulissen einer Branche, in der Mäuse, Ratten, Hunde, Affen, Kaninchen, Schweine und viele weitere Tiere für Experimente missbraucht werden.


Millionen Tiere leiden für „wissenschaftliche Zwecke“


Nach den offiziellen Zahlen wurden in Deutschland

im Jahr 2024 über drei Millionen Tiere

 für „wissenschaftliche Zwecke“ missbraucht. Einen großen Teil nimmt die Grundlagenforschung ein, in der Tieren zum Beispiel der Schädel aufgebohrt wird, um Elektroden in ihr Gehirn zu setzen. In regulatorischen, gesetzlich vorgeschriebenen Tests werden die Tiere teils vergiftet und getötet.


Solche Experimente finden nicht irgendwo weit entfernt statt, sondern an verschiedenen Forschungseinrichtungen in Deutschland.

Experimente an Affen

, die in der Dokumentation ebenfalls thematisiert werden, sind in der Hälfte der Bundesländer vertreten.


Was passiert in den Versuchslaboren?


Für die Dokumentation hat der Journalist Manfred Karremann mehr als ein Jahr lang versucht, Einblicke in deutsche Tierversuchslabore zu bekommen. Trotz angebotener Anonymität erklärte sich nur eine Einrichtung bereit, ein wenig Einblick zu geben.


Die Dokumentation macht damit ein Problem sichtbar, das Tierschützer:innen seit Jahren kritisieren: Tierversuche finden weitgehend im Verborgenen statt. Sie werden verharmlost und die wenigsten Menschen erfahren, was den Tieren tatsächlich angetan wird. Dabei geht es um Lebewesen, die Angst und Schmerzen empfinden wie wir – und die schlichtweg nicht dazu da sind, dass wir an ihnen experimentieren.


Die Dokumentation zeigt unter anderem Aufnahmen aus einem britischen Labor. Zu sehen sind Hunde,

Affen

, Kaninchen und Ratten, die für sogenannte

Giftigkeitstests

 missbraucht werden. Die Versuche gelten als standardisierte Verfahren und werden nach internationalen Richtlinien durchgeführt – auch in der EU. Tiere müssen dabei beispielsweise Chemikalien einatmen oder bekommen Testsubstanzen über einen Schlauch direkt in den Magen verabreicht.


Jetzt lesen


Forschung und Medizin


Tierversuche in Deutschland: Was wirklich in den Versuchslaboren passiert


In deutschen Tierversuchslaboren werden Affen, Hunde, Katzen, Nagetiere, Fische & Insekten gequält. Erfahren Sie hier mehr über die Versuche!


Jetzt lesen


Tierversuche sind keine gute Wissenschaft


Tierversuche werden oft als „wissenschaftlich notwendig“ gerechtfertigt – doch die Dokumentation zeigt, dass die Wissenschaft längst mit Methoden arbeitet, die ohne Tiermissbrauch auskommen. Expert:innen aus Industrie und Wissenschaft kommen zu Wort und erklären, warum modernste Methoden wie menschliche Zellkulturen oder Organs-on-a-Chip Tierversuchen nicht nur ethisch, sondern auch wissenschaftlich überlegen sind.


Diese Ansätze arbeiten direkt mit menschlichen Zellen und menschlichem Gewebe. Dadurch können sie bei bestimmten Fragestellungen auch Erkenntnisse liefern, die sich besser auf Menschen übertragen lassen.


Jetzt einschalten und hinschauen!


Die „37°“-Dokumentation gibt einen seltenen Einblick in die abgeschottete Welt, in der Tiere in Laboren ihr Leben lang gefangen sind – und zeigt gleichzeitig, warum es längst überfällig ist, dass sich Wissenschaft und Forschung von Tierversuchen abwenden.


„37°: Geheimsache Tierversuche – Unter Ausschluss der Öffentlichkeit“

 läuft am

Dienstag, 29. September 2026, um 22:15 Uhr im ZDF.

 Ab 5:00 Uhr ist die Dokumentation auch über das ZDF-Streaming-Angebot abrufbar.


Jede Unterschrift zählt


PETA fordert von nationalen und internationalen Entscheidungsträger:innen einen strategischen Ausstieg aus Tierversuchen und eine Modernisierung der Forschung. Unterstützen Sie den Research Modernisation Deal und helfen Sie uns, grausame Tierversuche endlich zu beenden.


Jetzt unterschreiben


The post

Geheimsache Tierversuche: Neue ZDF-Doku zeigt Tierleid hinter verschlossenen Labortüren

 appeared first on

PETA Deutschland e.V.

.

title: Nourrir ou trahir. Comment l’élevage intensif saigne la France.
content:
On doit changer de modèle, découvrez comment :

Peu importe qui vous êtes et ce en quoi vous croyez : l’élevage intensif trahit vos valeurs.

Nous mangeons 85 kilos de viande par personne et par an, le double de la moyenne mondiale. Ni accident ni dérive, cette consommation de masse est le produit d’un système dont l’élevage intensif est la pierre angulaire.

Souveraineté alimentaire, santé publique, déforestation, biodiversité, ressource en eau, revenu des agriculteurs, sort des animaux : sur chacun de ces fronts, l’élevage intensif nous trahit. Il nous rend dépendants d’engrais et de soja importés, endette les éleveurs, favorise pandémies et antibiorésistance, nuit à l’environnement et entraîne l’abattage de plus de 3 millions d’animaux chaque jour pour la seule consommation française.

Nous n’avons pas choisi ce modèle. D’autres l’ont choisi pour nous. Ce livre, rédigé par Brigitte Gothière et Sébastien Arsac, cofondateurs de L214, défend une proposition pour reprendre la main ensemble : donnons-nous l’objectif de réduire de moitié le nombre d’animaux tués d’ici 2030. Parce que c’est possible. Parce que c’est vital.

d’animaux abattus chaque jour pour la seule consommation française.

Vous entrez dans un supermarché. Vous prenez un caddie. Vous suivez un itinéraire balisé. Vous voyez ce qui doit être vu, à la hauteur qu'il faut, au prix qu'il faut. Vous croisez la viande partout, les légumineuses presque nulle part. À la sortie, vous avez le sentiment d'avoir choisi.

« On nous a fait croire qu’il fallait choisir son camp : pour les agriculteurs ou pour les animaux, pour le climat ou pour la souveraineté alimentaire. Mais l’élevage intensif ne défend aucun de ces camps, il les renie tous en même temps. C’est ce que ce livre documente, chiffres à l’appui. »

« C’est un livre sur une impasse dont nous devons sortir collectivement. Réduire de moitié le nombre d’animaux tués d’ici 2030 est une nécessité, soutenue par une majorité de Français. Ceux qui croient que l’élevage intensif peut durer se bercent d’illusions. »

Nourrir ou trahir, comment l’élevage intensif saigne la France paru le 30 septembre 2026 aux éditions Payot, disponible au prix de 19 € sur notre boutique en ligne et en librairie.

author: Animal Rising Press
title: Guilty Verdict For King’s Sheep Rescuers In Theft Trial
content:
After a four-day trial at Norwich Crown Court, Rose Patterson, Sarah Foy, and Rosa Sharkey have all been found guilty of theft after the rescue of three lambs from King Charles III’s Sandringham Estate in May 2023. Sentencing to follow today.

Despite the verdict, Animal Rising claims that the rescue and subsequent trial have helped to put a spotlight on the reality behind animal farming in the UK, with over 10 million sheep being slaughtered yearly [1].

The controversial rescue made front-page news across the UK and headlines around the world [2]. It captured the attention of the British public, questioning how we relate to animals in the food system and if it’s a rescue or a theft to take them from farms.

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, alongside Rosa Sharkey and Sarah Foy, rescued the lambs - Sammy, Sunny and Sooty - before informing police the following day. The women held signs outside Windsor Castle reading “I rescued the King’s sheep” before reporting what they had done to police. They each face up to 7 years' imprisonment.

Earlier this year, Patterson was found not guilty by a jury over another Animal Rising open rescue, after helping to rescue beagle puppies from MBR Acres, a facility breeding animals for testing [3].

Animal Rising director Rose Patterson, one of the three defendants found guilty today, said:

Sammy, Sunny and Sooty remain safe and are now fully grown.

The trial followed a series of open-rescue trials relating to Animal Rising’s rescue of beagles from MBR Acres. In January this year, Animal Rising made history by securing the UK’s first-ever not-guilty verdict in an open-rescue case [4]. The lambs were rescued from Appleton Farm, which forms part of the Sandringham estate.

Defendants Patterson and Foy are available for comment or broadcast interview upon request.

For further information, comment, or to arrange an interview, please email press@animalrising.org or call +44 1225 29 6691

High-Quality Pictures and Videos: https://show.pics.io/animal-rising-breaking-news

All images and videos in this file, on our social media, and website can be used with credit to Animal Rising under ‘fair use’ for the purposes of reporting.

[1] https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/cattle-sheep-and-pig-slaughter

[2] https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-12431619/Animal-Rising-protesters-charged-stealing-Kings-sheep-royal-Sandringham-Estate-driving-away-animals.html

https://www.dailymail.com/news/article-12126009/Will-stop-eco-clowns-Just-Stop-Oil-throw-orange-powder-Animal-Rising-kidnap-lambs.html

[3] https://www.cambsnews.co.uk/peterborough-court-acquittal-animal-rescue-beagles/

[4] https://www.animalrising.org/post/not-guilty-verdict-for-beagle-puppy-rescuers-in-landmark-legal-case

Rose Patterson, 37, is the Director of Animal Rising. An advocate for animals since 2012, she holds an MSc in Animal Welfare Science, Ethics, and Law and previously worked with World Animal Protection before joining Animal Rising in 2020.

Sarah Foy, 26, has been involved in a range of campaigns advocating for a just and sustainable food system that works for animals, farmers, and the planet. She brings a practical, hands-on approach to her advocacy, with real-world experience caring for rescued farm animals at sanctuaries and protesting alongside farmers.

Rosa Sharkey, 26, is a food charity worker. She is passionately committed to reducing the impact of our food system on the climate crisis, community action, and animal rights.

Animal Rising is a nonviolent campaign group working to fundamentally transform our relationship with animals and nature, and build a more sustainable future for animals, people and the planet. Animal Rising is calling on the Government to end factory farming by 2040 and support a transition to a sustainable plant-based food system.

The group has used a variety of civil disobedience and nonviolent direct action tactics, notably blockading McDonald's distribution centres in May 2021, blockading dairy industry sites in September 2022, disrupting the 2023 Grand National, rescuing lambs belonging to King Charles III in May 2023, and carrying out the UK’s largest undercover farm investigation in 2024.

author: Sophie Lemcke
title: So ist es, als Huhn in der Fleischindustrie leben zu müssen
content:
Die Hühnermast ist ein grausames System, das auf maximale Schnelligkeit, Wachstum und Profit ausgelegt ist und mit einem gewaltvollen Tod für die Tiere endet.


Wie fühlt es sich an, als „Masthuhn“ geboren zu werden

, ohne die Möglichkeit, der leidvollen Industrie zu entkommen

?


Der einzige Grund, weshalb die Industrie dich „produziert“ hat: Du sollst so schnell wie möglich so schwer wie möglich werden – und wirst dann getötet.


Du kommst in einem Hühnerschlupfbetrieb mit tausenden anderen Küken zur Welt. Um dich herum piepsen sie verzweifelt. Und auch du suchst nach Nähe und Wärme. Aber da ist keine Mutter, in deren Gefieder du dich kuscheln kannst – und du wirst sie auch niemals kennenlernen.

Noch am ersten Tag deines Lebens wirst du über Förderbänder geschleudert und in eine Kiste gepackt. Dann beginnt die oftmals stundenlange Fahrt zum Mastbetrieb – eingepfercht mit Dutzenden anderen Küken, ohne Wasser, ohne Nahrung.


Foto: Andrew Skowron


Du kommst in einer riesigen Halle an. Hier wirst du die nächsten rund 5 Wochen verbringen – die einzigen Wochen deines Lebens.


Um dich herum Tausende andere Küken. Du teilst dir einen Quadratmeter mit bis zu 23 anderen Tieren. Jetzt seid ihr noch klein, doch das wird sich schnell ändern.


Du wächst. Unnatürlich schnell. Das Futter steht dir Tag und Nacht zur Verfügung – hochkalorisch, proteinreich, entwickelt für maximales Wachstum in kürzester Zeit.


Du hast keinen Platz, um dich natürlich zu bewegen, es gibt nichts zum Erkunden. Keinerlei Möglichkeiten, deine natürlichen Verhaltensweisen auszuleben. Es ist trist und laut. Da ist nur diese Enge.


Die Luft ist stickig. Der Ammoniakgeruch von den Ausscheidungen Tausender Tiere brennt in deinen Augen, in deinen Lungen. Du bekommst Atemwegserkrankungen. Jeder Atemzug tut weh.


Dein Körper wurde durch jahrzehntelange Züchtung so manipuliert, dass du in wenigen Wochen das Gewicht erreichst, für das ein Huhn unter natürlichen Bedingungen Monate bräuchte.


Foto: Andrew Skowron


Deine Brustmuskeln wachsen so schnell und werden so schwer, dass deine Knochen dein Gewicht nicht mehr tragen können. Deine Beine verformen sich. Dein Herz ist zu klein für deinen massiven Körper, es hat Probleme, deine Organe mit ausreichend Blut zu versorgen. Du hast Schmerzen beim Gehen und deine Gelenke sind entzündet.


Um dich herum sind Hühner, die gar nicht mehr aufstehen können. Sie liegen in ihrem eigenen Kot und leiden unter extremen Schmerzen. Sie verdursten und verhungern.


Andere Hühner werden aufgrund der Enge von ihren Artgenossen versehentlich totgetrampelt und erdrückt – ihre Körper verwesen zwischen dir und den tausenden anderen Tieren. Auch du hast keine Chance, den anderen Hühnern auszuweichen.


Dann ist es soweit. Menschen kommen und packen dich. An deinen Beinen, kopfüber, werden du und deine Artgenossen gegriffen und in enge Transportkisten geworfen. Deine ohnehin schon schmerzenden Beine brechen unter der groben Behandlung. Du hast Schmerzen und Todesangst.


Zusammengepfercht, ohne Wasser, ohne Futter, geht es zum Schlachthof. Die Fahrt kann Stunden dauern. Manche Hühner sterben bereits im Transporter – vor Stress, vor Erschöpfung, erdrückt von anderen Tieren.


Foto: Andrew Skowron


Im Schlachthof riechst du Blut. Du hörst die Schreie anderer Hühner. Dann bist du selbst an der Reihe. Unter grausamen Bedingungen wirst du betäubt und getötet. Du bist gerade einmal 35 bis 42 Tage alt geworden.


Es ist unvorstellbar, was Hühner in der Fleischindustrie erleiden müssen.


Die Wahrheit hinter „Hähnchenfleisch“


Wie grausam das kurze Leben von sogenannten Masthühnern ist, haben wir schon mehrfach bei Undercover-Recherchen aufgedeckt, beispielsweise in einem (jetzt ehemaligen) Zuliefererbetrieb der großen Marke Wiesenhof. Hier erfährst du mehr über unsere Aufdeckungen und kannst unsere Petition für strengere Tierschutzvorgaben, -kontrollen und -strafen unterzeichnen:


Jetzt für Hühner unterschreiben 


In Deutschland wird mehr Fleisch von Hühnern konsumiert als produziert – und die Nachfrage ist in den vergangenen Jahren stetig gestiegen. Unterstütze dieses grausame System nicht: Entscheide dich konsequent für pflanzliche Lebensmittel.


In den meisten Supermärkten findest du mittlerweile eine Vielfalt tierfreundlicher Alternativen, die hervorragende Proteinquellen sind – probiere sie aus. Oder koche unsere zahlreichen pflanzlichen Rezepte von Love Veg nach, wie unsere

knusprigen Tofu-Nuggets

.


Erfahre mehr:

title: Eggesford in the Dock: Huntsman Convicted of Illegal Hunting
content:
Eggesford Hunt huntsman Jason Marles has been convicted of illegally hunting a fox with hounds following an incident captured on drone footage during the hunt’s Boxing Day meet in December 2025.


Jason Marles, huntsman of the Eggesford Hunt.


Marles, 44, pleaded guilty to hunting a wild mammal with dogs at Pudson Farm, near Okehampton, when he appeared before Exeter Magistrates’ Court on 23 September 2026.


His conviction followed footage recorded by Devon County Hunt Saboteurs which showed a fox being bolted from an area of rubble before being pursued by hounds. Hunt saboteurs positioned on a farm track nearby were in position to stop the hounds from chasing the fox, and they confirmed that the fox managed to evade capture.


The footage shows Marles standing beside the area where the fox had taken refuge, close to a cattle barn. Two men with spades are moving rubble and digging at the site, while a child, who had dismounted from their pony, also watches what is happening.


Huntsman Jason Marles looks on as landowner Lloyd Heard and terrier-man Tom Bounsall dig and remove the rubble protecting the hunted fox. Image credit: Devon County Hunt Saboteurs.


Devon County Hunt Sabs identify the two men digging as Eggesford terrier man Tom Bounsall and landowner Lloyd Heard.


WATCH THE VIDEO


After Marles realised a drone was overhead, and they had walked back to the farmyard, Marles and Heard swapped coats in a comical, and ultimately futile attempt to avoid identification.


Huntsman Jason Marles wearing Lloyd Heard’s jacket after the dig out. Tom Bounsall follows behind on a quad. Image: Devon County Hunt Saboteurs.


Bounsall is a terrier-man for both the Eggesford Hunt and the Spooners & West Dartmoor Hunt. Pictured here at a Spooners meet in March 2026. Image: Plymouth & West Devon Hunt Sabs.


After several minutes, the fox bolts from its refuge and runs for the surrounding cover. The hounds follow, beginning the chase. No attempt to call the hounds back was made.


Heard was also charged alongside Marles with hunting offences relating to both the Boxing Day incident at Pudson Farm and a second incident near Crediton in February 2026.


As the landowner of Pudson Farm, Heard also faced a further charge under Section 3 of the Hunting Act of knowingly permitting his land to be used for hunting a wild mammal with dogs.


Lloyd Heard, landowner of Pudson Farm, where the fox was dug out and subsequently pursued by hounds. Image: Devon County Hunt Saboteurs.


The proceedings against Heard were

subsequently withdrawn by the prosecution

. No reason for that decision has been made public.


Heard also has a close family connection to the leadership of hunting’s governing body. He is the son-in-law of British Hound Sports Association

Executive Director Julian Barnfield

.


Barnfield is himself a former huntsman with previous Hunting Act convictions. Whilst huntsman of the Heythrop Hunt, he pleaded guilty to

four separate counts of unlawfully hunting foxes

 between 2011 and 2012.


Julian Barnfield (right), who turned up to Crewe Magistrates court in 2022 to support another convicted fox hunter – former Quorn Huntsman Ollie Finnegan (left). Image: Cheshire Against Blood Sports (CABS).


Barnfield also has a longstanding connection to former Prime Minister David Cameron. In 2008, when Barnfield was facing an earlier prosecution under the Hunting Act, Cameron – then leader of the Opposition and Barnfield’s constituency MP –

wrote to the Attorney General on his behalf

 following a private meeting between the two. Those proceedings against Barnfield were subsequently discontinued on a technical issue.


The connection is worth noting. The Heythrop was David Cameron’s local hunt, and

he rode with it on numerous occasions

 before the Hunting Act came into force. It is also reported that David Cameron is ‘friendly’ with Barnfield, Heard’s father-in-law.


David Cameron

 pictured with the Heythrop Hunt in 2004. Image: Daily Mail.


Cameron remains a vocal supporter of fox hunting. As recently as September 2026,

he described the incoming ban on so-called ‘trail hunting

’ as “completely wrong”, urging the minority within the rural community who support hunting to “stand together and fight together”.


None of this establishes that political connections played any part in the decision to drop the charges against Heard. But it does illustrate something that has long characterised fox hunting – those who enjoy hunting …

author: Frey Blake-Pijogge
title: In a warming Arctic, Inuit bear guards protect communities
content:
This story is published through the Indigenous News Alliance.


After retiring from a long career as a conservation officer with the Canadian government, Derrick Pottle devoted himself to guiding people on the land, carving, hunting, and training bear guards.


Pottle, an elder and skilled guide from the Inuit community of Tikigâksuagusik in Nunatsiavut, founded BearSafe Planning in 2005. The program trains and certifies students to guard against the polar bears and black bears found throughout northern Labrador. The three-day course is advertised as offering “safety, protection, confidence in bear country.”


More than two decades later, that work has taken on renewed urgency. As climate change reshapes the Arctic — particularly the sea ice polar bears rely on to travel and hunt — Inuit are seeing the animals at different times of year and in places they rarely encountered before. Pottle says those changes are increasing the need for people who know

how to keep people and bears safe

. That, he said, is “the whole objective of the course.”


Graduates of the program keep watch for bears to prevent encounters and learn to recognize signs that a bear is not comfortable. “They may feel threatened, they may feel intimidated, and they may even charge or attack you,” Pottle said. He teaches students “how to recognize those signs, how to prepare yourself for them, the tools you have to use to do your job.”


Canadian officials say encounters between people and polar bears

are becoming more likely

 as a lengthening ice-free season keeps bears on land longer. Inuit and Cree communities have reported polar bears appearing more frequently and in places where they were once rare. Researchers have

linked the increase to several factors

, including longer ice-free periods, changes in bear abundance and condition, and growing human activity in polar bear habitat. 


Pottle developed BearSafe Planning’s training program with input from groups that included Parks Canada, conservationists, Inuit elders, and academics. It started “out of a necessity,” Pottle said, after the creation of Tongait KakKasuangita SilakKijapvinga, (Torngat Mountains National Park) under the 2005 Labrador Inuit Land Claims Agreement. 


“They needed bear guards,” Pottle said. We didn’t have trainers in Nunatsiavut at the time. Somebody had to do it.”


Inuk elder Derrick Pottle founded BearSafe Planning in 2005 to keep people and bears safe. That work has taken on renewed urgency as climate change reshapes the Arctic and encounters with bears grow more common.


Frey Blake-Pijogge / IndigiNews


The Arctic is warming

nearly four times faster

 than the rest of the planet. As climate change remakes landscapes across the North, the need for guards is only for “all species of bears,” Pottle said. 


“We’re seeing more and more bears now in this time of our lives than we ever saw before,” he said.  “People are seeing polar bears in this part of Inuit Nunangat — where polar bears used to travel north late in the spring — and now are staying all summer long.”


The province’s Endangered Species Act lists polar bears as “vulnerable,” while the federal government deems them a “species of special concern.” Sixty to 80 per cent of the world’s polar bear population lives in Canada, according to Environment and Climate Change Canada. The massive carnivores, which can weigh as much as 1,400 pounds, rely upon sea ice to travel, mate, and hunt. “Climate change is the main threat to polar bears,” the agency notes.


Becoming a bear guard can offer employment opportunities, but also can be used for personal safety. “Lots of people just use the bear guard course for their own personal protection when they’re out on the land with their families fishing, hunting and participating in Inuit lifestyle.”


Sherri Wolfrey, a mother of four, is a trained bear guard in Tikigâksuagusik. She recounted how, in 2015, she became “interested in the program and just thought ‘OK, maybe someday I might want to try for a job that involves bear monitoring.’”


Wolfrey is the secretary of Northern Lights Academy and uses her training when she’s out on the land. Last year, she put her certification to work professionally for the first time, when she was contracted as a bear guard in Akami-Uapishkᵁ-KakKasuak (Mealy Mountains National Park Reserve). “Especially up in that area in the bottom of the Mealy’s, it was so beautiful up there,” she told IndigiNews.


She finds the skills valuable even …

author: Emma Honeybun
title: Educators say introducing kids to reconciliation requires kinship, cultural approach
content:
When it comes to educating kids about truth and reconciliation, several educators in Winnipeg are approaching the subject with an air of culture, rather than caution.


To mark the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation (NDTR), several organizations offered educational opportunities for families to engage with survivors, knowledge keepers, and Indigenous teachers to learn more about the outstanding impact of residential schools, as well as engage with First Nations cultures and storytelling.


When it comes to what occurred at residential schools, parents, teachers and relatives are often tasked with the challenge of approaching the subject in a way that does not cause further harm.


The Kapabamayak Achaak Healing Forest in Winnipeg, which saw approximately 600 students the week of the NDTR this year, handles the responsibility in a variety of ways.


The forest, which is centred by a gathering space with room for a sacred fire, was established in 2016 and has since been a community resource and “living memorial,”

according to its website

, “to honour Indigenous children lost to or affected by the residential school system.”


Kerry Saner-Harvey has been involved since the beginning. He noted that “age-appropriateness is important.”


He said that, until children reach a certain age, residential schools are not covered in depth.


“We get a whole range,” he said. “One group was grades two, three… our Elder was very good about saying kids were hurt, but not saying details.”


On the other hand, Saner-Harvey continued, kids from the junior high groups heard more stories about “what actually happened.”


He said, when it comes to educating kids, “being able to just be present is significant.”


The space is looked after by a group of volunteers called the keepers of the forest. The keepers take care of the space, located in the back corner of St. John’s Park in Winnipeg’s North End neighbourhood, as well as function similarly to board members.


Many are members of the congregation at the neighbouring St. John’s Anglican Cathedral, which founded the area in collaboration with community Elders.


Saner-Harvey said the opportunity to teach these subjects outside, on the land, is also significant.


“Reconnecting with the land, to remind us that a reason that this happened is because [it was taken away],” he said.


He said the stories read at the gathering space have a heavy focus on the relationship with the land, but it’s presented in ways that are universal.


“Finding your sit-spot … rocks,” he said, with a laugh. “Things like that are a way to remind kids of the teachings that were lost, and that they can be relearned. The knowledge is still there, so let’s relearn that. It’s not just about learning the atrocities.”


Georges Beaudry addresses a class at the Kapabamayak Achaak Healing Forest last year. Photo: Kapabamayak Achaak Healing Forest.


Michael Redhead Champagne, a member of Shamattawa First Nation, is a public speaker and children’s author. He said he approaches the subject in two ways.


Firstly, he said, “the kinship approach.


“Just explain. People were taken from their families, and one way to make that better is to repair families,” he said. “Then, the education approach, where we say schools hurt Indigenous kids in the past. Let’s make sure school today help Indigenous Peoples.”


He can even then mesh the two into one sentence, he said — what can schools do today to support families who were hurt in the past?


“[The approaches] provide opportunities to learn and build relationships,” Redhead Champagne said, adding that through its simplicity, it works with adults, too.


For example, the Kapabamayak Achaak Healing Forest hosted an event on the morning of Sept. 30, when residential school survivor Gerry Shingoose, known by many as “Gramma Shingoose” in her community advocacy work, shared her story to a small crowd of varying ages around a sacred fire.


It was closed with the Travelling Song, performed by Knowledge Keeper Heather Bjorklund, accompanied by her daughter and granddaughter. Although, the youngest spent much of the song hiding in her mother’s jacket to avoid the crowd.


Redhead Champagne said it was an appropriate finish to the gathering, as it was an “act of intergenerational love.”


The power to act


Learning about reconciliation can be hands-on, too.


While the forest is volunteer-operated, similar approaches emphasizing kinship and reconnection exist in a national …

title: Besê Hozat: Women are the vanguard of this process and its defining force
content:
Besê Hozat, co-chair of the KCK Executive Council, said in an interview with Medya Haber that the Peace and Democratic Society Process cannot succeed in Turkey without democratization.


The first part of the interview can be read

here

.


A campaign has been launched by a number of writers, intellectuals, and politicians in this regard – taking responsibility within this process – called “1001 Signatures.” Presuming that you are aware of this campaign, how do you assess it?


This, for example, is truly a meaningful and valuable initiative. It needs to be expanded further and make it more widespread. What is Turkey’s fundamental impasse? In Turkey, many groups are waging their struggles in their own separate spheres. These struggles do not converge, do not unite, and do not transform into synergy. The women’s movement is waging a struggle on its own front, the youth on theirs, the ecological and environmental movements on theirs, workers on theirs, peasants on theirs, and the democratic forces on theirs – everyone is waging a struggle in their own neighborhood, on their own periphery, in their own lane. If we think of each of these as a river, every river flows from a different place and flows to a different destination. If these rivers were to merge, if these dynamics of struggle were to come together and transform into a common, united struggle, this would give rise to a very powerful democratic movement in Turkey – a very powerful democratic dynamic – and this process would also foster a strong sense of ownership. It would play a decisive role in the success of the Peace and Democratic Society Process.


This newly launched initiative, developed primarily by intellectuals, is very valuable and meaningful. But if it remains limited to intellectuals alone – and if it is confined solely to a petition drive with a thousand or so signatures, or a stance that barely goes beyond that – it certainly has meaning and value, however, in terms of the results it will produce, its impact would remain limited.


There was also a decision by autonomous women’s organizations. They will organize a conference – involving artists, politicians, intellectuals, and academics – to discuss women’s role in the Peace and Democratic Society process and to create a common front against male and state violence.


Correct. Women have also launched a process under the name “Side by Side,” a process of struggle. I believe they will hold a meeting in late October or early November, where they will develop a joint plan for their struggle. And it will be a united and collective struggle. This is very important. So, this struggle led by women unites all workers, environmental and ecological movements, and all democratic forces in Turkey into a single pot if it transforms into a common struggle, and if the central demand of all those at the heart of this struggle is, after all, democracy, freedom, equality, justice, and a shared, democratic life – then this will give serious rise to a very powerful democratic movement in Turkey. It will also play a decisive role in the success of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, and I am convinced that it will accelerate this process.


It will also create serious pressure on the government. It will compel both the government and the state to take democratic, political, and legal steps more quickly, without dragging their feet. This can only happen through struggle. Sitting back and watching, waiting, or having everyone continue this limited struggle only in their own neighborhoods will not lead this process to success in the short term. I reiterate that these struggles do have meaning, but we need to bring them together in a joint effort, transforming them into a common struggle and a shared synergy. This will bring to the fore a very strong democratic will, power, and movement and will compel the state and the government to take democratic steps. It will facilitate the swift advancement of this process. We need to develop this further.


The same applies to women. Women are the pioneers of this process. They are its vanguard and its defining force. They are the driving force behind the construction of a democratic society – its fundamental building block. This process will develop under women’s leadership, with their significant and active participation and struggle. Women must be able to bring their struggle together with other democratic dynamics in society and unite them. They must succeed in …

author: Dennis Pillion
title: Trump Rollback of Fuel Economy Standards Will Deal Blows to Climate and Health
content:
“There’s nothing Trump won’t sacrifice on the altar of fealty to Big Oil and auto polluters,” said one critic.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The Trump administration Monday finalized the rollback of a major fuel economy standard for cars and trucks, a move critics say will cause more climate-warming pollution, human health problems and higher fuel costs for consumers.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, a part of the Department of Transportation, published new Corporate Average Fuel Economy standards Monday, greatly reducing the fuel efficiency for new passenger cars and light trucks made between 2022 and 2031.

The Department of Transportation estimates that the new standards would correspond to an industry fleetwide average of about 34.9 miles per gallon for new vehicles in model year 2031. The previous standard, set in 2022 during the Biden administration, would have required around 50.4 miles per gallon, driving automakers to invest more heavily in gasoline-free electric vehicles.

The DOT said in a news release the move would give automakers more flexibility, reduce the average cost of a new vehicle and encourage new car sales. The Trump administration continued to call the Biden rules an EV “mandate.”

“Thanks to President Trump’s leadership, we have finally ended the illegal mandate that forced automakers to produce more expensive electric vehicles that American families didn’t want,” Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said.

The Alliance for Automotive Innovation, a group that advocates on behalf of auto manufacturers, praised the new standards.

“The standards finalized under the previous administration effectively required a switchover to electric vehicles that was out of step with market realities and customer demand,” John Bozella the Alliance’s president and CEO, said in a news release. “Today’s final rule is an appropriate course correction.”

But the changes will likely mean that new cars produced will be less efficient and emit more greenhouse gases and harmful air pollutants that studies show are responsible for 9 million deaths per year worldwide.

“Today’s rule to weaken fuel economy standards will create more air pollution, harm health and accelerate climate change,” American Lung Association President and CEO Harold Wimmer said in a news release.

“For decades, fuel economy standards have ensured that new cars, SUVs and pickup trucks are more efficient, which saves lives and money,” Wimmer said. “There is no reason to weaken standards that are technologically feasible and have a direct benefit for the quality of the air people breathe.”

Transportation accounts for about 28 percent of U.S. greenhouse gas emissions, according to the Environmental Protection Agency, more than electric power generation (25 percent) or industry (23 percent).

Monday’s rule finalized plans Trump announced in December to reduce the fuel efficiency standards. But in between, the war in Iran has sent gas prices skyrocketing to an average of $4.48 per gallon, according to the American Automobile Association.

Jason Schwartz, regulatory policy director at the Institute for Policy Integrity at New York University’s School of Law, said the repeal will result in higher fuel costs for consumers and make them more vulnerable to “price shocks” in the cost of gasoline.

“The 2024 fuel-economy standards were projected to save consumers $80 billion in fuel costs and reduce more than $125 billion in damages from climate change,” Schwartz said. “Today, [the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration] made those savings disappear, and households that are already stretched thin will pay the price.”

The Institute for Policy Integrity says more than $17 billion in projected annual consumer savings are now at risk due to regulatory rollbacks by the Trump administration.

Environmental and health groups and others say they plan to contest the new standards.

“Americans need relief from high costs, but instead Trump is giving automakers a free pass on pollution and handing families the bill — at the pump and with their health,” Katherine García, director of the Sierra Club’s Clean Transportation for All program, said in a news release.

“The Sierra Club will fight this senseless rollback every step of the way,” Garcia said. “We’re going to continue to fight back against this administration’s dangerous and costly attacks on cleaner …

content:

I’m always a bit annoyed when some ecoactivists are are all

“Hope! Degrowth! The planet can heal!”

 without giving an honest time frame for that.

Like, even if we manage to end capitalism and degrow an all of that, the CO2 that’s already in the air will continue to heat up the planet for decades and the results of that will be with us for this century at the very least.

Yes,

ecosystems can heal,

yes,

 that’s worth fighting for. But it’ll get worse before it gets better and most of us won’t be there for the good parts. You can leave that out to spread “Hope”, but all that will do is make people optimistic for a short time only for them to feel hurt and betrayed when they figure out the truth.

An worse then feeling cheated our of a bright future, people acting on this false optimistic worldview won’t build the kind of support networks that we are going to need to survive our real future. Preparing for a more ecologically unstable earth must be part of our work, even as we continue to strive for the end of capitalism an a shift to a far more sustainable way of living.

Basically, if you’re trying to boost your movement this way, your eco-activism strategy is…ehhh.. unsustainable?


What are ways we can prepare for a more ecologically unstable Earth? I honestly don’t feel very hopeful that we’re going to overthrow capitalism in time and even if we do, like you said, the Earth is going to continue to heat up. Trying to find ways to cope with and prepare for that reality actually feel more hopeful and realistic to me and I’d love to learn about them.


There are a lot of things you can do, here’s a few:

Get into the habit of sharing stuff for free with others.

We’re probably going to experience some forms of scarcity and when that happens, all we have is each other. Self-sufficiency is a myth, community self-sufficiency isn’t. Create neighborhood resources. A tool-sharing shed or a water
filter for ground or rain water could make a difference here and now,
but will also matter in the future.

Advance mode:
Start Mutual Aid collectives.

Learn first aid and other emergency medical skills.

 Whether your region is vulnerable to heat waves, wild fires, flooding, drought, extreme cold or electrical failures, there will be people in need of help an medical systems are unlikely to be able to cope with it all. Learning to take care of others is always useful, even if you’re lucky enough to not experience any disasters at all.

Advanced mode: Start a DIY medicine collective or learn an advance skill like growing medicinal herbs or physical therapy.


Learn to break the law.

As the crisis deepens, governments will let more
 and more people fall through the cracks. Refugees and undocumented
people are likely to be the first targets but other minorities can be
targetted too. Those people won’t be able to survive unless people are
willing to break the law to get them housing, food, etc.

Advanced mode:
get experience breaking the law together and put it to work actually
helping undocumented people.


Learn to support each other.

 Our mental health is as important as our physical health and to truly support each other we need more than good intentions.
Learn psychological first aid, learn how to structurally support trauma survivors, people who are mourning, people struggling with depression and more.

Advanced mode: start a Support & Recovery collective.

Work on building a community without discrimination and systematic injustice.

 All of the things to come will hit the most marginalized harder. We can only get through it together if our communities truly value everyone in it and we understand that an injury to one is an injury to all. Learn about systematic oppression, learn about privilege, learn about conflict resolution an mediation and put that to work in your community.

Advanced mode: start a transformative justice collective.

… and more.

Important: don’t take on every burden, pick a few things you enjoy doing

. None of us can do all of the above and none of us can single-highhandedly prepare our whole community for what is to come. Find a way you can support your community and trust that others will do the same.

title: El pueblo Mbyá resiste y lucha
content:
La resistencia y lucha de los pueblos originarios, hoy en día se lleva a cabo de diversas formas y con distintas estrategias, por eso queremos hacer notar los esfuerzos que desde diferentes espacios se suman a lo que ya se viene haciendo desde hace un tiempo.


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/MBYA-KAY-PACHA.mp3


https://argentina.indymedia.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/MBYA-KAY-PACHA.mp3


Descargar audio


Y en este caso nos referimos al pueblo Mbyá guaraní de Misiones, que además de las movilizaciones, y las distintas gestiones para enfrentar las amenazas contra sus derechos y territorios, encontramos a jóvenes comunicadores que se ocupan de difundir, explicar y reflexionar sobre los diferentes temas que tienen como protagonistas a distintas comunidades de su pueblo.  Nos referimos al joven William Ayala conocido como Wilicho.


También destacamos la resistencia de la comunidad Puente Quemado II, que a pesar del desalojo, detención de algunos hermanos y amenazas del empresario forestal Alfredo Ruff, volvieron a su tierra y en forma pacífica pero segura, se instalaron nuevamente en el lugar de donde no debieron haber salido nunca.


Al mismo tiempo no dejamos de reconocer la importancia de la organización  del pueblo Mbyá, que a través del Aty Ñechiró viene discutiendo y tomando decisiones que acompañan a las comunidades en la defensa de sus territorios.


Por eso decimos que son diferentes formas de resistencia y lucha, pero las tres son válidas y necesarias, y por eso queremos destacarlas, haciendo conocerlas.


Escucharemos a un joven Mbyá que participó en la reunión del Aty Ñechiró, a Wilicho y a Santiago Ramos, cacique de la Comunidad Puente Quemado II.


El Micro Kay Pacha se realiza con el apoyo de la organización Otto per Mille-Chiessa Valdense.

Avec la participation de personnes qui rendront compte des avancées des groupes de « Buscador@s » souhaitant participer aux rencontres (Centre des droits humains Fray Bartolomé de las Casas) ; des finances pour le voyage (collectif Llegó la hora de los pueblos [L’heure des peuples est arrivée]) ; de l’hébergement et du ravitaillement de la délégation zapatiste et des groupes de « Buscador@s » (Casa Samir Flores Soberanes) ; des campagnes artistiques menées pour récolter des fonds ; de la liste des activités proposées pour décembre 2026-janvier 2027 au centre du pays (collectif Red Universitaria Anticapitalista – RUA [Réseau Universitaire Anticapitaliste] ; des activités qui sont déjà réalisées par divers groupes de musique, Otroas, quartiers, danseurs et danseuses, étudiantes et étudiants (à l’exclusion de l’IA, bien entendu) ; et la participation de la Commission Sexta Zapatiste qui précisera les objectifs du voyage initial de la Tournée pour la Vie Chapitre Mexique (Commission Sexta Zapatiste).

­ – Retour le dimanche 4 octobre.

Les sessions d’information seront transmises en direct. Étant donné que cela représente un coût et d’éventuels problèmes économiques, de santé, professionnels et/ou familiaux, il est recommandé de ne pas tous venir, mais d’envoyer quelqu’un·e qui pourra relayer les informations détaillées. Ou bien de demander à l’une des personnes qui se rendront sur place qu’elle vous transmette ces informations et qu’elle recueille vos doutes et vos questions pendant les pauses pour les soumettre à la réunion en présentiel.

Il s’agira donc d’une réunion hybride : en présentiel et virtuelle.

Nous ferons connaître prochainement l’adresse électronique pour la transmission en direct.

Il n’est pas nécessaire de s’inscrire à l’avance pour la session physique/en présentiel. Vous pourrez vous inscrire à votre arrivée au CIDECI.

Depuis les montagnes du Sud-est mexicain.

Sous-commandant insurgé Moisés. Mexique, septembre 2026.

author: Unknown
title: 'Aile Sağlığı Merkezleri, satılacak bina değil, sağlık merkezidir'
content:
Eylem Nazlıer [email protected]

Türkiye’de koruyucu, birinci basamak sağlık hizmetlerinin yurttaşla buluştuğu en önemli noktalardan biri olan Aile Sağlığı Merkezlerinin (ASM) geleceği, merkezlerin fiziki koşullarından kira giderlerine, deprem güvenliğinden personel eksikliğine kadar risk altında. Kamuya ait binalarda bile kiralarına yüzde 300’e varan zamlar istenen ASM’lerde aile hekimleri zor durumda.

Birlik ve Dayanışma Sendikası Genel Başkanı Dr. Ahmet Mehlepçi, ASM’lerin mümkün olduğunca kamuya ait, depreme dayanıklı ve sağlık hizmetinin gerektirdiği fiziki standartlara uygun binalarda hizmet vermesi gerektiğine vurgu yaparak “ASM’ler yalnızca hekim, ebe ve hemşirelerin görev yaptığı binalar değildi. ASM’ler; koruyucu sağlık hizmetlerinin, gebe, bebek ve çocuk izlemlerinin, bağışıklama hizmetlerinin, kronik hastalık takiplerinin ve vatandaşın sağlık sistemiyle ilk temasının gerçekleştiği temel sağlık kuruluşlarıdır” hatırlatmasını yaptı. Bu nedenle ASM’lerin geleceğine ilişkin kararların yalnızca bina, taşınmaz veya bütçe konusu olarak değerlendirilemeyeceğini dile getiren Mehlepçi, “Konu doğrudan sağlık hizmetine erişim, hizmetin sürekliliği ve kamu yararıdır” diye konuştu.

Sağlık Bakanı Kemal Memişoğlu’nun Kasım 2025’te 1000 yeni ASM yapacaklarını açıklamasından bu yana sadece 278 ASM’nin hizmete girdiğini, 370 ASM’nin inşaatının sürdüğünü ve 352 ASM’nin proje aşamasında olduğu bilgisini veren Mehlepçi, Türkiye genelinde ise yaklaşık 8 bin 300 ASM bulunduğunu söyledi.

Yeni ASM yatırımlarının elbette önemli olduğunu belirten Mehlepçi, mevcut merkezlerin ise kentsel dönüşüm, deprem riski, yüksek kiralar veya taşınmaz satışları nedeniyle hizmet dışı kalmasının önlenmesi gerektiğini vurguladı.

Bir taraftan yeni ASM’ler yapılırken diğer taraftan mevcut merkezlerin kentsel dönüşüm, deprem riski, yüksek kiralar veya taşınmaz satışları nedeniyle hizmet dışı kalma tehlikesiyle karşı karşıya olduğuna dikkati çeken Mehlpeçi “Mart 2026’da TBMM’ye sunulan soru önergesine verilen cevapta İstanbul Kadıköy’deki 33 ASM’den 7’sinin kentsel dönüşüm nedeniyle yıkıldığı ve hizmet veremez hale geldiğini söyledi. Mahlepçi kaç yeni ASM açıldığı kadar, kaç ASM’nin kapandığı, yıkıldığı, tahliye edildiği, taşındığı veya başka bir ASM’nin içine sıkıştırıldığının da kamuoyuyla paylaşılması gerektiğini aktardı.

ASM binalarının deprem güvenliğinin de önemli bir sorun olduğunu belirten Mehlepçi, 2025 yılında yapılan bir çalışmada ASM binalarının yaklaşık üçte birinin 1999 öncesinde inşa edildiğinin ortaya çıktığını söyledi. 6 Şubat 2023 yaşanan depremlerde ortaya çıkan tablonun bu konuda vahim olduğunu hatırlatan Mehlepçi “2026 yılı başında sahadan elde edilen verilere göre Hatay’da 96 ASM konteynerlerde hizmet veriyor. 103 ASM kendi binasında hizmet vermeye devam ediyor ancak bunların bir bölümü deprem güvenliği açısından risk taşıyor. Yaklaşık 56 ASM ise tahliye veya yıkım sürecinde” dedi.

Öte yandan ASM’ler için sorunun yalnızca deprem güvenliğiyle sınırlı olmadığını, ASM’lerdeki sağlık hizmetinin niteliği ve çalışanların koşullarını etkileyen başka fiziki sorunların bulunduğunu da dile getiren Mehlepçi durumu şöyle anlattı: “Penceresi, yeterli mekanik havalandırması bulunmayan kan alma odaları, lavabosu olmayan, iki veya üç sağlık çalışanının aynı odayı kullanmak zorunda kaldığı ASM’ler de var. Hatta bazı çalışma alanları hasta mahremiyetini sağlamaya da elverişli değil.”

Yıkım veya tahliye kararı verilen merkezlerde görev yapan sağlık çalışanlarının başka bir ASM’nin mutfağına, dinlenme odasına veya ortak kullanım alanına yerleştirilerek yeni bir aile hekimliği birimi oluşturulmasının kalıcı bir çözüm olmadığının altını çizen Mehlepçi, “Bir sağlık hizmetinin verilebilmesi için yalnızca bir oda bulunması yeterli değildir. O alanın sağlık hizmetinin niteliğine, çalışan güvenliğine ve hasta mahremiyetine uygun olması gerekir” dedi.

Kamusal sağlık hizmeti sunulan ASM’lerde yükün önemli bir bölümünün aile hekimlerinin üzerine yıkıldığına ve özellikle büyükşehirlerde uygun bina bulmanın giderek zorlaştığına işaret eden Mehlepçi “Kiralar da ASM’lerin sürdürülebilirliğini tehdit eden seviyelere ulaştı. Aylık 100 bin TL ve üzerinde kira ödeyen ASM örnekleri var. Elazığ’da bazı ASM’ler yüzde 350’ye varan kira artış talepleriyle karşılaştı. ASM’ler birer ticarethane değildir. Burada yürütülen faaliyet kamu sağlık hizmetidir” uyarısını yaparak buna rağmen yüksek kira bedellerinin yanı sıra elektrik, su, doğalgaz, temizlik, bakım-onarım …

author: Lisa Song
title: New Rule Would Ban the Use of Federal Grant Money for Voter Registration Drives
content:
Advocates worry that the loss of federal funding will effectively disenfranchise many voters with disabilities.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Without Amy Miller, some elderly and disabled people wouldn’t be able to vote.

The attorney for Disability Rights Nebraska travels the state, investigating the quality of nursing homes and assisted living facilities. As she reminds the residents how they can report abuse or neglect, she also offers voter registration forms. Last month, she helped a veteran with a traumatic brain injury fill out change-of-address paperwork so he could vote in the upcoming midterm elections. “He 100% knew who he wanted to vote for,” Miller said, but he struggled to write with a pen.

Congress funds her organization’s efforts to ensure that even people who might not have access to the internet or transportation have the opportunity to participate in elections.

Now a White House proposal threatens that work.

The White House Office of Management and Budget wants to change spending rules to prohibit anyone from using federal grant money for voter registration drives or what it vaguely calls “related activities.” The office is headed by Russell Vought, who has long criticized the use of taxpayer money for voter registration efforts and who more recently used his position to cancel, freeze or redirect vast amounts of federal funding in defiance of Congress’ orders.

Miller, who has worked at her nonprofit for six years, said she’s never faced regulators wanting to impede her work.

“Shutting that down and making it more difficult for these Americans to access the ballot box is bewildering to me,” she said.

The proposal is part of the Trump administration’s broader assault on federal efforts to expand access to voting, especially among groups that have historically faced discrimination and disenfranchisement.

President Donald Trump has championed the SAVE America Act, a bill that would require people to provide documents proving their citizenship when registering to vote, and that may require everyone to deliver that proof in person, which would effectively end voter registration drives.

Last year, the Trump administration banned nongovernmental organizations from conducting registration drives at naturalization ceremonies, though the agency temporarily lifted the ban amid litigation over the policy change. The Department of Education also sent a letter to colleges and universities stating that they could not use federal work-study dollars to support voting-related work. (The directive has been contested.) Previously, those funds were used to pay students who had part-time jobs to conduct voter registration on campus and in neighboring communities.

And on the first day of Trump’s second term, the president rescinded an executive order signed by Joe Biden that had directed federal agencies to expand opportunities for registration. Biden’s order acknowledged that some Americans, including Black citizens and people with disabilities, face historic and ongoing barriers to voting access.

Neither Vought nor his office responded to ProPublica’s questions about the proposed change. But in a letter sent to state officials in 2022, he condemned Biden’s executive order as a “power grab” that would “increase voter registration and turnout, especially among Democratic Party supporters.”

Vought’s proposed change, which wouldn’t go into effect until after the 2026 midterms, could have ramifications for the next presidential election well beyond voting accessibility.

Nonprofits that receive government funds to help people sign up for Medicaid benefits, food stamps or other programs subject to the National Voter Registration Act are required to provide registration forms and help people fill them out. Like Disability Rights Nebraska, these groups would be caught between contradictory federal directives if the proposed ban is finalized.

Thousands more nonprofits receive federal funds for other services but provide voter outreach using private donations. Nonprofit experts said the confusion over which groups the ban affects and the burden of proving an organization is in compliance could lead many to pause or curb registration efforts ahead of the 2028 election. Colleges and universities that help students navigate registering to vote while away from home could be similarly affected.

author: Slingshot robot #1
title: Mental Health Reminders
content:
These are dark times. It is, in fact, the world that is crazy – despair and anxiety are natural responses to watching society destroy itself for the wealthy and powerful. But by reaching out to each other, we can find the courage to stay engaged with the world, to survive, and to fight back. Mental health and mental health crises vary a lot between people, and are often intertwined with class, race, gender, and activism. These suggestions are generic, but may be useful for yourself or others. If you find yourself or someone you love having delusional thinking or consider self-harm or other violence, these suggestions probably aren’t enough. Remember that it is okay to reach out for professional help!

• Our brains are connected to our bodies, so physical health can help with mental distress. Eating healthy food on a regular schedule and getting enough sleep are necessary for mental stability and sustained activism. Exercise, dance, and physical movement help, too. So can fresh air and having a stable, calming place to stay. Try to recognize if you’re missing one of these, and if that’s causing distress.

• An important component of mental health is the ability to know ourselves, understand our needs, and be able to talk about them to the other people in our lives. This can be really challenging and can often take guidance from others who have learned how to do it with one another.

• It can help to have language for mental crisis that feels comfortable and makes more sense than the dominant medical language. Transmission of language often happens in groups. Talk to friends about the different ways you can feel “off” and develop your own shorthand to describe them.

• Joining a mutual support group of peers listening to and helping peers as equals can be validating, while not necessarily endorsing your feelings. You can form one yourself or join an ongoing group.

• If possible, find a therapist or counselor who supports your self-determination. Ask about confidentiality if someone else — such as your parents, boss, or governmental program — is paying.

• Drugs and alcohol usually make mental health problems worse.

• Psychiatric drugs such as those for depression or bipolar disorder can help some people reduce distress and maintain stability, while other people with similar symptoms may experience distress or harm from the same drugs. Figuring out what works for you can be a process because people differ.

• Nature and wilderness can be our greatest healers. Spend some time outside the city to get centered. Get away from pollution, which is in itself mind-altering. Look up “Ecopsychology” to learn more.

• Allow social, political, and environmental crises unfolding around you to radicalize you, rather than driving you to despair. Actually articulate the world you would want to be living in; work towards it. Remember change happens collectively – look for ways to plug in. Small acts like talking to neighbors or submitting art to Slingshot can help you feel political agency between larger or more radical actions.

• Many communities have 24 hour a day crisis hotlines or crisis centers. Call 800-SUICIDE if you’re thinking about killing yourself or 800 646-HOPE to reach a rape crisis line for survivors of sexual violence. Warning: if you call and say you want to kill yourself police may arrive at your door.

• Things that can help your mental health day-to-day might not be as effective when you’re in crisis. Review the above reminders, and try to eat, exercise, journal, etc., but it’s okay if that isn’t helping.

• Distracting yourself from depressed or anxious thoughts can help: listening to music, making art, washing dishes, doing a project alone or with others. Embrace sensation: use your hands or massage your fingers. Hold onto an ice cube, or take a hot or cold shower. Give yourself time to gather resources.

• Some current emotional crises may be caused by traumas from the past, which may need to be emotionally and consciously processed in order not to keep recurring; that processing might take time.

• When in crisis, it may help to realize that the feeling will eventually pass and your life will begin to feel manageable and meaningful again later. Depression may feel like lack of feelings and a lack of connection to feeling. Anxiety may feel like rapidly cycling concern for what might happen. Both inhibit your ability to perceive and understand the world correctly. Your perceptions of hopelessness are NOT …

content:

We join women, girls, and human rights defenders across Africa and the globe on this 28th day of September to commemorate the 2026 International Safe Abortion Day, reaffirming a simple truth: safe abortion is essential healthcare.

We are reminded of the transformative power of the Protocol to the African Charter on Human and Peoples’ Rights on the Rights of Women in Africa (the Maputo Protocol), which is lauded as one of the most progressive and comprehensive legal instruments for the promotion and protection of women’s rights globally, particularly in the area of sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR). Adopted in 2003 by the African Union, the Protocol goes beyond existing international human rights standards by explicitly articulating a wide array of SRHR protections that are often left ambiguous or unstated in other international and regional human rights instruments.

Article 14 of the Maputo Protocol guarantees women’s rights to health and reproductive autonomy, including the right to control their fertility, decide on family size and spacing, and to choose their method of contraception. Most critically, Article 14 makes the Maputo Protocol the first and only binding international human rights treaty to explicitly guarantee access to safe medical abortion in specific circumstances—namely, where the continued pregnancy endangers the mental or physical health of the mother or the life of the mother or the fetus, or in cases of sexual assault, rape, or incest. This Article also mandates access to comprehensive reproductive health services, including antenatal care, safe delivery, family planning, and sexual and reproductive health education. In doing so, the Protocol moves abortion access from a matter left to state discretion to one of binding treaty obligation — a distinction that remains central to the advocacy for its full domestication across the continent.

Currently, 46 of the 55 African states have ratified the Maputo Protocol, while nine – Burundi, Chad, Egypt, Eritrea, Madagascar, Morocco, Niger, Somalia, and Sudan – are yet to ratify it. Bringing these final states on board is vital because over 150 million African women and girls currently live outside the protective legal framework of the Maputo Protocol.

Despite its progressiveness, 9 out of the 46 member states have placed reservations to various provisions of the Maputo Protocol, with Article 14 being the most reserved provision. A reservation lowers the minimum human rights standards contained in a particular treaty for the reserving states and enables the reserving states to escape accountability for human rights violations.

Currently, Africa accounts for 70% of global maternal deaths. These preventable deaths are compounded by persistent gaps in access to sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) services, which are essential to safeguarding the lives and dignity of women, children and adolescents. Unsafe abortions continue to claim the lives of thousands of African women and girls, while millions more are left with severe injuries and long-term health complications. According to the World Health Organization, nearly half of all abortions worldwide are unsafe, with Sub-Saharan Africa carrying the highest burden. author: Unknown
title: Pourquoi et comment brûler la psychiatrie ? Discussion pour des perspectives antipsy anticarcérales
content:
Le mercredi 23 septembre 2026, l'Assemblée Anticarcérale Paris & Environs organise une discussion antipsychiatrie anticarcérale à la bibliothèque queer anarchiste la

BARK

, qui se trouve à la Parole Errante à Montreuil.


Mercredi 23 Septembre à 18h : Discussion antipsy anticarcérale à la

BARK

 

!


Depuis son lancement, l'Assemblée Anticarcérale Paris & Environs s'efforce de s'organiser contre l'enfermement psychiatrique. La psychiatrie nous apparaît naturellement comme un maillon important de la domination : que ce soit par les moyens par lesquels elle enferme des personnes, par son utilisation répressive et pacificatrice dans les autres lieux d'enfermement, ou par ses dispositifs carcéraux de contrôle dans la société. Dans une optique de s'informer sur les luttes contre la psychiatrie et d'y intervenir, on veut prendre en compte le fait que nous n'avons pas toustes les mêmes expériences et connaissances sur le sujet.


L'idée de cette discussion est donc de poser des bases, ensemble, sur ce qu'est l'antipsy pour nous, que ce soit pour découvrir ses courants ou pour développer ce qui nous parle dedans. Quels sont les dispositifs d'enfermement de la psychiatrie

 

? Pourquoi viser à sa destruction

 

? Quels liens faisons-nous depuis nos perspectives anticarcérales

 

? Comment la domination psychiatrique est elle étendue ces dernières années

 

? Comment s'organiser pour la brûler

 

?


Une base d'infokiosque sera aussi proposée pour approfondir certaines questions spécifiques, mais il ne faut pas hésiter à apporter toute brochure que l'on voudrait discuter, conseiller, diffuser, etc.


La discussion commencera dès 18h à la bibliothèque queer anarchiste la

BARK

 (5 rue francois debergue à la Parole Errante à Montreuil, en passant par le jardin à gauche de la librairie Michèle Firk). La permanence de la bibliothèque commence elle dès 16h, et l'infokiosque y sera installé en avance

title: Future of Egypt enters healthcare: Govt, military hospitals to serve tourist dollars
content:
In its first public move into the healthcare sector, the Future of Egypt for Sustainable Development Authority

unveiled

 last week the launch of the Future of Egypt Medical Alliance Company.


According to reports announcing the authority’s participation in this year’s Egy Health Exhibition and Conference, the company is chaired by Major General Khaled Oweida, the physician and former director of the Air Force Specialized Hospital, and is set to provide specialized medical services, training and research, digital and technological healthcare solutions, as well as medical tourism services.


In the first phase of its operations, the reports stated, the company will incorporate the International Medical Center and the Air Force Specialized Hospital, both of which are affiliated with the Armed Forces. The two facilities provide medical services to military personnel through the Armed Forces’ health insurance system, while also treating civilians for a fee or through

contracts

 with the Universal Health Insurance system or other entities.


The company plans to expand gradually by bringing additional facilities and hospitals under its umbrella.


This year’s Egy Health Exhibition and Conference, held September 15-17. Courtesy: Menassat website


Future of Egypt

also announced

 that the company was taking part in the exhibition, which was held from September 15 to 17, in order to “showcase its integrated medical system’s components and the range of specialties, services and advanced solutions it offers.”


Coverage of the exhibition focused on what media outlets described as the Future of Egypt Medical Alliance Company’s vision for developing medical tourism — mapping the international patient journey that runs from pre-travel consultations and case assessment, through travel, reception, accommodation and translation, to post-treatment follow-up.


According to media

coverage

, the company intends to pursue this by building a network of medical partners and tourism operators and establishing cooperation channels with entities involved in medical tourism and target markets.


Steps to foster a state vision for medical tourism date back to at least 2017, when Prime Minister Mostafa Madbuly

established

 the Supreme Committee for Medical Tourism by decree to be headed by the health minister. The decree set out several objectives, including implementing the medical tourism components of the Egypt Vision 2030, restoring the confidence of foreign patients, attracting Arab and foreign investment to establish projects serving medical tourism and involving civil society and the private sector.


During a committee meeting in December 2024, chaired by Madbuly, Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar

said

 the committee’s technical secretariat had begun preparing a unified national strategy for medical tourism. According to a Cabinet

statement

, the committee had contacted all relevant entities involved in health tourism in Egypt to solicit their proposals for the strategy.


At the same meeting, Madbuly said that it was agreed to establish a national council for medical tourism, with a technical secretariat tasked with following up on all matters related to this portfolio.


The council was established by a prime ministerial decree in June 2025. In its first meeting,

chaired

by the health minister, a proposal setting out criteria for service providers to join the national health tourism platform was reviewed. The providers included healthcare, hotel and hospitality, transportation and logistics services.


A senior Health Ministry official told Mada Masr on condition of anonymity that the Future of Egypt Medical Alliance Company is primarily focused on providing treatment to tourists: “[The company] is targeting Gulf nationals and foreign tourists in Egypt whose treatment costs are paid in dollars by international insurance companies.”


As an example, the official said, “if we perform open heart surgery for LE200,000 for someone insured in Egypt, [Future of Egypt’s] hospitals would perform the same operation for a foreign tourist staying in, say, Sharm el-Sheikh, and their insurance company would pay US$10,000. And we benefit from the difference in the exchange rate.”


According to the official, one of the main criteria for selecting hospitals to be transferred to Future of Egypt is having a helipad equipped to receive emergency cases, as well as facilities equipped for major surgeries and subspeciality medical care …

author: dev
title: Le sacrifice du ciel
content:
Le philosophe Mohamed Amer Meziane publie son troisième livre,

Le Sacrifice du ciel. Une autre histoire de la raison

, qui vient rouvrir, reprendre et poursuivre le cycle ouvert par

Des empires sous la terre

 (2021) et

Au bord des mondes

 (2023).


Le thème du « sacrifice du ciel » fait écho à ceux de la sécularisation, de la mort de Dieu et du « désenchantement du monde ». Ces lieux communs, au sein de l'attirail des pensées critiques, ressemblent à des enjeux à la fois familiers et méconnus.


À voir lundi 21 septembre à partir de 20h


Les « statuaires de la pensée », expression du livre renvoyant au panthéon fatigué des « grands auteurs » européens, ne nous ont légué que peu d'outils pour y faire face. Il se pourrait, en plus, que ces thèmes « biens connus » (c'est-à-dire peut-être totalement impensés) aient obscurci la compréhension qu'on a de ces grands auteurs eux-mêmes. C'est la conséquence d'un des points principaux du livre : l'

orientalisme

, sous la forme de la critique historique des textes sacrés, a joué un rôle matriciel pour la production du savoir occidentalisé.


À partir de là, l'enquête donne lieu à une autre histoire de la philosophie : au prisme de l'orientalisme, Spinoza, Kant et Hegel apparaissent sous un autre jour. Leurs façons de penser la religion, ses rapports à la pensée et à la politique, est très loin cependant de s'être cantonnée au seul domaine de la philosophie. Elles participent de mouvements qui les précèdent et leur survivent, et qui constituent le sol sur lequel se sont déployées les sciences humaines et sociales « modernes ». Un ensemble de mythes vivaces s'ancrent dans cette histoire : le christianisme comme seule religion de la sortie de la religion, le protestantisme comme religion du monde moderne, le monothéisme comme origine de la violence, le fanatisme comme caractéristique des « religions de la Loi »…


Le Sacrifice du ciel

 se présente comme une critique des savoirs, une « histoire souterraine » de la connaissance. Celle-ci ne se contente pas d'en exhumer les marges, mais entend ressaisir l'héritage d'un centre occulté en montrant que la raison n'est pas « occidentale ». Se pose alors une question simple, mais trop souvent ignorée (y compris par la critique décoloniale) : comment les « orientaux » ont-ils eux-mêmes pensé l'orientalisme ? La philosophie d'Afghāni et la « métaphysique insurrectionnelle » de l'émir Abdelkader ont été les lieux d'une résistance formulée au nom du savoir et d'une « critique traditionnelle de la tradition », et deviennent ici ceux de l'élaboration d'une « pensée-autre » (comme le disait Abdelkébir Khatibi, en partant de Fanon).


« La tâche de cet anti-impérialisme philosophique a surtout été de montrer la profonde irrationalité de tout ce système militaro-fossile qui, avec un fracas et une morgue confinant à la folie, s'est targué d'être la seule Raison qui soit. »


Pour aller plus loin (ou revenir quelques crans en arrière), nous renvoyons à nos deux précédents entretiens avec Mohamed Amer Meziane

autour de

Des empires sous la terre

 et après la publication de

Au bord des mondes
