author: Gustavo Faleiros
title: Religião nas eleições com pitadas de meio ambiente
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a newsletter Ligando os pontos, enviada toda quinta-feira. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui

.


Não tenho boas pesquisas de opinião para provar o argumento. Tenho uma percepção. Pode ser até mesmo uma crença, uma questão de fé…


Eu acredito que o tema do meio ambiente nos une. Não importa a coloração política ou a religião que você professa; em princípio, estamos irmanados na preocupação com a água que vamos beber, o ar que respiramos e a boa comida em nossos pratos.


A polêmica sobre

Nossa Senhora Aparecida

, que agora domina o debate eleitoral, me fez lembrar de um exemplo em que a questão ambiental ajuda a unir mundos diferentes. Existe uma

iniciativa inter religiosa para a proteção das florestas

. Criada há sete anos por várias organizações não governamentais e a seção de meio ambiente das Nações Unidas, esta aliança tem colocado lado-a-lado pastores, padres, rabinos, pais-de-santo e pajés para discutir a proteção do meio ambiente, em especial da Amazônia.


Quem me contou os resultados desta iniciativa foi seu facilitador no Brasil, Carlos Vicente, engenheiro florestal acreano que por muitos anos foi um dos assessores mais próximos da ex-ministra do Meio Ambiente e atual candidata ao Senado por São Paulo, Marina Silva. Em muitas conferências nas quais nos encontramos, ele me relatou com um brilho nos olhos como estes líderes religiosos aparentemente tão distantes em seu dia-a-dia convergiam em uma visão sobre a importância de respeitar a vida e a sacralidade da natureza.


Algo que Carlos destacou foi o profundo impacto que uma visita ao Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (INPE) causou a um pastor evangélico. A viagem à sede da instituição, em São José dos Campos, no interior de São Paulo, ocorreu na época em que Bolsonaro e membros de seu governo, como o General Heleno e o então ministro do Meio Ambiente, Ricardo Salles, atacavam o INPE. Os cientistas apenas faziam seu trabalho ao divulgar os dados que mostravam aumento do desmatamento. Depois de entender como funcionavam os sistemas de monitoramento, o pastor defendeu a proteção da Amazônia em um de seus sermões.


A lembrança do que me contou Carlos Vicente em meio a este turbilhão que mistura Nossa Senhora com eleições me deu um pouco de esperança. Me confirmou algo que eu já havia sentido nas eleições de 2018 e logo no início do governo Bolsonaro, quando houve a crise das queimadas. O tema da Amazônia e do combate ao desmatamento é um caminho de diálogo com indecisos. Em conversas casuais, é difícil encontrar alguém que defenda abertamente derrubadas, poluição e maus-tratos aos animais.


Minha impressão se tornou então mais forte com o que aconteceu em 2019, logo após o fatídico dia 18 de agosto, quando a fumaça das queimadas na Amazônia transformou em noite uma tarde de São Paulo. Aquelas imagens, seguidas por investigações jornalísticas que mostraram uma articulação de produtores rurais para celebrarem um Dia do Fogo, geraram uma mobilização nacional e internacional frente aos descalabros da política anti-ambiental de Bolsonaro.


Esta pressão da opinião pública fez com que Bolsonaro tivesse que recuar. Lembrem-se que o vice-presidente Hamilton Mourão foi designado para apaziguar os ânimos, fazendo a interlocução com parceiros históricos do Brasil nos investimentos em conservação, como a Alemanha e a Noruega. 


Enquanto o mundo estava cobrando o governo Bolsonaro, a questão ambiental e a Amazônia estavam também no centro da Igreja Católica. O Papa Francisco fez das mudanças climáticas e da proteção à Amazônia uma das principais marcas de seu pontificado.

 Realizou o primeiro encontro de bispos para propor uma ação conjunta com os povos indígenas,

o Sínodo da Amazônia.

 Estendeu os braços aos melhores cientistas do mundo no tema. Os brasileiros Carlos Nobre, do INPE, e Ima Vieira, do Museu Emílio Goeldi, foram alguns dos que tiveram o ouvido atento de Francisco.


Por isso, não me parece aleatório que Flávio Bolsonaro tenha resolvido atacar a Confederação Nacional dos Bispos do Brasil (CNBB) para achar um culpado ao dano que lhe faz a polêmica da Nossa Senhora. Os bispos sempre estiveram antenados com a questão ambiental e suas campanhas, ao longo dos anos, destacaram temas como o direito à terra, a proteção das terras indígenas e contra a estatização do acesso à água. A CNBB sempre foi uma defensora do meio ambiente como algo primordial na …

author: Charlotte Reck
title: Stop Helping Saudi Arabia Bomb Yemen, Rights Experts Tell Burnham
content:
Rights experts have urged prime minister Andy Burnham to reverse a decision to refuel Saudi Arabian warplanes as they bomb Yemen.


An open letter to Burnham and foreign secretary Ed Miliband said the UK risks being “complicit in further war crimes” after the government announced last week it would support the Saudi dictatorship’s latest attacks. 


The

letter is signed by NGOs

 including Shadow World Investigations UK and Campaign Against Arms Trade, as well as eleven human rights and international relations experts. 


It notes the Saudi-led coalition, which the UK first joined in 2015, “stands credibly accused of using starvation as a war tactic” against Yemen and of “widespread attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure.” 


The UN estimates 377,000 were killed in the war on Yemen – which involved 25,000 Saudi-led air raids – between 2015 and 2022, when a ceasefire was announced. 


The new Saudi bombing campaign began after the Houthis seized large areas of land along the Red Sea coast, giving them more leverage over a crucial global shipping route.  


Recent escalation by the Houthis, the letter argues, has been driven by Israel’s UK-backed genocide in Gaza – which saw the Houthis enforce a naval blockade against Israel from 2023 – as well as the illegal US-Israeli war on Iran, a key Houthi ally. 


The latest bombings, like previous attacks, are unlikely to “weaken or dislodge the Houthis”, the letter adds. “There is a real risk that further UK military support for Saudi Arabia will not achieve the desired outcome and could make the UK complicit in further war crimes and violations of international humanitarian law,” it says. 


Earlier this week, ten union leaders

wrote to Burnham

 urging him to end military collaboration with Saudi Arabia and UK support for the war on Iran. 


“Britain should not collaborate with a military that has repeatedly violated international law and has been central to creating one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises in Yemen,” said the letter, signed by Unison general secretary Andrea Egan and the National Education Union’s Daniel Kebede, among others. 


“Providing military support to Saudi Arabia inflames the war started by the US and Israel against Iran in February, which has expanded across the region,” it added. “The more this war expands, the more expensive our bills will get. The only way out is a diplomatic settlement to the regional war.”

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Amélie Béchard hopes to maintain CAQ hold on Ungava
content:
Nunatsiaq News reached out to each candidate running in the Ungava riding ahead of Quebec’s Oct. 5 provincial election. Here’s what Coalition avenir Québec candidate Amélie Béchard had to share with us.


Amélie Béchard isn’t a career politician. She says she decided to run for office in Ungava with the Coalition avenir Québec because she wants to make a difference.


“I’m here for the people,” said Béchard, speaking to Nunatsiaq News from her hometown of Matagami.


The candidate hopes to replace former Coalition avenir Québec member Denis Lamothe, who held the seat for two terms, from 2018 to 2026.


“I could be a strong voice in Quebec City — bringing our issues to the forefront, defending them, and helping our region grow,” said Béchard, who visited Whapmagoostui and Kuujjuarapik last week.


She owns a forestry consulting company in Matagami that specializes in operations management and has worked alongside the provincial government and Cree communities — experiences she says make her fit to lead economic development in northern Quebec.


She has also sat on boards of directors, such as the economic development society of Baie-James and Matagami’s business development society.


She has also sat on the board of Femmes Essor de la Jamésie, an organization that promotes entrepreneurship among women.


She said the cost of living for Cree and Inuit is especially high and that she wants to reduce the amount of transportation costs on essential items like food that are being passed onto consumers.


To address the cost of living, she mentioned that the party’s promising to increase tax credits for seniors over 65 as well as for first-time homebuyers. It has also promised to triple the amount it currently gives to local business in remote areas, through a regional economic fund.


Béchard said the party also wants to ensure royalties from mining are re-invested into critical infrastructure and services that nearby communities rely on. The party previously projected those royalties could generate as much as $78 million a year.


Béchard is among five candidates running for Ungava in Quebec’s provincial election. Advance polls have been open since Saturday and will stay open until Wednesday. Election day is on Monday, Oct. 5.

author: Nadia Salem
title: Interior Ministry accuses Matsda2sh of belonging to Muslim Brotherhood in claim founder says ‘authorities know is untrue’
content:
Over 48 hours since authorities initiated the arrest and forced disappearance of six Matsda2sh journalists, the Interior Ministry acknowledged on Thursday morning that it had detained the independent fact-checking platform’s staff. 


The journalists’ whereabouts remain unknown, according to their legal representatives at the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, and they have not been presented for investigation before prosecuting authorities.


The ministry accused the journalists of belonging to the Muslim Brotherhood, a claim the founder of the independent fact-checking platform said authorities know to be untrue in comments to Mada Masr.


In the statement published Thursday morning, the Interior Ministry

said

 Matsda2sh aims to undermine the country’s stability by “fabricating lies and spreading rumors.” The statement added that it is an unlicensed page, managed from abroad to broadcast false news and distort facts. It also accused the platform’s founder, Abdel Rahman Mansour, of being a “fugitive member of the Brotherhood” and that he is working in cooperation with “a number of  Brotherhood elements in other countries, in exchange for funding they receive from abroad.”


EIPR lawyer Islam Salama said that the six journalists have still not been brought before the Supreme State Security Prosecution, which handles terrorism investigations, and said authorities are yet to inform the journalists’ families and lawyers of their place of detention. He added that lawyers have submitted requests to authorities to ensure they are able to attend investigations with the detainees, and that they have gone to wait at the prosecution headquarters for the journalists to be brought there, though authorities have not yet permitted them into the building. 


Mansour told Mada Masr that authorities know that Matsda2sh is not affiliated with the Muslim Brotherhood and that it is a professional journalism platform. He pointed to the prior summoning of one of the platform’s journalists for investigation in 2023. The journalist was released shortly after the summons. “Why are they now saying that they are Brotherhood?” he asked. 


“We know that there are voices who support us from within the state because they know us, and because they are committed to sound governance and believe that not all voices should be silenced,” Mansour added. His personal priority, he continued, is “human dignity and defending the right to hold on to the ideas one wishes to hold on to, and to adopt one’s own causes in a peaceful manner.” 


Authorities

arrested

 several members of Matsda2sh’s team three years ago following their

coverage of a case involving the arrest of Egyptian nationals in Zambia who were

onboard a

private

jet carrying cash, counterfeit gold and weapons

. They were forced to erase the coverage from their pages, and the journalists were

released

 after two days and allowed to continue their work. 


In the aftermath of the 2023 campaign,

Matsda2sh proposed to security authorities that they legalize their status as an official journalistic platform and establish headquarters to gather the team together inside Egypt, as other journalistic organizations are allowed to do. This initiative was ignored by security authorities, according to an informed source who spoke to Mada Masr on condition of anonymity.


A source from the Journalists Syndicate informed of the ongoing mediation between the syndicate and authorities since the arrests confirmed the initiatives had taken place, adding that the same proposal “and more” is currently being put forward, but that security authorities are not engaging with the suggestions. 


The same source, alongside another source from the syndicate, clarified that security authorities, during the course of mediation, have pointed to a letter the syndicate had previously sent to all official entities, including the Interior Ministry, to say that state officials should only speak to  journalists registered with the syndicate, trainees at syndicate-accredited newspapers or trainees with media websites and agencies licensed by, or who have applied for a license, from the Supreme Media Regulatory Council.


Security authorities used that letter to repudiate the syndicate’s attempts at mediation for the six Matsda2sh journalists, claiming the platform is a social media page operating without a license from the Supreme Media Regulatory Council and that it has not applied for one.

author: Unknown
title: Dr Bogos Yalim: No democratisation without confronting the past
content:
Dr Bogos Yalim, who has lived in Belgium for many years and is known for his work within the Armenian community, spoke about the historical experiences of Armenians and developments in Turkey. Yalim said the Armenian community approached developments in Turkey with caution because of the collective memory shaped by the 1915 Genocide, while stressing their support for the Kurdish people’s struggle for rights and freedoms.


Yalim said the historical memory of the 1915 Genocide played a decisive role in how the Armenian community viewed developments in Turkey, adding that its cautious approach to the peace process stemmed primarily from a historical distrust of state policies.


Gains for the Kurdish people would make us happy


Yalim said that despite historical problems between the Armenian and Kurdish communities, Armenians supported Kurdish demands for rights and freedoms. He stressed that they respected the Kurdish people’s right to determine their own future and said the Kurdish people securing their rights would be a positive development for Armenians.


Yalim said, “If the Kurdish people gain certain rights there, that would make us happy. Nothing more than that,” adding that the concerns arising from the Armenian community’s historical experiences did not mean opposition to Kurdish demands for rights and freedoms.


Yalim said the Kurdish movement would make its own decisions based on its historical experience and current circumstances, while the Armenian community’s concerns about the process stemmed from its own experiences of the past.


Yalim said, “What we see is shaped by our own history and what we have lived through,” stressing that the process should therefore be considered in light of historical experience.


The Kurdish movement knows its own reality better than we do


Bogos Yalim said the Peace and Democratic Society Process could not be considered separately from the Kurdish people’s decades-long struggle, adding that the Kurdish movement itself was best placed to assess the current circumstances, the balance of power and the stage the struggle had reached.


Yalim said it would not be appropriate for outsiders to make definitive judgements about how the process should proceed. He said, “The Kurdish movement knows its own reality better than we do. What is its position today? What is the balance of power? What is its own strength? How should it respond? These are matters for them to decide. Ultimately, they are the ones who will make the decisions.”


Steps will not be enough without fundamental change


Dr Bogos Yalim said discussions about the constitution, democratisation and fundamental rights had once again come to the fore alongside the peace process in Turkey, stressing that the state needed to undergo a transformation that recognised the existence and identities of different peoples.


Yalim said the Armenian community’s historical experiences shaped its assessment of the issue. He recalled that constitutional reforms and debates over freedoms had taken place during the final years of the Ottoman Empire. He said expectations of change had emerged through relations between Armenian political organisations and the Committee of Union and Progress, but were followed by the 1915 Genocide, leaving a profound mark on the Armenian community’s approach to state policies.


Yalim stressed the importance of the Turkish state confronting its past and described the Armenian community’s historical view of the state’s foundation: “Our view of the Turkish state is that it is a state founded on genocide. From our perspective, it is very difficult to believe that this state can make progress unless it confronts its own reality.”


Yalim stressed that democratisation could not be achieved through legal or administrative measures alone, saying different peoples needed to be recognised with their own identities and social realities.


Yalim said any steps taken would be insufficient without fundamental changes to the structure of the state. He said, “As long as the Turkish state does not change its own structure and accept other peoples with their own identities and realities, everything it does will be cosmetic.”


How free is Kurdish, and how much space has it found in education?


Bogos Yalim said language, identity and educational rights were crucial in assessing the social outcomes of the peace process, stressing that representation in political and administrative institutions alone would not resolve …

title: Ayyıldız: Economic crisis and social decay deepen social problems
content:
The deepening economic crisis, lack of employment opportunities and problems with public services in Kurdish cities are having an increasingly visible impact on social life. Migration driven by a lack of investment, problems with the quality of education and unemployment are exacerbating social problems affecting broad sections of society, particularly women and young people.


Insufficient investment in the region and limited employment opportunities are driving young people in particular to migrate to other cities, while unemployment and economic deprivation are also taking a toll on social life.


Social worker Berfin Ayyıldız spoke to ANF about the issue.


Economic crisis deepens the social cycle


Berfin Ayyıldız said there were many factors affecting the social fabric, with economic problems among the most significant.


Ayyıldız said economic difficulties did not affect only individuals or families, but had consequences for society as a whole. 


She said: “Economic problems do not affect only an individual or a family. They affect society as a whole. A family facing economic hardship may be forced to migrate. They may have to take insecure jobs outside the home, on the streets or in their neighbourhood, or someone may turn to illegal means to earn money. This can then trigger other problems, such as violence, addiction or involvement in crime.”


Young people are caught between education and their future


Ayyıldız said young people they worked with often told them, “Going to school is not a solution for me. It does not give me anything because I will not be able to find a job.” 


Ayyıldız continued: “A large proportion of the young population in our region is struggling with this economic crisis. Simply going to school and receiving an education is no longer enough. Many of the people we work with tell us, ‘Going to school is not a solution for me. It does not give me anything because I will not be able to find a job.’ They are studying, but they are worried that they will not find employment. There is also the anxiety of wondering, ‘Will I be able to build a life for myself in this city? Will I be able to find employment here?’ This is one of the factors contributing to higher school dropout rates.


An increase in school dropouts means that young people are more likely to encounter and remain in harmful environments. As I said at the beginning, this creates a cycle. Economic problems have a profoundly negative impact on people and can create circumstances that make it difficult for them to break out of that cycle.”


Women face economic dependency


Ayyıldız said the exclusion of women from employment was also exacerbating economic and social problems. She said: “When we look at last year’s data from the Turkish Statistical Institute (TÜİK), we can see that women’s employment is around 20 to 25 per cent. There are systemic problems that make it difficult for women to enter employment and deliberately keep them out of the workforce. Kurdistan is, of course, one of the regions most severely affected by these problems.


Women, particularly those experiencing addiction, are constantly confronted with new trauma. They are already struggling with addiction, trying to overcome it and access treatment. At the same time, women without employment are economically dependent on others. This economic dependency can inevitably push them into other difficult circumstances, making the situation increasingly difficult to escape.”


Addiction cannot be explained by a single cause


Berfin Ayyıldız stressed that rising levels of addiction could not be explained solely by economic problems. She said: “This does not mean that everyone who is unemployed has an addiction or that everyone with an addiction is unemployed. People with very high socioeconomic status can also use substances and have a history of addiction, whether to gambling or alcohol. Addiction cannot therefore be categorised by gender or age, whether someone is a woman, man, young person, adult, older person or child. But disadvantaged groups are, of course, among those who are more vulnerable and more severely affected.”


Violence and addiction should be considered together


Ayyıldız said violence and addiction could overlap in some cases, but stressed that it would be wrong to explain violence solely through addiction. She continued: “We often observe that a history of violence can overlap with addiction, but we do not actually have a scientific basis for …

title: Psychologist Kaya: Peace cannot be achieved through a declaration alone
content:
Academic Orhan Kaya, discussing the historical dimensions of collective trauma, the Kurdish people's resistance, and conflict resolution processes, said that approaches focusing exclusively on trauma are incomplete. He also commented on expectations and disappointments surrounding the current process, hopes of return among the diaspora, distrust between communities, and the conditions necessary for peace to be felt throughout society. Kaya said that the atmosphere of distrust must be eliminated for peace to be experienced and that fundamental steps are needed to achieve this.


The Kurdish people did not just experience traumatic processes, they resisted


Kaya added that the history of collective trauma runs very deep and has been discussed in psychology for many years. He described trauma as unexpected and sudden events that affect human life in its entirety. Noting that people in Turkey, particularly the Kurdish population, have been exposed to traumatic experiences for decades, Kaya said that focusing solely on trauma would be an incomplete approach.


 


Kaya argued that the history of resistance must also be examined alongside trauma. He said: “When traumatic processes have continued for such a long time, discussing only trauma would be an incomplete approach. Because just as there is a history of trauma, there is also a history of resistance. Yes, the Kurdish people have been exposed to traumatic processes for years, even decades, but psychology continually focuses on these traumatic experiences. What is overlooked, on the other hand, is that the Kurdish people have also been resisting for decades.”


Conflict resolution processes do not progress easily 


Kaya underlined that just as collective trauma can persist for a long time, conflict resolution processes also take a long time. He said that expectations and disappointments concerning the current process should be understood in this context. Emphasizing that conflict resolution is not straightforward, he said: “Conflict resolution, reconciliation, and reconstruction processes do not happen easily. They take at least as long as traumatic processes.”


Kaya said that expectations that the process would be completed quickly were unrealistic. He stated: “There is a perception that peace will be achieved immediately, that traumatic processes will be healed overnight, or that our social life will suddenly change. I think this perception is mistaken. While I understand and accept these expectations, and acknowledge that they are legitimate expectations, I think we need to approach the situation a little more realistically.”


New traumatic processes must be prevented


Kaya said that people in Turkey want their problems resolved as soon as possible, but said the process must advance in stages. Emphasizing that new traumatic experiences must be avoided, he noted that the current process appears to be proceeding more cautiously than previous ones.


Kaya said: “It needs to progress step by step. From what I have observed, unlike previous processes, this one is moving forward somewhat more cautiously. Whether in the preparation stages or the implementation stages, everything so far has been proceeding in a way intended to prevent new traumatic experiences. This applies to both sides.”


Kaya is also an academic in Germany and works with the Kurdish diaspora. He explained that people in the diaspora have different expectations regarding the process. Some are preparing to return to their homeland, but past experiences have also created distrust towards the process.


Kaya said: “They are making plans to return to their country, even saying, ‘Let’s get our preparations done as soon as possible; there will be peace, and we will go back.’ They have expectations, too. Of course, there are also people who approach the process with distrust, absolutely. At this point, past experiences contribute to that distrust. Because previous experiences have generally been negative, when these expectations are not met, or when things do not happen overnight, people become disappointed. As a result, opposition to the process develops among certain groups.”


Trust must be built


Kaya reiterated that conflict resolution processes do not progress easily and stated that ending conflict and achieving peace are not the same thing. He also drew attention to the distrust created in society by nearly a century of policies directed against the Kurdish people, emphasizing that the cessation of …

title: DFG Media Report: A free and pluralistic media is necessary for socialization of peace
content:
A report published by the Dicle Fırat Journalists Association (DFG) examined the language used in coverage of the process, headlines, news sources, and the actors given visibility.


The report covers the period 27 February 2025 to 1 October 2026. It underlined that media outlets close to the government predominantly framed the process through concepts such as “security,” “terrorism,” “dissolution,” and “liquidation,” while opposition media placed greater emphasis on the policies of the political government, previous peace-process experiences, and the political objectives of the current process.


The DFG noted that reporting unverified claims in some media outlets affected public discussions about the process. It also stated that publications within the Free Press tended to address developments more through concepts such as “peace,” “negotiation,” “democratic solution,” and “a new political era.”


Who is speaking and who is not visible


The report also drew attention to the diversity of sources used by media organizations. The DFG stated that statements by state institutions, government representatives, and political party officials dominated coverage of the process, while the views of Kurdish political actors, civil society organizations, academics, journalists, and different segments of society received more limited coverage. The DFG said that media analysis should consider not only the framework in which news is presented, but also the questions “Who is speaking?” and “Who is not visible?”


The report emphasized that the Kurdish question and the Peace and Democratic Society Process should not be addressed solely through the lenses of security, terrorism, and disarmament. The DFG stated that issues such as democratization, the rule of law, political participation, rights, and social peace should also be made visible in news coverage.


The association also called for news language to be free of discriminatory and exclusionary expressions, for the distinction between news and commentary to be maintained, and for the sources of the descriptions and characterizations used in reporting to be clearly identified.


Journalists's direct access to information


The DFG highlighted the importance of journalists being able to speak directly with the main actors in the process, noting in particular that Abdullah Öcalan’s views should be conveyed to the public through direct questions from journalists.


The report also recommended that media organizations increase the diversity of their sources and actors, remove restrictions on direct access to information about the process, and give greater space to the expectations and experiences of different segments of society.


Call to media organizations


T

he report stated that media organizations should review their own language and editorial policies, and called for headlines to accurately reflect the content of news reports and for political developments not to be reduced to a single framework.


The report stated: “Media organizations should review their own language and editorial policies. During periods with significant social impact, such as the Peace and Democratic Society Process, media organizations need to regularly assess the concepts they use, their news sources, their approach to headline writing, and their policies regarding visibility. As DFG, we consider it important that this assessment be carried out on the basis of the professional principles of journalism.”


Free, pluralistic and rights-based journalism


The DFG said: “For peace to become rooted in society, the media must also operate according to an understanding of journalism that is free, pluralistic, and rights-based. The DFG calls for all obstacles preventing journalists from accessing information to be removed, and for the media to confront its own responsibilities and undergo transformation during this process.”

author: Unknown
title: Eren: Concrete steps needed for democratisation and clear status
content:
The “1001 Signatures for a Democratic Republic and Peace” campaign, launched to contribute to the Peace and Democratic Society Process, was announced to the public on 12 September. The campaign calls for support for non-violence and disarmament, constitutional guarantees for equal citizenship, the strengthening of the democratic rule of law and the creation of conditions for free and equal negotiations. It also seeks to broaden social participation in the process and enable different sections of society to become active participants.


Journalist Faruk Eren, a relative of a disappeared person and one of the campaign’s signatories, spoke to ANF about the campaign’s aims, the importance of democratisation amid the ongoing period without conflict, the concrete steps needed for the process to move forward on a sound footing, and the need to confront the truth in order to achieve lasting peace. Eren also discussed the prevailing language in the media and peace journalism.


 


Eren explained why he had signed the campaign, saying first that he was generally reluctant to support signature campaigns. He drew attention to the relationship between journalism and activism, saying that the state of democracy in Turkey had also changed the role of journalists.


Eren said: “Normally, journalists are not activists. But the situation in Turkey has long gone beyond the idea that ‘journalists are not activists’. Democracy is under severe attack. In fact, we have reached a point where it is almost impossible to speak of democracy at all. In such circumstances, journalists can also become activists through their reporting and their views.”


It is impossible to remain neutral and stay out of the process


Eren said it was impossible to remain neutral towards the process, adding that the campaign offered proposals in response to the concerns and anxieties felt by different sections of society.


Eren said a process was under way in Turkey and that different sections of society described it in different terms. He added that it could be turned into an opportunity for peace.


Eren said he signed the campaign because: “There is a process under way in Turkey. Some call it a ‘peace process’. The government calls it a ‘terror-free Turkey’. Ultimately, it is a process towards which you cannot remain neutral. It can be turned into an opportunity, and I believe it will be. Once I heard about the campaign and read the text, I signed it as well. Because it is not really possible to remain neutral towards this process and simply say, ‘I’m staying out of it.’


First of all, there has been a war going on for years. This war had to end. An important step towards peace has been taken, and further steps will undoubtedly follow. Of course, many people have concerns and anxieties about the process. Both the parties involved and society have their own concerns. The campaign text essentially voices these concerns and puts forward proposals. That is why I signed it.”


Eren stressed that democratisation was vital to resolving the Kurdish question and achieving peace. He said: “One of the most important dimensions of this process is democratisation. For the Kurdish question to be resolved and genuine peace to be achieved, the country needs to democratise.”


Failure to implement ECtHR and Constitutional Court rulings is a problem in itself


Eren said the first and perhaps most important step towards democratisation concerned the prison: “The first urgent step must be to release the thousands of people who are being unjustly held in prison. There are thousands of people imprisoned for political reasons. A significant number of them are Kurdish politicians, members of organisations, or people accused of membership despite not actually being members. These are steps that could be taken simply by applying existing laws and implementing the rulings of the European Court of Human Rights.”


Faruk Eren stressed that releases alone would not be enough, describing the failure to implement rulings by the European Court of Human Rights (ECtHR) and the Constitutional Court as a problem in itself: “For the country to democratise, many anti-democratic provisions, particularly those in the criminal law, need to be removed. The obstacles to freedom of thought and expression must be lifted. There is currently a great deal of arbitrariness in the judiciary. The failure to implement ECtHR or Constitutional Court rulings is itself a major problem. I do not think much …

title: DEM Party calls for respect for the will of the people of Mersin
content:
DEM Party Co-Chairs Tülay Hatimoğulları and Tuncer Bakırhans said: “We do not accept the operations targeting 59 people, including Mersin Metropolitan Municipality mayor Vahap Seçer, Yenişehir mayor Abdullah Özyiğit, and Mezitli mayor Ahmet Serkan Tuncer.”


The Co-Chairs added that the will of the people expressed at the ballot box is continually being suppressed through judicial processes, arguing that “the will of the people has effectively been rendered inoperative.”


The DEM Party Co-Chairs continued: “We know this method very well. We encountered the same approach when our municipalities were seized and handed over to trustees. The people were granted the right to vote, but the person they elected was not granted the right to govern. If the right to vote and stand for election is violated in one place, the consequences do not remain confined there.”


The statement said: “If the will of the people is valid only when the election result is liked, then this is not democracy. Whoever the people of Mersin elected should govern Mersin. The will of the people must be respected, and the judiciary must be removed from the sphere of political reckoning.”

title: Iraqi Islamic Resistance Movement: We will not surrender our weapons
content:
Jafar Husseini, spokesperson for the Iraqi Islamic Resistance Movement, issued a statement on bringing weapons under state control and the withdrawal of the International Coalition against ISIS from Iraq.


Husseini said that their movement is not bound by any agreement or decision made by the government or political parties, adding: “Our weapons are still in the hands of our fighters.”


The statement said that the movement has been holding talks with the Coordination Framework Committee for more than 40 days regarding the reorganization of weapons, and called for the withdrawal of US and NATO forces, as well as all foreign military forces, from Iraq.


Stating that no response has yet been received from the Iraqi government regarding the talks, the statement said: “We will fight any enemy that targets Iraq and its people. Our door is open to any dialogue that will safeguard Iraq’s sovereignty and freedom.”


The statement came on the day the International Coalition announced its withdrawal from Iraq. The process of bringing weapons under state control was reportedly postponed until June 2027.

author: Redazione_web
title: Zombie: un archetipo culturale e politico
content:
Valentina Cardella e Igor Cardella – “L’invasione degli zombie – per una filosofia dei non morti” – Mimesis 2026


Chi, o cosa, è uno zombie? È l’interrogativo a cui danno forma, e risposta, Valentina e Igor Cardella, fratelli palermitani ed entrambi docenti, l’una all’Università di Messina, l’altro in un liceo del capoluogo siciliano. Il loro libro, “L’invasione degli zombie – per una filosofia dei non morti”, è edito da Mimesis. «Il nostro lavoro – spiegano – nasce dall’esigenza di rivalutare la figura dello zombie e l’horror in generale come potenti dispositivi di riflessione filosofica, politica e morale. La percezione del mostro muta nel corso della Storia e vi si adatta per rifletterne i momenti critici. A esempio, lo “zombie” successivo all’11 settembre risponde a traumi e paranoie collettive completamente diverse rispetto al suo omologo degli anni ’70». Non solo un mostro, dunque, ma un vero e proprio archetipo culturale e politico. La figura dello “zombie” nasce ad Haiti, teatro della prima rivoluzione schiavista della storia, per mano dei bokor, sacerdoti legati alle credenze vudù. La propaganda coloniale ha poi sfruttato le credenze popolari per ribadire che gli schiavi devono rimanere al proprio posto. Successivamente il mostro è stato utilizzato dall’immaginario occidentale, sul piano letterario e cinematografico dal romanzo “Io sono leggenda” di Richard Matheson degli anni ’50, insieme al film che ne è stato tratto, “L’ultimo uomo della Terra”, per poi diventare icona pop con il noto “La notte dei morti viventi” del ’68, di George Romero. La fame atavica dello zombie è ancora quella dello “sfruttato per eccellenza”, con l’accezione politica dell’incarnazione delle masse dei lavoratori o dei consumatori. Ma il saggio di Valentina e Igor Cardella non è solamente una ricognizione sull’archetipo zombiesco dalle origini alla modernità, quanto una potente riflessione, dicevamo anche filosofica, sulla condizione umana e la sua fine: da un lato c’è il terrore della perdita di coscienza legata alla tecnologia, dall’altro si collega a malattie odierne come la demenza o l’Alzheimer. O al più lento e velenoso anestetico moderno: la dipendenza dai social, che non a caso è chiamata “zombie scrolling”, lo scroll compulsivo da cellulare. «Gli zombie mettono in ridicolo le nostre priorità – dichiarano i Cardella – Quando si accalcano fuori da un supermercato, parodizzano il consumismo e diventano il nostro riflesso grottesco». Una forma di estrema auto-ironia con venature noir, dunque, ma con ricadute anche positive: oltre a un’esorcizzazione delle paure, nelle pagine del libro i due scrittori palermitani parlano anche dello zombie come paradossale apologia della lentezza in una società capitalistica e ipervelocizzata, qualcosa di lento ma inesorabile. Una lettura interessante e formativa, con la quale non vedrete più gli zombie sul grande schermo con gli stessi occhi. Se vi rimarranno ancora.


“

L’invasione degli zombie – per una filosofia dei non morti” viene presentato da Valentina e Igor Cardella lunedì 5 ottobre alle 18:00, presso la Feltrinelli di Palermo in via Cavour.


Gabriele Costa

Zombie: un archetipo culturale e politico

title: Del zenit al ¿ocaso? de la «anomalía argentina»: ofensiva patronal y desafíos estratégicos de la clase trabajadora
content:
Agustín Tosco con delegadas del Sindicato de Luz y Fuerza, en una marcha en 1971 pidiendo el cese de intervención al sindicato. Foto: Carlos Ardiles. Gentileza de Bibiana Fulchieri.


Lo que históricamente se conoció como la “anomalía argentina” – una clase trabajadora dotada de una capacidad de movilización excepcional en el contexto latinoamericano – enfrenta hoy una encrucijada. La prolongada decadencia del capitalismo argentino y el deterioro de su mercado de trabajo permiten comprender tanto el proceso que hizo posible la actual ofensiva patronal como las transformaciones que atraviesan al movimiento obrero. En este escenario, la construcción de una alternativa política propia aparece como una necesidad para la clase trabajadora, tanto para resistir el avance libertario como para superar las estrategias que, desde el progresismo, contribuyeron a allanar el camino para la llegada de Milei.

Por Cristian Caracoche (economista, docente e investigador).


Una parte importante de la historiografía que ha estudiado el desarrollo del capitalismo argentino coincide en señalar que este presentó, en relación con el resto de los países de la región, un conjunto de características distintivas, entre las que sobresalen la elevada capacidad de movilización de su clase trabajadora y los altos niveles de conflictividad social. Intelectuales de diversas vertientes intentaron explicar estas particularidades. Es así como desde la Sociología surgieron tesis clásicas como el “impulso igualitario” de Gino Germani, el “empate hegemónico” de Juan Carlos Portantiero y el concepto de la “alianza defensiva” de Guillermo O’Donnell. Desde la Economía, autores de la talla de Richard Mallon, Juan Sourrouille y Julio Hipólito Olivera atribuyeron las crisis recurrentes y la persistencia de la inflación a la existencia de un conflicto distributivo estructural, en el que el “equilibrio social” colisionaba permanentemente con el “equilibrio de mercado”. Por su parte, autores como Adolfo Gilly señalaban que esta “anomalía argentina” encontraba sus razones en las características singulares de su movimiento obrero y en su particular grado de politización.


A diferencia de países como México, Paraguay o Chile, donde la organización gremial se estructuró a nivel de la empresa, en la Argentina se consolidó un esquema sindical centralizado, estructurado bajo la personería gremial única por rama de actividad y unificado a nivel país en torno a una central ampliamente predominante como la CGT. La fuerza material de esta estructura se asentaba en una densidad sindical extraordinariamente elevada que, desde mediados del siglo XX hasta el presente, ha exhibido los niveles de afiliación sindical más altos de toda la región. Asimismo, esta capacidad de afiliación estuvo acompañada por una amplia cobertura de la negociación colectiva que, junto con la registrada en Brasil y Uruguay, también se encuentra entre las más elevadas del continente.


A nivel de fábrica, la “anomalía argentina” mostró su mayor capilaridad mediante la representación obrera en los lugares de trabajo, a través de los cuerpos de delegados y las comisiones internas, un fenómeno generalizado desde el peronismo y consolidado posteriormente en el artículo 14 bis de la Constitución de 1957. Asimismo, el derecho de huelga en Argentina gozó de uno de los marcos más permisivos de la región, ya que no establecía restricciones para modalidades de protesta como la ocupación de planta, las huelgas por solidaridad y las huelgas políticas, que sí encontraban limitaciones en todos los países limítrofes.


Esta amalgama de recursos organizativos permite explicar que, en términos comparados, la conflictividad social en la Argentina fuera persistente y alcanzara una magnitud excepcional en la región, destacándose particularmente la conflictividad laboral protagonizada por su poderoso movimiento obrero.


Sin embargo, los recursos de poder con los que cuenta la clase trabajadora no flotan en el vacío de la voluntad política, sino que están fuertemente condicionados por la dinámica de la acumulación de capital y la estructura del mercado laboral. Durante las décadas de oro del capitalismo de posguerra, la base material de la Argentina ofreció condiciones excepcionales para la organización obrera. El país presentaba el mayor stock de capital por ocupado de América Latina. Además, se caracterizaba por un mercado de trabajo integrado, con tasas de asalarización elevadas, un desempleo limitado y una baja …

author: Lilli Akpaleeapik
title: I’m growing older than my anaanatsiaq will ever be
content:
Not everyone has the privilege of growing up with their grandparents presence and knowledge. It’s a blessing I didn’t have.


My anaanatsiaq was Tookasie Akpaleeapik. When my family, who is from Pond Inlet, was chosen to help the Inujjuarmiut (families from Inukjuak) adjust during the High Arctic Relocation in the 1950s, she followed to Grise Fiord.


Author Larry Audlaluk mentions my grandmother in his memoir

What I Remember, What I Know: The Life of a High Arctic Exile

.


“When we arrived in Grise, after the aircraft’s engines stopped and the pilot opened the door to let us out, none of us wanted to be the first to get out. We were too shy. Tookashie was the brave one, getting out first.”


After the relocation she was sent to Churchill, Man., where she attended residential school. After graduation, Tookasie Akpaleeapik moved to Ottawa to practise nursing.


She took her own life shortly after, and that loss still affects my family. Grief doesn’t just magically go away over time; it stays with us throughout generations.


Everyone remembers her as a strong young woman who wasn’t scared to follow her dreams, regardless of hardships.


Her soul is still shining bright through my oldest sister, Maggie Tookasie, who was given my anaanatsiaq’s name by my anaana (mother) Katie Koonoo.


I believe Tookasie Akpaleeapik would be so proud of all of us and our accomplishments, especially her panik (daughter), Katie Koonoo, who is an amazing nurse. I know she’s watching over us and smiling.


Although I didn’t grow up knowing her, I find ways to keep her memory alive and honour her name.


On Sept. 17, I participated in Isaksimagit Inuusirmi Katujjiqatigiit Embrace Life Council’s polar dip at Apex beach in Iqaluit to honour her and to raise awareness for suicide prevention.


Nunavut Tunnavik Inc. and the Nunavut government

declared

 last June that suicide is still a crisis in Nunavut, marking 10 years since they

made their initial declaration

 in 2015.


Lilli Akpaleeapik smiles after she participates in Isaksimagit Inuusirmi Katujjiqatigiit Embrace Life Council’s polar dip at Apex beach on Sept. 17. (Photo courtesy of Lilli Akpaleeapik)


Hosting events raises awareness and fosters community, both of which are crucial, even if an activity like a polar dip isn’t well known within Inuit culture.


Running into the icy water gives people a reset if they need it, and it provides a space for people who are affected by the same issue to gather.


Before it was my time to go into the ice cold bay, I sat on the beach watching the water, thinking of my loved ones and their suicide attempts, reminiscing about my own attempts to take my life when I was younger.


After hearing Tookasie’s name announced, I got ready to head into the water. The crowd cheered me on as I ran in solo.


It was amazing to hear so many Inuit say her name again, to hear her story, to remember her accomplishments, her smile, and who she was — not only for the tragedies faced or losses experienced.


I was born and raised down south. This year marked my first time ever stepping foot on the nuna (Inuit land), and it was so powerful being back home. I wanted to reconnect with my family.


The dip was one way of doing that. It marked my first time being in the Arctic Ocean, in the waters that my family has used for generations.


Feeling that ice cold water surrounding my body from head-to-toe was refreshing. It silenced my thoughts for a moment. It reminded me that I’m alive and that I’m capable of doing hard things. The experience also provided me with a sense a relief for when life feels overwhelming.


Suicide has followed me and my family since childhood. It’s hard to heal from things you can’t escape. But I will never forget those who we have lost. I will continue to honour them daily.

title: The Real Existential Risk Is AI CEOs Avoiding Oversight: "Alternative Nobel" Winner Timnit Gebru
content:
We speak to the prominent AI researcher and leading critic of the AI industry, Timnit Gebru, who was recently awarded a 2026 Right Livelihood Award for her work investigating the harms and hype behind the global buildup of artificial intelligence.


“Instead of discussing faulty, unreliable systems,” Gebru says tech leaders like SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk, OpenAI’s Sam Altman and Anthropic’s Dario Amodei are “marketing their systems as all-knowing, superpowerful, superintelligent,” and lobbying for “self-policing and self-regulation” to avoid being held “liable through existing laws.” Gebru expresses skepticism over increasingly widespread claims that AI algorithms pose an existential risk to humanity, warning that such claims are overblown and that “what is actually happening is regulatory capture.”

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: Police Broke Teeth and Bones of Students at US Encampments for Gaza
content:
Thousands of pro-Palestine students were arrested on US college campuses, as part of a “widespread, McCarthyite censorship and retaliation campaign”,

a new report has found

.


Threatened with funding cuts by the Trump administration, colleges and universities across the US played an active role in suppressing pro-Palestinian solidarity, with many students and scholars facing expulsions and deportations.


The report from the American Civil Liberties Union and Amnesty International USA, concludes that universities and law enforcement agencies acted unlawfully during the nationwide crackdown on student-led pro-Palestinian activism.


“Colleges and universities violated basic free speech, association and assembly rights and caused serious harm when they summoned campus police and local law enforcement, resulting in arrests and unlawful and unnecessary use of force,” the report says. 


The report, which spans two years of protests and their aftermath, examined 80 universities across 28 states and Washington DC, and brings together existing research combining documentary evidence with interviews and testimony to identify a broader pattern of repression.


It says universities and law enforcement repeatedly used “heavy-handed and excessive” measures against largely peaceful pro-Palestinian protesters, noting that some students had their teeth and bones broken by police.


Universities were targeted by president Donald Trump, who weaponised federal funds, civil rights enforcement and immigration powers in order to force universities into submission. 


After Trump threatened to withhold $400m (£300m) in federal funding from Columbia University in March 2025, the university agreed to create 36 new patrol officer positions with the power to arrest students.


Soon after, more than 70 Columbia students were the subject of disciplinary action by the university’s judicial board, which either suspended, expelled or revoked their degrees because of their pro-Palestinian activism.


Collectively, efforts to clamp down on Palestine advocacy were “more punitive in comparison with their historical responses to other comparable demonstrations over decades,”

 Amnesty

said.


While the crackdown began under former president Joe Biden, things escalated upon Trump’s return to power. The report describes an “ideological deportation policy” targeting non US-citizens, with officials admitting that “any criticism of Israel could merit immigration consequences”.

author: anred
title: La Plata: con el foco en la precarización y las nuevas tecnologías, convocan a discutir el Estatuto del Periodista
content:
En un contexto atravesado por la precarización laboral y los desafíos tecnológicos en el campo de la comunicación, el Sindicato de Prensa Bonaerense (SiPreBo) y la Federación Argentina de Trabajadores de Prensa (FATPREN) realizarán hoy, jueves 1º de octubre, el «Foro por el Estatuto del Periodista y la Libertad de Expresión». El evento tendrá lugar a las 11 en el Salón Auditorio de la Cámara de Diputados bonaerense (Edificio Anexo, calle 53 N° 671 entre 8 y 9, La Plata). Bajo la consigna «Por una comunicación democrática y el derecho a la Información», la jornada reunirá a legisladores/as, gremios, universidades, periodistas y trabajadores/as de prensa con el objetivo de debatir la actualización de las normativas que rigen el sector. «El proyecto que será abordado durante el Foro propone actualizar el Estatuto frente a las transformaciones que atravesó la actividad en las últimas décadas, con particular atención al impacto de las nuevas tecnologías, las plataformas digitales y la inteligencia artificial sobre el trabajo periodístico», detallan.

Por ANRed.


Este

jueves 1º de octubre, desde las 11 horas

, se llevará adelante en la Cámara de Diputados de la provincia de Buenos Aires una jornada de debate abierta convocada por el

Sindicato de Prensa Bonaerense (SiPreBo)

y la

 Federación Argentina de Trabajadores de Prensa (FATPREN)

. El encuentro abordará la

actualización del marco normativo del sector, las transformaciones tecnológicas en los medios y la garantía de derechos para los y las trabajadoras

.


La jornada de debate plural busca discutir el proyecto de actualización del Estatuto del Periodista Profesional presentado en el Senado de la Nación. Bajo la consigna «

Por una comunicación democrática y el derecho a la Información

«, la actividad se llevará a cabo en el

Salón Auditorio de la Cámara de Diputados de la provincia de Buenos Aires (Edificio Anexo, primer piso, calle 53 N° 671 entre 8 y 9, La Plata)

.


«En el panel de apertura estarán presentes la secretaria general de la Federación Argentina de Trabajadores de Prensa (Fatpren) y secretaria de Géneros de la CGT,

Carla Gaudensi

; el secretario general del SiPreBo,

David Barresi

; la decana de la Facultad de Periodismo y Comunicación Social de la Universidad Nacional de La Plata (UNLP),

Ayelén Sidún

; la periodista

Juliana Ricaldoni,

 y presidentes de las comisiones de Libertad Expresión de la Cámara de Diputados y del Senado provincial», detallan desde el sindicato y la federación.


La iniciativa surge en respuesta a los cambios estructurales que ha sufrido la comunicación en los últimos años y a las profundas transformaciones en el trabajo de prensa: «el proyecto que será abordado durante el Foro propone

actualizar el Estatuto frente a las transformaciones que atravesó la actividad en las últimas décadas, con particular atención al impacto de las nuevas tecnologías, las plataformas digitales y la inteligencia artificial sobre el trabajo periodístico

«. Además, «la iniciativa también contempla al personal administrativo de las empresas periodísticas y plantea la incorporación y ampliación de distintas garantías vinculadas al ejercicio profesional», amplía la convocatoria.


El temario abarca puntos centrales para las condiciones de trabajo diario y los derechos fundamentales del sector periodístico: «entre los aspectos que forman parte del debate aparecen

la libertad de expresión

, el

derecho a la información

, el

acceso a las fuentes

, la

protección de las fuentes periodísticas

, la

equidad de género

, los

derechos de cuidado

, el

resguardo frente a situaciones de violencia laboral

 y la

seguridad de quienes ejercen la profesión

«.


Frente a la precarización que afecta cotidianamente a las y los trabajadores de los medios tanto tradicionales como comunitarios y digitales, desde el SiPreBo subrayan la necesidad de construir respuestas colectivas: «el objetivo del encuentro es abrir una discusión colectiva sobre los desafíos que atraviesa el periodismo y sobre las condiciones necesarias para garantizar el ejercicio del oficio con libertad y derechos. Por ese motivo, se invita a medios de comunicación y periodistas a participar y cubrir la jornada».

 David Barresi (2214555949).

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: Prosecutors Asked to Consider Manslaughter Charges Over Grenfell Fire
content:
Police investigating the Grenfell Tower fire have submitted evidence to the Crown Prosecution Service, paving the way for potential criminal charges.


The Metropolitan Police’s investigation into the fire in North Kensington has identified 54 individuals and 20 companies and organisations. The CPS will now consider whether to move forward with prosecution.


The offences include corporate manslaughter, gross negligence manslaughter, fraud, health and safety offences, as well as misconduct in public office.


The Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea (RBKC), the council responsible for Grenfell, is among the organisations facing criminal charges.


Almost a decade after the fire, which claimed the lives of 72 people on 14 June 2017, no charges have been brought.


The files submitted today cover all but three of the individuals the Met had said it had identified as being potentially criminally responsible back in

May.


The CPS has said it is committed to making a decision regarding charges ahead of the 10th anniversary of the fire next year, with trials unlikely to begin before 2029.


As part of its investigation, the police looked into more than 15,000 people and 700 organisations, took 14,700 statements and gathered 165 million electronic files and more than 27,000 physical exhibits.


The Met’s investigation ran alongside the public inquiry, whose final report in 2024 found that the disaster was avoidable and exposed decades of failures involving government, regulators and companies involved in the tower’s refurbishment.


But for bereaved families and survivors, the wait for criminal accountability has been agonising.


“No family should have to fight this hard, for this long, for justice,” said Grenfell United, which represents bereaved families and survivors.


“We want those responsible to face justice. If people are found guilty of crimes that cost our loved ones their lives, we want to see them behind bars.


“Only then will people see that there are real consequences for what happened at Grenfell.”

title: Continúa el plan de lucha de residentes y concurrentes que trabajan en hospitales porteños
content:
Imagen: La Izquierda Diario


Trabajadores/as residentes de más de 25 hospitales y efectores de salud de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires se movilizaron la semana pasada en reclamo de una recomposición salarial urgente. Luego, llevaron adelante una asamblea donde se votó seguir con distintas acciones como asambleas en todos los hospitales, campañas de visibilización y un paro con movilización para este jueves 1 de octubre.

Por Red Eco Alternativo.


Los residentes y concurrentes aseguran que su situación salarial no da para más, y que eso se expresa no sólo en sus condiciones concretas de vida como trabajadores, sino también en las precarias condiciones en las que se desarrollan profesionalmente: “El ajuste en salud se siente también en nuestras salas de espera, hospitales, cesacs y farmacias, exigimos presupuesto para salud, para brindar salud pública y de calidad”.


Tras la movilización de la semana pasada fueron recibidos por Cecilia Klappenbach (Directora General de Administración y Desarrollo de Recursos Humanos), Diego Vacchino (Director General de Atención Primaria), Paola Manso (parte de la Subsecretaria de Atención Hospitalaria) y Maria Eugenia Centurion (parte de la Subsecretaria de Atencion Hospitalaria), quienes aseguraron que harán llegar la carta de reclamo salarial al ministro de Salud porteño, Fernan Quiros.


“Exigimos a todas las asociaciones gremiales que integran la Federación que acompañen activamente nuestros reclamos y pongan sus herramientas gremiales al servicio de fortalecer la lucha votada por la Asamblea, también a la Asociacion de Médicos Municipales a que acompañe la medida, convocando a un paro para lograr la movilizacion masiva de les trabajadores de la salud”, afirmaron desde la Asamblea CABA.

author: Hassan Alnaser
title: Drones target Addis Ababa military headquarters; Federal forces advance on Tigrayan capital
content:
The Ethiopian military headquarters in Addis Ababa was targeted in a drone attack in the early hours of Thursday, an Ethiopian security source in the capital told Mada Masr. 


At 6 am, Ethiopian defense systems detected a “simultaneous terrorist attack attempt using suicide drones targeting vital facilities within the capital,” the security source said. “The attack aimed to strike the military command headquarters in the Tor Hailoch area, as well as the vicinity of the 24th Infantry Division headquarters in the Kirkos district of central Addis Ababa.”


A resident of Tor Hailoch who lives near the Ethiopian military headquarters reported hearing  two explosions near the headquarters, the first at 6:30 am and another 45 minutes later. 


The resident told Mada Masr that he saw ambulances and fire trucks rushing through the streets shortly after the blast.


The security source suggested that the drones were downed by the Ethiopian National Defense Force’s air defense systems. 


“Our technical and engineering teams are currently conducting a precise and comprehensive assessment of the material damage caused by projectile shrapnel and are tracing the launch points of these drones, while security forces have established a tight security perimeter and are on high alert around the targeted sites to ensure operational safety.”


The attack comes hours after the Ethiopian National Intelligence and Security Service decided on September 30 to indefinitely ban the use of all types of drones in Addis Ababa and surrounding areas, while announcing the deployment of anti-drone systems and specialized teams to protect airspace and critical infrastructure. 


The security source in the capital told Mada Masr that these measures had been put in place after the September 27 attack on the Harar Meda Air Base in Bishoftu, located approximately 35 miles southeast of Addis Ababa, in which two soldiers were killed, and attacks on Kombolcha Airport and a military base near Bahir Dar Airport. 


A military source in Tigray told Mada Masr that strikes deep within Ethiopian territory are part of an effort to disrupt federal forces’ ability to use air power and drones in the ongoing battles inside Tigray, adding that aerial operations have become integral to the conflict alongside ground maneuvers.


But the attacks are not stopping the advance of federal forces, who are proceeding through southern Tigray toward the state’s capital of Mekelle. 


Following days of fighting, government forces and their allies captured the city of Alamata, approximately 120 kilometers south of Mekelle, in southern Tigray, on September 28, establishing it as a staging point for a northward offensive.


The Tigrayan military source told Mada Masr that the fighting in the region’s south is linked to federal forces’ attempts to open a direct axis toward Mekelle, noting that Tigrayan forces had redeployed to various positions as the pressure shifted to the southern front.


In Mekelle, a strike targeting the Tigray TV station headquarters on September 27 halted the channel’s live broadcasting. The source said that the building was hit by a drone shortly after staff had left the premises. 


The attack on the building came two days after communications across Tigray were cut. 


A political source from Tigray told Mada Masr that the communications blackout and the targeting of Tigray TV station have severely limited information flowing from Mekelle, adding that the political and military leadership is operating under extraordinary communication constraints amid ongoing federal pressure from the south.


To the east of Tigray, a Tigrayan military source in the field told Mada Masr that Tigrayan forces and allied Afar forces are continuing to advance within the Afar region. These forces captured Eribti on September 27 and subsequently advanced along a secondary road connecting to the main Ethiopia-Djibouti highway near Semera. According to the military source, this maneuver is militarily significant due to its link to the A1 highway — known as the Ethiopia-Djibouti road.


A former security source within the Ethiopian intelligence agency told Mada Masr that the push into Afar aims to pressure the supply line connected to Djibouti.

author: CNT Aragón-Rioja
title: CNT Zaragoza pide la nulidad de los despidos en el juicio contra el ERE de Majorel
content:
El pasado 24 de septiembre se celebró en la Audiencia Nacional el juicio contra el ERE de Majorel (TelePerformance), en el que CNT Zaragoza se personó para solicitar que se declarase nulo el despido colectivo y consiguientemente se readmitiese a todas las personas que fueron despedidas.


Esta conocida empresa, situada en el Edificio El Trovador en Zaragoza, ya realizó un primer ERE en febrero de 2026, afectando a decenas de trabajadores de atención telemática y telemarketing para Orange, Tiktok, Lowi, Vodafone, LDA y Naturgy por todo el país. Fue el segundo ERE, que la Sección Sindical de

CNT Zaragoza rechazó y enfrentó durante el mes de mayo

, el que destruyó prácticamente la totalidad de la plantilla en nuestra ciudad, con más de 400 despidos.


Pese a ser conscientes de las escasas posibilidades de obtener una sentencia judicial favorable ante un ERE que, lamentablemente, fue firmado por una mayoría (CCOO y USO) de la comisión negociadora, desde CNT Zaragoza consideramos que debíamos apostar por agotar todas las posibilidades a nuestro alcance para tratar de revertir un despido colectivo que jamás debió producirse.


Animamos a los trabajadores y trabajadoras de Zaragoza a organizarse en el sindicato, porque en

CNT lo tenemos claro: nosotras no firmamos EREs,

 porque no compramos la idea de que perder un trabajo se arregla con dinero. Para nosotras, lo primero debería ser evitar que se destruyan puestos de trabajo,

y esa idea hemos mantenido firmes hasta el final

.

title: Antifa: sentenza d’appello a Budapest, mentre Parigi conferma l’estradizione di Gino verso la Germania
content:
Sentenza a

Budapest

, mercoledì 30 settembre 2026,

nel processo d’appello ai danni di Maja T., Gabri e Anna, tre delle persone antifasciste

 nel mirino della repressione ungherese per aver partecipato – nel febbraio 2023 – alle manifestazioni contro il raduno neonazista del cosiddetto “Giorno dell’onore”.


Da Radio Onda d’Urto


Maja, persona non binaria tedesca, è stata condannata a 8 anni in primo grado, diventati ora 7 in appello. Gabriele, compagno italiano che si trova attualmente, libero, nel nostro Paese, era stato condannato in primo grado a 7 anni, diventati in appello 6. Anna, compagna tedesca oggi in Germania, in primo grado si era vista comminare 2 anni e mezzo; la sentenza d’appello ha confermato la condanna, ma con sospensione della pena carceraria. Il tribunale di Budapest ha chiesto alla Germania di farsi carico dell’esecuzione della pena di Maja. Cosa significa? L’aggiornamento da Budapest con

la giornalista Marta Massa, di Merce, piattaforma di informazione della sinistra ungherese, collaboratrice del Manifesto.


La sentenza di Budapest arriva nello stesso giorno in cui la Corte di Cassazione francese ha rifiutato il ricorso presentato dalla difesa di Rezhino

Gino,

 confermando l’estradizione del militante antifascista verso la Germania.”Se l’estradizione dovesse confermarsi”, scrive Free All Antifas Italy nel dare la notizia, “si teme che Berlino possa favorire la consegna di Gino ai tribunali ungheresi – dove è stato riconosciuto, anche dalla corte francese, un serio rischio di violazione dei suoi diritti”.


Per Gino e per tutte e tutti, oggi alle ore 18 corteo a Milano dal consolato ungherese a quello francese, con Free All Antifas e Comitato contro la repressione.

Nik, del comitato contro la repressione di Milano, raggiunto poco prima delle iniziative del pomeriggio.


Giornata di iniziative fino dal mattino anche a Parigi, da dove avevamo sentito in mattinata Duccio, compagno solidale.

author: cnt.es
title: Reseña del libro ‘Pierre-Joseph Proudhon. Federalismo y mutualismo anarquistas’
content:
Pierre-Joseph Proudhon. Federalismo y mutualismo anarquistas

Florentino Iglesias


Florentino Iglesias nació en Salamanca en 1947, en Ciudad Rodrigo, su familia emigró a Francia, en 1958, cuando él contaba once años. Estudió enseñanza primaria y luego formación profesional en hostelería en Mulhouse, Alsacia. Sus primeros trabajos estuvieron relacionados con su especialidad, al principio en Francia y más tarde en Suiza. En Basilea su puesto de trabajo se encontraba cerca de una librería especializada en historia cuyo escaparate observaba con curiosidad y admiración siempre que pasaba delante de él. En esa librería conoció a Heinrich Koechlin —escritor y militante anarquista— con el que trabó amistad. Esa relación le permitió contactar con libertarios españoles que formaban parte de un grupo de Basilea. A partir de ese momento su proceso de inmersión ideológica fue intenso y frecuentó otros militantes ácratas como Ramón Álvarez (CNT), Louis Lecoin o Gaston Leval. Antes de unirse al grupo de Leval, participó en el grupo anarquista del distrito 18 liderado por Maurice Joyeux y su compañera Suzy Chevet. Pero finalmente, donde se encontró más cómodo fue en el grupo de Gastón Leval, que según su apreciación estaba compuesto por personas muy preparadas. En ese tiempo recuperó el contacto con Julián Gorkin a quien había conocido años atrás. En 1968 participó en los acontecimientos de mayo en París. Siete años después, en 1975, regresó a España e intervino en la reconstrucción de la CNT. Se puede decir que sus fuentes de formación política e intelectual han sido amplias y le han llevado a estudiar las más variadas disciplinas. Con el paso del tiempo y su profundización en la cultura anarquista, nació su pasión por la obra de Pierre-Joseph Proudhon de la que surge el texto que se reseña.


Este libro hace un recorrido exhaustivo por la obra de Proudhon. Comienza con un análisis de la revolución de 1848 y sigue con otros temas relevantes, como su antagonismo con Marx, su crítica al Estado y al principio de autoridad; también examina su pensamiento económico, hace énfasis en la lacra social que supone la “propiedad privada” e indaga en las connotaciones del vocablo “Anarquía” y sobre la teoría del contrato social, la organización mutualista, los fundamentos del federalismo, la justicia, el derecho, la religión y la revolución como desarrollo progresivo.


Según describe Iglesias, para Proudhon la Revolución de 1848 fue un suceso trascendental que no sólo marcó muchas de sus reflexiones posteriores sino que le dio a conocer entre la clase obrera. Para él la revolución no se podía producir de manera improvisada o precipitada. En el periódico que editaba,

Le Peuple

, explicó su programa y acusó a la izquierda de “infantilismo revolucionario”. Esa revolución fue importante porque la clase trabajadora, por primera vez, reivindicó una “reorganización de la sociedad, el derecho al trabajo y la justicia social”. En ese momento la organización obrera se basaba en sociedades de socorro mutuo; es a partir de este punto histórico donde se van a sentar las bases del “sindicalismo moderno”. Durante la Revolución del 48 el autor francés rechazó cualquier solución política “viendo en ella una fuente de alienación”. Proudhon se preguntaba entonces: “¿Quién debe gestionar la economía?”. En dicha revolución las fuerzas participantes eran tres, la clase trabajadora y la burguesía grande y pequeña, y al respecto dijo: “[…] Nosotros queremos que sean las asociaciones el primer núcleo de una vasta federación de compañías y de sociedades, que creen la república democrática y social. […] No queremos ni gobierno del hombre por el hombre ni la explotación del hombre por el hombre”. Proudhon propuso la creación de un Banco del Pueblo. En su folleto

Solución del problema social,

 resumió sus ideas económicas. Consideraba que una revolución desde arriba sería antirrevolucionaria. A pesar de que parecía tener claro lo poco que se podía conseguir desde las instituciones, se presentó a las elecciones y fue elegido. “El 31 de julio, por fin, Proudhon expone su proyecto de ley ante una Asamblea recelosa y agitada”, apunta Iglesias. Desde luego, su iniciativa no fue apoyada y en un escrito posterior dijo: “Desde que puse los pies en el Sinaí parlamentario, dejé de estar en contacto con las masas”. A raíz de esta experiencia sólo tuvo una preocupación: “Atraer la atención de la clase obrera sobre los problemas económicos y desviarla de toda política puramente …
