author: Meli Newen
title: Malleco: Pueblo mapuche en lucha por territorio ocupado por la «industria de la basura»
content:
Rodrigo Curipán es werken del lof Rankilko, y vocero de las cuatro comunidades que se han opuesto al relleno sanitario en territorio mapuche, ubicado alrededor de 8 kilómetros de Collipulli, provincia de Malleco, Región de La Araucanía.

Se trata de un centro de residuos domiciliarios de grandes dimensiones que se instaló sin el consentimiento de la población originaria de la zona y que lleva 6 años de funcionamiento. Es administrado por una empresa que, en principio, se ocupó de procesar los desechos de las ciudades de Collipulli, Ercilla, Angol y Renaico. «Originalmente, una asociación de municipales buscó un espacio donde botar la basura y ese espacio lo definió dentro del territorio mapuche. Según los municipios, le compraron el terreno a Forestal Mininco (grupo Matte). Para ello, primero debió levantarse una infraestructura adecuada. Contra esa infraestructura estamos luchando», explica Curipán.

«En un pozo gigante al que le ponen algunas capas de plástico para evitar que los percolados salgan a la superficie, sin éxito. Es un terreno de 14 a 15 hectáreas. Y la gestión del relleno está bajo control de la compañía privada Cosemar y William Ives S.A., toda vez que el territorio es nuestro.»

– ¿Cuáles son los perjuicios fundamentales para las familias mapuche?

«El daño irreversible que nos provoca no sólo es ambiental, sino que cultural, medicinal y espiritual porque ya no podemos acceder al lugar. Por su parte, el consorcio se saltó toda la legislación chilena y se edificó con la intención premeditada de perjudicar a los mapuche. El estudio de impacto ambiental incurrió en varias irregularidades, en particular en lo concerniente a la prohibición de levantar este tipo de proyectos cuando afectan humedales y agua destinada al consumo humano. Las comunidades tampoco fueron consultadas.

Por eso, el año 2023, con el propósito de detener la construcción del relleno sanitario, recurrimos a la Corte de Apelaciones de Temuco a través de un recurso de protección que fue acogido en primera instancia y en forma unánime por los jueces, porque el hecho es ilegal, arbitrario y discriminatorio. Sin embargo, entre el desacato, la burocracia y los informes de la Corporación Nacional de Desarrollo Indígena, Conadi, que favorecieron con mentiras descaradas los intereses de la empresa al escribir que en el territorio disputado no existen comunidades, pues todavía estamos luchando.»

– ¿Qué significado cultural tiene la ciénaga donde ahora está el relleno para la cosmovisión mapuche?

«El Menuko es el corazón de todas las actividades espirituales del pueblo mapuche y el Estado chileno nos desplazó de ese sitio sagrado, desapareciéndolo con un basurero. Como si no fuera suficiente el agravio, la empresa que destruye nuestra espiritualidad hoy está custodiada por policías y militares.»

– ¿Por qué ustedes debieron acudir a la Comisión Interamericana de Derechos Humanos, CIDH?

«La Corte Suprema cambió el fallo de la Corte de Apelaciones de Temuco por una cuestión de forma y no de fondo, y le dio el favor a la compañía de relleno. Aquí nosotros consideramos que hubo una intervención política del gobierno de Piñera para que se contradijera el fallo de la Corte de Apelaciones, con el fin de que las comunidades mapuche retrocedan en su proceso de recuperación territorial.

La primera petición a la CIDH la hicimos el 17 de mayo de 2021, la cual fue notificada al Estado de Chile el 7 de septiembre de 2023, casi dos años después. Y nosotros recibimos la primera respuesta de la Comisión el 28 de octubre de 2024. Ella nos comunicó que nuestra petición, efectivamente, reúne las condiciones suficientes para revisar la causa, y en julio de 2026 nos informó que nuestra demanda contra el Estado cuenta con admisibilidad, o sea que tiene sentido jurídico, y que el Estado chileno pudo vulnerar nuestros derechos.

Ahora tenemos de 4 a 6 meses para reunir más antecedentes para fortalecer nuestra argumentación, los cuales tenemos de sobra. De este modo, la Comisión puede pasar el caso a la Corte Interamericana de DDHH, o bien buscar una instancia para conversar con el Estado y establecer un acuerdo. Ahora, nosotros sabemos perfectamente que el Estado chileno no actúa de buena fe y, por tanto, una vez que sepamos qué solución de fondo recomendará la Comisión, persistiremos en nuestro objetivo inicial: la desmantelación y erradicación del basural. No nos interesan las compensaciones económicas porque nuestros propósitos son culturales y territoriales, o …

author: Meli Newen
title: Opinión: Asesinos de Palestina, asesinos de América Latina
content:
Los asesinos de Palestina ahora vienen por América Latina. Vienen por el agua para intensificar el capital de la gran agricultura en contra de los pequeños, para nutrir de armas a las Fuerzas Armadas e involucrarnos en sus guerras; para abastecer de ciberseguridad a las proliferantes empresas de seguridad e intensificar los dispositivos de control para que miles de Cerimedos sean posibles y así las repúblicas latinoamericanas sean destruidas y sustituyan al sujeto pueblo por el sujeto algoritmo.

FUENTE: La Voz de los que Sobran

25 de septiembre, 2026 – Palestina al olvido -tal y como el sueño sionista aspira. Palestina recluida, nuevamente, a ser negada. Los medios no son neutrales respecto de la nakba, constituyen parte de ella, de su maquinaria de borramiento, precisamente en el instante en que docilizan al espectador con un genocidio en vivo en orden a normalizar las pasiones y despotenciar el horror que experimentamos. La idea sionista de colonización de Palestina no consistió jamás en la simple “ocupación” sobre el territorio para vaciarlo, expulsando enteramente a su población. Su apuesta fue siempre más allá: no solo expulsar población, sino negar completamente su existencia.

Todo el proyecto de colonización sionista no solo implicó la sustitución de la población nativa por la población colona sino también, la negación de que dicha población nativa realmente existía. Bien decían Elías Sanbar y Gilles Deleuze a principios de los años 80: el proyecto sionista sobre Palestina consistió en la producción de un vacío. Sin embargo, este proceso de borramiento ya no es solo un proyecto circunscrito a Palestina. Es, sobre todo, una apuesta desplegada a nivel global: los medios no solo niegan la existencia de Palestina y, con ello, colaboran todos los días, con la empresa de la nakba perpetrada por Israel y el imperialismo occidental, sino también a las multitudes que resisten la imposición de su dominio.

Los asesinos de Palestina ahora vienen por América Latina. Vienen por el agua para intensificar el capital de la gran agricultura en contra de los pequeños, para nutrir de armas a las Fuerzas Armadas e involucrarnos en sus guerras; para abastecer de ciberseguridad a las proliferantes empresas de seguridad e intensificar los dispositivos de control para que miles de Cerimedos sean posibles y así las repúblicas latinoamericanas sean destruidas y sustituyan al sujeto pueblo por el sujeto algoritmo.

Pero, sobre todo, la penetración estadounidense-israelí (el sionismo, al fin y al cabo) en América Latina va sobre los recursos naturales: agua y las “tierras raras” que ofrece el territorio nacional, dado que China tiene alrededor del 80% de ellas, el desarrollo de la industria de Inteligencia Artificial por parte de Estados Unidos e Israel, así lo demanda. Es clave, en este sentido, el hecho de que hoy asistimos a una palestinización de América Latina: no sólo Estados Unidos ha sometido al continente a partir del Escudo de las Américas sino conjuntamente con Israel que, a partir de los Acuerdos de Issac que ha firmado con Argentina, intenta proyectarse en el continente en función de la sangrienta competencia por la industria de la Inteligencia Artificial. En este marco, la sionización de las oligarquías latinoamericanas y la palestinización de sus pueblos es ya una realidad: el gobierno de Kast es el primer gobierno sionista de la República de Chile.

Ahora bien, la palestinización del mundo y la sionización del imperialismo no constituye una novedad para la historia. En 1492 mientras las naves de Cristóbal Colón llegaban a las imaginarias “Indias” para encontrar un atajo a China, los Reyes Católicos terminaban la conquista de Al Andalus obligando al último reino musulmán de Granada a su capitulación. Todos los métodos que los católicos usaron contra los musulmanes y judíos en orden a la conquista de la península ibérica fueron utilizados, posteriormente, en la conquista de las tierras americanas. Por eso, la palestinización del mundo no es una anomalía al funcionamiento del orden imperial, sino su regla. Al igual que la experiencia andalusí, todas las tecnologías de despojamiento que Israel aplica contra los palestinos lo vende globalmente en sus empresas de armas, seguridad y aguas.

Ahora bien, detengámonos en el nombre dado a los acuerdos reservados para América Latina: Isaac. Ante todo, tenemos que leer bajo la rúbrica de la teología política sionista que traduce el relato bíblico en una narrativa de la muerte que …

author: Chris Walker
title: Paxton Caught on Tape Saying Trump’s Midterm Convention Dragged Republicans Down
content:
“Everybody’s numbers dropped” after Trump’s midterm convention event, the Senate candidate from Texas was heard saying.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

An audio recording of a private conversation between U.S. Senate candidate Ken Paxton (R-Texas) and conservative donors last week reveals that he may view President Donald Trump as a “drag” on his and other Republicans’ campaigns.

It’s unclear whether the discussion in the recording is directly about Trump, and parts of it are difficult to hear or understand. In the recording, a donor asks Paxton, who is the current Texas attorney general, whether the candidate feels “like he’s a little bit of a drag,” without explicitly stating who “he” is.

Paxton responds by discussing the recently held GOP midterm convention, which was heavily promoted by Trump.

“So to be honest with you, the numbers — when we did that convention — it dropped our numbers. Everybody’s numbers dropped. Right now, yeah, not good,” Paxton says in the recording.

The conversation occurred during a GOP fundraising event last week. The New York Times obtained audio of the discussion from a source who attended the event, who describes themselves as opposed to Paxton’s campaign.

Leaked audio of Ken Paxton:Q: Do you think Trump is a bit of a drag?Paxton: To be honest with you, when we did that midterm convention, it dropped our numbers. Everybody’s numbers dropped. Yeah. Not good.

The conversation — whether Trump was the subject or not — is likely to upset the president, who called for as many Republicans as possible to attend the midterm convention. The event, held in Paxton’s home state of Texas, was billed as a means to promote GOP candidates throughout the country, though many in the party were skeptical of having Trump as the headliner.

Trump has embarrassed Paxton, too, albeit more publicly. Earlier this month, Trump said Paxton “may not be the best-looking guy I’ve ever seen,” at an event where he was attempting to promote the candidate.

Paxton may be correct that the midterm convention for the party hasn’t helped him or other Republicans. According to an average of polling data collected by FiftyPlusOne, Paxton was within 2-3 percentage points of his Democratic opponent, state Rep. James Talarico, during the first few days of September. Currently — weeks after the convention was held — Talarico has expanded his lead slightly, leading Paxton by 3-4 points in the polls over the past several days of averages.

Republicans in general have seen their numbers slip since the convention. In an Economist/YouGov poll conducted from September 4-8 (just days before the convention began), Democrats led Republicans by 11 points among likely voters. In the most recent poll, conducted September 25-28, that lead has widened to 15 points.

Other surveys have indicated that Republicans’ continued fealty to Trump is dragging them down, making it more likely that Democrats will win control of the House and potentially even the Senate in the midterms. According to a recent NPR/PBS NewsHour/Marist poll, 45 percent of Americans said they wanted their vote to be viewed as symbolic opposition to the Trump administration, while only 24 percent said they wanted it to be seen as a vote in support of Trump.

author: Kelcie Moseley-Morris
title: Republican Attorneys General Sue Abortion “Shield Law” States in Supreme Court
content:
The AGs also filed a separate lawsuit in a Louisiana district court against individual providers in three states.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Louisiana Attorney General Liz Murrill and the attorneys general in Arkansas and Alabama filed a lawsuit Tuesday in the U.S. Supreme Court, suing California, Massachusetts and New York to invalidate the so-called “shield laws” that have allowed providers in those states to send abortion medication to people in states with abortion bans.

The state officials, all Republicans, also filed a lawsuit in federal district court against individual abortion providers in the same three states.

“We will not allow activist states, activist providers or distributors profiting from killing babies to threaten Louisiana’s sovereignty, violate Louisiana’s laws and endanger Louisiana women and Louisiana babies,” Murrill said at a news conference on Tuesday. Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin and Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall of Alabama also were present.

The lawsuit filed in the Western District of Louisiana seeks to stop the individual providers named from being able to prescribe and send abortion medication to those states, while the Supreme Court complaint asks the justices to find the shield laws are a constitutional violation of state sovereignty..

“Today, plaintiff states filed a lawsuit against as many organizations and individuals as they have been able to identify notwithstanding the shield laws intended to thwart such litigation,” the Supreme Court complaint reads. “To fully obtain relief, however, they must also eliminate other contributing causes for the harm that they are suffering, including … the shield laws.”

The district court suit names 30 defendants, including the Massachusetts Medication Abortion Access Project and its founder, Angel Foster, Dr. Remy Coeytaux in California and other telehealth providers around the country.

The complaint compares the mailing of abortion medication to anthrax, mail bombs and chemical weapons, despite studies since 2000 showing that abortion medication is safe and effective to use.

“(Defendants) think themselves invincible because their agents swear to never step foot in plaintiff states (thereby avoiding arrest), and their home states have enacted so-called ‘shield laws’ intended to thwart legal liability for individuals perpetrating this interstate abortion scheme,” the complaint says.

Following the U.S. Supreme Court’s decision in 2022 allowing states to ban abortion at any stage of pregnancy, 13 states now have near-total bans, while others have expanded abortion access. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration allowed the drug mifepristone, one of two commonly used to terminate a pregnancy in the first trimester or to treat miscarriages, to be dispensed without a visit to an in-person provider in 2023, after years of safety studies.

Providers in states with access can prescribe and mail the medication to states with bans, and Murrill, along with other state AGs, has tried to extradite those providers to Louisiana to face legal charges for violating the ban. One of the providers Murrill tried to extradite in January was Coeytoux in California. Governors in those states have refused to comply with the extradition requests.

To protect those providers, California, Massachusetts and New York were among the 22 states and the District of Columbia that passed shield laws to block out-of-state investigations and prosecutions against providers dispensing for abortion medications to patients in other states.

Murrill is also leading a lawsuit against the FDA to reverse the 2023 provision allowing telehealth access to mifepristone, and two other lawsuits of a similar nature are ongoing in Missouri and Texas. The 5th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals heard arguments in Louisiana’s case earlier this month and is expected to issue a decision in the coming weeks about the future of nationwide access to the drug.

Louisiana Illuminator reporter Piper Hutchinson contributed to this report.

author: Redazione_web
title: Iniziato l’abbattimento di Bosco Ospizio a Reggio Emilia
content:
Oggi 30 settembre le ruspe hanno iniziato ad abbattere gli alberi del Bosco Ospizio.  


Le ruspe sono entrate dopo più di una settimana di serrato tamtam sulle testate locali della stampa serva -televisiva e cartacea- e sui social, in cui conad illustrava la bontà e la bellezza del suo progetto, ponendosi quasi come un ente no profit dedito alla cura e salvaguardia dell’ambiente e non come una comune azienda capitalista affamata di profitto.   


A proteggere le ruspe c’erano decine di poliziotti in tenuta antisommossa e parecchi altri in borghese, nonché varie pattuglie di vigili urbani armati di taser, pronti ad affrontare chissà quali minacce. 


Ma non c’erano solo loro: erano -e mentre scrivo sono ancora- presenti anche tante di quelle persone che in questi mesi hanno portato avanti il presidio permanente in difesa del bosco, e tante altre che sono passate a testimoniare l’ennesimo scempio della natura in favore del cemento. Scempio ben rappresentato dall’abbattimento di un acero di circa vent’anni e sei metri di altezza, contro il quale una ruspa si è accanita per una buona mezz’ora prima di riuscire a spezzarlo. Sì, perché nemmeno l’onore della motosega è stato riservato alla vegetazione: forse per “dimostrare” che non era un bosco si sono usati mezzi più adatti a estirpare dei cespugli. Una tristezza infinita. Tante persone presenti avevano le lacrime agli occhi, altre erano decisamente incazzate.  


La violenza del capitale sta già distruggendo il Bosco Ospizio. Per evitare altri crimini contro l’ambiente, in questa città e ovunque, servirà una mobilitazione più generale e permanente. 


J.Scaltriti

author: David Swanson
title: World Teachers’ Day: What Kind of Future Are We Educating For?
content:
By Phill Gittins, World BEYOND War, September 30, 2026


On World Teachers’ Day, we want to begin with a simple message: 

Thank you.


To teachers, facilitators, trainers, youth workers, community educators and everyone helping people learn, question and act: thank you for the work you do.


This year’s

World Teachers’ Day theme

 speaks of teachers ‘shaping our futures.’ It raises a simple question:


What kind of future are we educating for?


Education shapes how we understand peace, conflict, security and war; what futures we can imagine; and what we believe we can change.


At

World BEYOND War

, education is one of the main ways we work for change.


We call our approach

pro-peace and anti-war education

: helping people develop the knowledge, skills, relationships and collective capacity to build peace and contribute to more peaceful, just and inclusive societies, while critically examining the systems, institutions, cultural norms and interests that prepare for, normalize and sustain war.


The aim is not to tell people what to think, but to help them question, imagine alternatives and build the confidence and capacity to act — individually and together.


We do this through

online courses and programs

; webinars and podcasts; books, study guides, research and publications; curricula and free resources, including our

Anti-War & Pro-Peace Resources Database

; workshops and training; and education woven through our

chapter and campaign work

,

media and communications

.


We also work with educators, activists and organizers, as well as groups, organizations, communities, networks and movements, to strengthen practice, adapt learning to different contexts and help others learn more effectively.


More than 4,000 people around the world have taken part in our online education courses. In 2027, when our forthcoming book,

From the War System to a Peace System

, is published, we hope to bring more of these alumni together around it for further learning, discussion and action.


From learning to action


Education matters, but on its own it is not enough. One of the ways we connect learning with action is through our

Peace Education and Action for Impact program (PEAI)

.


Since 2021, PEAI has connected and supported young people, adult mentors and community partners in more than 25 countries across five continents, including Afghanistan, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Colombia, Ethiopia, Haiti, Iraq, the Philippines, Russia, South Sudan, Ukraine, Venezuela and elsewhere.


The 14-week program combines six weeks of online peace education with eight weeks of youth-led, community-rooted action, alongside mentoring, intergenerational collaboration and cross-cultural exchange. Participants use what they learn to design, implement and communicate projects responding to issues in their own communities.


One recent example: PEAI Sri Lanka


Sarala Nihari


PEAI Sri Lanka 2025


“PEAI taught me that we do not have to wait for peace to happen. We can begin building it ourselves through one conversation, one act of respect, and one small positive action at a time.”


Rev. P. Gnanalakkhana


PEAI Sri Lanka 2025


“One significant result of this experience was the translation of academic frameworks into community-level interventions.”


In February 2027, we plan to build on this with a new university-community PEAI initiative across eight universities in Sri Lanka. The program will build the capacity of young people, university faculty and administrators through peace education and mentoring, strengthen connections between universities and their surrounding communities, and culminate in eight locally led peace projects in different parts of the country.


Helping strengthen peace education beyond our own programs


Alongside working directly with learners, educators, activists and organizations, we also contribute to the wider research, policy and practice around peace education.


One current example is follow-up work on

Recommendation CM/Rec(2026)11 of the Committee of Ministers on peace education by, with and for young people

. This builds on earlier independent consultancy for the Council of Europe during the Recommendation’s development and now involves collaboration with Council of Europe colleagues and others on taking it forward.


In the short term, this includes publications and a planned webinar bringing together organizations working on peace education in Europe and beyond. Longer term, we hope this work …

author: Anjali Kamat
title: Mahmoud Khalil’s New Memoir, No Land to Stand On, Looks Beyond His Own Case
content:
The Palestinian activist discusses his book, his lawsuit against Columbia University, and fighting deportation.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

We speak with Palestinian activist Mahmoud Khalil about his new memoir, No Land to Stand On: Notes from Detention. It details his 104 days of detention inside a Louisiana ICE jail after he was targeted for arrest and deportation by the Trump administration over his pro-Palestine campus advocacy at Columbia University. Khalil missed the birth of his first child, Deen, while he was separated from his wife, Noor Abdalla, who is a U.S. citizen. The administration is still trying to deport Khalil, who has launched civil rights lawsuits against the government and Columbia University over his treatment.

“Eighteen months after my arrest, this administration has never charged me with any crime or even presented any evidence that I committed any crimes, yet they are able to get away with this because I’m Palestinian,” Mahmoud tells Democracy Now!

Khalil’s memoir also looks beyond his own case, recounting the people he met behind bars and what their stories taught him about the broader human cost of the U.S. immigration detention system. “This book is about a story of so many incredible men, fathers and workers who came here seeking safety and a better future, only to be snatched off the street,” he says.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

ANJALI KAMAT: No Land to Stand On: Notes from Detention. That’s the title of a searing new memoir by the first pro-Palestinian campus protester to be jailed by the Trump administration: Columbia University graduate and Palestinian student protest leader Mahmoud Khalil. On March 8th, 2025, Mahmoud was detained by plainclothes police officers who did not identify themselves in the lobby of his apartment building in Columbia University housing. His wife, Noor Abdalla, who was eight months pregnant at the time, filmed this video of his arrest as Mahmoud was being taken away. Her voice is heard in the clip.

DR. NOOR ABDALLA: Can you — can you please specify what agency is taking him, please? Excuse me. They’re — nobody — they’re not talking to me. I don’t know. Excuse me, the lawyer would like to speak to somebody. Oh my god, they’re literally running away from me.

AMY GOODMAN: That was March 8th, 2025. Mahmoud was taken into immigration detention, ultimately transported more than 1,300 miles away, to Louisiana. He spent over a hundred days in jail and was denied permission to attend the birth of his first child, Deen. He could only listen on the phone.

Mahmoud Khalil’s new memoir also looks beyond his own case, recounting the people he met behind bars, including immigrants who had lived in the United States for years and parents who were separated from their children, and what their stories taught him about the broader human cost of the U.S. immigration crackdown.

Mahmoud Khalil was released in June of last year and spoke outside the detention facility, the ICE jail, in Jena, Louisiana.

MAHMOUD KHALIL: No one is illegal. No human is illegal. That’s the message. The message is: Justice will prevail, no matter what this administration may try to portray.

ANJALI KAMAT: More than a year after Mahmoud Khalil’s release, the Trump administration is still seeking to deport Khalil. The Board of Immigration Appeals has approved his removal, and this week the board denied Khalil’s request to end his removal proceedings. His lawyers are pursuing further appeals, including seeking review by the Supreme Court.

In his new memoir, Khalil takes on not only the Trump administration, but also Columbia University, which he sued earlier this month, alleging it failed to protect pro-Palestinian students, instead retaliating against them when they reported harassment. Khalil writes in his new memoir, quote, “Rather than protecting its doxxed students, Columbia leaned into the intimidation campaign.”

In his memoir, Khalil describes the moment, just days after his arrest, when he came to see himself not simply as an individual facing deportation, but as a test case. He writes about his decision to take on the Trump administration and fight for his freedom, saying, quote, “My case was the blueprint they wanted to set, and the one we had to tear up.”

AMY GOODMAN: Well, for more, we’re joined now by Mahmoud Khalil to …

author: Thiago Domenici
title: iFood passa R$ 3 milhões para pesquisa científica após acordo para encerrar inquéritos
content:
Em 16 de abril de 2021, um homem de colete preto circulava entre os entregadores do iFood que faziam greve em frente ao estádio do Pacaembu, em São Paulo. Tinha um adesivo no boné, outro no face shield, além de uma faixa de três metros de comprimento e pacotes de adesivos para distribuir. Todos diziam a mesma coisa: “vacina pros entregadores de aplicativo já”.


Parecia mais um motoboy, mas segundo a

Agência Pública

 revelou,

era um funcionário de uma agência de monitoramento digital a serviço de uma campanha contratada pelo iFood. A ideia da empresa era levantar a pauta das vacinas para esvaziar a reivindicação da greve.

 Funcionou: naquele dia, parte da imprensa

noticiou

 que os entregadores pediam vacinas.


A cena abre “A máquina oculta de propaganda do iFood”,

reportagem

 de Clarissa Levy para a

Pública

, de abril de 2022. Com base em mais de 30 documentos e em relatos de quem trabalhou no projeto, a apuração descreveu como as agências Benjamim Comunicação e Social QI (SQi) teriam operado, entre 2020 e 2021, uma propaganda “lado B” contra os “Breques dos Apps”.


Um documento de orientação resumia a regra: “NUNCA assinado como iFood para que ninguém desconfie”.

Numa reunião gravada, obtida pela reportagem, publicitários da Benjamim avaliaram que a Não Breca Meu Trampo “cumpriu uma missão” ao enfraquecer Paulo Lima, o Galo, líder dos Entregadores Antifascistas.

 O iFood negou qualquer relação com a SQi e disse que não compactua com perfis falsos. As agências contestaram a reportagem à época.


iFood não pode interferir em greves de entregadores


Nesta semana, o caso chegou a uma nova etapa, conforme

informou

 o Ministério Público Federal (MPF), nesta terça-feira, 29 de setembro.

O iFood repassou R$ 3 milhões ao Conselho Nacional de Desenvolvimento Científico e Tecnológico (CNPq) para financiar pesquisas como parte de um Termo de Ajustamento de Conduta (TAC) que a empresa, a Benjamim e a SQi assinaram em 7 de julho de 2023 com o MPF e o Ministério Público do Trabalho (MPT) para encerrar três inquéritos abertos a partir da denúncia da

Pública

.


Apesar de ter aceitado o acordo, o iFood não reconhece as condutas e repete isso na

página que mantém sobre o TAC

: afirma que “não cometeu qualquer uma das condutas investigadas” e que assinou o TAC para evitar um processo “longo e desgastante”.


O TAC se divide em três eixos: satisfação, não repetição e compensação. Os dois primeiros, segundo o MPF, foram cumpridos “em larga medida”.


A declaração pública conjunta veio primeiro. Pelo registro do próprio iFood, saiu no site da empresa em 10 de julho de 2023, na página inicial da

Folha de S.Paulo

 no dia 16 e, entre 18 de julho e 5 de agosto, em dias alternados, no Instagram, no Facebook e no Twitter.


Depois, veio a campanha sobre o direito à informação e a liberdade de expressão dos entregadores, com três meses de peças semanais nos perfis oficiais do iFood, criadas com a Benjamim e com alcance medido pela SQi. A proposta foi entregue aos procuradores em setembro de 2023. O MPF informa que a campanha foi realizada.


No eixo de não repetição, o iFood indicou três consultorias em direitos humanos em agosto de 2023. O MPF escolheu uma em outubro, e a contratação foi concluída em dezembro. Cabe à consultoria elaborar um programa interno para identificar riscos à transparência e à liberdade de expressão nas atividades da empresa, com relatórios semestrais ao MPF por dois anos. O MPF diz que a medida é inédita em TACs e que o programa segue “sob acompanhamento”. Por seis meses, o iFood também ficou proibido de anunciar suas próprias medidas de respeito ao direito de greve.


Outras obrigações não têm prazo para serem cumpridas.

Perante o MPT, o iFood se comprometeu a não bloquear, suspender ou descredenciar entregadores por participação em greves ou sindicatos, a não usar “prepostos ou instrumentos tecnológicos” para interferir em manifestações e a não premiar quem deixar de aderir a paralisações.

 Benjamim e SQi assumiram compromissos semelhantes. Cada obrigação descumprida gera multa de R$ 50 mil por mês, até o limite de R$ 500 mil por ano.


Dinheiro vai para pesquisas sobre trabalho de entregadores e responsabilidade de plataformas


O eixo de compensação é o que se movimenta mais lentamente.

O TAC fixou em R$ 6 milhões o valor que o iFood deve investir em pesquisas sobre três temas: relações de trabalho dos entregadores, mercado publicitário e responsabilidade das plataformas.

 O acordo não …

title: Öcalan: The YBŞ must become part of the Iraqi army and remain in Shengal
content:
The Shengal People’s Council provided information on the latest developments in the region during an assembly. Representatives of Yazidi civil society organizations, the local population, and Yazidi security forces took part in the meeting on Wednesday. A message from Abdullah Öcalan was read out during the assembly.


In the message, the Kurdish leader focuses in particular on the future of the Shengal Resistance Units (YBŞ) and the protection of Yazidi society. He advocates integrating the YBŞ into the Iraqi army while allowing it to remain in Shengal as a local force. “The YBŞ must remain in Shengal,” Öcalan states, describing the Yazidis’ own self-defense forces as necessary.


Öcalan also addresses the talks between the YBŞ and the Iraqi government. According to the information available to him, an agreement has already been drafted but has not yet been signed by the Iraqi prime minister. Reports indicate that the agreement is being blocked by Turkey. Öcalan calls on Ankara not to obstruct it and emphasizes that the Yazidis are not demanding an autonomous region, but local democracy.


Abdullah Öcalan's message to the Yazidi community reads as follows:


“Do Yazidi women have a strong stance in the face of ISIS attacks? This needs to be understood. Yazidi culture alone is also not sufficient for freedom. I say this, and I have also told the state the same thing, and I repeat it: In view of the threat of attacks against the Yazidis in general, we will protect them through armed means. Even if everything goes well here, we will shift more of our focus there and protect them. The state must understand this as well.


My message to this young woman is this: What has happened to you must make you stronger. You must develop your personality. A common language must be created that will carry the line forward. If you know Kurdish, you should also learn to write it and use the language extensively. You should write down what you have experienced and preserve it for history. I hope that we will see each other soon.


The YBŞ must remain in Shengal. If this does not happen, neither Barzani nor the Arabs will grant them the right to live. If the YBŞ becomes part of the Iraqi army, they must remain where they are. A decision has been made to eliminate them. The Yazidis must have their own self-defense forces. The Yazidi people are currently undergoing a process of genocide and have no legal protection.


According to the statements that have been made, talks are taking place between the YBŞ and the Iraqi government. An agreement is even said to have already been drafted. However, the prime minister has not signed it. It is said that the Turkish state is blocking the agreement. The Turkish state must not obstruct it. Because the Yazidis are not talking about an autonomous region. They want local democracy. We will discuss all of this with the High Committee. I assume that our demands will be readily accepted. It is the KDP that seeks discrimination and division. We will also discuss this at our committee meeting.


For Shengal, a model similar to the one in Turkey should be developed. That is why I removed the obstacle posed by the PKK. The PKK is no longer an obstacle to resolving the problems. In other words, the PKK has completed its time and fulfilled its role. However, if action is not taken in accordance with this reality, it will become incapable of acting during this process. Ultimately, I decided to dissolve the PKK, and I take responsibility for that decision. There may be some shortcomings, but this approach is correct.


Self-defense is a necessity in Shengal. The YBŞ must take its place within the Iraqi army. According to what has been reported, Iraq has agreed to this. If that is the case, it is a good thing. It is still unclear who is behind ISIS. Arab nationalism is strong. Even if this nationalism is pushed back, they will eliminate the Yazidi people as soon as they have the opportunity. Arab nationalism subjected the Turkmens in Kirkuk to a massacre. Local security is necessary to prevent this from happening again.


In Iraq, this applies to almost every tribe. The system that exists in Turkey does not exist in Iraq. Such protection is also necessary for the Turkmens and Yazidis. The problems of the Yazidis must also be resolved. A close relationship must be established with Shengal.”

title: Conference in London: The path for democratic politics must be opened to achieve lasting peace
content:
On the second day of the Peace and Democratic Integration Conference in London, the future of the Kurdish question was discussed by individuals with direct experience of the struggle and resolution processes. İmralı Secretariat member Veysi Aktaş spoke about the 1999 disarmament experience, while Çetin Arkaş recounted his 33.5 years in prison and the period he spent on İmralı. Legal guarantees for disarmament, opening up space for democratic politics, and the role of women in the peace process emerged as key themes of the panel.


The first session of the second day, titled “Post-Conflict Kurdish Democratic Politics,” featured İmralı Secretariat members Veysi Aktaş and Çetin Arkaş, Nesrin Akgül representing the Kurdish Women’s Movement, and Yüksel Genç, a member of the First Peace Group. Moderated by journalist Tuğçe Tatari, the session addressed the transition from armed struggle to democratic politics, experiences from previous processes, legal guarantees, conditions on İmralı, and the role of women in the new period.


Speaking at the opening of the second day, politician Serpil Kemalbay said that the Kurdish political movement had begun to open the way for a new and different form of struggle. Emphasizing that peace does not simply mean the silencing of weapons, she stressed that coexistence must be built on political will and strong legal guarantees.


Aktaş recounts the 1999 experience


Veysi Aktaş based his speech on previous attempts to resolve the Kurdish question and on his own experiences.


Recalling the 1999 call for disarmament and a transition to the political sphere, Aktaş recalled that they had also taken steps and laid down their arms at the time in order to strengthen the prospects for peace, but he subsequently spent more than five years in prison. He said the 1999 experience demonstrated that laying down arms alone was not enough to produce a result.


After all these years, democratic politics, law, and disarmament are once again being discussed today, said Arkaş, according to whom the resolution of the Kurdish question must be addressed beyond the framework of security policies.


During the panel’s question-and-answer session, Aktaş also addressed the debate over laying down arms and self-defense, saying that Öcalan supports resolving the Kurdish question through democratic means in all four parts of Kurdistan.


Emphasizing that keeping channels for democratic politics open is crucial, Aktaş said: “If the avenues for democratic politics are open, there is no place for violence. Violence must absolutely be abandoned. This is President Abdullah Öcalan’s position.”


Drawing attention to the current legal and political conditions, Aktaş underlined that Kurdish identity and freedoms must be placed under legal protection and that opportunities for democratic political participation must be expanded.


Genç: Without legal guarantees, the process remains fragile


Drawing on past experiences, Yüksel Genç highlighted the legal gaps between disarmament and the transition to democratic politics. Recounting the experience of the 34-member group that entered Turkey in 2009, Genç recalled that 29 people were initially released, while five were referred to court and ultimately released as well. However, she said that different judicial proceedings and detention orders were later brought against 30 of the 34 members.


This experience demonstrates that political will and legal guarantees are not the same thing, she said, adding: “As long as all of this is not placed under legal protection, the process remains fragile.”


Emphasizing that people who lay down their arms must know in advance what they will face the following day, Genç said that questions such as where they will live, how they will work, how they will continue their education, how they will return to social life, and under what conditions they will participate in democratic politics cannot be left unanswered.


Yüksel Genç stated that every stage of disarmament must have a clear legal framework, emphasizing that peace should not be limited solely to the future of those who have participated in armed struggle, but must also encompass freedom of expression, political representation, a voice in local decision-making, cultural rights, and the space for civil society.

title: Removed co-mayors of the DEM Party demand an end to trustee rule
content:
The removed co-mayors of ten DEM Party-run municipalities have called for an end to trustee rule and for their reinstatement to the offices to which they were elected. At a meeting in Mardin on Wednesday, they assessed the consequences of the trustee policy and linked their demand to the Peace and Democratic Society Process.


Following the meeting, Devrim Demir, the removed co-mayor of Mardin Metropolitan Municipality, said that the discussions had focused on the consequences of trustee rule in the ten affected municipalities. “The picture that has emerged clearly shows that trustee rule means plunder and the usurpation of political will.” Demir also criticized the fact that government austerity measures apparently do not apply in the same way to municipalities under trustee rule. “All the avenues that were closed to us to prevent us from providing municipal services are open to the trustees. This policy must be ended as soon as possible.”


With regard to the Peace and Democratic Society Process, Demir said that the steps taken by the Kurdish Freedom Movement had so far not been met with corresponding steps by the state. The removed mayors called on the government to seize the current historic opportunity through decisive measures. “The conditions must be created for Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan to live and work freely. The usurpation of political will must end immediately, and all of our friends must return to their offices,” Demir said.


Ahmet Türk: Trustee rule must be completely ended


The removed co-mayor of Mardin, Ahmet Türk, also accused the appointed trustees of plunder and corruption. However, he said that the decisive issue was the interference with the political will of the population. “Trustee rule means plunder, corruption, and the seizure of the people’s political will. We condemn this policy not only because of the corruption, but above all because it usurps the will of our people,” Türk said. The politician called on the public, civil society organizations, and all democratic forces to act together against the system of trustee rule.


“The process needs a legal foundation”


Türk also placed particular emphasis on the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Recalling the political developments since MHP Chair Devlet Bahçeli shook hands with DEM Party MPs in parliament in October 2024, he said that Abdullah Öcalan had taken responsibility on his part for transforming the process that had begun into a lasting peace. “There is a process underway, and this process is very valuable to us. We have demands to ensure that it can lead to lasting peace. For this, a legal foundation must be established,” Türk said.


Referring to the start of the new legislative session of the Turkish parliament on October 1, he said they would continue to insist on their demands for the necessary legal arrangements. “We, our party, and Mr. Abdullah Öcalan will insist until the very end that the legal demands are met. We are following and supporting this process with patience.”

author: Unknown
title: Kurdish nurse tortured after arrest by Iranian intelligence
content:
Iranian Ministry of Intelligence agents arrested Kurdish nurse Foad Ghaderi on 21 September as he travelled from Sanandaj to Javanrud.


During several days of interrogation at the ministry’s detention facility in Javanrud, he was subjected to severe physical and psychological torture in an attempt to force him to confess. He was then transferred to Dizel Abad Prison in Kermanshah.


The Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) has reported that Ghaderi, from the village of Sarrud-e Olya in Javanrud, worked as a nurse at a private medical centre in Sanandaj. Agents arrested him at the Naleh Shekineh mountain pass on the road between Kamyaran and Ravansar and took him to the Javanrud detention facility.


After his arrest, Ministry of Intelligence agents raided his family home and took away some of his personal belongings.


Since his arrest, he has been denied access to a lawyer and visits from his family. The charges against him remain unknown.

title: Conference in London: Integration is possible through rights and freedoms
content:
The second day of the Peace and Democratic Integration Conference, organized by the Centre for Kurdish Affairs in London, continued with discussions on the political future of the Kurdish question in its different parts.


The session, titled “The Kurdish Question Across Borders,” was moderated by journalist Fréderike Geerdink. Ilham Ehmed participated via video message, while Dr. Abdulkerîm Omer, Dr. Shilan Fuad Huseyîn, and Dr. Hêmin Seyîdî contributed their assessments.


 


Ehmed said integration must be based on freedom and rights


Ilham Ehmed discussed the process underway in Syria and the position of the Kurds in the country’s future. She said that an agreement providing for a ceasefire had been reached on January 29, adding that the aim was to end the war and establish a process that would enable Kurds to participate in the Syrian state and its institutions.


Ehmed said that, within this framework, the integration of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) into the army, the Internal Security Forces into the Ministry of Interior, and the institutions of the Autonomous Administration into state institutions were on the agenda. She noted that some steps had been taken, but that serious problems remained, particularly in the field of education.


Ehmed said that the teaching of Kurdish for three hours a week in government schools had been accepted, but that Kurdish had not been recognized as an official language of education. She pointed out that there are children who have been educated in their mother tongue for years and who speak only Kurdish. Saying that changing the education system overnight could negatively affect these children’s future, Ehmed stated that they want Kurdish to be recognized as an official language of education for Kurds in the Syrian Constitution.


Stating that Kurds should be represented in all of Syria’s institutions and ministries, Ehmed said that, in addition to the Kurdish community’s cultural, geographic, and social rights, its right to engage in political activity must also be guaranteed. Emphasizing the importance of women’s participation in political and administrative decision-making mechanisms, Ehmed said: “The integration being discussed must be genuine and must be based on freedom and rights.”


The struggle will continue through peaceful methods


Dr. Abdulkerîm Omer said that one of the main issues going forward would be how democratic forces should organize themselves. Noting that discussions were continuing over how the new political structure in Rojava would take shape, Omer said it had not yet been decided whether it would be a party or a broader and more inclusive political formation.


Omer said that different options were being discussed: a political structure consisting solely of Kurds, or a common structure encompassing the different peoples, social groups, political forces, and ideas in Syria. Within this framework, he added, a national and democratic political formation addressing all of Syria was also among the options.


Emphasizing that the position on the methods of struggle going forward was clear, Omer said: “From now on, the struggle will not continue through weapons and military methods, but through politics, diplomacy, and peaceful struggle.”


Stating that political organization needed to be strengthened and channels of dialogue and diplomacy developed, Omer said the aim was for Kurds to take part in Syria’s future with their own identity and rights, and to build a common, democratic, and peaceful future together with other peoples and social groups.


Saying that they viewed the process with hope, Omer stressed the need to stay away from political demagoguery and narrow calculations. “The real issue is not repeating what happened in the past, but how we will build the future,” he said.


Without women's freedom, unity remains incomplete


In her speech, Dr. Shilan Fuad Huseyîn drew attention to the relationship between Kurdish unity, autonomy, and women’s freedom. She said that Kurdish unity could not be understood merely as geography, borders, language, or the bringing together of different political parties under a single national name. Unity, she argued, should be a relationship that recognizes differences, shares power, and guarantees freedom equally.


Emphasizing that the question of women was one of the fundamental criteria for the political and social structure being sought, Huseyîn said: “Without women’s freedom, unity remains incomplete …

author: Unknown
title: Conference in London: Democratic transformation essential for peace
content:
On the second and final day of the Peace and Democratic Integration Conference, held in London, the panel titled “Inclusive Peace: Women, Minorities, Human Rights and Justice Systems” took place.


The panel was moderated by Dr. Nisan Alıcı and featured politician Gültan Kışanak, DEM Party parliamentary group deputy chair and Qers MP Gülistan Kılıç Koçyiğit, Dr. Güneş Daşlı, a research fellow at Loughborough University’s CARA, journalist and writer Ali Duran Topuz, and lawyer and writer Gürkan Çakıroğlu. Topuz and Çakıroğlu joined the panel online.


The panel addressed women’s role in the peace process, a democratic solution to the Kurdish question, social reconciliation, legal guarantees, truth and justice, and the role of the media.


Kışanak: Women must be founding agents of peace


Politician Gültan Kışanak emphasized that speaking only with the government would not be enough to resolve the Kurdish question and that broader social reconciliation also needed to be achieved.


Drawing attention to how state and government policies have deepened social polarization, Kışanak said that Kurdish demands and the Kurdish struggle had been stigmatized through narratives such as “a foreign powers’ plot” and “a threat to national survival.”


 


Stressing the importance of women being present at the negotiating table, participating in decision-making processes, and being recognized as political agents in their own right, Kışanak said that the Kurdish women’s movement had been involved in the struggle from the outset as both a social movement and a founding force. She highlighted equal representation, co-chairmanship, and women’s organized presence in political life.


Kışanak recalled that Abdullah Öcalan had stated during discussions that the process could not move forward without women’s participation, emphasizing the importance of women’s involvement in decision-making mechanisms.


In her speech, Kışanak placed particular emphasis on the Peace Mothers, noting that mothers who had lost their children had taken their demand for peace into the streets. She said that the Peace Mothers’ stance gave them strength.


Recalling that women had established peace initiatives in different parts of Turkey during previous processes and had worked to make peace a broader social cause and overcome opposition to the Kurdish question, Kışanak stressed: “It is not only Kurds who need peace; everyone needs peace.”


Kışanak noted that the state had not taken sufficient steps to make peace a broader social issue in the current process and that women’s participation had also remained limited.


She continued: “The struggle for peace is too important to be left to the government, the ruling elites, and imperialists.”


Kışanak said that those who seek freedom, equality, and peace must regard this struggle as their own. She added that peace politics needed to be strengthened within broader areas of social struggle and that diplomatic efforts should be expanded.


Silencing the guns doesn't solve the Kurdish question


DEM Party parliamentary group deputy chair Gülistan Kılıç Koçyiğit referred to the Kurdish question’s century-long history, saying that a new period was emerging amid developments in the Middle East and around the world. Koçyiğit identified one of the main obstacles to the process as the continued framing of the Kurdish question in terms of security and “terrorism.”


She said that the PKK laying down its arms or the end of armed conflict would not, in itself, resolve the Kurdish question. She emphasized that a state of “negative peace,” in which weapons are silent and there is no armed conflict, would not be sufficient for a democratic solution.


Koçyiğit described the steps taken so far as a beginning, but stressed that the process needed to be expanded and brought into society. She said that society should not merely observe the process but should actively shape it.


Koçyiğit said that the state and government needed to take concrete steps, drawing attention to the appointment of trustees to replace elected local officials, prisons, local government, the Anti-Terror Law, and the need for changes to criminal and prison legislation. Addressing the debate on democratic integration, Koçyiğit asked: “Then what are we going to integrate into, democratically? It is clear and obvious that we cannot integrate into the existing order. We did not struggle in order to integrate into a patriarchal system in the first place.”

title: Συγκεντρώσεις αλληλεγγύης και διαμαρτυρίας, Πέμπτη 1/10
content:
>Συγκέντρωση αλληλεγγύης σε συλληφθέντα αντισιωνιστικής παρέμβασης, 10:30 δικαστήρια Ευελπίδων


>Συγκέντρωση ενάντια στις αστυνομικές εισβολές στη Φιλοσοφική, 11:30 στην είσοδο της σχολής


>

Κάλεσμα σε συγκέντρωση αλληλεγγύης στον συλληφθέντα σύντροφο της αντισιωνιστικής παρέμβασης


Δικαστήρια Πρώην Σχολής Ευελπίδων – Πέμπτη 1/10 10:30 (Κτίριο 3, Αίθουσα 3)


Το Σάββατο 12/07/25, πραγματοποιήθηκε από την ανοιχτή αντισιωνιστική συνέλευση στο κέντρο της πόλης μία ακόμα παρέμβαση ενάντια στους σιωνιστές δολοφόνους και τη γενοκτονία του παλαιστινιακού λαού. Μετά την ολοκλήρωση της παρέμβασης, οι ένστολοι υπηρέτες του αστικού κράτους, εγκλώβισαν το σώμα της πορείας και επιβάτες του ηλεκτρικού για αρκετά λεπτά στο σταθμό στο Θησείο, δίνοντας εντολές για ακινητοποίηση του συρμού. Παράλληλα, επιτέθηκαν απρόκλητα στον κόσμο που βρισκόταν μέσα στο συρμό, τραυματίζοντας και τον -μετέπειτα συλληφθέντα- σύντροφο, ενώ πραγματοποιήθηκαν και άλλες 8 πολύωρες προσαγωγές σε περιοχές πέριξ του κέντρου.


Ο συλληφθείς σύντροφος, ο οποίος, αν και ήταν χτυπημένος, κρατήθηκε μέχρι και τη Δευτέρα 14.07.25 και καλείται να παρουσιαστεί στα δικαστήρια της Ευελπίδων την Πέμπτη 01/10, αντιμετωπίζοντας σωρεία πλημελληματικών κατηγοριών.


Το καλοκαίρι του 2025 υπήρξε μια περίοδος κατά την οποία οι δράσεις αλληλεγγύης στον παλαιστινιακό λαό πολλαπλασιάστηκαν σε όλη την Ελλάδα και το ελληνικό κράτος, ως πιστός συνεργάτης της σιωνιστικής οντότητας, επιλέξε να τις χτυπήσει με κάθε μέσο.


Το βάθεμα της σχέσης του ελληνικού κράτους και του σιωνιστικού μορφώματος, η αυξανόμενη διείσδυση του ισραηλινού κεφαλαίου στην ελλάδα επιτάσσουν από τη μία τη χρήση ιδεολογικών μηχανισμών και πρακτικών, όπως αυτή της “αντισημιτικής ρητορικής” για το ξέπλυμα των εγκλημάτων των σιωνιστών δολοφόνων, και από την άλλη την χρήση άμεσων κατασταλτικών τακτικών. Με σαφή στόχο την τρομοκράτηση των αλληλέγγυων και τελικά την επιβολή σιγής ιχθύος στις λαϊκές και ταξικές δυνάμεις που υπερασπίζονται το δικαίωμα του παλαιστινιακού λαού στην αυτοδιάθεση, το δικαίωμά του για Γη και Ελευθερία.


Απέναντι στην όξυνση της κρατικής καταστολής, εν μέσω μιας συντελούμενης γενοκτονίας και της αδούλωτης στάσης του παλαιστινιακού λαού, το ελάχιστο που μπορούμε να πράξουμε είναι να ακυρώσουμε στην πράξη τους σχεδιασμούς του ελληνικού κράτους και της ελληνικής αστικής τάξης, σχεδιασμοί που βρίσκονται σε πλήρη σύμπλευση με τους ιμπεριαλιστικούς σχεδιασμούς ΗΠΑ-ΕΕ-ΝΑΤΟ-Ισραήλ, στεκόμενοι δίπλα σε κάθε σύντροφο που αντιμετωπίζει τον κρατικό ρεβανσισμό και δυναμώνοντας τις δράσεις αλληλεγγύης στον παλαιστινιακό λαό.


ΑΛΛΗΛΕΓΓΥΗ ΜΕ ΤΟΝ ΣΥΛΛΗΦΘΕΝΤΑ ΣΥΝΤΡΟΦΟ Γ.Π.

Από το Πάσχα μέχρι και σήμερα, σε διάστημα 6 μηνών, έχουν πραγματοποιηθεί τρεις αστυνομικές εισβολές στη φιλοσοφική σχολή Αθηνών. Τι δουλειά έχουν, όμως, οι μπάτσοι στις σχολές και τι θέλουν να πετύχουν;


Το προπαγανδιστικό αφήγημα της πάταξης «της ανομίας και της εγκληματικότητας» δεν μπορεί να πείσει κανέναν που δεν φορά τα μυωπικά γυαλιά της αστικής προπαγάνδας και έχει έστω και μια ελάχιστη εικόνα του τι συμβαίνει μέσα στα πανεπιστήμια. Όχι, οι μπάτσοι δεν μπουκάρουν στις σχολές για να συλλάβουν «κακοποιούς», μαφιόζους και εμπόρους ναρκωτικούς. Με αυτούς, άλλωστε, δεν έχουν πρόβλημα οι πρυτανικές αρχές, όπως έχει δείξει και η μακροχρόνια συνεργασία τους με την εργολαβία των μαφιόζων της “ΜyServices”.


Οι μπάτσοι εισβάλουν στα πανεπιστήμια για να καταστείλουν τους φοιτητικούς αγώνες, τις αντιστάσεις, τις κινητοποιήσεις και τις καταλήψεις των φοιτητών που στρέφονται ενάντια στα αστικά σχέδια των ταξικών φραγμών και των ιδιωτικοποιήσεων που επιχειρούνται να επιβληθούν στην τριτοβάθμια εκπαίδευση. Εισβάλουν για να εκκενώσουν χώρους αντίστασης, αγώνα, πολιτικοποίησης και ριζοσπαστικοποίησης της …

author: Kiara Green
title: 2026 Midterm Elections: A Guide to Voting and Making an Informed Choice
content:
With Election Day less than 40 days away, voters across the country are preparing to cast ballots in the 2026 midterm elections. On November 3, voters will decide congressional, state, and local races, and ballot measures in states across the country.

With so many races and issues on the same ballot, it is crucial that citizens are making informed decisions when they cast their ballot. Voters may encounter campaign advertisements, social media posts, news coverage, and information from candidates themselves, making it difficult to find a clear overview of where candidates stand on the issues.

One resource that can help is guides.vote, a non-partisan voter guide that provides information about candidates and their stances on a range of issues.

Guides.vote produces nonpartisan voter guides with the help of experienced editors, researchers, and veteran journalists. The guides provide information about candidates’ positions on issues and are designed to help voters compare candidates before casting their ballots.

These guides are available digitally and in print and are offered in both English or Spanish. Guides.vote currently includes 2026 election information for races in states across the country.

The organization includes candidates who are polling at 15% or more in the races covered by its guides. Its 2026 guides address issues including abortion, climate change, criminal justice, education, health care, immigration, labor, LGBTQ+ rights, taxes, gun laws, and voting rules.

Rather than telling voters how to vote, the guides provide information that voters can use to make their own decisions.

Start by Checking your Voter Registration

Before researching candidates, make sure you are registered to vote at your current address.

Voter registration deadlines vary by state. Some states allow eligible voters to register in person and cast your ballot during early voting or on Election Day. Ballotpedia maintains a state-by-state list of registration deadlines.

Voters should also check that their registration is active and that their address and other information are up to date.

Find Out What Is on Your Ballot

Casting an informed ballot is built on knowing what’s on the ballot.

Depending on where you live, your ballot may include candidates for the US House and Senate, governor, state legislature, judges, and local offices. It may also include ballot measures. Ballot measures are questions that voters get to decide on often about alterations to laws, policies, taxes, and constitutional amendments. The wording of ballot measures can be deceiving so understanding them before walking to the polls is important.

Sample ballots are often available through state and local election offices. Reviewing your sample ballot before voting can help you understand which races and measures you will be deciding.

This is where resources such as guides.vote can be particularly useful.

Voters can use the guides to learn where candidates stand on issues and compare their positions before Election Day. Because state and local elections can have a direct impact on people’s daily lives, voters should look beyond federal races when researching their ballot.

For local elections and additional voting information, voters can also visit vote411.org/feminist.

Election Day is Tuesday, November 3, but that is the last day to vote for many states. Early voting and mail voting options vary by state—all of which accommodate obstacles that may prevent people from casting their ballot.

Check your state’s election website for information about early voting locations, mail-in voting, polling places, voter ID requirements, and election deadlines.

Once you know your options, make a plan. Decide when and how you will vote, find your polling location if you are voting in person, and make sure you know what identification you may need.

Participating in elections gives voters a voice in the decisions that shape their communities. With control of the House and Senate at stake this November, voters will have the opportunity to shape the direction of federal policy, while state and local elections will determine leadership and policies closer to home. Check your registration, research your ballot, make a voting plan, and be ready and empowered to vote!

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Report: Nearly 1,300 Schools, 210 Health Centers Damaged in Iran Amid US Assault
content:
The war has knocked out six hospitals, including a children’s cancer hospital that was temporarily rendered inoperable.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

A new report details the widespread damage to civilian infrastructure in Iran amid the U.S.-Israeli war, adding to war crimes allegations as the U.S. openly targets civilian sites and threatens genocide against the country’s 92 million residents.

An analysis of media, economic, and government reports by the National Iranian American Council (NIAC) released on Tuesday found that strikes against sites like schools, airports, health centers, and civilian-related industries “present a pattern in which economic infrastructure was a target category itself.”

“The consequences did not remain at the strike sites. They propagated through every system that connects a modern society,” the report found. “Iran’s people entered this war already impoverished, already traumatized by a lethal crackdown, already disconnected from the war. The war took much of what remained.”

As of late August, before the latest renewal of strikes, the war had damaged or destroyed 80 energy facilities, 27 airports, 12 bridges, two tunnels, over 210 health centers, and at least 1,288 schools, including 32 universities, in Iran, the report finds. The war has also had dire impacts on industries that support Iran’s economy, taking out, at one point, 70 percent of Iran’s refining throughput, while 70 percent of steel production capacity has been destroyed.

It is difficult to statistically quantify the human toll amid the war, as Iran’s government does not regularly report losses. According to the UN, over 3,400 civilians had been killed in Iran as of the end of June, with 33,000 injured and 149,000 civilian units damaged.

The damages have had catastrophic consequences for the economy, with over 1 million jobs lost and food inflation up by 100 percent, deepening deprivation in a country already suffering from widespread poverty as a result of decades of U.S. and other international sanctions. Some strikes have directly hit food-related infrastructures, like wheat storage silos and fishing vessels.

This week, the rial hit another record low after the Trump administration’s latest escalation of its sanctions regime, which has been likened to collective punishment by Iranian officials. The economic impacts of the war have led to “daily deprivation” for Iranians, the report says, citing testimonies from residents who say they are cutting back on certain types of food or going without it altogether because of skyrocketing prices.

While NIAC’s report focuses on damage to civilian sites in Iran, Iranian forces have also struck civilian sites in other countries as Iran retaliated against U.S.-Israeli strikes.

NIAC’s findings come as the U.S. has come under international scrutiny for civilian harms and war crimes. A UN mission found in a report released this month that the U.S. committed war crimes in its strikes on February 28 on a school in Minab and a sports facility in Lamerd.

One airport, the Bushehr International Airport, was completely destroyed during 13 nights of consecutive U.S. strikes in July, the report found. The airport was the main civilian airport in the area, but was also used for military purposes; the report notes that the “military function at one part of a shared airfield cannot license the destruction of the passenger terminal … particularly in a war waged without authorization from the UN Security Council.”

In April, Iranian officials announced that over 210 medical centers were hit during the war, but the Iranian Red Crescent said that month that 339 medical facilities had been damaged. Around that time, the UN noted that between 24 and 26 health workers had been killed.

One of the worst incidents was the damage to a cancer hospital for children, the Shahid Baghaei Hospital in Ahvaz, in southern Iran. The hospital was temporarily taken out of service in July and over 200 patients were forced to evacuate after U.S. strikes nearby caused shockwaves that damaged the facility.

author: CMI Argentina
title: “Denunciar el genocidio en Gaza no es delito”
content:
Esta mañana la Policía Federal allanó los domicilios de dos militantes de Izquierda Socialista en Rosario, aludiendo a sus actividades en redes sociales en el marco de la Asamblea por Palestina.


Al respecto, Carla Deiana expresó: “Hoy por la mañana allanaron los domicilios particulares de dos militantes de IS y el Frente de Izquierda de Rosario, por el solo hecho de participar en actividades que denuncian del genocidio en Gaza, en el marco de la Asamblea multisectorial de Acción por Palestina. ¿Saben qué actividad estaban impulsando para hoy por la tarde? La proyección de la película Gran Palestina, la misma por la que persiguen a docentes de la Facultad de Humanidades y Artes de la Universidad Nacional de Rosario. La Justicia Federal ha sido reducida en Argentina a una máquina de censura al servicio del estado de Israel”.


Para Deiana: “Esta acción de amedrentamiento muestra que no es broma cuando Milei dice que ‘echó a 20.000 terroristas’. Forma parte de una política de persecución y espionaje contra los que denuncian el terrorismo que ejecuta el estado Israel contra el pueblo palestino. Que el fundamento sea lo expresado en redes sociales, muestra que el operativo de ciberpatrullaje que impulsó Bullrich está armado para perseguir a quienes son opositores al alineamento del gobierno de Milei con Netanyahu”. Y concluyó: “Denunciar un genocidio no es delito. Viva Palestina Libre. Repudio total al operativo de la Policía Federal”.

title: Ante la amenaza de la instalación de torres de alta tensión comunidades recurrirán a la justicia contra el proyecto Itahue-Hualqui
content:
La iniciativa contempla una línea de transmisión de 407 kilómetros entre el Maule y Biobío, y ha sido cuestionada por los efectos que generaría sobre ecosistemas, actividades productivas y formas de vida locales, así como por la falta de una evaluación integral de sus impactos acumulativos relacionados con otras iniciativas extractivas que se proyectan para estas regiones, tanto energéticas como vinculadas a la minería de tierras raras.


La acción judicial será presentada ante el Segundo Tribunal Ambiental para solicitar la revisión de la decisión que mantuvo vigente la aprobación ambiental del proyecto Sistema de Transmisión Zonal Grupo 3 S/E Itahue – S/E Hualqui, luego del rechazo del recurso administrativo de invalidación.


Con esta acción se inicia una nueva etapa en la judicialización del proyecto, luego de que el Comité de Ministros resolviera mantener su aprobación ambiental. La reclamación cuestionará tanto aspectos de forma como de fondo de la decisión adoptada durante el procedimiento de evaluación ambiental.


La iniciativa, presentada por el consorcio español CELEO Redes, a través de su empresa Mataquito Transmisora de Energía, contempla una línea de 407 kilómetros entre el Maule y Biobío, amenazando los ecosistemas y la calidad de vida de los habitantes de 20 comunas. Expertos advierten vacíos técnicos en la evaluación ambiental y riesgos acumulativos por la concentración de infraestructura eléctrica.


Los argumentos


Entre los principales argumentos que serán presentados ante el Tribunal se encuentra la falta de fundamentación técnica para revertir los pronunciamientos desfavorables de organismos sectoriales, particularmente aquellos formulados por CONAF y otros organismos con competencia ambiental.


La acción también cuestiona las deficiencias de la línea de base en materia de flora y vegetación, incluyendo la caracterización de especies en categoría de conservación, ecosistemas críticos y bosque nativo remanente en sectores próximos al área de amortiguación e influencia del Parque Nacional Nonguén.


En materia de fauna, se señala que la evaluación ambiental no habría considerado adecuadamente la pérdida y fragmentación de hábitats, los impactos acústicos asociados a las líneas de transmisión y los riesgos de colisión y electrocución para aves migratorias, rapaces y especies amenazadas o endémicas.


La reclamación también aborda deficiencias relacionadas con recursos hídricos y suelos, particularmente por la construcción de torres, caminos e instalaciones en sectores de ladera, junto con los posibles efectos de erosión y arrastre de sedimentos y la afectación de humedales, vegas y cursos de agua.


Consulta indígena y participación ciudadana


Otro de los ejes de la acción judicial es la falta de consulta indígena, en relación con los efectos que el proyecto tendría sobre territorios ancestrales, sitios de significación cultural y ceremonial, espacios de recolección de

lawen

 y prácticas tradicionales de comunidades y asociaciones indígenas de las comunas involucradas.


Asimismo, se cuestiona la evaluación de los impactos sobre los sistemas de vida y costumbres de las comunidades locales, considerando actividades agrícolas, apícolas, ganaderas y de subsistencia, además de aspectos como la división de terrenos, pérdida de valor predial, ruido, contaminación electromagnética y riesgos asociados a incendios forestales.


Para Marioles Quevedo, vecina de Maqueuto Sur, la instalación de las torres representa una amenaza para un territorio donde se desarrollan actividades agrícolas, apícolas y ganaderas.


“Defendiendo mi territorio, defendiendo mi naturaleza y los animales silvestres de Maqueuto Sur, donde quieren instalar doce hectáreas de torres produciendo un gran daño al ecosistema, un impacto ambiental. Nuestro entorno es apícola, agrícola y ganadero. Todos mis vecinos y mi familia no queremos este tipo de torres de transmisión eléctrica, debido a su alto impacto a nuestro ecosistema y su entorno natural”.


A ello se suma el cuestionamiento a los procesos de participación ciudadana, respecto de los cuales se alegará la exclusión de organizaciones comunitarias e indígenas y la insuficiencia de las instancias desarrolladas durante la evaluación ambiental.


Para Macarena Lagos, integrante de la agrupación Toconey No Se Toca, de la región del Maule, la decisión de recurrir a tribunales responde a la necesidad de continuar defendiendo el territorio frente a los efectos negativos que la …

author: Unknown
title: We can definitely use the words estrogen and testosterone (though ‘get curvy HRT’ might also involve…
content:
trackerkitsune

:

queeranarchism

:

nico-thenecromancer

:

mx-macintosh

:

they are estrogen and testosterone

.

they are estrogenizing and androgenizing hrt.

 stop fucking calling them transfem and transmasc hrt. stop fucking calling them mtf and ftm hrt. stop fucking calling them feminizing and masculinizing hrt.

stop going out of your way to exclude non-binary and intersex people.

As a non-binary person on hrt (and in the process of getting off it) I approve this message!

Honestly I have mixed feelings about this, because I encounter a lot of trans people who didn’t stay in school long enough to learn to read, or who don’t have English as their first language, or have a disability that impacts language, for whom learning the words ‘estrogenizing and androgenizing’ are not easy tasks.

Communicating in this ways would alienate them from the spaces in which I am trying to talk about HRT. & those spaces are already far too dominated by college educated white middle class trans kids.

Like, I could see myself explaining all the effects of both options and then calling it 'get curvy HRT’ and 'grow hair everywhere’ HRT’. But I would not go for words that make it qall sound even more complicated.

As a nonbinary person, have we tried just calling them estrogen and testosterone??? And not infantilising whole people who can, in fact, learn to say words with a bit of patience and grace given to them?

Can we stop dumbing down language?


We can definitely use the words estrogen and testosterone (though 'get curvy HRT’ might also involve progesterone and one of 6 different kinds of blockers) but we still have to explain what they are and what they do.

Because people do. not. know. I’ve done a lot of trans-on-trans education and people with language-barriers often lack the most basic knowledge about what hrt does and doesn’t do. I’ve met people who thought they could grow fully functional penis and balls on T and could get women pregnant with sperm from those new balls. I’ve met people who thought it was impossible to grow boobs on E.

People don’t know and they can not 'just google it’ because that requires access to written text or being able to navigate complicated text-to-speech software. It’s overwhelming and asking for help is scary because ignorance and illiteracy gets shamed a lot. So when they do ask for help, they need someone to explain HRT to them in words that they already know.

There is nothing 'infantilising’ about meeting people where they’re at and including the whole spectrum of disabilities in our spaces without expecting them to first learn enough to meet our communication standards. Simple language is a basic accessibility issue for a lot of people. So yeah, we

need

 to dumb down language if we actually want

all

 trans people to have access to care and community.

author: Publicación Abierta
title: Farsacracia Argentina: el infame recorrido de los traidores
content:
La historia reciente de la Argentina parece escrita por manos que confunden poder con impunidad. El artículo 154 del inconstitucional DNU 70/2023 marcó el inicio de una ofensiva contra la soberanía nacional: al permitir la venta ilimitada de tierras a extranjeros, se abrió la puerta a la entrega del territorio, disfrazada de “modernización” y “libertad económica”. Fue el primer acto de una farsa institucional que hoy alcanza su clímax.


La reacción popular no tardó. Las movilizaciones ciudadanas, las organizaciones sociales y los centros de excombatientes denunciaron el atropello y lograron que la justicia declarara la

inconstitucionalidad del decreto

, recordando que ningún gobierno puede disponer del suelo argentino como si fuera mercancía. Ese fallo fue una victoria de la ciudadanía, un recordatorio de que la soberanía no se negocia.


Pero los intereses espurios no descansan. El siguiente intento llegó bajo otro nombre: el proyecto de

“Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada”

, una maniobra legislativa que buscaba reinstalar el mismo espíritu entreguista, esta vez con ropaje jurídico. El Senado, presionado por la movilización popular, rechazó el proyecto. Otra vez, la calle impuso su voz frente al poder.


Sin embargo, la trama no terminó allí. La reciente decisión de la

Corte Suprema de Justicia

 de revocar el fallo que había frenado la derogación de la Ley de Tierras y restablecer el artículo 154 del DNU 70/2023 representa el último capítulo de esta farsacracia: un sistema donde las instituciones parecen servir más a los intereses del capital extranjero que al pueblo argentino. La Corte, escudada en tecnicismos, evitó pronunciarse sobre el fondo, pero su silencio es cómplice. Con su fallo, deja nuevamente abierta la puerta a la extranjerización del territorio.


Cada intento de entrega fue frenado por la movilización ciudadana. Cada vez, el pueblo salió a defender lo que es suyo. Pero los poderes económicos, los lobbies y los jueces funcionales al modelo de dependencia han demostrado que pueden imponerse incluso contra la voluntad popular.


Hoy, más que nunca,

la soberanía está en peligro

. No por invasiones externas, sino por traiciones internas. Por quienes, desde los despachos, venden el país pedazo a pedazo mientras hablan de progreso.


La historia no se repite: se profundiza. Si el pueblo no vuelve a ocupar las calles, si no defiende su tierra, su agua y su futuro, la Argentina quedará reducida a un territorio administrado por intereses ajenos. Es hora de despertar, de organizarse, de resistir. Porque

la soberanía no se mendiga: se defiende.


La entrada

Farsacracia Argentina: el infame recorrido de los traidores

 se publicó primero en

Indymedia Argentina Centro de Medios Independientes (( i ))

.
