title: Jorge Macri redobla la apuesta represiva en CABA
content:
El gobierno de CABA busca avanzar con la implementación y el uso de sistemas de reconocimiento facial en el espacio público. Nuevo desalojo. Las escuelas asociadas al sistema penal. Contra la Marcha del Orgullo


Por Mario Hernandez


El gobierno de la Ciudad está intentando reactivar el sistema de reconocimiento facial mediante cámaras instaladas por todo Buenos Aires. El viernes pasado se celebró una audiencia judicial para revisar el nuevo proceso de licitación impulsado por el gobierno. ¿Por qué una audiencia judicial? Porque existe una causa legal en curso que ha mantenido suspendido el sistema de reconocimiento facial durante cuatro años. En abril de 2019, la ciudad activó el sistema de reconocimiento facial, cuyo objetivo declarado era identificar a prófugos y personas con órdenes de captura pendientes.


El sistema no se utilizaba para localizar a prófugos; por el contrario, terminaron incluyendo indiscriminadamente a 10 millones de personas. Elaboraban listas arbitrarias y actuaban a partir de ahí. Todo esto salió a la luz gracias a la labor del CELS, ODIA, Ceprodh y diversas organizaciones de Derechos Humanos dedicadas a estas cuestiones. En 2022, la justicia declaró inconstitucional la implementación del sistema y, en 2023, la Cámara de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires ratificó dicho fallo.


“Ley y Orden”, dejó a 60 personas en la calle


Durante la mañana del martes, bajo la lluvia, un operativo de la Policía de la Ciudad desalojó a 60 personas de un edificio del barrio porteño de Constitución. En el inmueble ubicado de la calle Luis Sáenz Peña 1700, donde antiguamente funcionaba un hotel, vivían desde hace 21 años familias con niños, incluso.


Tres camiones, un vallado y varios efectivos fueron dispuestos para llevar adelante la medida. La orden judicial fue dispuesta por el Juzgado de Primera Instancia en lo Contencioso Administrativo y Tributario N°9.


Desde el Gobierno porteño señalaron que el inmueble no reúne condiciones de seguridad para ser habitado debido a su deterioro edilicio y a la falta de mantenimiento. Sin embargo, como se ha advertido, es la modalidad utilizada por la justicia porteña servil a los intereses del PRO para avanzar con esta verdadera expulsión de personas.


Denuncian que Jorge Macri convierte a las escuelas en una puerta de entrada al sistema penal


El Gobierno de la Ciudad avanza con la implementación del Régimen Penal Juvenil dentro de las escuelas porteñas. Un nuevo protocolo establece que las autoridades educativas tienen el “deber de denunciar” ante situaciones que pudieran constituir delitos y dispone mecanismos para la intervención de la Policía y la Justicia. La medida se aplica en el marco del nuevo régimen que establece la responsabilidad penal desde los 14 años.


Entrevistado en

AM750

, Federico Puy, secretario general adjunto de Ademys, denunció el nuevo protocolo del Gobierno porteño que obliga a las autoridades escolares a denunciar hechos que pudieran constituir delitos e incorpora la intervención policial y judicial en las escuelas. “Es parte de una política de criminalización de las juventudes”, señaló.


La normativa alcanza a las situaciones que ocurran dentro de los establecimientos educativos, pero también contempla hechos que involucren a estudiantes y estén vinculados con la comunidad educativa. Frente a determinadas situaciones, los directivos deberán dar intervención al 911, al SAME y a organismos de protección de derechos. En otros casos, deberán realizar la denuncia ante el Ministerio Público Fiscal. De esta manera, conflictos que hasta ahora podían abordarse mediante herramientas de convivencia escolar quedan bajo la posibilidad de una intervención penal.


“La escuela pasa a ser un lugar donde se denuncia a los pibes”, cuestionó Federico Puy, al referirse al nuevo protocolo. El dirigente docente señaló que la medida debe ser leída en conjunto con el avance del Régimen Penal Juvenil y advirtió sobre el peligro de transformar a las instituciones educativas en espacios atravesados por la lógica policial y judicial.


El protocolo también habilita la presencia policial dentro de las escuelas en determinadas circunstancias. Para los docentes, esto supone un cambio profundo en el funcionamiento de las instituciones: frente a situaciones de conflicto, en lugar de fortalecer los equipos de orientación, trabajadores sociales y herramientas pedagógicas, el Gobierno incorpora como respuesta la denuncia, la Policía y el Ministerio Público Fiscal. author: Elizabeth Weill-Greenberg
title: Activists Are Targeting One of ICE’s Key Staging Grounds — Parking Spots
content:
Protesters say they are “throwing sand in the gears” of the agency’s deportation and abduction machine.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

The Trump administration’s abduction and deportation machine is multifaceted. There are clear-cut components — agents, shackles, and jails — and less obvious, although no less essential, ones — cars and parking spaces.

In an effort to impede the attacks on immigrants, mayors of some of the country’s largest cities, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Chicago Mayor Brandon Johnson, and Boston Mayor Michelle Wu, have issued executive orders banning Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) from using city-owned parking lots and properties.

But even in cities where mayors have banned ICE from using government-owned properties, ICE still has free reign to contract with private companies. After the federal agency posted a notice seeking “Surge Parking” in 14 cities, including Boston, Wu released a public letter to local parking garage and lot owners, warning them that if ICE were “to procure such resources, it would constitute an unprovoked and unwarranted escalation, creating potentially significant risks to public safety and halting economic activity across our entire region.”

“Today, I ask you to join us: Reject any proposition by ICE to facilitate an attack on the people of Boston,” she wrote. “In the face of escalating attacks on cities across the country, we have repeatedly seen that the strongest defense is solidarity.”

In the Boston suburb of Burlington, Massachusetts, Bearing Witness New England has been holding weekly protests outside ICE’s Boston Field Office, where people are held for days in inhumane conditions. Activists say ICE has been keeping its vehicles in a nearby parking lot owned by local developer National Development.

According to a report by NPR affiliate WBUR, the company sent a letter to local activists in February, stating that ICE vehicles were being “improperly parked” in its parking spaces, and that it had “reached an arrangement with ICE that they would no longer park their vehicles on our property.”

However, the company also said that the government agency, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), has rights to use the garage and the company does not have authority over how the FAA parcels out parking spaces to other federal agencies, according to WBUR’s report.

Nathan Phillips, a Boston University professor who organizes with the Burlington-area coalition Building Up Resilience Networks (B.U.R.N.), says ICE has continued to park in sections of lots National Development leases to the FAA that exceed what the lease allows.

Protests that target parking garages are “throwing sand in the gears” of ICE’s deportation and abduction machine, he says.

“So much of their operation depends on logistics of transport and travel … It’s human trafficking, and so if we can go after the trafficking, the means by which they’re doing this, that can have a really effective impact.”

“So much of their operation depends on logistics of transport and travel,” Phillips told Truthout. “It’s human trafficking, and so if we can go after the trafficking, the means by which they’re doing this, that can have a really effective impact.”

Fellow B.U.R.N. activist Josh Model says National Development’s recent actions contradict its public image as a philanthropic company committed to improving communities.

“National Development Corporation, which, as a local developer, likes to promote that they’re cognizant of community needs and give to charity and all these nice things,” but they’re “letting ICE stage kidnappings” from their property, said Model.

While the government spending website, usaspending.gov, only lists 12 active contracts for parking spaces, as of September 28, the true number of parking lots that ICE uses is likely much higher, said Model. It’s difficult to untangle where ICE is parking, in part, because many of the contracts are not with ICE, but through another federal agency, the General Services Administration (GSA), he said. The GSA manages government buildings and real estate, and owns or leases space in more than 8,300 buildings, according to an explainer on the agency published by the Congressional Research Service.

In the case of National Development, ICE is using parking leased by the GSA for the FAA, according to Model.

content:
Με το υπ. αριθμ.

3763/2026 βούλευμα του Συμβουλίου

 Πλημμελειοδικών Αθηνών

απορρίφθηκε ηπροσφυγή

της 46χρονης κατηγορούμενης για την υπόθεση Μarfin

 εναντίον του εντάλματος προσωρινής κράτησης

, που προφυλακίστηκε χωρίς η ανακρίτρια και ο εισαγγελέας που την αποφάσισαν να λάβουν υπ όψη τους το απαλλακτικό δεδικασμένο του 2022, την ομολογημένη από τη ΔΕΕ/ΕΛΑΣ έλλειψη ταυτοποίησης της με το πρόσωπο που εικονίζεται ως ύποπτο και την τεράστια

καταστροφή στη ζωή της ίδιας και της πεντάχρονης κόρης της

 που προξενείται.


Η εισαγγελική πρόταση που είχε προηγηθεί ήταν

απορριπτική για την προσφυγή,

 κάτι που ήταν αναμενόμενο αφού επιλογές ανωτέρων της είναι εκείνες που έχουν αναλάβει την νομική ευθύνη για την ανάσυρση της δικογραφίας και την άσκηση της ποινικής δίωξης. Τα επιχειρήματά της

απαντήθηκαν αναλυτικά με υπόμνημα

 που κατατέθηκε στις 2.9.2026 υπ όψη του Συμβουλίου, αλλά δεν προκύπτει από το περιεχόμενο του βουλεύματος ότι ελήφθη υπ όψη.


Αξιοσημείωτη είναι η καθυστέρηση ανάμεσα στην ημερομηνία διάσκεψης (10.9.2026) και την ημερομηνία έκδοσης του βουλεύματος (25.9.2026). Και ακόμα περισσότερο το ότι με

διαφορετική επιχειρηματολογία και επίκληση νομικών διατάξεων από την εισαγγελέα

το συμβούλιο επιχειρεί να  παρακάμψει την ύπαρξη δεδικασμένου. Η διαφοροποίηση από την εισαγγελική πρόταση επιβεβαιώνει την αβεβαιότητα και τη σύγχυση για τη νομιμότητα της δίωξης και παρά το δυσμενές διατακτικό δικαιώνει και μόνο εξ αυτού τις αντιρρήσεις μας. Σχετικά με την έλλειψη ταυτοποίησης το Συμβούλιο δεν διατυπώνει ιδιαίτερες κρίσεις. Επαφίεται στην εισαγγελική πρόταση και σιωπά στα εναντίον της επιχειρήματα του υπομνήματός μας και της τεχνικής έκθεσης του κ. Καραθανάση, την ύπαρξη των οποίων ούτε καν αναφέρει.


Τελικό συμπέρασμα είναι ότι τα αρμόδια δικαστικά όργανα δεν έχουν ακόμα ξεπεράσει το σοκ από τον πρόσφατο επικοινωνιακό βομβαρδισμό κυβέρνησης και Μ.Μ.Ε. και την περιρρέουσα ατμόσφαιρα, που αργεί ακόμα να διαλυθείπαρά το γεγονός ότι όλον αυτόν τον καιρό

δεν υπήρξε κάποιος

 από την κυβέρνηση η την αστυνομία

για να διαψεύσει

 όσα έχουμε καταγγείλει.


Ετσι η 46χρονη παραμένει θύμα της κατάστασης αυτής,

προφυλακισμένη άδικα, χωρίς στοιχεία εναντίον της, χωρίς ταυτοποίηση και κατά παράβαση δεδικασμένου

και αντιμετωπίζει την

καταστροφή της ζωής της και την αποκοπή της από την πεντάχρονη κόρη της

 μέχρι νεωτέρας. Ενώ η ανάκριση δεν έχει προχωρήσει

ούτε καν στην ανεύρεση του αποστολέα του ανώνυμου μέηλ

 που προκάλεσε τη δίωξη. Μόνο στις προφυλακίσεις !


Είναι αυτονόητο ότι θα εξαντλήσουμε κάθε νόμιμο μέσο μέχρι τη δικαίωση.


Αθήνα,

30.9.2026

author: David Swanson
title: 10 Reasons to Oppose the “Arc de Trump”
content:
Culture of Peace, North America

By Medea Benjamin, September 30, 2026

There was already widespread opposition to Trump’s proposed arch at Memorial Circle in Arlington, Virginia—a 250-foot structure, roughly the height of a 20-story building and 50 percent taller than Paris’s Arc de Triomphe. Now the controversy has intensified: Trump says the arch, which originally included plans for an observation deck, a café, a gift shop and exhibition space, would also function as a military complex, housing drones, snipers and ammunition.

Here are 10 reasons (really 9 plus your own) to oppose the “Arc de Trump.”

1. It would overwhelm one of America’s most important historic landscapes. The giant arch would sit directly on the ceremonial axis connecting Arlington House, Arlington National Cemetery, Memorial Bridge and the Lincoln Memorial, dramatically altering this historic view and dwarfing the surrounding monuments rather than complementing them.

2. It clashes with the very meaning of the site. Arlington Memorial Bridge and the surrounding landscape were conceived as symbols of national reconciliation after the Civil War. And Arlington National Cemetery is a solemn resting place for hundreds of thousands of service members. Inserting a gigantic triumphal arch into this setting would transform a landscape devoted to reconciliation, remembrance and sacrifice into a monument celebrating triumph and power.

3. Congress never authorized it, and veterans are taking Trump to court. Three Vietnam War veterans and an architectural historian have filed a federal lawsuit arguing that Trump cannot unilaterally erect such a monumental structure without congressional authorization and the legally required reviews. A federal judge has already imposed restrictions on work at the site while the legal challenge proceeds. The question is simple: Does a president have the right to build whatever monument he wants on public land without congressional approval?

4. Construction would disrupt commuters and military funerals. Building a 250-foot monument at this location could mean years of construction along a major commuter artery connecting Washington, DC, and Virginia. Excavation, heavy equipment, traffic disruptions, noise and dust would also affect the area immediately outside Arlington National Cemetery, where military funerals and burials take place.

5. Trump now proposes turning the arch into an armed military complex. Trump has said the arch would house large numbers of drones and sniper ammunition, with positions for snipers on the roof and plaza. Why in the world would we want to militarize this historic site when the Pentagon is just two miles away? And what exactly is the purpose of stationing snipers and drones at a ceremonial monument?

6. Drones, snipers and ammunition raise serious safety concerns. The proposed location is only about 3,000 feet from Reagan National Airport and lies near its approach and departure corridors. Adding drone operations, ammunition storage and armed positions to an already heavily traveled location raises obvious aviation and public safety questions. Drone flights in the Washington area are already subject to exceptionally strict restrictions. What additional risks would this new military complex create?

7. The price could be enormous. Estimates for the arch were already running above $100 million before Trump announced his military ambitions for the project. Adding drone facilities, ammunition storage, sniper positions, communications equipment and security infrastructure could drive the cost substantially higher. At a time when Americans are struggling to afford housing, healthcare and other basic necessities, why should taxpayers foot the bill for Trump’s monumental ambitions?

8. National security could become an excuse to circumvent the law. Trump originally promoted the project as a ceremonial triumphal arch. His announcement that it would also serve as a military complex raises a new set of questions about how the administration intends to justify the project. Critics, including Rep. Don Beyer, whose district includes the proposed site, have questioned whether national security is being invoked to overcome legal and preservation obstacles. Will the administration use security claims to evade the normal approval process?

9. It is a monument to Trump’s colossal ego. Trump has repeatedly treated beloved national spaces as extensions of his personal brand—from his $400 million White House …

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Rejects AI Regulation as Tech CEOs Sign Voluntary “Self-Policing” Accord
content:
Critics warn that self-regulation isn’t enough to prevent AI models from making disastrous mistakes in the future.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

On Tuesday, President Donald Trump announced that several tech firm executives had signed an accord agreeing to self-regulate their artificial intelligence (AI) ventures amid growing concerns about the technology’s rapid expansion.

Before the accord was signed, Trump said that “self-regulation is very important” — dismissing calls for formal government regulation, even as industry experts warn that AI’s unfettered expansion could lead to catastrophic outcomes.

In remarks to reporters after the accord was signed, Trump touted the unenforceable measure as a positive move.

“I think I’m seeing tremendous self-policing. And they understand that they have to self-police,” Trump insisted.

But when questioned over a hypothetical scenario about an AI bot going rogue and committing a crime — and who should be held responsible for such an event — Trump ignored the query altogether, instead ranting about how he no longer calls the technology AI but instead “SI,” or “super intelligence.”

“We changed the name officially today to ‘SI.’ You know what that means? Super intelligence. The name has been officially changed,” Trump said.

Q: Who should be held accountable when the AI agents commit a crime?TRUMP: It's not AI. That's the other thing. We changed the name officially today to SI. Like sigh.

Trump signed an order on Tuesday changing the name in all executive branch documents.

The accord was signed by multiple tech barons, including X’s Elon Musk, Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, Anthropic’s Dario Amodei, Google’s Sundar Pichai, and OpenAI’s Greg Brockman. Notably, Palantir’s Alex Karp did not sign the accord.

The document, entitled the “White House Accord on Super Intelligence,” calls on companies to “implement robust internal controls to monitor the capabilities and alignment” of their AI models. It also calls for “an internal team” within the companies “to ensure all of the controls, monitoring, and detection are operating as intended,” and to partner with external auditors to “carry out independent assessments.”

These measures are entirely voluntary, with no requirement for the signatories of the document to abide by them.

The document features Trump’s signature above the tech moguls’, listing him as “President of the Unites States,” misspelling the word “United” in his title.

Interestingly, the document contradicts what Trump has said regarding government-imposed regulation, recognizing that, “Over time, it may make sense to codify these steps into laws.”

Several critics of AI, including former workers at tech firms, have demanded that more be done by the federal government, and internationally, to curtail the expansion of AI.

“We can and should be demanding that our governments protect us from the catastrophe of out-of-control AI. … Today’s AIs appear to occasionally lie or cheat, even when they know better,” Alex Turner, a former research scientist at Google DeepMind, wrote in an op-ed for The Guardian earlier this month.

“AI billionaires have shown us that they’re willing to chase a dollar bill off the side of a cliff if it makes them a dollar richer. But Donald Trump doesn’t give a damn if AI puts us in harm’s way, as long as he can make himself richer in the process,” read a statement from Maurice Mitchell, national director of the Working Families Party. “We cannot trust a multi-billion dollar AI industry to regulate itself.”

author: Mada Masr
title: Parliament approves last-minute delay to Criminal Procedures Code enactment
content:
The Criminal Procedures Code’s enactment was

postponed

 for one year, after Parliament gave their final approval to an amendment during an emergency session on Wednesday morning.


The law, which has been

likened

 to “a second constitution” in terms of its foundational importance to Egypt’s legal system, was due to come into effect less than 24 hours after the session, on October 1.


Parliamentary Affairs Minister Hany Hanna

attended

 the session to argue in favor of the postponement, which he said had been called for by over 60 MPs — the required quorum for a proposal’s presentation to the plenary session.


Hanna, whose comments were relayed in a Cabinet

statement

 on Wednesday evening, expressed the government’s backing for the postponement, adding that it would ensure the law’s provisions can be implemented without obstacles. He specifically highlighted the benefit this extra time would grant in allowing for the completion of the new digital system — to be used for judicial notifications and remote court proceedings — while also ensuring that it can be properly tested.


The government’s request was preceded by calls for the law’s postponement from legal rights advocates who voiced concerns that the new law would do more to threaten defendants’ access to fair terms of investigation, detention and trial than it would to improve the workings of the criminal justice system.


A delay would “allow time to address the contentious issues raised concerning the law, which civil society organizations, legal scholars and United Nations rapporteurs believe significantly undermine procedural guarantees, violate the right to defense and compromise the standards of fair and equitable trials,” the Arab Center for Independence of the Judiciary and the Legal Profession said in a September

statement

.


The law is one of the most important texts determining the function of criminal justice and law enforcement as enacted by security, investigative and judicial authorities. Its provisions govern criminal prosecution, trial and appeals systems; investigation and arrest terms; criminal sentencing; law enforcement and judicial cooperation with other countries.


The law that was amended Wednesday

surfaced

 in bill form in July 2024, when the House Constitutional and Legislative Affairs Committee announced plans to discuss the draft during the House recess that summer.


The step immediately sparked anger among former prisoners, civil society figures and rights advocates who were participating in a parallel, state-led process set up to brainstorm ideas for the criminal justice system’s reform — particularly with regard to the use of remand detention to hold people for extended periods without trial. While the law does reduce the time a defendant can be held in remand, it comes

short

 of addressing the practice of charging defendants with multiple similar charges, which can result in them being held for many consecutive remand periods.


Criticism has also been

levied

 at other elements of the law, such as its establishment of remote hearings as a standard practice, which rights experts believe will weaken defendants’ access to a fair trial as well as  allowing the seizure and monitoring of electronic devices, belongings and online accounts — an inclusion which some believe threatens constitutional privacy protections.


Participants in the National Dialogue forum at the time expressed consternation that a draft law had already been formulated and submitted for parliamentary review without their knowledge. Similar grievances were expressed by the lawyers and

journalists

 syndicates.


The draft nevertheless progressed rapidly through Parliament, with less than a year’s passage all in all between the draft’s submission and its final approval in April, 2025.

The post

Parliament approves last-minute delay to Criminal Procedures Code enactment

 first appeared on

Mada Masr

.

author: Redazione_web
title: Assemblea internazionale FICEDL
content:
Si è svolta a Bologna, lo scorso 11-13 settembre, l’assemblea della Federazione Internazionale dei Centri di Studio e Documentazione Libertari. La precedente assemblea generale si era tenuta esattamente 10 anni or sono ancora a Bologna sempre al Circolo Anarchico C. Berneri.


L’incontro ha registrato una grande partecipazione. Oltre 40 archivi, biblioteche, centri di studio e documentazione erano presenti, altri hanno inviato comunicati e saluti. Di questi, circa la metà erano italiani ed erano presenti compagne e compagni da Francia, Spagna, Svizzera, Austria, Inghilterra, Romania, Brasile e Cile. Le relazioni di presentazione hanno manifestato la diffusione ed il radicamento del movimento anarchico e libertario legato alla conservazione della documentazione delle attività del movimento, ma anche alle attività contemporanee, svolgendo un’importante attività culturale e sociale.


Al sito

https://ficedl2026.bida.im/

 potete trovare maggiori dettagli dell’incontro.


A questo link

https://tubocatodico.bida.im/c/ficedl_2026__berneri/videos

 trovate le registrazioni di tutti gli incontri.


Al sito

https://ficedl.info/

 la storia della Federazione.


L’intervento di Lorenzo Pezzica, svoltosi venerdì nel tardo pomeriggio, ha rimarcato il carattere “non museale” dell’attività dei nostri archivi e delle nostre biblioteche. Se è pur necessario un approccio “tecnico” alla conservazione, catalogazione, diffusione dei materiali, questa attività non deve essere avulsa dalla relazione con i movimenti che si danno nella società contemporanea. Impostazione che è stata ripresa e confermata da moltissimi degli interventi presenti, sia nei workshop del pomeriggio di sabato che nella carrellata di presentazioni della mattina, come già accennato.


Durante i workshop sono emerse diverse esperienze in atto che propongono e già in parte realizzano piattaforme di scambio e federazione degli archivi e del materiale.


La disponibilità per l’organizzazione del prossimo incontro della rete FICEDL (2027) è arrivata dalle compagne e dai compagni di Anarhiva e si dovrebbe tenere a Cluj-Napoca in Romania. In tempi brevi arriverà da parte loro la conferma ufficiale.


Per il 2029 si sono resti disponibili invece le compagne e i compagni della Biblioteca Terra Livre di Sao Paolo e dell’Archivo La Revuelta di Santiago del Cile. Entrambi compiono vent’anni, sarà dunque l’occasione per festeggiare a dovere.


Nello spirito di coinvolgimento di realtà attive e affini alla FICEDL, all’incontro hanno partecipato anche alcuni archivi che non fanno ancora parte della rete. Molti di loro hanno chiesto di aderire.


Si sono poi messi in cantiere una serie di gruppi di lavoro per coadiuvare la gestione del sito ufficiale della Federazione, per la redazione di un “annuario”, per la realizzazione di una cassa di mutuo appoggio (che permetta di coprire i costi organizzativi e di spostamento per i prossimi incontri), per organizzare una lista di traduttrici/tori in simultanea o in consecutiva che agevolino i prossimi incontri.


Infine l’assemblea ha approvato una mozione di solidarietà ad Autistici/Inventati e di denuncia dei provvedimenti sempre più autoritari contro i movimenti. Qui il testo della mozione

https://ficedl2026.bida.im/mozione/

.


Non sono mancati i momenti conviviali come in ogni convegno di compagne e compagni. Cena, pranzo e cena al Berneri con concerto di Mars on Pluto il venerdì sera e la cantata con il Coro delle Mondine di Bentivoglio il sabato sera e il partecipatissimo pranzo della domenica al VAG, in via Paolo Fabbri, dove si era svolta l’assemblea della Federazione nella mattinata. Qui si svolgeva un’iniziativa di solidarietà con grande pranzo popolare per sostenere le spese legali della famiglia di Abderrahim Fakir, cittadino bolognese ucciso dalla polizia nel luglio scorso in città.

author: David Swanson
title: Trump’s Offer to Sell Weapons to China Is Wonderful
content:
Asia, Demilitarization, North America, Stop Arms Trade, World

By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, September 30, 2026

Wednesday morning I was speaking by Zoom to a college class about war and peace, and one of the students asked about the risk of the U.S. demilitarizing and other nations not. I gave a standard answer about how a reverse arms race could be done in stages. The U.S. could commit to not spending more than three times any other nation on its military and proceed downward from there. Of the couple of dozen nations that spend much of anything on their militaries, all but three are U.S. allies and weapons customers being hammered hard by the U.S. government (and NATO) to spend more. The only country spending more than a tiny fraction of the U.S. — in fact, spending close to a third of U.S. military spending as it’s usually reported or a sixth of what it really is — is China. If the U.S. were to keep its nukes out of South Korea and Japan, and its troops out of South Korea, and finally end the war and turn South Korea’s military over to South Korea, and start joining treaties and courts and beginning a general disarmament, North Korea would almost certainly join in serious negotiations about getting rid of its nukes, while China would — I guaranteed to this college class — not keep increasing its own military spending.

Within a minute of saying goodbye on Zoom, I saw that Trump had offered to sell weapons to China. This is terrific news. I have no idea whether Trump knows that a lot of people still want to hear some excuse for dumping virtually all of our money into the biggest war machine ever — much less for handing the decisions about the wars over to the actual weapons. I have no idea whether he’s noticed that every conversation in Congress and corporate media quickly becomes a competition about competing with China. I do know that he wants decisions to be simply about the Will of Donald Trump. So, he may not care about China as the big excuse for military spending, but I certainly care about the wonderful news that he’s taken that excuse away.

Surely we do not need trillions more dumped into the Pentagon because of China while Trump is trying to sell China weapons. Surely the rest of the world’s governments that Trump is badgering to spend more on weapons do not need to do so because of China while Trump is trying to sell China weapons. Surely Australia, for example, does not need to be filled up with U.S. troops because of China while Trump is pitching China on his favorite weapons.

So, phone the neighbors, wake the kids, and pinch the lazy new panda bears because a peace dividend is surely on the way if enough people find out that Trump has tried to sell China weapons and think about it for a few seconds and do something about it for a few days. That last bit is the sticking point I know. But let’s try!

author: Andrés
title: Tandil moviliza contra la corrupción del negocio inmobiliario
content:
La Asamblea por la Preservación de las Sierras de Tandil se manifestará este viernes 2 de octubre a las 18 horas en la Plaza Independencia, frente al Palacio Municipal de la ciudad. Denuncia a funcionarios políticos por el crecimiento indiscriminado de las construcciones en las sierras y expone su desidia ante los intereses inmobiliarios.

Por Nicolás Scipione (ANRed).


La ciudad de Tandil es epicentro de un corredor serrano de unos 250 millones de años de vida que, en las últimas décadas, está siendo cada vez más afectado por el corrimiento de la frontera agropecuaria, como otras tantas ciudades y zonas del país que no son históricamente productoras de soja. Por un lado, las plantaciones de soja han modificado el ambiente porque han reducido los humedales y, por ende, modificado la flora y la fauna de la zona pero, además, han provocado un nivel de migración en la ciudad y desigualdades económicas que cada vez es más difícil de ocultar. La proliferación del mercado inmobiliario tiene consecuencias cada vez más indisimulables: no se puede tapar el sol con las manos ni tampoco las sierras con construcciones.


En 2005 el Municipio promulgó un Plan de Ordenamiento Territorial (PDT) que pone restricciones, regula situaciones y promete proteger el ecosistema serrano. Sin embargo, los vecinos y vecinas, desde 2010 dicen que se empezaron a comprar pequeños terrenos para hacer cabañas y que, en los últimos años, hay intereses económicos más grandes que no están en la ciudad y quieren convencer a porteños para que no compren propiedades en el conurbano de Buenos Aires y vengan a Tandil. Lo hacen con un discurso publicitario que enaltece las condiciones de una ciudad más segura y más cercana al aire libre de polución que AMBA. Además, este PDT se combinó con un plan de fomento del turismo que alienta visitas de mayor poder adquisitivo al que los funcionarios siempre aparecen dispuestos a favorecer.


La Asamblea


En 1999 se conformó una multisectorial por la preservación de las sierras para articular la defensa del territorio. El problema fundamental que tenía la ciudad en ese tiempo eran las explosiones de dinamita controlada que las empresas hacían en las canteras de piedra y afectaban no solo el ecosistema sino también a las personas que viven cerca de las canteras. Para 2007, con el impacto de las luchas en las calles contra las pasteras en Gualeguaychú, esa multisectorial fue mutando a lo que es hoy: la

Asamblea por la Preservación de las Sierras de Tandi

l

 una organización social que centra actividad en las denuncias por la desidia del Estado Municipal.


Esta asamblea toma el de muchas otras del país que surgen alrededor de problemáticas ambientales,

sus reclamos se sostienen en el artículo 28 de la Constitución de la Provincia Buenos Aires

, que promueve que

“los habitantes de la Provincia tienen el derecho a gozar de un ambiente sano y el deber de conservarlo y protegerlo en su provecho y en el de las generaciones futuras. (…) Toda persona física o jurídica cuya acción u omisión pueda degradar el ambiente está obligada a tomar todas las precauciones para evitarlo”

.

 Y, además, en el artículo 41 de la Constitución Nacional

 que impone que “

Las autoridades proveerán a la protección de este derecho, a la utilización racional de los recursos naturales, a la preservación del patrimonio natural y cultural y de la diversidad biológica, y a la información y educación ambientales.”


La Asamblea se define como un espacio que discute hasta llegar al consenso. Más allá de las pertenencias partidarias que puedan tener sus miembros, evita la relación directa con los partidos políticos. Sobre todo, porque

“

los políticos nunca mostraron reales intereses por nuestras denuncias y nuestras peleas”

.

 Participantes de la Asamblea, la definen como un espacio

“político pero no partidario”

. Consideran que así garantizan la perdurabilidad del espacio independientemente de las personas que participen en él, y además habilita más ampliamente la colaboración de vecinos y vecinas, de distinta forma. Incluso mucha de la información recabada y las imágenes de 27 casos de construcciones clandestinas o ilegales que tiene el informe que presentaron públicamente hace algunas semanas, fueron acercadas por personas que no participan cotidianamente de las reuniones y que, sin embargo, son documentos que solventan sus denuncias.

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Administration Plans to Add 5,000 New ICE Employees by End of Year
content:
Recent recruitment strategies have included using neo-Nazi memes to appeal to potential hires.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

A new report suggests that the Trump administration is planning to drastically ramp up recruitment efforts at Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), expanding the federal agency that has been widely criticized for its violent tactics in carrying out President Donald Trump’s mass deportation campaign.

According to The New York Times, which cited four sources with knowledge of the administration’s plans, ICE is seeking to grow its workforce by 5,000 new employees, hoping to reach that number by the end of the year. Most of the new hires are expected to be “deportation officers” whose tasks will include participating in detaining people, those sources indicated.

The 5,000 new employees would be part of a series of increases to the agency during Trump’s second term. ICE has grown by 8,000 employees since the start of 2025, reaching 29,000 employees as of July. The new recruitment number being discussed would amount to a 17 percent increase over that latter figure.

ICE has ramped up its efforts during the Trump administration, using violent — and in some cases, deadly — methods and violating the due process rights of those they detain. Recruitment efforts last year included finding agents and placing them in the field with limited to no vetting and significantly reduced training.

The sources speaking to the Times indicated that the agency plans to rectify those issues by implementing higher standards for recruits, but it’s unclear if that’s possible, given the high number of agents the agency is seeking over the next few months.

“Adequately vetting people takes time,” said Deborah Fleischaker, a former chief of staff at ICE who worked during the Biden administration.

Indeed, recent recruitment strategies have included the use of neo-Nazi memes to appeal to potential hires, and seeking out extremists at events like gun shows, Ultimate Fight Club venues, and other places where far right individuals are typically present.

The planned recruitment comes as the movement to abolish ICE is gaining momentum across the country. Polling indicates that support for terminating the agency is supported by a majority of Americans.

According to an Economist/YouGov survey published in March, 56 percent of respondents said they had “only a little” or no confidence at all in the agency, while only 39 percent said they had a “great deal” or “some” confidence. Asked whether they backed abolishing ICE, 50 percent said they supported that idea, while only 39 percent said they opposed doing so.

author: Jake Johnson
title: Fetterman Joins GOP to Block Effort to Expose Israeli Abuses in West Bank
content:
The measure would’ve required the State Department to issue a report on Israeli human rights practices in the West Bank.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Democratic US Sen. John Fetterman joined nearly every Republican senator on Tuesday in voting against a resolution that would have required the Trump administration to produce an unclassified report on Israeli abuses in the illegally occupied West Bank, including the imprisonment and killing of Palestinian Americans.

The resolution, led by Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), narrowly failed 47-51, with Sen. Rand Paul (R-Ky.) joining every Democrat except Fetterman in supporting the measure. Van Hollen and other supporters of the resolution lamented the failed vote but celebrated the historic support it received as public opposition to Israeli atrocities — and US funding of Israel’s military — continues to grow.

“Tonight, 47 senators supported my resolution to get accountability for the nine Americans killed on the West Bank and for Palestinians who face injustices daily,” Van Hollen wrote in a social media post. “That’s more support than we’ve ever had in this fight. Republicans blocked us, but we won’t stop until we get justice.”

In 2024, just 11 senators — all members of the Democratic caucus except Paul — backed a similar resolution led by Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.).

“Listen to the American people: NO MORE MILITARY AID TO ISRAEL,” Sanders wrote in response to Tuesday’s vote.

If passed, Van Hollen’s resolution would have required the US State Department to issue a report within 30 days on Israeli human rights practices in the West Bank, where Palestinians have faced a historic level of violence by Israeli settlers and soldiers this year.

The resolution, which invoked Section 502B(c) of the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961, specifically called on the Trump administration to provide “all credible information of which the Department of State is aware concerning the alleged killing of United States citizens by the Israel Defense Forces, other Israeli security forces, or Israeli settlers since January 1, 2022,” as well as “an assessment on any United States citizens currently held in Israeli prisons.”

Under the Foreign Assistance Act, a failure to produce the required report would have resulted in a freeze on some US military assistance to Israel.

Josh Ruebner, policy director at the IMEU Policy Project, said that while the resolution “narrowly failed” due to near-unanimous Republican opposition, “make no mistake: this is historic.”

The resolution’s text highlights the case of Sama Safi, a 20-year-old Palestinian American student with a chronic health condition who was abducted by Israeli forces during a West Bank raid in June and has reportedly been detained without charge for months.

On Tuesday morning, Zeteo highlighted the case of Abdalkareem Issa Ahmed Safi, “an American teenager with Texas roots” whom Israeli forces snatched “from his family’s West Bank home in the middle of the night” in late June. Zeteo noted that he is the third young American known to be “languishing in Israeli prison.”

“Only one Republican voted to even somewhat hold Israel accountable for acts like this,” Zeteo’s Prem Thakker wrote late Tuesday.

author: CMI Argentina
title: “La Corte Suprema puso a la Argentina en venta”: revocó un fallo y habilitó la venta sin límites de tierras a extranjeros
content:
La Corte Suprema de Justicia de la Nación revocó este martes 29 de septiembre el fallo de la Cámara Federal de La Plata que había declarado inconstitucional el artículo 154 del DNU 70/2023 del gobierno de Javier Milei, que derogaba la Ley 26.737 de Tierras Rurales, y eliminó los límites para la adquisición de campos argentinos por parte de extranjeros. Lo hizo al rechazar la demanda presentada por el Centro de Ex Combatientes Islas Malvinas (CECIM) La Plata, argumentando que la organización no tiene legitimación para promoverla. “Para esta Corte, podemos morir en defensa de la soberanía, pero no acudir a un Tribunal”, respondió el CECIM La Plata. Y agregó: “la Corte resolvió el problema político de Milei. Decretó que la soberanía no es un bien jurídico y puso a la Argentina en venta”. Así, la decisión de tres integrantes de una Corte que nadie eligió democráticamente vuelve a dejar vigente la derogación de la norma que establecía un límite del 15% para la titularidad extranjera de tierras rurales y restricciones adicionales para un mismo titular extranjero, después de que una masiva movilización popular obligara al Gobierno a retirar del Congreso su intento de flexibilizar todavía más la normativa.


Carlos Rosenkrantz, Horacio Rosatti y Ricardo Lorenzetti


Dos meses después de que el gobierno de Javier Milei retirara del proyecto de Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada el capítulo que modificaba el régimen de tierras rurales extranjeras, ante la falta de votos para aprobarlo en el Senado, y tras el masivo rechazo popular en las calles, la Corte Suprema de Justicia de la Nación revocó este martes 29 de septiembre el fallo de la Cámara Federal de La Plata que había declarado inconstitucional el artículo 154 del DNU 70/2023, mediante el cual el gobierno nacional derogó la Ley 26.737, conocida como Ley de Tierras Rurales, al rechazar la demanda presentada por el Centro de Ex Combatientes Islas Malvinas La Plata (CECIM), al considerar que la organización no estaba legitimada para promover la acción colectiva y que no existía un “caso o controversia” en los términos constitucionales.


El fallo no declaró constitucional al artículo 154 ni analizó el fondo de la derogación y la propia Corte señaló que su decisión “se limita al rechazo de la demanda con fundamento en la falta de legitimación de la actora y la ausencia del requisito constitucional de caso o controversia”. Sin embargo, al revocar la sentencia de la Cámara Federal platense que había frenado el DNU, volvió a quedar vigente la derogación de la Ley de Tierras.


Imagen: La Política Ambiental.


La Ley 26.737 establecía un tope general del 15% para la titularidad extranjera de tierras rurales sobre el territorio nacional, provincial y departamental, además de establecer que las personas de una misma nacionalidad no podían superar el 30% de ese porcentaje y que un mismo titular extranjero no podía superar las 1.000 hectáreas en la zona núcleo, o la superficie equivalente según la región. También incluía restricciones para determinados inmuebles vinculados con cuerpos de agua y zonas de frontera.


En enero de 2024, un juzgado federal de La Plata había suspendido cautelarmente el artículo 154 del DNU 70/2023 a partir de la presentación del CECIM La Plata. Luego, la Cámara Federal de La Plata declaró su inconstitucionalidad. El Estado nacional apeló y el expediente llegó finalmente a la Corte Suprema, que falló en contra del amparo.


En este marco, el CECIM La Plata repudió el fallo: “en un fallo escueto, la Corte Suprema de Justicia de la Nación acaba de resolver el problema político en que el gobierno de Milei se había metido. Mientras el pueblo gritó con fuerza que ‘La patria no se vende’, la Corte entendió que no existe algo así como un bien jurídico soberanía, y rechazó nuestra demanda para evitar la derogación de la Ley de Tierras, que el presidente intentó a poco de asumir, mediante el Decreto 70/23. Lo hizo pateando la pelota afuera. No exploró el planteo jurídico. Dijo que el Centro de Ex Combatientes Islas Malvinas La Plata (CECIM) no estaba legitimada. Dijo, con claridad, que este grupo de ex soldados conscriptos, combatientes de Malvinas, no podemos acudir a la Justicia en defensa de la soberanía. Extraño razonamiento, si atendemos a que esta Corte conforma el Estado argentino, en su esquema de tripartición de poderes. Un Estado argentino que, en 1982, nos mandó a batallar bajo el argumento de la ‘defensa de la soberanía nacional’. Rara …

Stoprep lycées


https://www.infolibertaire.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/mouvement-lyceen-dans-le-93-stop-a-la-repression-09-26-2026.jpg


Cette semaine a été marquée par une mobilisation lycéenne dans tout le 93, comme à Saint-Denis, Stains, Le Bourget, Aubervilliers, Épinay-sur-Seine, Saint-Ouen, etc.


Les élèves ont exprimé leur colère face à leurs conditions d'études, en évoquant des revendications nombreuses : des dysfonctionnements forts dans les emplois du temps amenant à faire 8h – 18h ou même 19h, des bâtis dégradés qui ne permettent pas d'aller aux toilettes ou exposent aux nuisibles, des violences discriminatoires commises par des membres du personnel, la sélection sur Parcoursup, la pression sur leurs tenues vestimentaires…


Nous soutenons leurs revendications, elles sont légitimes et sont aussi celles que nous défendons, à travers le Plan d'urgence 93, notre opposition toujours pleine et entière à la réforme du lycée et au tri social opéré par Parcousup dans l'accès aux études supérieures.


Pourtant, la seule réponse des institutions a été l'ignorance ou la violence : certains établissements ont voulu maintenir les cours à toute force, sans laisser la possibilité aux élèves de s'exprimer et de s'organiser autour de leurs revendications. Les consignes contradictoires des directions ont mis en danger les élèves en refusant de les laisser partir, alors même que des départs de feu ou des mouvements de foule avaient lieu à proximité des établissements. Des élèves ont été menacé⋅es de passer en conseil de discipline. Les interventions policières ont été nombreuses et violentes, aboutissant à plusieurs arrestations de lycéen⋅nes dans le département.


Nous dénonçons fermement ces violences. Les lycéen⋅nes ont le droit de se mobiliser et doivent être entendu⋅es. Nous exigeons la libération de tou⋅tes les lycéen⋅nes arrêté⋅es, sans suite judiciaire. Dans nos établissements, nous nous opposerons à toutes les formes de répression de la mobilisation : absences injustifiées, punitions, sanctions et conseils de discipline.


SUD

 éducation 93 appelle les personnels des établissements concernés à soutenir les élèves dans leurs revendications et à s'opposer à la répression. Des préavis de grèves quotidiens sont déposés, permettant de débrayer.


La jeunesse du 93 est la première à payer le prix de réformes iniques et de la montée de l'extrême-droite : elle a le droit de se mobiliser et d'être écouté⋅e

 

!

Toute l'année nous travaillons dans de mauvaises conditions, vous nous forcez à nous lever tôt pour au final avoir un manque de personnel. Aujourd'hui nous nous révoltons pour les bonnes causes :

et lorsque nous nous plaignons on nous dit je cite «

author: Redazione_web
title: Abitare la speculazione. Carrara – l’affare Politeama
content:
L’ultima edizione del Festival Con.vivere (festival che si svolge ogni anno a Carrara con tematiche differenti) svoltosi all’inizio di settembre ha avuto come tema l’abitare e non sono mancati gli interventi di illustri relatori che hanno sviscerato l’argomento in maniera trasversale.


Il gruppo Germinal durante lo svolgimento di questo evento ha colto l’occasione per ricordare alla città una storia in cui il fil rouge è ancora una volta il denaro.


Abbiamo organizzato nell’odierna sede provvisoria di Piazza Duomo una mostra espositiva e informativa con foto, scritti di denuncia e manifesti con slogan di protesta contro la speculazione edilizia perpetrata ai danni del palazzo Politeama, all’interno del quale il gruppo Germinal aveva la propria sede.


Nella storia del Politeama il denaro è stato il vero protagonista fin dalla sua costruzione, e, come nel più classico dei copioni, se poi a guadagnare sono pochi e a pagare sono i cittadini, allora si possono annullare accordi ufficiali, spiegare ali laterali abusive non previste e sovraccaricare la struttura di un edificio di duemilasettecento metri quadrati destinato al pubblico spettacolo per realizzare abitazioni private. Dal 1989 si susseguiranno con effetto domino una serie di cedimenti, di interventi parziali e infelici, di periodi d’ incuria, per arrivare al 2008, data della chiusura definitiva dell’intero edificio.


Crolli, paura, processi, rinvii e lunghi silenzi. Cosa manca alla fine della storia e cosa resta? Manca uno spazio sociale che i cittadini possano abitare, manca dignità alla città che si ritrova con un mausoleo marcescente nella piazza d’ingresso, manca la sede storica che il C.N.L. assegnò agli anarchici a riconoscimento della loro partecipazione attiva e fondamentale alla lotta di Liberazione, manca un luogo adeguato al prezioso Archivio. Del resto, si sa, le nostre attività non sono a scopo di lucro, quindi di nessuno interesse. Rispetto a tutto ciò che manca, che cosa resta? Il “Caprice” (ditta che ha commesso l’abuso edilizio) di pochi costato carissimo a tutti.


In una città sempre più distretto minerario, la questione abitativa non è un emergenza episodica, né una sfortunata anomalia di mercato, ma uno dei pilastri su cui si regge la diseguaglianza.


Come anarchici, anche noi colpiti da queste speculazioni, continuiamo a denunciare la schifezza avvenuta attorno al Politeama, rimarcando, nella piccola sede di piazza Duomo, l’importanza e la volontà di vivere la città. Non quartieri dormitorio, non piazze e strade abbandonate, ma un rifugio che abbraccia e si apre alla gente promuovendo relazioni sociali e pratiche di resistenza.


Gruppo Germinal FAI Carrara

ᑭᓕᒃᕙᒃ ᑲᑉᓘᓇ ᐃᓚᐅᓂᐊᓯᔪᖅ ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᓂ ᐋᖅᑭᒋᐊᒃᑲᓐᓂᕐᓂᕐᒧᑦ


“ᐱᒃᑯᓇᑦᑎᐊᕐᑐᖅ,” ᑲᑉᓘᓇ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᓯᑎᐱᕆ 17-ᒥ ᐊᐱᕐᓱᖅᑕᐅᑎᓪᓗᒍ.


ᓯᕗᓂᐊᓂ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᓚᐅᖅᑎᓐᓇᒍ ᓄᓇᕗᑦ ᑐᙵᕕᒃᑯᓐᓂ, ᓄᓇᕗᒥᑦ ᒐᕙᒪᒃᑯᓐᓄ ᐃᓚᒋᔭᐅᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᒥᓂᔅᑕᓄ ᑐᒡᓕᕆᔭᐅᔪᓄᑦ, ᑲᒪᒋᔭᖃᖅᖢᓂ ᐃᓅᓯᖃᑦᑎᐊᕐᓂᕐᒥᓐ, ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᔪᖅ ᓄᓇᕗᒥᑦ ᐃᒻᒥᓃᖃᑦᑕᕐᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᓂ.


ᑕᐃᑲᓂᓕ ᐃᑲᔪᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᒃᓴᖅᑖᕋᓱᖕᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᐅᑯᓄᖓ ᐊᖅᑯᓴᕆᐊᖅ ᒪᒥᓴᕐᕕᒃᒧᑦ ᐃᖃᓗᖕᓂᑦ, ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ, ᐱᓕᕆᐊᒃᓴᖅ ᒪᓕᒃᓯᒪᔪᖅ ᐃᓚᒋᔭᐅᔪᓂᒃ ᓱᓕᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐋᖅᑭᒋᐊᕐᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᑲᒥᓴᓐᑯ ᐊᑐᖁᓯᒪᔭᖏᓐᓂᒃ ᐱᐅᓯᕚᓪᓕᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒥ ᓄᓇᖃᖅᑳᖅᑐᑦ ᒪᒥᓴᖅᐸᓪᓕᐅᔾᔪᑎᒃᓴᖏᓐᓂ.


“ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔮᖃᕐᓂᓐᓂ ᑕᑯᓯᒪᕗᖓ ᐱᕙᓪᓕᐊᔪᓐᓇᕐᓂᕐᒥ ᖃᓄᐃᙱᓐᓂᕐᓴᐅᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᐃᓅᖃᑎᒌᑦᑎᐊᕐᓂᕐᒥ ᒪᐅᓇ ᐊᑐᓕᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᒃᑯ  ᐅᓂᒃᑳᓕᐊᕆᔭᐅᓯᒪᔪᓂ,” ᑲᑉᓘᓇ ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ.


ᐋᓐᓂᐊᖃᖅᑕᐃᓕᓂᕐᒥ ᑲᒪᒋᔭᖃᕐᓂᖅ ᓄᓇᕗᒥᑦ ᐱᐅᓯᕚᓪᓕᒃᑲᓐᓂᕆᐊᖃᕐᒪᓐ, ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ. ᐅᓄᕐᓂᕐᓴᐃᑦ ᐃᓄᐃᑦ ᑖᒃᑯᓇᓂ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖃᕐᓂᕐᓴᐅᔭᕆᐊᖃᕐᒪᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐊᔪᕈᓐᓃᖅᓴᕐᕕᒃᓴᓂ ᐊᑐᐃᓐᓇᖃᕐᓗᓂ, ᑖᓐᓇᑦᑕᐅᖅ ᓇᓗᓇᐃᖅᑕᐅᓯᒪᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕈᑎᐅᔭᕆᐊᖃᕐᓂᖓᓂ, ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ.


“ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕈᑎᒃᓴᑦ ᐊᑐᖅᑕᐅᑲᐅᑎᒋᔪᓐᓇᔾᔮᙱᑦᑐᑦ, ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᓂᒃᑰᖓᓂᖓᓄᑦ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐱᒻᒪᕆᐅᓪᓗᓂ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖃᐃᓐᓇᕐᓂᕐᒥ ᐋᖅᑭᒋᐊᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᓂᕐᒥᒃ, ᐅᓇ ᐅᖃᐅᓯᒃᓴᑐᐃᓐᓇᐅᙱᑦᑐᖅ,” ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ.


ᔫᓴᕝ ᒨᑖᒃ-ᕙᓚᐅᕙᔅ, ᐃᓚᐅᓕᕐᓂ ᐱᒋᐊᓕᖅᑎᓪᓗᒋᑦ ᑲᑎᒪᔩᑦ ᒫᔅᓯ 2025-ᒥ, ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ ᑲᑉᓘᓇᒎ ᐃᓱᒪᒋᑦᑎᐊᕐᓇᕐᒪᓐ ᑖᓐᓇᓗ ᐃᖅᑲᓇᐃᔭᕐᓂᑰᓪᓗᓂ ᐅᖃᐅᔾᔪᐃᔨᐅᓂᕐᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᓕᒪᓂᕐᓴᒃᑯᑦ ᐃᒻᒥᓃᖅᑎᑦᑎᑦᑕᐃᓕᓂᕐᒥᒃ.


“ᐱᓇᓱᑦᑎᐊᒻᒪᕆᖕᒪᓐ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐱᓇᓱᐊᑦᑎᐊᖅᖢᓂ ᐱᓕᕆᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᐊᑐᖅᑕᐅᔭᕆᐊᓕᖕᓂ ᐋᖅᑭᒋᐊᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᓂᕐᒧᑦ. ᐊᒃᑐᐃᓯᒪᓂᖃᕐᒪᓐ ᓄᓇᓕᖕᓂ ᓄᓇᖃᖅᑎᑕᐅᕙᓪᓕᐊᓂᑯᓂ ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐋᖅᑭᒋᐊᒃᑲᓐᓂᕐᓂᕐᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖃᕆᐊᖃᕐᓂᕐᒥ ᑕᒪᑐᒧᖓ,” ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ ᒨᑖᒃ-ᕙᓚᐅᕙᔅ.


ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᑲᑎᒪᔩᑦ ᐱᑕᖃᖅᑎᑕᐅᔪᑦ ᑲᓇᑕ ᒪᓕᒃᑲᓗᐊᕐᒪᖔᑦ 94-ᓂ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᖁᔭᐅᔪᓂ ᐅᓂᒃᑳᓕᐊᑎᒍᑦ ᐅᑯᓇᙵᑦ ᓱᓕᓂᕐᒧᓐ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐋᖅᑭᒋᐊᕐᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᑲᒥᓴᓐᑯᓐᓂ, ᑖᒃᑯᐊᓗ 2015-ᒥ ᑎᑎᕋᐅᓯᖃᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᕈᑎᕕᓂᕐᓂ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐊᒃᑐᐃᓯᒪᔾᔪᑎᖏᓐᓂᒃ ᐃᓕᓐᓂᐊᕆᐊᕕᐅᖃᑦᑕᕐᓂᑯᓄᑦ.


ᐃᒻᒥᒃᑰᖓᓪᓗᑎᒃ ᐊᒻᒪ ᓄᓇᖃᖅᑳᖅᑐᓄᑦ ᐊᐅᓚᑕᐅᓪᓗᓂ ᑲᒪᒋᔭᖃᖅᑐᑦ ᐅᓂᒃᑳᓕᐅᖃᑦᑕᕆᐊᖃᕐᓂᕐᒥᒃ ᑲᓇᑕᐅᑉ ᖃᓄᐃᓕᐅᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᓂᖓᓂ ᐊᕐᕌᒍᙳᕌᖓᑦ. ᐋᖅᑭᒃᑕᐅᓚᐅᕐᓯᒪᔪᑦ 2025-ᒥ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐅᓂᒃᑳᓕᐊᖏᓐᓂ ᐊᐅᔭᖅ ᑐᓂᓯᑕᐃᓐᓇᖅᖢᑎᒃ.


ᑕᕝᕙᓂᓕ ᐅᓂᒃᑳᓂ ᐅᖃᕐᓯᒪᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᑲᓇᑕ ᑕᒪᑐᒥᖓ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖃᖅᐸᓪᓕᐊᓂᖓᓂᒃ ᐊᑐᖁᔭᐅᓯᒪᔪᓂᒃ ᒪᐅᓇ ᓴᖅᑭᑎᑦᑎᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᐱᔪᓐᓇᐅᑎᒃᑰᖓᔪᓂ ᒪᓕᒐᓕᐅᕐᓂᕐᒥ, ᓱᕈᓯᕐᓄᑦ ᐱᑦᑎᐊᖅᑕᐅᙱᔾᔪᑎᕕᓂᕐᓄᑦ ᐋᖅᑭᒋᐊᖅᓯᓂᒃᑯᑦ, ᐃᑲᔫᑎᖃᒃᑲᓐᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᐊᖏᒡᓕᕚᓪᓕᖅᑎᑦᑎᓂᕐᒥ ᐱᓕᕆᖃᑎᒌᖃᑎᖃᕐᓂᕐᒥᒃ.


ᑭᓯᐊᓂᓕ, ᓇᓕᒧᒌᒃᑎᑦᑎᓂᖃᙱᓐᓂᖅ ᓱᕈᓯᓕᕆᓂᒃᑯᑦ, ᐃᓕᓐᓂᐊᖅᑐᓕᕆᓂᒃᑯᑦ, ᑮᓇᐅᔭᓕᐅᕈᑎᑎᒍᑦ, ᐋᓐᓂᐊᖃᖅᑕᐃᓕᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᐊᒻᒪ ᒪᓕᒐᓕᕆᓂᒃᑯᑦ ᓱᓕ ᐱᑕᖃᕐᒪᑕ, ᐅᖃᕐᓯᒪᖕᒥᔪᖅ ᐅᓂᒃᑳᑦ.


ᒨᑖᒃ-ᕙᓚᐅᕙᔅ ᐅᖃᓚᐅᕐᑐᖅ ᐅᓄᕐᑐᐃᑦ ᐊᓯᔾᔨᖅᑕᐅᔭᕆᐊᓖᑦ ᓱᓕ ᑲᒪᒋᔭᐅᔭᕆᐊᖃᕐᒪᑕ. ᐅᖃᖅᖢᓂ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖃᐃᓐᓇᖅᑐᖃᙱᓗᐊᕐᓂᖓᓂᒃ, ᐊᑯᓂᒍᓗᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᒧᑦ ᐃᑲᔫᑎᒃᓴᖃᙱᓐᓂ ᒐᕙᒪᒃᑯᓐᓂ ᐃᓚᒋᔭᐅᓪᓗᓂ.


“ᖃᐅᔨᒪᖕᒥᔪᒍᑦ ᑕᐃᒪᐃᙱᓐᓂᕋᐃᕙᓪᓕᐊᓂᖏᓐᓂᒃ ᑲᓇᑕᒥ,” ᐅᖃᕐᒥᔪᖅ.


ᑲᑉᓘᓇ ᐃᓚᒋᔭᐅᔪᖅ ᐱᖓᓱᓂ ᓄᑖᓂ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᐅᓂᐊᓕᖅᑐᓂ ᑖᒃᑯᓇᓂ, ᑖᒃᑯᐊᓗ ᐱᑕᖃᐃᓐᓇᕐᓂᐊᓕᖅᖢᑎᒃ, ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ ᐃᒃᓯᕙᐅᑕᕆᔭᐅᔪᖅ ᔫᓕ ᐋᓐ ᐅᕆᔅᑕ ᑐᓴᒐᒃᓴᓕᐊᑎᒍᑦ.


“ᐋᖅᑭᒃᓱᐃᓂᖅ ᓯᕗᓪᓕᖅᐹᒥ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᓂ ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᑲᑎᒪᔨᓂ ᐋᖅᑭᒃᓱᐃᕙᓪᓕᐊᓂᕐᒧᑦ ᐱᒋᐊᕈᑎᒻᒪᕆᐅᔪᖅ. ᑐᙵᓱᒃᑎᑉᐸᕗᑦ ᐱᓕᕆᐊᖑᔪᖅ ᐊᒻᒪ ᑲᒪᒋᑦᑎᐊᕆᐊᖃᕐᓂᐊᖅᖢᑎᒍᑦ,” ᐅᕆᔅᑕᓐ ᐅᖃᕐᑐᖅ.


ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐃᓚᐅᖃᑕᐅᓕᕐᒥᔪᖅ ᐅᓇ ᐹᐳᕋ ᕕᓕᐊᓐ, ᐃᓚᒋᔭᐅᔪᖅ ᐃᓄ ᓄᓇᖏᓐᓂ ᒪᔅᑎᐅᐊᔅ ᐅᕙᓂ ᓵᒐᓂ-ᓛᒃ-ᓴᐃᓐ-ᔮᓐ (Innu Nation of Mashteuiatsh in Saguenay–Lac-Saint-Jean) ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᐃᓚᒋᔭᐅᓪᓗᓂ ᑲᓇᑕᒥ ᑲᒥᓴᓐᑯᓐᓂ ᐅᑯᓄᖓ UNESCO, ᐊᒻᒪᓗ ᑯᓗᐊᓐ ᐋᑕᒥᒃ-ᐋᓐᔨᑯᓐᓂ (Kluane Adamek–Aagé), ᑲᑎᒪᔨᐅᓂᑯᑦ ᓄᓇᖃᖅᑳᖅᑐᓄᑦ ᐊᓪᓚᓄᑦ ᔫᑲᓐᒥ ᐊᖓᔪᖅᑳᖅ ᐅᕙᙵᑦ ᑯᓗᐊᓐ ᓄᓇᖃᖅᑳᖅᑐᓂ ᐊᓪᓚᓂ.

author: Soraya Kishtwari
title: UK Universities Set to Strike in ‘Last-Ditch Fight Over Existential Cuts’
content:
University lecturers are set to walk out over “existential” cuts and course closures, as thousands of students face major disruptions as the new academic year begins.


At least eight universities have announced industrial action for the coming year, including three Russell Group institutions.


At Edinburgh, staff are striking for five weeks to protest £140m of cuts, 1,800 potential job losses and management’s refusal to rule out compulsory redundancies.


The university has also announced that 90 degree programmes will be scrapped from 2027.


The kind of cuts many universities are proposing “will fundamentally reshape higher education in the UK”, Emile Chabal professor of contemporary history at Edinburgh University, told Novara Media. He added there was a risk of university contraction leading to a

“second deindustrialisation”, given the outsized contribution universities make to local economies.  


Peter Mathieson, Edinburgh University’s principal and vice-chancellor received

£422,000 in total remuneration in 2023/24

 – equivalent to more than 10 times the university’s

median staff pay

. As part of his package,

Mathieson lives rent-free in a university-owned mansion

 on one of Edinburgh’s premier streets, where maintenance costs are also borne by the university.


Since Mathieson took up the role in February 2018, the university has acquired more than

£1bn

 in capital assets. Staff at the university have described its financial woes as “

manufactured

”.


Writing on X, Chabal, said: “I am not given to hyperbole when it comes to university industrial relations, but this feels like an existential event. The heart of the university is being torn out, with long-lasting consequences. These strikes are a last-ditch attempt to stop that. Will anyone listen?”


91% of union members at the University of Exeter voted in favour of industrial action, although dates have yet to be set for the walkout. As many as

500 jobs are at risk

, with the University and College Union (UCU) warning that more than 80% of arts and humanities staff were at risk of losing their jobs.


Starting today, staff at Nottingham University, are also set to strike for 67 days this


autumn, amid plans to restructure departments and potentially close courses.


In Scotland, the universities of Dundee, Glasgow Caledonian and Heriot-Watt have also voted to strike, as have the universities of Essex, Exeter and Sussex in England.


Lopa Leach, professor of vascular biology and former president of Nottingham’s UCU branch,

told the Guardian

: “The word is carnage, it is carnage what they are doing now – at the local level and also at the national, senior management level in the UK. Why are they thinking about the destruction of higher education?”

author: Unknown
title: Mazloum Abdi issues message on Kurdish-language education
content:
Syrian Presidential Adviser Mazloum Abdi delivered a video message through ANHA on Kurdish-language education, the situation of schools, Rojava University and Kobanê University.


The message was as follows:


“Dear people, the Kurdish language is our identity. Protecting and developing Kurdish has always been a fundamental objective of the struggle we have waged to this day. Learning and receiving an education in one’s mother tongue is a natural right of all peoples, and education in Kurdish is likewise a fundamental and natural right of the Kurdish people. Over the past 14 years, during the Rojava Revolution, tremendous efforts have been made to provide Kurdish-language education and establish an education system despite the conditions of war. Although it has had shortcomings and weaknesses, it was something new and represented a historic step in the history of Rojava.


I would like to take this opportunity to salute all the families who sent their children to Kurdish-language schools despite the war, difficulties and obstacles. I also congratulate all the teachers and staff who have contributed to the teaching and study of the Kurdish language over the past 14 years.


It has been one year and eight months since the fall of the Baath regime. Our efforts to make Kurdish an official part of Syria’s education system are continuing. Numerous meetings, initiatives and discussions have taken place towards this goal. As a result, the Ministry of Education issued a decision concerning the Kurdish language. Our people and students did not consider this decision sufficient and organised demonstrations, expressed their position and continued their struggle. We regard this as a right of our students and stand with them in this process.


However, as the new academic year has begun and we are in a transitional period, we need to ensure that the education system continues successfully through to the end of the year. Necessary measures have been taken to ensure that children attending Kurdish schools do not face difficulties. The children will not be disadvantaged; they will learn Arabic while continuing their education in Kurdish.


We expect families and students to continue sending their children to schools where Kurdish is the primary language of instruction. This will allow us to successfully complete the new academic year during this transitional period and secure greater rights for the Kurdish language next year. This will provide a foundation for achieving all our rights concerning the Kurdish language in full.


This year, ninth-grade and baccalaureate education will continue under the Autonomous Administration’s education system.


I therefore ask all students in these two grades to continue their studies under the existing Kurdish-language education system in order to better safeguard their future.


Discussions and negotiations are still continuing over the official recognition of Rojava University and Kobanê University. Although no final decision has yet been reached, we hope that an appropriate decision will be made in the interests of our students at both universities.


For the new academic year at both universities, we ask students who completed their education in Kurdish to submit their preferences in accordance with the system published by the Ministry of Higher Education so that they can secure their places at these universities.


Finally, I congratulate everyone on the new academic year and wish you all success.”

title: Mother of NATO prisoner: We are now victims of the judiciary too
content:
Twenty-nine-year-old earthquake survivor Halil Yakut was among those imprisoned in what was described as a witch-hunt against opposition groups ahead of the NATO Summit on 7–8 July 2026. Yakut, whose family home in Antakya was destroyed in the Maraş-centred earthquakes, was detained on 23 June 2026 in Muğla, hundreds of kilometres from Ankara, on the assumption that he was planning to stage a protest, and was subsequently imprisoned. An indictment prepared months later included anti-NATO articles published in Halk Okulu magazine and social media posts by Halkın Sesi TV concerning NATO bases as evidence relating to the alleged preparations for a protest ahead of the summit. It also referred to previous cases in which Yakut had been tried, including cases in which he had been acquitted. The indictment was submitted to the Istanbul 14th High Criminal Court, which ruled that it lacked jurisdiction over the case. Halil Yakut’s mother, Gülten Yakut, spoke to ANF and said: “We are earthquake survivors, but the injustice inflicted on my son has now made us victims of the judicial system as well.”


Gülten Yakut, whose family home in Antakya was destroyed in the Maraş-centred earthquakes, said she had not even had time to recover from the devastation because of what she described as the systematic use of hostile law against her son. She said Halil had repeatedly been imprisoned because of his struggle against injustice and unlawful practices. Yakut said, “We are earthquake survivors, but now we have also been made victims of the judiciary,” and expressing her anger at what her family had endured over the years. She said her son had been repeatedly targeted because he had been flagged by the police. Yakut recalled that Halil had previously been imprisoned in connection with the 6 February attack at Çağlayan Courthouse and said he had now been held for three months on the assumption that he was planning a protest ahead of the NATO Summit.


He was detained at the bus station before he could even set foot in Muğla


Yakut said her son was detained on 23 June 2026 in Muğla, hundreds of kilometres from Ankara, where the NATO Summit was due to take place. Yakut also said: “Halil was detained at the bus station before he could even set foot in Muğla. He had gone to Datça for a holiday. As soon as he got off the bus, the police detained him and held him in custody for three days. They asked whether he was preparing any action related to the NATO Summit and whether he knew anything about statements against NATO published on Halkın Sesi TV’s social media accounts. Although he said he had nothing to do with them, he was hastily imprisoned.” Yakut said that on the same day her son was detained, police simultaneously raided both the container home where the family was staying and the house they were renting in Hatay. Yakut added that her husband, who has Parkinson’s and Alzheimer’s disease, was at home during the raid but could not remember what had happened.


Halil’s imprisonment disrupted both our affairs and his treatment


Yakut said her son was initially held in a solitary isolation cell at Muğla E-Type Prison before being transferred to İzmir Şakran T-Type Prison. She said: “Halil had submitted a petition asking to be transferred to a prison in Adana so that he could be closer to us, but that did not happen. They transferred him to İzmir Şakran instead.” Yakut recalled that her son had also previously been imprisoned in what she described as unlawful circumstances and said: “Halil had previously been imprisoned on the pretext of the attack on Çağlayan Courthouse on 6 February. My son was forcibly transferred from Silivri Prison to Kırşehir Pit-Type Prison, where he began an indefinite hunger strike to protest against the isolation conditions imposed on prisoners. He was released on the 100th day of his hunger strike. Afterwards, he was working on a documentary about the earthquake, helping us with the sale of our land and also receiving medical treatment. His imprisonment once again on the pretext of the NATO Summit has disrupted both our affairs and his treatment.”


They keep putting my son’s old case files in front of him


Yakut said the indictment was issued in the third month of her son’s imprisonment. She pointed out that the indictment, which alleged preparations for a protest ahead of the NATO Summit, once again relied on accusations made by the same witnesses whose statements had been used to justify his imprisonment …

title: Öcalan must be able to carry out his work as Coordinator for Peace and Political Transition
content:
As a well-known saying goes, there can be no proper treatment without a correct diagnosis. Whatever anyone may say, the main issue on Turkey’s agenda today is the Peace and Democratic Society process, which began with Abdullah Öcalan’s call for the dissolution of the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK). The President of Turkey and the Speaker of Parliament have said that the process is important and progressing well. Yet recent developments raise doubts about how accurately the state understands the process. If there is a problem and a process aimed at resolving it, it can only be addressed with the parties directly concerned. The leadership of the Kurdish Freedom Movement, one of the principal parties to the issue, says that the process is not progressing well. Doubts inevitably grow when one side says things are not going well while the other insists that they are.


On the day the so-called framework law was passed, Justice and Development Party (AKP) Deputy Parliamentary Group Chair Abdullah Güler said that Abdullah Öcalan’s status would change and that he would subsequently meet with many different groups. Two months have passed, yet there has been no tangible outcome from those remarks. Nationalist Movement Party (MHP) leader Devlet Bahçeli and some government officials also said months ago that Öcalan would become the Coordinator for Peace and Political Transition, but those words have likewise remained unfulfilled. Anyone who now claims that the issue can be resolved without Öcalan assuming an open and official role is deceiving themselves. The leadership of the Communalist Movement is surely not issuing statements and assessments for the sake of it. The issue to which this movement is most sensitive is its leadership. Its cadres and fighters will therefore take no action unless what they say concerning their leadership is taken into account.


There is now a debate over disarmament. The very fact that the issue is being treated solely as a matter of disarmament shows that it has not been properly understood. It also suggests that a movement which has waged an extremely difficult struggle for 50 years has not been properly understood either. Its cadres and fighters say that unless their leadership is openly and officially involved in the process, there will be no laying down of arms and no return to Turkey. If the AKP government fails to take this seriously, it will run into a major obstacle. The government can therefore no longer conduct this process behind closed doors. Some aspects may not be made public, but the parties to the process must be able to act openly. Öcalan must now be able to carry out his work openly. Without this, there can be no progress in the process, because the Movement’s leadership wants Öcalan to be able to work openly and freely.


Kurdish People’s Leader Abdullah Öcalan must, of course, be able to meet frequently with his own organisation for the process to move forward. If he cannot meet with the organisation’s leadership and cadres over such a difficult issue, the process cannot develop properly. Failure to understand this would justify doubts about whether the state is serious about the process. The urgent priority, therefore, is for Kurdish People’s Leader Abdullah Öcalan to immediately begin carrying out his work as Coordinator for Peace and Political Transition. According to information we have received, if there is no development on this issue in the first week of October, the process could face its first genuine deadlock. Everything that happened before the law was passed was part of the discussion. The process has now entered the implementation phase. If Abdullah Öcalan, the chief negotiator of the Kurdish people, cannot work freely and fulfil his role, how can there be any talk of a process? The Kurdish people and democratic forces expect political actors to take steps towards democratisation. If the guerrillas are to lay down their arms and engage in politics, then democratic conditions must be created in which they can freely participate in political life.


Democratic politics cannot be pursued under the current legal and judicial conditions in Turkey. If parties operating within the existing political system cannot freely engage in politics and political groups are subjected to operations every day, then it is impossible to pursue a democratic political struggle that also encompasses the Kurdish people’s demand for a free and democratic life. Under such circumstances, how …

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: PQ’s Sonia Caron looks to switch from education to politics
content:
Nunatsiaq News reached out to each candidate running in the Ungava riding ahead of Quebec’s Oct. 5 provincial election. Here’s what Parti Québecois candidate Sonia Caron had to share.


Sonia Caron said she never saw herself going into politics. Her decision to run for MNA in the Ungava riding came after four parties approached her.


“After a very long reflection, I decided to make the jump,” the Parti Québécois candidate said in an interview from Lebel-sur-Quévillon.


A lifelong supporter of the party from Chibougamau, Caron has spent the last 25 years working in education. She serves as the director of professional development at the Centre de services scolaire de la Baie-James, which oversees trades programs in northern Quebec.


She said her priorities are the lack of frontline health services and clean drinking water in many remote communities, issues that need to be treated with urgency.


“I told myself, ‘We have to do something,’ because our region is undergoing major upheavals, and public services are constantly deteriorating,” Caron said.


The current opposition party has promised to double the budget for medical travel reimbursements and a massive increase in funding for frontline care to be offered at community clinics.


Caron has long worked alongside economic leaders in Quebec as a member of the Société du Plan Nord, which advises the provincial government on economic and social development in the north, and as a board member of Quebec’s mining industry institute.


She is also the president of the Conseil régional des Partenaires du Marché du travail de la Jamésie, which advises the province on labour supply and demand.


She said that the party wants to work hand in hand with Cree and Inuit on economic and social development and that it wants communities to benefit from royalties from the mining industry.


“I’ve always cared deeply about the Inuit villages,” Caron said, adding that she worked as a high school French teacher in Inukjuak in 2003.


Caron is among five candidates running for Ungava in Quebec’s provincial election. Advance polls have been open since Saturday and will close Wednesday. Election day is set for Oct. 5.

title: Yılmaz: Visually impaired people face barriers to sport
content:
Sport is one of the key areas that strengthens individuals’ participation in physical and social life, yet barriers preventing visually impaired people from accessing sport persist. Inaccessible sports facilities, limited opportunities for different sports and training, transport difficulties and economic constraints make it harder for visually impaired people to participate in sporting activities regularly and independently.


The lack of accessibility at sports facilities, particularly in urban areas, makes it difficult for visually impaired people to reach them independently and participate regularly in sporting activities.


Abdülmecit Yılmaz, President of the Amed Visually Impaired Sports Club and the Amed Federation of People with Disabilities, spoke to ANF about the difficulties visually impaired people face in accessing sport.


The biggest barriers are the lack of facilities and infrastructure


Yılmaz said people with disabilities were unable to participate freely in sport in the city and that the most fundamental problem was the lack of facilities where they could train and compete.


Yılmaz drew attention to goalball, a sport specifically designed for visually impaired people and said: “We face enormous difficulties in accessing sporting activities, particularly as visually impaired people. There is a sport for visually impaired people called goalball, but we do not have a court where we can play it. We do not have anywhere to train. This is one of the main problems we face. Because we have no court, we cannot train properly or go into our matches adequately prepared. When we travel to tournaments in western provinces, unfortunately we can find ourselves effectively defeated before we even arrive because we have not been able to train.”


We face serious barriers to participating in social life


Yılmaz said that, in addition to difficulties participating in sport, visually impaired people also faced serious barriers in accessing stadium stands and taking part in social life.


He said: “We can face a number of accessibility problems when we go to Amedspor matches. There is a great deal of interest in the city and in sport, but we have problems accessing tickets. Take the Passo app, for example. It was not designed to be accessible to visually impaired people. We use screen readers on our phones, and when apps are not designed to work with them, we cannot easily buy tickets. If we cannot get an e-ticket, we are effectively unable to exercise that right.


There is also an internet problem at the stadium. As a visually impaired person, when I go to a match, I want to experience the atmosphere but also know what is happening on the pitch. Since I cannot expect someone to describe everything to me, I need to follow the match on the radio or through an online broadcast. When there is no internet connection, we cannot access the broadcast and are left with nothing but the noise of the crowd. So, we cannot fully experience the atmosphere.”


Practices used in other cities should also be introduced locally


Yılmaz recalled the queues of people with disabilities waiting for tickets outside Amed Stadium and continued: “Last week, there was a queue of people with disabilities waiting for tickets outside Amed Stadium. These people encounter this situation simply because they want to watch an Amedspor match. You go to the match full of enthusiasm, but when you cannot watch it or encounter an upsetting situation, it takes all the enjoyment out of the experience.


The Federation, the Ministry of Youth and Sports and the Amedspor management need to find a joint solution to the ticketing problem. There are different practices at other clubs: people can obtain tickets online, or when they make a request, club officials can allocate tickets to people with disabilities. So why should people with disabilities in our city have to wait in ticket queues? We expect these problems to be resolved.”


Our athletes face serious financial difficulties


Abdülmecit Yılmaz said the proportion of people with disabilities and the potential pool of athletes in the region were above the average in Turkey. 


He said: “Research conducted in Turkey put the proportion of people with disabilities at 12.29 per cent, while the figure in Diyarbakır (Amed) is higher, at 15 per cent. Inevitably, this is also reflected in sport. Sports organisations working with visually impaired people carry out these activities on a voluntary basis, but we …
