title: Razzisti dentro. Esclusione sociale: dallo sdoganamento alla rivendicazione
content:
L’imbarbarimento del dibattito politico, in Italia e nel mondo, è un po’ lo specchio del vistoso arretramento culturale che sta investendo le nostre società. Stiamo attraversando una fase particolarmente critica, contraddistinta da tensioni che erodono, giorno dopo giorno, i legami sociali. Più di trent’anni di globalizzazione neoliberista e di turbocapitalismo hanno progressivamente impoverito gran parte della popolazione mondiale. Guerra e terrorismo fanno ormai parte del vissuto quotidiano di milioni di persone e rappresentano una cornice esistenziale percepita come quasi ineluttabile per la maggior parte di noi. Lo sviluppo esponenziale della tecnologia è diventato un formidabile trampolino di lancio per l’implementazione di sistemi militari, di controllo e di repressione sempre più sofisticati. Lo sfruttamento brutale della Terra e delle sue risorse ci sta portando dritti verso la catastrofe climatica. Aree sempre più vaste del pianeta sono sempre meno vivibili ed è anche per questo che i fenomeni migratori si fanno sempre più consistenti. Internet, i social media, l’intelligenza artificiale, sono il terreno privilegiato di un potere economico e politico manipolativo e invadente, un tecnofascismo che ha costruito una realtà distopica con la sua neolingua, i suoi disvalori, il suo mondo al contrario.


Già: il mondo al contrario. Sono passati tre anni da quando con questo titolo – accattivante come ogni retorica qualunquista che cerca di sollecitare la parte peggiore di noi – Roberto Vannacci ha dato alle stampe il suo libricino per mettere nero su bianco le sue aberrazioni. E sono passati già quattro anni da quando in Italia si è insediato il governo più fascista della storia repubblicana. Un governo di fascisti che è, tra le altre cose, il più longevo di sempre e che si appresta a concludere, pressoché indisturbato, la legislatura.


È abbastanza evidente che l’ascesa al potere di una classe dirigente tanto impresentabile è andata di pari passo con il progressivo degrado del discorso pubblico. Un degrado accompagnato dal peggioramento della qualità del personale politico di ogni schieramento, da destra a sinistra – nessuno escluso – e dallo spaventoso impoverimento, sempre in termini qualitativi, dell’offerta informativa.


Ed è così che, di fronte alla propria inadeguatezza, il governo è tornato a giocare la carta ben collaudata della distrazione di massa: spostare l’attenzione dalle vere cause dei nostri problemi. Ancora una volta, il dito viene puntato sugli stranieri, sugli immigrati, sugli indesiderabili, alimentando un razzismo che cova da sempre nel ventre molle della società italiana.


Il razzismo italiano deriva dal fatto che questo paese non ha mai fatto davvero i conti con la propria storia. È successo con il fascismo, per esempio, così come con il colonialismo. I cattivi erano sempre gli altri: i nazisti con i loro campi di concentramento o gli inglesi e gli americani con la tratta degli schiavi e la segregazione. Mentre noi, italiani-brava-gente, non abbiamo mai fatto niente di tutto questo. «Noi non siamo razzisti» – ci siamo sempre detti. E invece sì, altroché.


Questa specie di autoassoluzione, consolidatasi per anni, ha retto finché l’Italia – un paese storicamente fatto per lo più da emigranti – non è diventata essa stessa un luogo di immigrazione, scontando, peraltro, un vistoso ritardo rispetto ad altre società europee (e non solo).


Il processo, relativamente recente, è stato affrontato dalla classe dirigente italiana con un approccio squisitamente utilitaristico e repressivo che ha oggettivamente rallentato (se non addirittura ostacolato) la convivenza e l’integrazione. La resa produttiva dell’immigrato o la sua potenziale pericolosità sono stati gli unici criteri su cui è stata realizzata un’architettura di leggi e normative che strozzano, ancora oggi, le vite di migliaia di persone costringendole all’irregolarità, alla marginalità sociale o alla devianza a causa di una burocrazia criminogena, tanto cinica quanto demenziale, che nel pretendere di risolvere i problemi ne crea, invece, sempre di nuovi. Nel corso degli anni queste politiche sono state accompagnate da una comunicazione pubblica basata essenzialmente sull’allarmismo, sull’emergenza o anche sulla semplice diffidenza. L’immigrato in Italia è sempre stato un diverso, un alieno, un corpo estraneo. “Vucumprà” prima, “extracomunitario” poi.

author: Moataz Hagag, Mada Masr
title: Italian court sentences 3 Egyptian officers to jail in Regeni murder case
content:
An Italian court

sentenced

 on Monday three Egyptian security officers to 10 years imprisonment in absentia for the 2016 kidnapping of Giulio Regeni.

 


The convicted officers are Major Magdy Sherif of the National Security Agency and police officers Colonel Ather Kamal and Colonel Hesham Helmy. 


The court dismissed the charge of

conspiracy to commit aggravated murder

 that was leveled against Sherif, while another security official implicated in the case,

Major General Tarek Saber, was acquitted of all charges.

 


The Italian prosecution had requested in its closing arguments a life sentence for Sherif and 17 years and six months for the three other defendants.


“A ruling issued in the name of the Italian people, a ruling that stands as a safeguard for all the Giulios and Giulias of the world,” said Alessandra Ballerini, the family’s lawyer. Ballerini added that the verdict proves that the body of evidence presented before the court withstood its scrutiny.


“From this evening on, all regimes, along with their apparatuses and agents, will be forced to remember that human dignity is inviolable, as are human bodies; that impunity can be defeated; and that democracies can put a stop to arbitrary abuse,” she added.


Riccardo Noury, Amnesty International Italy’s spokesperson, believes the verdict played an important role in “scratching the wall of impunity built by the Egyptian authorities, since it found three security service officials guilty of a serious crime of international law. It is a victory for human rights and for accountability.”


But Noury added that a full read out of the verdict needs to take place. “There was not sufficient evidence to corroborate the charge of murder. As for the crime of torture, no one of the accused was found guilty, because in 2016 torture was not recognized as a crime in the Italian law. Otherwise, the sentences could have been harder.”


Yet, “the Italian judiciary was our best ally,” Noury concluded, adding that the Italian authorities might not welcome the verdict.


In his

statements

 following the verdict, Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said that “Egypt has not been convicted, three people have been convicted,” in a nod to how the verdict would not affect bilateral relations.

  


Tajani was

in Cairo

 earlier in September to sign off some bilateral agreements concerning human trafficking and irregular migration.

Meanwhile, Italian Prime Minister Georgia Meloni made a

major visit to Egypt in March 2024

, alongside other European leaders, to sign off the “comprehensive strategic agreement” between Egypt and the European Union, which elevated relations, including with a 7.4 billion euro in financial support.

 


On the Egyptian front, a government source told Mada Masr that a high-level call between the Egyptian and Italian leaderships took place ahead of the verdict to find a legal way out that takes into consideration the nature of bilateral relations. 


According to Italian law, there are levels of appeal before a final ruling is reached, and it is not believed at this time that there will be any

requests

 for the accused’s extradition to Italy.

 


***


A PhD student at the University of Cambridge, 28-year old Regeni had been in Egypt studying independent trade unions when he disappeared from a downtown Cairo metro station while on his way to meet a friend on January 25, 2016, the fifth anniversary of the 2011 revolution. His body was found just over a week later on February 3 by a highway on the outskirts of Cairo.


Upon hearing that a body had been discovered, then-Italian ambassador to Egypt Maurizio Massari promptly

visited


Zeinhom morgue.


He and his entourage were at first refused entry but after their insisting were allowed in, where they found Regeni’s body disfigured, showing marks of heavy torture.

 


A joint Italian-Egyptian investigation was launched.

Egyptian investigators

initially

 denied that Regeni’s body bore marks of torture and gave a number of narratives behind his murder, including that he died in a car accident, before announcing in March 2016 that they had

killed

 five members of a criminal gang specialized in robbing foreigners and impersonating police officers, as well as the discovery of Regeni’s passport and personal belongings in a flat owned by one of the gang members’ sister.

rejected

author: Joe Sandler Clarke
title: UN’s Israeli Settlements Blacklist Names Firms With UK Public Contracts
content:
Several companies with major British government contracts have once again been named in a

UN database of firms

 involved in the expansion of illegal Israeli settlements.


The database names 214 companies – 61 more than the previous year – that the UN human rights office has “reasonable grounds to believe” are involved in activities linked to Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank.


Earlier this month, the UK government announced new sanctions targeting the settlements, including a ban on the import of goods. 


Foreign secretary Ed Miliband

said the move

 – which will also involve action against companies that support settlement expansion – was the “beginning of a new approach”.


The firms named in the UN list include French infrastructure giant Egis, which operates the M40 motorway for National Highways; Motorola Solutions, which owns Airwave, the radio network used by British emergency services; and Heidelberg Materials, with which the UK government agreed a major carbon capture deal in 2025. 


Egis was listed for its role in planning the construction of a new light rail network in Jerusalem, which

rights groups say

 will connect Israeli settlements in occupied East Jerusalem with each other. An Egis spokesperson said the firm “has formally expressed its disagreement with this inclusion” in the UN database. 


Norwegian pension fund KLP

divested from Motorola

 in 2021 over the firm’s involvement in providing services for use in surveillance in the West Bank. 


Heidelberg directed us to

a statement it issued last year

 where it said its Israeli subsidiary had ceased all operations at the Nahal Raba quarry – located in the  West Bank – in 2023, and that neither it nor its Israeli subsidiary operates “any facilities in the occupied Palestinian territories, including East Jerusalem”. 


Spanish trainmaker CAF, which is involved in the Jerusalem light rail project, was also named in the UN list. The firm is in the running to build new trains for a suburban rail service in Scotland.

Trade unions have urged

 the Scottish government to exclude CAF over its links to the expansion of Israeli settlements in the West Bank, while ScotRail drivers have said they will

refuse to drive

 CAF trains if the deal goes ahead. 


ScotRail, which has the final say on the new train deal, told Novara Media it is “committed to a thorough evaluation” to ensure the final decision on the deal is fair. 


CAF has said

 its “operations cannot be interpreted as contributing to, facilitating, or benefiting from settlement related practices”. 


On the publication of the most recent database, Volker Türk, the UN human rights chief, said: “This report is another reminder to companies that they have human rights responsibilities and are expected to conduct due diligence to ensure that they do not become involved in human rights violations or abuses.” 


A spokesperson for the Scottish government’s transport department said its guidance holds that “firms who are exploiting assets in illegal settlements can be excluded from tender exercises for grave professional misconduct. The Scottish Government is clear that all Public Bodies should take any such evidence into account when deciding where to award public contracts.”

author: Alessandra Bergamin
title: Lebanon’s Environmental Defenders Say Israel Is Deliberately Targeting Them
content:
Israel has decimated Lebanon’s land — and is also slaughtering the people who protect it.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

In late April 2025, after 41-year-old farmer Oussama Farhat was discharged from the hospital, two pieces of shrapnel still lodged in his body, he hurried to check on an injured red fox. In his southern Lebanon village of Meiss el-Jabal, Farhat, a volunteer with the environmental organization Green Southerners, had helped rescue the cub from beneath the rubble of ongoing Israeli air strikes — the same kind that has decimated southern Lebanon and its people for the past three years. Now, the young fox was curled atop a starry blanket, its outstretched leg wrapped in a blue bandage.

In a message to Hisham Younes, the founder and president of Green Southerners, Farhat wrote that the fox cub would soon be ready for release.

Concerned, Younes replied: “Oussama, where are you?”

A member of the Lebanese Civil Defense, Farhat had been injured on April 25, 2025, after he and a fellow volunteer went to check for casualties unknowingly halfway through an Israeli double-tap strike — a tactic where an attack is followed by a second in the same location. In the days following October 7, 2023, Hezbollah, an armed group and political party formed in response to Israel’s 1982 invasion of Lebanon, launched rockets and artillery into occupied Shebaa Farms as an act of solidarity with the Palestinian people. Since then, Israel has continued to attack southern Lebanon near-daily, making Farhat’s village — just 700 yards from the UN-demarcated “Blue Line” that separates the two states — a hotspot.

After Farhat was discharged from the hospital, Younes implored him to go to Nabatieh, about an hour north, and rest with his family, including his elderly mother. But, says Younes, steadfast in his commitment to the south, Farhat explained that he needed to stay in Meiss el-Jabal.

“Please Oussama, you need to leave,” Younes replied.

The next day, Farhat was killed.

For the past three years and over two ceasefire agreements, Israel has systematically and violently erased life from southern Lebanon, committing what many, including Lebanon’s environment minister, have deemed an ecocide. An agricultural borderland in the heart of the historic fertile crescent, Israel has transformed southern Lebanon from small-scale and subsistence farms of tobacco, olives, and goats to a landscape set ablaze by white phosphorus munitions, littered with unexploded ordnance, and poisoned by the pesticide glyphosate. In a region where around 70 percent of families rely on farming, explained Ghassan Makarem, an organizer with the Lebanese food sovereignty organization AgriMovement, Israel has used airstrikes, shelling, and the steady roar of bulldozers to destroy around a quarter of the country’s cultivated land, burning olive groves to ash, slaughtering flocks of livestock, and flattening entire villages.

“Nothing that lives has been spared … It’s all part of the genocide that’s occurring.”

“Nothing that lives has been spared,” said Makarem. “It’s all part of the genocide that’s occurring.”

Since 2023, that genocidal violence, as described by multiple outlets, has displaced more than 1 million people, killing nearly 9,000 and injuring more than 30,500, mostly in the south. Included within that figure, alongside a high number of emergency services workers, are southern Lebanon’s land and environmental defenders — displaced, disappeared, injured, and killed, because of their commitment to steward and protect the land.

As Julia Choucair Vizoso, a senior fellow at the Arab Reform Initiative and researcher for The Public Source who has written about environmental struggle and food sovereignty in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA), explained, Israel has long had a policy, stretching from occupied Palestine to southern Lebanon, of attacking those who resist occupation by refusing to leave. Because of that, farmers, shepherds, fishers, and beekeepers have not only suffered as Israel destroys their livelihoods and land, but have been marked as a threat because of their very connection to it in the first place.

Among those environmental defenders is Farhat.

Six years ago, explained Younes, the farmer reached out to Green Southerners asking how best he could help local animals, especially those that were injured or sick. Farhat soon became part of the all-volunteer team …

author: Chris Walker
title: Alito Reverses Course, Announces Recusal From Major Corporate Fossil Fuels Case
content:
The Supreme Court associate justice had previously refused to step away from a case involving fossil fuel companies.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Supreme Court Justice Samuel Alito is recusing himself from a climate crisis-related case before the court this year, reversing his previous announcement that he would remain on the case despite his personal financial interests in its outcome.

Clerk of Court Scott Harris sent the announcement to attorneys on both sides of the pending matter on Monday.

“I am writing to inform the parties that Justice Alito has determined that he will not continue to participate in this case,” Harris wrote.

The letter gave no explanation as to why Alito came to the decision to recuse himself.

The case features ExxonMobil and Suncor Energy, which are seeking to have a Colorado-based lawsuit against them dropped, citing federal law they claim supersedes state statutes. State municipalities are suing the companies, seeking to hold them financially liable for the impacts of the climate crisis.

Alito does not have any financial stakes in either company. However, the associate justice does hold stocks in other fossil fuel-based companies, which means the outcome of the case could still directly benefit him.

Earlier this year, Alito said he would not recuse himself from the case, claiming that, because he doesn’t have any stocks in those companies specifically, he doesn’t have a vested interest in the case’s outcome.

“Justice Alito does not have a financial interest in any party,” a statement from the court read in May.

A coalition of progressive watchdog groups pushed back against that assertion, submitting evidence to Congress that Alito could be influenced by the pending ruling and urging lawmakers to investigate.

Alexandra Nagy, organizing director for Consumer Watchdog, one of the organizations involved in that request, reacted positively to Alito’s decision to recuse.

“Justice Alito’s recusal from Suncor v. Boulder is the right decision, and one he should have made from the start,” Nagy said, noting that “the Supreme Court’s Code of Conduct says a justice should step aside when the justice has a financial interest in the subject matter of a case or another interest that could be substantially affected by its outcome.”

“The public should not have to wonder whether a justice’s personal investments could benefit from a ruling that shields the fossil-fuel industry from liability,” Nagy added.

Others reacted to the decision by calling for limits on the stocks justices are allowed to invest in — if they’re allowed to have stocks at all.

“The real question is: Why does any justice hold stock in an individual company that is part of an industry that is going to appear before the court?” asked Louis Virelli, a law professor at Stetson University and an expert on judicial recusals.

Alito’s refusal to recuse in other key cases has been highlighted in the past, including in 2024, when he refused to step aside in cases involving January 6 defendants and in other high profile cases relating to President Donald Trump.

That year, it was revealed that Alito had flown a U.S. flag upside down — a symbol adopted by Trump loyalists and the “Stop the Steal” movement — outside of his Virginia home in 2021, shortly after Trump was impeached for instigating the January 6 attack. Alito also flew an “Appeal to Heaven” flag outside his home, a symbol commonly used by Christian nationalists.

This past Supreme Court term has been viewed negatively by most Americans. According to an Economist/YouGov poll conducted in July, only 36 percent of respondents gave the high court approving marks, while 50 percent said they disapproved of the court’s job over the past year. Alito also received a negative review, garnering a -7 point net approval rating from voters.

author: Harriet Williamson
title: Pressure Mounts at Labour Conference to Kick Palantir Out of NHS
content:
The NHS’s contract with Palantir has come under pressure at Labour party conference, with 20k party members backing a motion to end the service’s reliance on the US spytech firm. 


Healthcare workers and patients protested outside the venue, calling for the government not to renew a highly controversial £330m patient data contract with Palantir.


The company provides tech to the Israeli military during its genocide in Gaza, as well as custom surveillance tools to ICE in the US.. 


A majority

 of Labour voters


(76%)

 believe Andy Burnham’s government should allow Palantir’s NHS contract to expire without renewal in February 2027.


Around 30 health workers dressed in scrubs attended the No Palantir in the NHS demo outside the conference in Liverpool on Tuesday, ahead of Burnham’s speech. 


NHS doctor Rhiannon Mihranian Osborne, a campaigner at Medact, told Novara Media: “The government has the perfect opportunity to end this contract. It can do so safely and transition over to NHS-owned infrastructure. 


“Palantir’s NHS contract is a threat to the ethics we sign up to as health workers, it’s a

threat to our patient relationships

 and data privacy, and it’s a threat to the integrity and independence of NHS infrastructure.”


Patients cannot opt out of having their sensitive healthcare data stored on Palantir’s Federated Data Platform (FDP), and some Palantir staff are granted

“unlimited access”

to identifiable patient data by NHS England. 


First secretary of state Louise Haigh used her conference speech to delegates on Sunday to say Burnham’s government will refuse to “be in hock to foreign giants”, in a comment

understood to be aimed at

 Palantir. 


The Cheltenham Constituency Labour Party (CLP)

tabled a conference motion

 on tech sovereignty on Monday, stating that overreliance on US tech “poses unacceptable risks to the independence and security of the UK, its institutions and its people”. 


Exeter CLP called on the government to allow the NHS’s Palantir contract to expire in 2027, look to Greater Manchester’s approach as a “blueprint” and build an NHS-controlled replacement system. 


However, the motion was not chosen for debate, despite more than

20k members

 voting for it. 


Greater Manchester, where Burnham served as mayor for nearly a decade, has repeatedly rejected Palantir’s FDP in its NHS services, using

 a UK-created alternative

instead. 


More protests against Palantir are set to take place across England as part of an international week of action uniting health workers and unions in the US, Brazil and Europe.

title: Puerta del Sol (Μαδρίτη): Ένα κίνημα ταξικής αλληλεγγύης
content:
Εδώ και 4 μέρες, στην πλατεία Σολ στη Μαδρίτη, ένα αυθεντικό κίνημα ταξικής αλληλεγγύης έχει πάρει σάρκα και οστά. Με αφορμή την απόπειρα έξωσης της 87χρονης Μαρικάρμεν, έπειτα από αύξηση ενοικίου από τον ιδιοκτήτη του σπιτιού από 500 σε 1.650 ευρώ (!)


Η ταξική αλληλεγγύη νίκησε, και η αλληλεγγύα συλλογική δράση στάθηκε εμπόδιο απέναντι στους αδήφαγους και απάνθρωπους landlords, που με τόσο απροκάλυπτο τρόπο αναδεικνύουν την ουσία του καπιταλιστικού συστήματος: δηλαδή της κοστολόγησης της κερδοφορίας ως ατομικού δικαίωμα, έναντι του συλλογικού δικαιώματος στην ζωή με αξιοπρέπεια.


Το κίνημα σαφώς συνεχίζει δυναμικά, καθώς πραγματοποιούνται ανά μέσο όρο 70 εξώσεις την ημέρα.


Αύριο, τίθενται προς ψήφιση από το κυβερνητικό συνασπισμό οι εξής προτάσεις, μετά από τις πιέσεις του εργατικού κινήματος:


– Περιορισμός στα νομικά πρόσωπα όσον αφορά την αγορά ακινήτων.


– Πάγωμα των εξώσεων μέχρι να ρυθμιστούν τα ενοίκια.


Στο πανό, διακρίνεται το σύνθημα ” Αφεντικά και Ιδιοκτήτες, εχθροί της εργατικής τάξης” στο πανό της αναρχοσυνδικαλιστικής συνομοσπονδίας CNT, στη συγκέντρωση στη πλατεία.

title: “Se crean más condiciones para el ingreso al sistema de encierro juvenil y menos oportunidades de salir”
content:
La Comisión Provincial por la Memoria (CPM) presentó la sección de niñez de su Informe Anual 2026, un diagnóstico sobre los lugares de encierro y el sistema de promoción y protección de derechos que realiza en su calidad de Mecanismo Local de Prevención de la Tortura. Con la presencia de funcionarios judiciales e integrantes de organizaciones por los derechos de la niñez, sindicales y políticas, se generó un espacio de diálogo y debate para pensar los desafíos en torno a las políticas destinadas a niños, niñas y jóvenes, en particular a partir de la puesta en vigencia de la nueva y regresiva ley penal juvenil. Los ejes de un debate de larga data que no parece avanzar en más oportunidades para las nuevas generaciones sino en más encierro y violencia.


Las políticas de niñez están en crisis y no pueden responder a los problemas actuales de les jóvenes. Las graves regresiones en derechos de la nueva ley penal juvenil son el último eslabón de una sistema que desde hace muchos años viene reforzando el sistema penal y punitivo en detrimento del sistema de promoción y protección de derechos. Un sistema que responde con más encierro y violencia a las y los jóvenes más vulnerables.


El diagnóstico parte de lo relevado por la Comisión Provincial por la Memoria en su calidad de Mecanismo Local de Prevención de la Tortura y se pública en la sección de niñez del Informe Anual 2026, El sistema de la crueldad XX, que el organismo presentó días atrás en su edificio.


Los datos aportan claridad a la discusión: la cantidad de niños, niñas y adolescentes abordados por el sistema de promoción y protección de derechos pasó de 41.511 en 2018 a 85.907 en 2025, sin que el sistema haya sido dotado de los recursos necesarios para ese abordaje. En el otro extremo se encuentra el fuero de responsabilidad penal juvenil extendido ahora por la nueva ley, aunque las estadísticas indiquen otro cosa: en los últimos 10 años la cantidad de jóvenes imputados descendió un 55% mientras que la de detenidos se mantuvo constante.


“Se recargan las capacidades de actuaciones punitivitas por parte de los mismos operadores judiciales que antes actuaban de otra manera. No logro entender esta extensión de la mirada punitivista sin nada que lo justifique porque el delito no creció”, describió brevemente el defensor del fuero penal juvenil de La Plata Ricardo Berenguer sobre las primeras reacciones de los funcionarios judiciales ante la puesta en vigencia de la reforma de la ley penal juvenil que bajó la edad de punibilidad a los 14 años y extendió, además, la persecución a delitos leves que antes no eran abordados por la justicia penal. El funcionario, no obstante, advirtió que la ley cristalizó acciones de la justicia que ya venían ocurriendo: “A la extensión de la prisión preventiva como regla se suma la retención de los jóvenes en el sistema. No hay revisión de las penas ni medidas morigeratorias, que sí se le conceden a los adultos”.


En esa línea coincidió la jueza de garantías del joven del departamento de Moreno-General Rodríguez Mirta Guarino: “Las llaves de cualquier medida, ya sea una internación en un hogar o una de seguridad, la tenemos los jueces, pero estamos en un momento muy crítico y hay magistrados que ni siquiera responden un teléfono”. La jueza también llamó a revisar el funcionamiento del sistema de promoción y protección de derechos que funciona en una fragmentación absoluta y aún más con el penal.


Los funcionarios judiciales fueron algunos de quienes tomaron la palabra durante la presentación de la sección de niñez del Informe Anual de la CPM junto a las organizaciones y el propio organismo. “Es el triunfo de las políticas neoliberales, que pensaron con estrategias muy precisas, como endurecer el sistema penal. En la provincia de Buenos Aires desde el gobernador Ruckauf hasta acá, se profundizaron las políticas punitivistas de mano dura y no podemos seguir sosteniendo que son los resabios del patronato: el sistema de promoción y protección ha creado sus propios monstruos”, señaló Roberto Cipriano García.


De hecho uno de los datos más sobresalientes del informe es cómo la baja en la edad de punibilidad que entró en vigencia recientemente a partir de la reforma de la ley penal juvenil ya se implementaba en los hechos: el 20% de los menores de edad encerrados en la Provincia durante 2025 tenían menos de 16 años y estaban detenidos con la aplicación de una medida de seguridad determinada por la justicia.

title: Besê Hozat: The process cannot succeed without democratization
content:
Besê Hozat, co-chair of the KCK Executive Council, said in an interview with Medya Haber that the Peace and Democratic Society Process cannot succeed in Turkey without democratization.


This is the first part of the interview.


The discussions regarding the Peace and Democratic Society Process are ongoing. As movement, you have already taken a number of significant steps in this regard. Also, before Parliament adjourned, the framework law – which you referred to as a law that creates a foundation on which to build on – was passed. What has been done afterward, and what hasn’t? Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmuş stated that the process is running smoothly. Do you assess it similarly?


Before addressing your question, September 25 marked the anniversary of the martyrdom of our comrade Rıza Altun. He was commemorated extensively both in Kurdistan and abroad, and many commemorations were held. I commemorate all the martyrs of the revolution and freedom – represented by our comrade Rıza – with respect, love, and gratitude. Our comrade Rıza holds a very significant place and value within our struggle. With his theoretical, ideological, political, and practical experiences, as well as his consciousness and expertise, he has contributed greatly to this struggle. He has contributed immense value to this struggle. On the path illuminated by comrade Rıza and all our martyred comrades, we will carry out this struggle successfully – with determination, conviction, and resolve – and we will achieve success based on the principle of living up to their memory. This struggle will lead to victory. I wish to reaffirm this pledge once again on the occasion of this anniversary.


Coming to your question; we have made several statements regarding the framework law. From the very beginning, both Rêber Apo [Kurdish people’s leader Abdullah Öcalan] and our movement have clearly laid out our standing on this matter. We have made many assessments and statements based on the premise that this law should be a comprehensive one, that it should truly play the role of a foundational law, and that it should pave the way for a democratic solution to the Kurdish issue. This law did not fully meet these criteria, and accordingly, we have criticized it. It is an extremely flawed, internally contradictory, and paradoxical law. Implementing it as it stands – in a straightforward manner – is hardly possible anyway. This is quite clear. When we speak of the law’s comprehensiveness, it should have encompassed Rêber Apo’s physical freedom, his conditions for a free life and work, the leadership of the movement as a whole, and the entire organizational structure – from the top leadership down to every level – including Rêber Apo, who is excluded from the scope of this law.


The law should have demonstrated an approach and a commitment to taking democratic, political, and legal steps. It is known that both the emergence of the PKK and the armed struggle came about because of the lack of this. The existence of the Kurdish issue gave rise to the PKK and to the armed struggle. There is a very serious need for democratic, political, and legal steps that lay the groundwork for and pave the way toward resolving this issue. This law did not fully address this; that much is clear. It is also very, very difficult to describe it as a truly fundamental law in this regard. It is a legal text, and in that sense, it may have some significance. It is a step – a step on the legal level – that has emerged and developed within this process. However, it would not be realistic to ascribe much more meaning to it beyond that. Since the process began, we have taken very important steps as a movement. In particular, many steps were taken following the Call for Peace and Democratic Society on February 27, 2025 by Rêber Apo.


The PKK’s dissolution congress was a historic development. At this congress, the decision was made to cease armed struggle against Turkey. However, for this process to proceed, it was established as a fundamental requirement that Rêber Apo’s physical freedom be secured, allowing him to freely lead this process. This remains valid today. Numan Kurtulmuş made a statement the other day saying the process is running “like clockwork.” In reality, there is no such process running “like clockwork.” That is the truth of the matter. There is a process that is moving extremely slowly, a process driven by unilateral steps. At present, the state has not taken any …
